The proposed framework consists of three key components: participant detection, sub event detection, and summary tweet extraction. To make the system applicable in real data, an online clustering approach is developed to participant detection and an online temporal content mixture model is proposed to conduct sub event detection. Experiments show that the proposed framework can achieve similar performance with its batch counterpart.

title: Sentence level Sentiment Classification with Weak Supervision
abstract: Sentence level sentiment classification is important to understand users' fine grained opinions. Existing methods for sentence level sentiment classification are mainly based on supervised learning. However, it is very difficult to obtain sentiment labels of sentences and manual annotation is expensive and time consuming. In this paper, we propose an effective approach for sentence level sentiment classification without the need of labels of sentences. More specifically, we propose a unified framework to incorporate two kinds of weak supervision, i.e., document level and word level sentiment labels, to learn sentence level sentiment classifier. In addition, the contextual information of sentences and words extracted from unlabeled sentences are incorporated into our approach to enhance the learning of sentiment classifier. Experiments on benchmark datasets validate that our approach can effectively improve the performance of sentence level sentiment classification and significantly outperform many baseline methods.

title: Essence Vector based Query Modeling: A Case Study on Spoken Document Retrieval
abstract: Spoken document retrieval (SDR) has become a prominently required application since unprecedented volumes of multimedia data have become available in our daily life. Stimulated by the exciting success in many natural language processing related applications, representation learning has been an active research topic recently. The representative pioneers can date back to the word embedding methods. However, learning of paragraph representations may be more promising for tasks such as information retrieval and sentiment analysis. Nevertheless, as far as we are aware, there has been relatively less work in launching unsupervised paragraph embedding methods and investigating the effectiveness of these methods in the SDR task. Motivated by these observations, this paper presents a novel paragraph embedding method, named the essence vector (EV) model, which aims at inferring a representation for a given paragraph by encapsulating the most representative information from the paragraph and excluding the general background information at the same time. On top of the EV model, we propose three query language modeling mechanisms to improve the SDR performance. A series of empirical SDR experiments conducted on two benchmark collections demonstrate the good efficacy of the proposed framework, compared to several existing strong baselines.

title: Delayed Feedback Strategies for Online Learning to Rank
abstract: Learning to rank is used in settings where document ranking may be subject to multiple ranking criteria. Online learning to rank methods learn to combine multiple ranking criteria by incrementally learning from user feedback. The performance of such methods suffer from delayed feedback. We propose a three stage model to deal with this type of delay based on a delay strategy, an update strategy, and a buffer strategy, and show that a proper treatment of delayed feedback for online learning to rank can boost performance.

title: A Novel Cascade Model for Learning Latent Similarity from Heterogeneous Sequential Data of MOOC
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the proliferation of Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs). Various teaching and learning activities can be offered by the MOOC platform, e.g., watching videos and discussing in forums. However, due to `Massive' and lack of efficient management, the discussion forums always have been in disorder and chaos. Therefore, we propose a new application for filing the forum contents, which is to associate forum threads to subtitles of video clips. We regard this task as a problem of document ranking, and the difficulty is how to learn a distinguishable document representation. Traditional textual representations, e.g., Bag of words(BOW), do not consider the latent semantics. Recent semantic word embeddings, e.g., Word2Vec and Para2Vec, do not capture the latent similarity between documents. In this paper, we propose a novel cascade model which can capture both the latent semantics and latent similarity by modeling heterogeneous sequential data of MOOC. Experimental results on two real world datasets demonstrate that our newly learned textual representation can outperform the state of the art unsupervised counterparts on the new application.

title: Discriminative approach to effective sentiment classification
abstract: Due to the explosive growth of user generated contents, understanding opinions (such as reviews on products) generated by Internet users are important for optimizing business decision. To achieve such understanding, this paper investigates a discriminative approach to classifying opinions according to sentiments. The discriminative approach builds a model with prior knowledge of categorization information in order to extract meaningful features from the unstructured texts. The prior knowledge includes ratio factors to reinforce terms sentiment polarity by using TF IDF. Experimental results with three datasets show the proposed approach is very competitive, compared to some of the previous works.

title: Determining Semantic Textual Similarity with Natural Deduction Proof
abstract: Determining semantic textual similarity is a core research subject in information retrieval. Although the Bag of Words model is widely used to represent sentences, it fails to capture accurate semantics. In contrast, logical semantic representations capture deeper levels of sentence semantics, but their symbolic nature does not offer graded notions of textual similarity. We propose a method of determining semantic textual similarity by combining superficial features with features extracted from the natural deduction proof of bidirectional entailment relations between sentence pairs. For the natural deduction proof, we use ccg2lambda, a higher order automatic inference system, which converts CCG derivation trees into logical semantic representations and carries out a natural deduction proof. Experiments show that our system outperforms other logic based systems and that logic based features are effective for learning textual similarity.

title: Content Recommendation and Native Advertisement: Friends or Foes?
abstract: Many Web pages include recommendation bars. The bars contain content recommendation items (i.e., references to other Web pages) where the goal is to increase long term engagement with the Web site and native advertisements (ads) intended for short term monetization. We present the first empirical study of the mutual effects, in terms of click through rates (CTR), of content recommendation items and native ads within bars. One of the important findings is the increase of the CTR for ads when placing just before them content recommendation items rather than other ads. We discuss the connections and implications of this finding and others, along with the general task of populating a recommendation bar, with work on aggregated Web search and learning to rank.

title: E commerce Product Query Classification Using Implicit User's Feedback from Clicks
abstract: Query classification (QC) has been widely studied to understand users' search intent. For e commerce search queries, users typically refer either to a specific product or a category of products. In both cases, a query can be associated to a category label that belongs to the taxonomy tree describing the items in the catalog. However, product related search queries are typically short, ambiguous, and continuously changing depending on seasonal and new products that the catalog is exposing over time. Traditional supervised approaches to e commerce QC are not feasible due to the high cost of manual annotation and high volume of traffic on e commerce search engines. In this work, we introduce an unsupervised method to collect large amount of query classification data by using user's implicit click feedback. We obtain a large multi label dataset containing 403,349 unique queries with 2,085 categories. We compare and contrast different state of the art text classifiers and demonstrate that an ensemble of linear SVMs models achieves 0.60 and 0.82 micro F1 score at leaf and top level, respectively.

title: Leveraging Ratings and Aspect Sentiment to Estimate Contradiction Intensity in Reviews
abstract: Analysis of opinions (reviews) generated by users becomes increasingly exploited by a variety of applications. It allows to follow the evolution of the opinions or to carry out investigations on products. The detection of contradictory opinions about a web resource (e.g., courses, movies, products, etc.) is an important task to evaluate the latter. This paper focuses on the problem of detecting contradictions based on the sentiment analysis around specific aspects of a resource (document). First, identifying certain aspects, according to the distributions of the emotional terms in the vicinity of the most frequent names in the whole of the reviews. Second, estimating the polarity of each review segment containing an aspect. Then taking only the resources containing these aspects with opposite polarities (positive, negative). Third, introducing a measure of the intensity of the contradiction based on the joint dispersion of the polarity and the rating of the reviews containing the aspects within each resource. The evaluation of our approach is conducted on the Massive Open Online Courses (MOOC) collection containing 2244 courses and their 73,873 reviews, collected from Coursera. The results of experiments revealed the effectiveness of the proposed approach to capture and quantify contradictions.

title: A Text Embedding Framework for Sub Entity Ranking from User Reviews
abstract: Although user reviews are now part of everyday decision making, it is often difficult for people to rapidly read through the numerous reviews to form a conclusion according to the review opinions. To facilitate decision making, this paper proposes a novel text embedding framework for ranking sub entities from user reviews of a given super entity. As experiments on two real world datasets show, the proposed method outperforms two baseline methods by a statistically significant amount. Intriguing cases from the experiments are discussed in the paper.

title: Web2Text: Deep Structured Boilerplate Removal
abstract: Web pages are a valuable source of information for many natural language processing and information retrieval tasks. Extracting the main content from those documents is essential for the performance of derived applications. To address this issue, we introduce a novel model that performs sequence labelling to collectively classify all blocks (i.e. text elements) in an HTML page as either boilerplate or content. Our method uses neural networks on top of DOM tree based block features to learn unary and pairwise potentials. These are then further combined in a structured loss function. On a set of experiments on the widely used CleanEval dataset, we show significantly improved performance compared to state of the art competitors.

title: Temporal and semantic reasoning about Lexical Chains: Application for MOOC story segmentation
abstract: When exploiting textual data, by humans or even by machines, it is not necessarily required to have the same treatment as when the data has initially been produced. However, in order to exploit the textual data in a consistent manner, it seems necessary to maintain a certain level of semantic and temporal homogeneity. In the case of sequentially generated text or speech data, it becomes natural to partially take into account the sequential aspects. We therefore propose to consider the temporal information of each term in addition to the information conveyed by their meaning. In this article, lexical chains are employed to characterize the temporal information. Thus, relying on the principles of Allen's temporal logic over lexical chains, enriched by word embedding, we introduce a reasoning method that leads to the identification of semantically homogeneous zones.

title: Practical Fraud Transaction Detection
abstract: Nowadays, online payment systems play an increasingly important role in our daily lives. A key component of an online payment system is to detect and prevent fraud transactions, for the sake of user account safety and platform security. In industrial practice, such a fraud transaction detection task is resolved into two tasks: 1) mining evidential features from user accounts and behaviors, and 2) building an effective model on these features. Traditionally, the most popular fraud transaction detection methods use elaborately designed features to build tree based models, such as Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Decision Trees (GBDT), which have achieved good results. However, in those methods, the designed features usually only contain static user features, which can not capture the dynamic details of user behaviors. In addition, the estimated risk score is just a linear combination of the scores from separate trees, which cannot learn the complex relationships between different features. To address these issues, we propose a systematic method for fraud transaction detection. Our model uses two kinds of information, i.e., users' static information from their profiles and users' dynamic information from their behaviors. By using both information, we first generate three kinds of features, i.e., user static feature, user dynamic feature, and user embedding feature obtained from users' dynamic information using N GRAM model. We then apply a tree based model to handle these three kinds of features, and finally adopt Deep Neural Network (DNN) to learn the high level features from the output of underlying trees. Extensive experiments show that our proposed model (with both static and dynamic features) significantly outperforms the existing tree based methods. In addition, using the embedding from dynamic features can further improve the performance of the hybrid model.

title: Cluster Based Label Propagation
abstract: In multi label classification, classifier quality heavily depends on the quality of the dataset; to obtain reasonable results, the dataset must provide accurate labels. However, preparing a high quality dataset can be difficult, especially in cases where there are many labels and each data might be assigned some labels simultaneously by multiple users. In this paper, we propose a novel graph based multi label classification algorithm, cluster based label propagation (CLP). To smooth the effects of missing labels, CLP performs a clustering procedure that integrates the fundamental assumption of graph based classification, which states that nodes in the same cluster tend to have common labels. CLP then propagates the labels of clusters instead of those of nodes. We show that CLP improves the stability of the state of the art algorithm when processing a dataset in which some data lack multiple suitable labels.

title: Improved Document Ranking with Word Embeddings
abstract: This paper evaluates existing and newly proposed document (re )ranking methods based on pre trained word embedding features. Word embeddings have been highly effective in a variety of natural language processing tasks and their integration into traditional information retrieval (IR) systems allows for the capture of semantic relatedness between query and document. Empirical results on three publicly available data sets show significant gains over traditional term frequency based approaches in both supervised and unsupervised settings. We show that combining these word embedding features with traditional learning to rank techniques can achieve similar performance to state of the art neural networks trained for the answer selection task.

title: Using Word Embedding for Ad hoc Information Retrieval
abstract: In recent years, words embedding algorithms and research have led to significant breakthroughs at natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, few positive results of them on ad hoc retrieval tasks, the challenge is to devise an effective and efficient strategy for obtaining representations of compound units of text, such as whole documents, (in comparison to the atomic words), for the purpose of indexing and scoring documents. Instead of striving for a suitable method to obtain a single vector representation of a large document of text, we aim to develop a simple method to learn semantically meaningful representations for words from local occurrences in local context, and integrated with BM25 to induce the data sparsity influence enhance performance in ad hoc retrieval task. Experiments conducted on three representative TREC collections of varied sizes and contents show that the proposed model improves the baseline models promisingly.

title: Semantic Based Document Retrieval Using Spatial Distributions of Concepts
abstract: Based on our indexing approach from content based image retrieval, we devise a representation for a text document, based on the spatial distribution of content semantics, utilizing lexical cohesion. We perform several experiments demonstrating the efficacy of our approach over the standard bag of words (BOW) approaches, both syntactically and semantically based.

title: Modeling and Predicting User Session Length in Media Streaming Using Survival Analysis
abstract: Session length is a very important aspect in determining a user's satisfaction with a media streaming service. Being able to predict how long a session will last can be of great use for various downstream tasks, such as recommendations and ad scheduling. Most of the related literature on user interaction duration has focused on dwell time for websites, usually in the context of approximating post click satisfaction either in search results, or display ads. In this work we present the first analysis of session length in a mobile focused online service, using a real world data set from a major music streaming service. We use survival analysis techniques to show that the characteristics of the length distributions can differ significantly between users, and use gradient boosted trees with appropriate objectives to predict the length of a session using only information available at its beginning. Our evaluation on real world data illustrates that our proposed technique outperforms the considered baseline.

title: Exploring the Query Halo Effect in Site Search: leading people to longer queries
abstract: People tend to type short queries, however, the belief is that longer queries are more effective. Consequently, a number of attempts have been made to encourage and motivate people to enter longer queries. While most have failed, a recent attempt conducted in a laboratory setup in which the query box has a halo or glow effect, that changes as the query becomes longer, has been shown to increase query length by one term, on average. In this paper, we test whether a similar increase is observed when the same component is deployed in a production system for site search and used by real end users. To this end, we conducted two separate experiments, varying the rate at which the color changes in the halo were induced. In both experiments users were assigned to one of two conditions: \halo{} and \nohalo. The experiments were ran over a fifty day period with 3,506 unique users submitting over six thousand queries. In both experiments, however, we observed no significant difference in query length. We also did not find longer queries to result in greater retrieval performance. While, we did not reproduce the previous findings, our results indicate that the query halo effect appears to be sensitive to performance and task, limiting its applicability to other contexts.

title: Quantization in Append Only Collections
abstract: Quantization is the pre calculation, and conversion to integers, of term/document weights in an index and is a well studied aspect of search engines that substantially improves retrieval efficiency. Prior work has considered the impact that quantization has on the efficiency and effectiveness trade offs within a search engine. For static web based collections a relationship between collection size and range of quantization was discovered. In this work we extend this work to append only collections and discuss whether quantization parameters derived from prior time periods can be applied in the future. We find that along with trends identified in the literature generalising to an additional ranking function, and collection with different characteristics that we can use previous quantization parameters without substantial loses in either efficiency or effectiveness.

title: Memory Retention in Neural Networks
abstract: We present a cognitively motivated framework to investigate memory retention, the ability of maintaining and retrieving previously seen information, in artificial neural networks. Our research is inspired by broad evidence in psychology which shows that the probability that a human recalls a previously seen item, e.g. the Japanese translation of a given English word, depends on the difficulty of the item, delay since last review of the item, and strength of the human memory. In this paper, we compare three widely used artificial neural networks in terms of the above factors and present new findings about their memory retention.

title: Local Event Discovery from Tweets Metadata
abstract: We present a two step strategy that addresses fundamental deficiencies in social media based event detection and achieves effective local event by taking advantage of geo located data from Twitter. While previous work has mainly relied on an analysis of tweet text to identify local events, we show how to reliably detect events using meta data analysis of geo tagged tweets. The first step of the method identifies several spatio temporal clusters within the dataset across both space and time using metadata to form potential candidate events. In the second step, it ranks all the candidates by the amount of hashtag/entity inequality. We used crowdsourcing to evaluate the proposed approach on a data set that contains millions of geo tagged tweets. The results show that our framework significantly outperforms existing methods in precision and discovers events faster.

title: Geolocating Tweets in Temporal Proximity
abstract: In fine grained tweet geolocation, tweets are linked to the specific venues from which they were posted. For this problem, we focus on the scenario where a user posts multiple tweets within a short time interval. Empirically, we observe users to be spatially focused in time. Within a short time interval, a user is more likely to be stationary at a venue or traversing between nearby venues, than traversing venues that are far apart. This means that a user's tweets in the described scenario are likely to be posted from the same venue or venues near each other. Such tweets may be useful for one another's geolocation by providing complementary information. To exploit this idea, we geolocate test tweets that are augmented by the contents of their temporal neighbors. Our approach is akin to treating the test tweet as a query and conducting query expansion using time. We derive a weighted naive bayes model which achieves promising results in our experiments.

title: Top N Recommendation with High Dimensional Side Information via Locality Preserving Projection
abstract: In this paper, we leverage high dimensional side information to enhance top n recommendations. To reduce the impact of the curse of high dimensionality, we incorporate a dimensionality reduction method, Locality Preserving Projection (LPP), into the recommendation model. A joint learning model is proposed to achieve the task of dimensionality reduction and recommendation simultaneously and iteratively. Specifically, item similarities generated by the recommendation model are used as the weights of the adjacency graph for LPP while the projections are used to bias the learning of item similarity. Employing LPP for recommendation not only preserves locality but also improves item similarity. Our experimental results illustrate that the proposed method is superior over state of the art methods.

title: Exploiting Local and Network Properties for Life Collaborator Prediction
abstract: While scientific collaboration can be critical for a scholar, some collaborator(s) can be more significant than others, a.k.a. life collaborator(s). This work aims to investigate whether it is possible to predict/identify life collaborators given a junior scholar's early profile. For this purpose, we propose a series of features by leveraging scholars' local and network properties. Extensive experiments on DBLP digital library demonstrate that life collaborators can be accurately predicted. The proposed model outperforms baseline model with various predictors. Our study may shed light on the exploration of scientific collaborations from the perspective of life long collaboration.

title: SCRec: Sustainable Collaborator Recommendation Based on Conference Closure
abstract: It is often hard for researchers to find a new collaborator due to the academic information overload. Previous work has proposed many scientific collaborator recommendation systems. However, most existing schemes evaluate their methods in terms of accuracy or precision, which does not comprehensively correspond to scholar need, for example, sustainable collaborations. A sustainable scholar will have a significant positive impact on productivity and impact. To address this problem, in this paper, we propose a sustainable collaborator recommendation system, which takes advantages of conference closure. The experimental results on a real data set show that integrating the scholars' personal information, e.g., conference attending, can recommend more sustainable collaborators. Despite its exploratory nature, this study offers some insights into scientific collaborator recommendation from the perspective of sustainability.

title: Definitions of Primitive Query Operations and Algebras for Temporal Social Network
abstract: The popularity of social networks has recently led to rapid growth of Temporal Social Network (TSN). Adding temporal information to an ordinary query for social network, it becomes interesting to discover historical insights of the result, and a fertile ground is created for novel social interactions and advertising. This paper is a subsequent work to our previous work which studied three kinds of specific TSN queries. As we discover that there are various kinds of TSN queries and it is difficult to measure which is more important and solve one by one. This paper draws the first systematic work by studying primitive query operations on TSN query processing. We define 4 primitive query types as basic query types and then design algebras to form complex or high level queries, finally we use case study to improve our primitive queries and algebras are capable to express various kinds of temporal queries in social networks.

title: Cross language Citation Recommendation via Publication Representation Merging Content and Citation
abstract: While citation recommendation can be important for scholars, unfortunately, because of language barrier, some scientists cannot efficiently retrieve and consume the publications hosted in a foreign language repository. In this study, we propose a novel solution, cross language citation recommendation via Publication Representation merging Content and Citation (PRCC). PRCC can learn a mapping function by mapping the publication to a low dimensional joint embedding space for both content semantic and citation relation. The proposed method can first apply a cross language content semantic enrichment for a given citation networks to generate a merged relation network, then optimize the publication representations by maximizing the likelihood of observing network neighborhoods of publications. Experimental results show that the proposed method can be promising for cross language citation recommendation.

title: Distributed Representation for Neighborhood based Collaborative Filtering
abstract: Collaborative filtering is widely used in recommender systems. When training data are high dimensional sparse, the current neighbor selection methods cannot work very effectively for the neighborhood based collaborative filtering. To address this issue, this paper proposes a distributed representation method that presents users as low dimensional vectors for neighbor selection by considering the chronological order of the users ratings. Experiments show that the proposed method outperforms the traditional neighbor selection methods according to precision and ranking.

title: Applying Information Extraction for Patent Structure Analysis
abstract: Patent engineers are spending significant time analyzing patent claim structures to grasp the range of technology covered or to compare similar patents in the same patent family. Though patent claims are the most important section in a patent, it is hard for a human to examine them. In this paper, we propose an information extraction based technique to grasp the patent claim structure. We confirmed that our approach is promising through empirical evaluation of entity mention extraction and the relation extraction method. We also built a preliminary interface to visualize patent structures, compare patents, and search similar patents.

title: Variational Random Function Model for Network Modeling
abstract: Link prediction is a fundamental problem in network modeling. A family of link prediction approaches is to treat network data as an exchangeable array whose entries can be explained by random functions (e.g., block models, Gaussian processes) over latent node factors. Despite their powerful ability in modeling missing links, these models tend to have a large computational complexity and thus are hard to deal with large networks. To address this problem, we develop a novel variational random function model by defining latent Gaussian processes on exchangeable arrays. This model not only inherits the ability of Gaussian process to describe the nonlinear interactions between nodes, but also enjoys significant reduction on computational complexity. To further make the model scalable to large network data, we develop an efficient key value free strategy under the Map Reduce framework to tremendously reduce the inference time. Experimental results on large network data have demonstrated both the efficacy and efficiency of the proposed method over state of arts methods in network modeling.

title: Enhancing Recurrent Neural Networks with Positional Attention for Question Answering
abstract: Attention based recurrent neural networks (RNN) have shown a great success for question answering (QA) in recent years. Although significant improvements can be achieved over the non attentive models, the position information is not well studied within the attention based framework. In this paper, motivated by the effectiveness of using the word positional context to enhance information retrieval, we assume that if a question word occurs in an answer sentence, the neighboring words should be given more attention since they may contain more valuable information for question answering than those far away. Based on this assumption, we propose a positional attention based RNN model, which incorporates the positional context of the question words into answers' attentive representations. Experiments on two benchmark datasets show the great advantages of our proposed model. Specifically, we achieve a maximum improvement of 8.83\% over the classical attention based RNN model in terms of mean average precision. Furthermore, our model is comparable to if not better than the state of the art approaches for question answering.

title: RevMap: A Visualized Framework For Holistic View of Reviews
abstract: Our daily digital life is surrounded by algorithmically selected contents such as recommendations, reviews, and news feeds. The process of extracting useful information out of large volumes data is imposing great impacts on many aspects of people's life. However, as the data volume becomes huge, users tend to get lost in details and miss the general picture. Indeed, the fast growing online data has required the development of systems that not only accurately distil useful and representative knowledge out of large data corpus but also display the extracted information in an easy to understand manner. In this paper, we propose a unified framework which generates visual structured summaries of customer reviews, thus providing a holistic view of a large group of reviews. Our model employs a deep neural network for opinion mining which relies on the character level inputs. To the best of our knowledge, previously there is no uniform framework that performs visual summarization of consumer opinions as proposed in this paper.

title: Infusing Latent User Concerns from User Reviews into Collaborative Filtering
abstract: Traditionally Collaborative Filtering (CF) based recommendation employs past rating behaviors of users on items to discover similar users and similar items. We can further improve on discovering user similarities by better understanding user behaviors through analyzing user reviews. In their reviews, users generally mention about things that are of greater interest to them, and these cues can provide an effective medium to discover users with similar interests and concerns. In this paper, we extract latent User Concerns from user reviews and construct their hierarchical tree (UC Tree). By associating each user with the corresponding concerns in the UC Tree, we then generate vectors that represent intricate user behaviors. Finally, we infuse such additional knowledge about the users into the conventional CF based rating prediction process. Our experiments and results show that such additional behavioral knowledge assists the discovery of similar users and improves the accuracy of conventional CF based rating prediction.

title: Denoising Clinical Notes for Medical Literature Retrieval with Convolutional Neural Model
abstract: The rapid increase of medical literature poses a significant challenge for physicians, who have repeatedly reported to struggle to keep up to date with developments in research. This gap is one of the main challenges in integrating recent advances in clinical research with day to day practice. In response, researchers have been proposing several clinical decision support (CDS) search systems that retrieve relevant medical literature given a clinical note describing a patient. We present a convolutional neural model aimed at reducing the noisy clinical notes to be used as queries for medical literature retrieval. This approach was evaluated on the 2016 TREC CDS track dataset, which contains real clinical notes alongside fictional summaries created by experts. The proposed method shows an improvement of 67% over the unmodified clinical note, and a 14% improvement over state of the art query reduction methods.

title: MIPEL: Multi Input Product Embedding Learning for E Commerce Applications
abstract: Recommender system is the cornerstone of E commerce applications. Many recommendation algorithms are trained on a single type of data source, and thus suffer from the cold start problem and do not scale to hundreds of millions of products. This paper presents MIPEL a scalable deep learning model for training product embeddings from multiple data sources, including behavior data, product meta data and descriptions. This novel model utilizes a pooling layer to aggregate projections from multiple inputs for behavior learning and semantic modeling simultaneously. Furthermore, techniques are proposed to accelerate model training. Finally, a set of online experiments are conducted with two large scale operational recommendation tasks. The results show that the recommendation performance using the proposed product embedding significantly outperforms several existing solutions.

title: Movie Rating Prediction using Recurrent Neural Network Regression
abstract: Movie rating is an essential criterion for evaluating the quality of a movie and a critical indicator that determines whether a customer would watch a movie. An important related research challenge is to predict the rating of a movie before it is released in cinema or even before it is produced. Many existing approaches to predicting movie ratings are based on post production factors such as review comments from social media, thus they are only applicable when a sufficient number of review comments are available, which are generally obtainable only after the movie has been released for a certain period of time. In this paper, we propose a recurrent neural network based regression model for predicting movie ratings by learning from a movie's intrinsic pillars which are obtainable before movie production such as the cast, director and storyline of the movie. Compared to previous work, our model explores the correlations between the rating of a movie and its intrinsic attributes, which provide a reference for investors and movie studios to determine an optimal portfolio for the production of the movie and a guidance for interested audiences to choose the movie. Extensive experiments on a real dataset are benchmarked against a set of baseline approaches and demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in predicting ratings.

title: Deep Discriminative Hash Ensemble for Mobile Visual Search
abstract: The strong need for mobile visual search and recognition has been emerging due to its broad applications and business potential. Since real valued image features can barely work in real large scale industry environment due to the heavy computation burden, hash based retrieval is becoming a hot research topic and the dominant approach for the real time mobile visual search system. However, existing image hashes can achieve very limited retrieval accuracy. Firstly, most existing hashing methods are basically extracted in an unsupervised manner, which is more suitable for dealing with the low level image search rather than the semantic similarity search. Second, the notorious missing bucket problem, which easily miss the nearest neighbor if a point has been hashed to a different bucket than its nearest neighbor, often cause another significant accuracy degradation in practice. In this paper, we propose a novel deep learning based method to compute an image hash that is both robust and efficient for mobile visual search. Unlike traditional hash that trades accuracy with speed, the proposed Runtime Dropout Ensemble unconventionally uses dropout in the runtime/testing stage to create multiple independent representation of an image. It thus increases the hit rate of true neighbor in hash bucket, and reduce the likelihood of missing bucket problem. Our evaluation on several benchmark datasets, including real world e commerce product images, verifies the efficacy and accuracy of the proposed framework.

title: Detecting True and False Duplicate Questions in Community Question Answering Archives
abstract: In this paper we introduce the task of false duplicate question detection for cQA question pairs. We show that it is possible to automatically identify false duplicate question pairs, and that this task is similar in complexity to duplicate question detection. We find that for both tasks, meta data features that capture user authority, question quality, and relational data between questions, outperform pure text based methods.

title: (1) Finding similar needles in a question haystack Using a tripartite network to improve similar question retrieval in CQA
abstract: Collective intelligence of the crowds is distilled together in various Community Question Answering (CQA) Services such as Quora, Yahoo Answers, Stack Overflow forums. Since users' information needs often overlap, very often, for a new incoming question, the answer is already present in the CQA dataset in the form of similar QA pair. Therefore, efficiently similar questions enables re use of existing knowledge. However similar question retrieval becomes challenging due to vocabulary diversity and lexical gap issues encountered in large CQAs. In this paper, we propose a a novel tripartite neural network based approach for addressing the similar question retrieval problem. The network takes inputs in the form of question answer and new question triplet and learns internal representations from similarities among them. Our approach achieves classification performance of upto 77% on a real world CQA dataset, specifically performing better in handling the problem of 'zero lexical overlap' among questions compared to baseline.

title: Event Early Embedding: Predicting Event Volume Dynamics at Early Stage
abstract: Social media has become one of the most credible sources for delivering messages, breaking news, as well as events. Predicting the future dynamics of an event at a very early stage is significantly valuable, e.g, helping company anticipate marketing trends before the event becomes mature. However, this prediction is non trivial because a) social events always stay with ``noise'' under the same topic and b) the information obtained at its early stage is too sparse and limited to support an accurate prediction. In order to overcome these two problems, in this paper, we design an event early embedding model (EEEM) that can 1) extract social events from noise, 2) find the previous similar events, and 3) predict future dynamics of a new event. Extensive experiments conducted on a large scale dataset of Twitter data demonstrate the capacity of our model on extract events and the promising performance of prediction by considering both volume information as well as content information.

title: POI Popularity Prediction via Hierarchical Fusion of Multiple Social Clues
abstract: Predicting the popularity of Point of Interest (POI) has become increasingly crucial for location based services, such as POI recommendation. Most of the existing methods can seldom achieve satisfactory performance due to the scarcity of POI's information, which tendentiously confines the recommendation to popular scene spots, and ignores the unpopular attractions with potentially precious values. In this paper, we propose a novel approach, termed Hierarchical Multi Clue Fusion (HMCF), for predicting the popularity of POIs. Specifically, we devise an effective hierarchy to comprehensively describe POI by integrating various types of media information (e.g., image and text) from multiple social sources. Each individual POI, we simultaneously inject semantic knowledge as well as multi clue representative power. We collect a multi source POI dataset from four widely used tourism platforms. Extensive experimental results show that the proposed method can significantly improve the performance of predicting the attractions' popularity as compared to several baselines.

title: Emotion Detection from Text via Ensemble Classification Using Word Embeddings
abstract: Emotion detection from text has become a popular task due to the key role of emotions in human machine interaction. Current approaches represent text as a sparse bag of words vector. In this work, we propose a new approach that utilizes pre trained, dense word embedding representations. We introduce an ensemble approach combining both sparse and dense representations. Our experiments include five datasets for emotion detection from different domains and show an average improvement of 11.6% in macro average F1 score.

title: Multitask Learning for Fine Grained Twitter Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Traditional sentiment analysis approaches tackle problems like ternary (3 category) and fine grained (5 category) classification by learning the tasks separately. We argue that such classification tasks are correlated and we propose a multitask approach based on a recurrent neural network that benefits by jointly learning them. Our study demonstrates the potential of multitask models on this type of problems and improves the state of the art results in the fine grained sentiment classification problem.

title: Example based Location Set Retrieval
abstract: Searching for spatial objects is prevalent in map services (e.g., Google Maps). To rent an apartment, for example, one will take into account its nearby facilities such as supermarkets, hospitals and subway stations. Traditional keyword search solutions, such as the nearby function in Google Maps, is not effective in expressing the often complex attribute/spatial requirements of sophisticated queries. However, such requirements are important to convey the user requirement (a.k.a search intention). To assist users in expressing such requirements, we propose Spatial Exemplar Query (SEQ), which allows the user to input a result example over an interface inside the map service. Then, we propose an effective similarity measure to evaluate the proximity between a candidate answer and the user's example. We also conduct a user study to demonstrate the effectiveness of SEQ. The result of user study shows that more than 88% of users would like to have an example assisted search in map services, and SEQ results get a 4.3/5.0 satisfactory score from users, compared with 1.8/5.0 of the baseline.

title: Micro Collaboration and Answer Quality in Social Q&A: An Exploratory Study of Zhihu
abstract: Online Q&A communities have increasingly become a platform for information seeking, sensemaking, knowledge creation and learning. This exploratory study investigated the initiation and response patterns of online micro collaboration among users in relation to answer quality in a social Q&A community, Zhihu.com(China). We sampled question answer pairs and comments made to them in the health domain and conducted content analysis of 220 micro collaboration cases occurred 20 answers and 2287 comments. Results show that: (1) The majority of microcollaboration instances were generated by asking a follow sub question or by criticizing or pointing out errors and mistakes in the answers; (2) Thirteen pairs of micro collaboration actions improved eight quality measurements, especially informativeness, completeness and level of detail; micro collaborations initiated by criticizing the original answer seem to be more related to improvement in objectivity and trustfulness.

title: Evolution of Information Needs based on Life Event Experiences with Topic Transition
abstract: We propose a method to clarify the evolution of users' information needs related to a users' interests and actions based upon life events such as "childbirth." First, we extract topic transitions using dynamic topic models from blogs posted by users who have experienced life events. Next, we select the topics by computing the differences in topic probabilities before and after the life event. We evaluated our method based on three life events: "childbirth," "finding employment," and "marriage." Our method selected life event relevant topics such as "child development," "working life," and "wedding ceremony." In the "childbirth" life event, we found mothers' information needs for such topics such as "baby food" and "crawling child." We also confirmed that the analysts could grasp that the relationship between allergies and the elapsed months after childbirth determine when to begin giving baby food.

title: Distribution oriented Aesthetics Assessment for Image Search
abstract: Aesthetics has become increasingly prominent for image search to enhance user satisfaction. Therefore, image aesthetics assessment is emerging as a promising research topic in recent years. In this paper, distinguished from existing studies relying on a single label, we propose to quantify the image aesthetics by a distribution over quality levels. The distribution representation can effectively characterize the disagreement among the aesthetic perceptions of users regarding the same image. Our framework is developed on the foundation of label distribution learning, in which the reliability of training examples and the correlations between quality levels are fully taken into account. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets well verified the potential of our approach for aesthetics assessment. The role of aesthetics in image search was also rigorously investigated.

title: On the effectiveness of feature set augmentation using clusters of word embeddings
abstract: Word clusters have been empirically shown to offer important performance improvements on various tasks. Despite their importance, their incorporation in the standard pipeline of feature engineering relies more on a trial and error procedure where one evaluates several hyper parameters, like the number of clusters to be used. In order to better understand the role of such features we systematically evaluate their effect on four tasks, those of named entity segmentation and classification as well as, those of five point sentiment classification and quantification. Our results strongly suggest that cluster membership features improve the performance.

title: Mining and Diversifying Query Subtopics Exploiting Web Documents
abstract: Generally, users are laconic in describing their search intention when they submit their query into the search engine. Therefore, a large number of search queries are usually short, ambiguous, and have multiple interpretations. Identifying possible subtopics is a fundamental step for effective search, particularly in search result diversification. In recent years, researchers have investigated subtopic mining through a variety of approaches. This paper is aimed at mining and diversifying subtopics underlying a query exploiting top retrieved web documents. Given a query, we select subtopic candidates from noun phrases extracted using web documents based on their relatedness with the query. To estimate the relevancy between query and subtopic, this paper introduces an approach using a locally trained sentence embedding model. Finally, we propose a novel diversification technique to rank the subtopic candidates combining their relevancy and the coverage in web documents. The experimental results on two NTCIR English subtopic mining datasets demonstrate that our proposed method achieves a new state of the art performance and significantly outperforms the known related methods.

title: Leveraging Moderate User Data for News Recommendation
abstract: The web provides access to a large amount of news articles coming from a variety of sources. It becomes crucial for news aggregator websites which are recent in the market to actively engage its existing users. It is very crucial for such sites to not lose its existing userbase. A recommendation system would help to tackle such a problem. However, due to the lack of sufficient amount of data, most of the state of the art methods perform poorly in terms of recommending relevant news items to the users. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for Item based Collaborative filtering for recommending news items using Markov Decision Process(MDP) to handle this issue. Due to the sequential nature of news reading, we choose MDP to model our recommendation system as it is based on a sequence optimisation paradigm. Further, we also incorporate factors like article freshness and similarity into our system by extrinsically modelling it in terms of reward for the MDP. We compare it with various other state of the art methods. On a moderately less amount of data we see that our MDP based approach outperforms the other approaches. One of the reasons for this is that the baselines fail to identify the underlying patterns within the sequence in which the articles are read by the users. Hence, the baselines are not able to generalise well. Firstly, we give a brief introduction followed by an overview of related work. Then, we present the architecture of our model. Finally, we compare it with other baselines, analyse and present our conclusion.

title: On the Benefit of Incorporating External Features in a Neural Architecture for Answer Sentence Selection
abstract: Incorporating conventional, unsupervised features into a neural architecture has the potential to improve modeling effectiveness, but this aspect is often overlooked in the research of deep learning models for information retrieval. We investigate this particular setting in the context of answer sentence selection, and show that combining a set of query matching, readability, and attention features into a simple Siamese convolutional neural network can lead to markedly increased effectiveness. Our results on two standard question answering datasets show the effectiveness of the combined model.

title: Hybrid MemNet for Extractive News Summarization
abstract: Extractive text summarization has been an extensive research problem in the field of natural language understanding. While the conventional approaches rely mostly on manually compiled features to generate summary, very few attempts have been made in developing data driven systems for extractive summarization. To this end, we present a fully data driven end to end deep network which we call as Hybrid MemNet for single document summarization task. The network learns the continuous unified representation of a document prior to its summary, that jointly captures local and global sentential information along with notion of summary worthy sentences. Experimental results on two different corpora confirms that our model shows significant performance gain compared with the state of the art baselines.

title: Collaborative Deep Learning with Social Regularization for Cold Start Recommendation
abstract: Cold start recommendation seeks to arrive at personalized recommendation of items, in scenarios where we have observed limited information on users' adoption of items. In the literature, there are two promising directions. One is to connect cold start items through similarity in content. The other is to connect cold start users through similarity in social relations. We seek to integrate both types of information, in addition to the adoption information, within a single integrated model. Our proposed SoCDL models item content via a topic model, and user communities via an autoencoder model, while bridging a user's community based preference to her topic based preference. Experiments on public real life data showcase the utility of the model, particularly when there is significant compatibility between communities and topics.

title: Personalized Response Generation via Domain adaptation
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel personalized response generation model via domain adaptation (PRG DM). Firstly, we learn the human responding style from large general data (without user specific information). Secondly, we fine tune the model on a small size of personalized data to generate personalized responses with a dual learning mechanism. Moreover, we propose three new rewards to characterize good conversations that are topic coherent, informative and grammatical. We employ the policy gradient method to generate highly rewarded responses. Experimental results show that our model can generate better personalized responses for different users. Quantitatively, our method achieves better performance than the state of the art conversational systems in terms of BLEU score, perplexity and human evaluation.

title: Exploratory Search Provides Opportunity to Find SEs
abstract: This paper proposes a search method that enables a user to search for sound effects (SEs) in an intuitive and exploratory manner. SEs play an important role in making a scene realistic for the audience of games and films. The creator has to retrieve an SE appropriate for a given scene, which is a time consuming and difficult task. To overcome this problem, the proposed SE retrieval system uses three types of information, namely, contexts, acoustics, and onomatopoeia, to determine the similarity among SEs. Through an experiment, conventional retrieval methods and the proposed method were compared in terms of retrieval time and the number of SEs heard. The results of the experiment showed that there is no statistical difference between the methods in terms of the retrieval time. However, the user can listen to significantly more number of SEs in the proposed methods, i.e., maximum of 2.7 times in the same period. These results suggest that the proposed search method provides the user with opportunities to examine many unknown SEs.

title: Term Mouse Fixations as an Indicator for Topical User Interests
abstract: Models in Interactive Information Retrieval (IIR) are grounded very much on the users task in order to give system support based on different task types and topics. However, the automatic recognition of user interests from log data in search systems is not trivial. Search queries entered by users a surely one such source, however, queries may be short or users are only browsing. In this paper we propose a method of term mouse fixations which takes the fixations on terms users are hovering over with the mouse into consideration to estimate user interests. We analyzed 22,397 search sessions over a time period of about 4 months. We compared these mouse fixations to user search terms and to document clicks in the result list. We found that in about 25% of the sessions user entered search terms were previously fixated with the mouse. These terms were fixated significantly longer than other terms. For document clicks we found that in about 80% of the sessions document keywords and title terms are found in the list of term mouse fixations and that they have significantly longer fixation times. This means, in these cases we are able to draw conclusions on user interests only from mouse fixation data.

title: Inferring Users Search Activity Using Interaction Logs and Gaze Data
abstract: Providing an individual user support regarding the current search activity is crucial for adaptive information retrieval systems but requires a reliable classification of user activities. Reliable and robust activity classifiers would also help to characterize and analyze complex search behavior of users. In order to develop robust classification models, we study in this paper what user interaction features can be used to improve classification. We provide a methodology for user modeling utilizing interaction data from interaction logs and eye tracking to classify the two search activities exploratory search and multitasking search. To identify adequate models and features we use a statistical framework that enables us to select relevant model parameters that are useful to understand the current search activity while holding certain discriminative properties between the activities. The model achieved a classification rate of 94.59\%

title: Local versus Global Radon Descriptors for Image Retrieval
abstract: Radon transform and its inverse are important techniques for a wide range of medical imaging processes, i.e., image reconstruction. Recently, there has been renewed interest in Radon transform for applications such as content based medical image retrieval. However, all studies so far have used Radon transform as a global image descriptor. This paper attempts to show that the dense sampling to generate the histogram of local Radon projections has a higher discrimination capability than the global one. We have introduced Local Radon Descriptor (LRD) and applied it to the IRMA dataset, which contains 14,410 medical images as well as to the Holiday dataset with 1,990 images as a non medical application. Our results reflect significant improvement in retrieval by using LRD versus its global version.

title: Topic Labelling from a Multilingual Perspective. Added Value and Evaluation in Light of Contextual Language Differences.
abstract: Within the last years, the problem of Topic Labelling the issue of associating an appropriate label for the automatically extracted clusters of keywords known as topics has become a widely studied question in Information Retrieval. Although many solutions have been proposed, several open questions remain, one of them being how we consider assigned labels in a multilingual context. We present a brief summary of the history of automated Topic Labelling research, noting that the prevalent techniques can be summarised along two methodologies, being automatic labelling using only the raw collection of documents and automatic labelling using knowledge bases. In a second step, we evaluate both methodologies within a multilingual context, more specifically on a parallel corpus in English, Dutch and German derived from DBpedia.

title: Fraud Detection via Coding Nominal Attributes
abstract: Research on advertisement has mainly focused on how to accurately predict the click through rate (CTR).Much less is known about fraud detection and malicious behavior defense. Previous studies usually use statistics, design threshold and manually make strategies, which cannot find potential fraud behavior effectively and suffer from new attacks. In this paper, we make the first step to understand the type of malicious activities on large scale online advertising platforms. By analyzing each feature comprehensively, we propose a novel coding approach to transform nominal attributes into numeric while maintaining the most effective information of the original data for fraud detection. Next, we code important features such as IP and cookie in our dataset and train machine learning methods to detect fraud traffic automatically. Experimental results on real datasets demonstrate that the proposed fraud detection method performs well considering both the accuracy and efficiency. Finally, we conclude how to design a defense system by considering which methods could be used for the anti spam gaming in the future.

title: Automatic Query Synthesis with an SMT Solver
abstract: Indices play a central role in modern information retrieval systems. Despite the decades of study of index structures for a large range of queries, we, somewhat surprisingly, still find our industry partners struggling with non standard queries absent from a well known index structure. Instead of developing yet another new index, we ask, Can we reuse existing indices for non standard queries? In this paper, we focus on high dimensional indices based on locality sensitive hashing (LSH). Given a non standard query, we synthesize a new set of queries to take advantage of existing indices. The key technical novelty is the use of an SMT solver to automatically synthesize these queries based on a set of sufficient conditions we proved for reusing indices. The index derived by our system is often efficient With our technique, we successfully speed up the production system of our industry partner by more than 10 times without any involvement from human engineers. We also analyze the limitations of our approach.

title: Learning Temporal Ambiguity in Web Search Queries
abstract: Time has strong influence on web search. The temporal intent of the searcher adds an important dimension to the relevance judgments of web queries. However, lack of understanding their temporal requirements increases the ambiguity of the queries, turning retrieval effectiveness improvements into a complex task. In this paper, we propose an approach to classify web queries into four different temporal categories. For each query, we develop features from its search volumes and related queries using Google trends and its related top Wikipedia pages. Our experiment results show that these features can determine temporal ambiguity of a given query with high accuracy. We have demonstrated that a Multilayer Perceptron Networks can achieve better results in classifying temporal class of queries in comparison to other classifiers.

title: Edgeless Graph: A New Graph Based Information Visualization Technique
abstract: Information visualization is the study of visual representations of abstract data in order to strengthen human understanding of the data. Graph Visualization is one of the sub fields of information visualization. It is used for the visualization of structured data. i.e.for inherently related data elements. In the traditional graph visualization techniques, nodes are used to represent data elements whereas edges are used to represent relations. In this paper, our focus is on the representation of structured data. According to us, key challenges for any graph based visualization technique are related with edges. Some of them are planar representation, minimization of edge crossing, minimizing the number of bends, distinguish between the vertices and the edges etc. In this paper, we propose two methods which use the same underlying idea: Assignment of unique label to each vertex of the graph and remove all the edges. Nodes are adjacent if and only if their corresponding labels are disjoint.Our proposed representations dont have edges so we dont need to consider the challenges related to edges that is the biggest advantage. Algorithm for obtaining valid labelling as well as procedures related to dynamic changes (addition/removal of edges and/or vertices) are explained in detail. Space complexities of the proposed methods are O(n^2) and O(n^3) where n denotes the number of nodes. Application of our proposed methods in the analysis of a social network site is also demonstrated. Characteristics of these methods are highlighted along with future possible modifications.

title: Linguistic Morpheme Segmentation Through An Unsupervised Numerical Scoring Approach and Thresholding
abstract: This paper presents a novel, unsupervised model for morpheme segmentation of words collected from a raw textual corpus of a natural language through a novel numerical scoring and thresholding technique. The model incorporates some basic linguistic ideas and statistical numeric quantities for finding legitimate morphemes over all probable morphemes. The model also introduces some hyper parameters for morpheme score adjustment and thresholding, which are calculated through the Kneedle algorithm. Eventually, an optimal morpheme set is obtained after thresholding on a feasible scored morpheme set. We ran our experiments on four different languages (English, Finish, Turkish and Bengali) and evaluated the model on the gold standard data. Evaluation results show that the proposed model performs well on these fours languages according to precision, recall and F measure.

title: An Accurate, Efficient, and Scalable Approach to Channel Matching in Smart TVs
abstract: Smart TVs are rapidly replacing conventional TVs. In a number of countries, set top boxes (STB) are widely used to relay TV channels to smart TVs. In such cases, smart TVs cannot identify which TV channel they are receiving. This situation makes it challenging for smart TVs to provide their users with a variety of personalized services, such as context aware services and recommendation services. In this paper, we propose a TV channel matching system that resolves such problems. By matching the images captured from a smart TV to the images captured from the TV stations, smart TVs should be able to identify which TV program their users are watching. In addition, we propose strategies for scaling out the matching system and improving its accuracy. Our extensive experiments successfully verified the accuracy, efficiency, and scalability of the matching system proposed.

title: Retrieving Compositional Documents Using Position Sensitive Word Movers Distance
abstract: Retrieving similar compositional documents which consist of ranked sub documents, such as threads of healthcare web fora containing community voted comments, has become increasingly important. However, approaches for this task have not exploited the semantic relationships between words so far and therefore do not use the effective generalization property present in semantic word embeddings. In this work, we propose an extension of the Word Mover's Distance for compositional documents consisting of ranked sub documents. In particular, we derive a Position sensitive Word Mover's Distance, which allows to retrieve compositional documents based on the semantic properties of their sub documents. Additionally, we introduce a novel benchmark dataset for this task, to facilitate other researchers to work on this relevant problem. The results obtained on the novel dataset and on the well known MovieLense dataset indicate that our approach is well suited for retrieving compositional documents. We conclude that incorporating semantic relations between words and sensitivity to the position and presentation bias is crucial for effective retrieval of such documents.

title: Top K Influential Nodes in Social Networks: A Game Perspective
abstract: Influence maximization, the fundamental of viral marketing, aims to find top K seed nodes maximizing influence spread under certain spreading models. In this paper, we study influence maximization from the perspective of game theory. We propose a Coordination Game (CG) model, in which every individuals make their decisions based on the benefit of coordination with their network neighbors, to study information propagation. Our model serves as the generalization of some existing models, such as Majority Vote model and Linear Threshold model. Under the generalized model, we study the hardness of influence maximization and the approximation guarantee of the greedy algorithm. We also combine several strategies to accelerate the algorithm. Experimental results show that after the acceleration, the accuracy of our algorithm is on par with the greedy algorithm's and better than other heuristics, while it is three orders of magnitude faster than the greedy algorithm.

title: Personalized Search Time Prediction using Markov Chains
abstract: A major goal of quantitative models of interactive information retrieval is to guide the user, in order to maximize the expected benefit of a search session. In this paper, we define benefit as (saved) search time for reaching a specific search goal, i.e. the next relevant document, thus using a criterion directly related to time based evaluation. We show how Markov models derived from search logs can be used for predicting search times, and describe a method for evaluating these predictions. For personalizing the predictions based on a few user events observed, we devise appropriate parameter estimation methods. Our experimental results show that by observing users for only 100 seconds, the personalized predictions are already significantly better than the global ones.

title: Online Learning to Rank for Cross Language Information Retrieval
abstract: Online learning to rank for information retrieval has shown great promise in optimization of Web search results based on user interactions. However, online learning to rank has been used only in monolingual setting where queries and documents are in the same language. In this work, we present the first empirical study of optimizing a model for Cross Language Information Retrieval (CLIR) based on implicit feedback inferred from user interactions. We show that ranking models for CLIR with higher performance can be learned in an online setting compared to the offline one.

title: An educational Ranking Principle of Web Resources for Teaching
abstract: Research in Information Retrieval significantly facilitated the seeking of web resources for a specific need of a user. This need can be about leisure, commerce and education just to mention few of them. Very important progress has been achieved, and users clearly benefit. However, some areas are left behind compared to others, like the retrieval of web resources for educational purposes. Some studies propose recommendation methods by using educational metadata provided with resources in ad hoc repositories. These methods are hardly applied to web resources, since they do not come with such educational metadata. This research presents a first step towards the design of an Educational Ranking Principle of web resources for teaching. The novelty of the method is the exploiting of the content of web pages, without any additional metadata, for ranking them according to the teaching context of the user. The new method has been compared with the Google's ranking of 35 searches performed by five instructors. Quality ranking and prediction accuracy measures report very positive results since the new method shows more effective and accurate ranking than Google.

title: Mining Business Opportunities from Location based Social Networks
abstract: Urbanization's rapid progress has modernized a large number of human beings' lives. This urbanization progress is accompanied by the increase of a variety of shops (e.g., restaurants and fitness centers) to meet the increasing citizens, which means business opportunities for the investors. Nevertheless, it is difficult for the investors to catch such opportunities because opening what kind of business at which place is not easy to decide. In this paper, we take this challenge and define the business opportunity mining problem, which recommends new business categories at a partitioned business district. Specifically, we exploit the data from location based social networks to mine the business opportunities, guiding the business owners to open new commercial shops in certain categories at a particular area. First, we define the properties of a business district and propose a greedy algorithm to partition a city into different districts. Next, we propose an embedding model to learn latent representations of categories, which captures the functional correlations among business categories. Furthermore, we propose a ranking model based on the pairwise loss to recommend categories for a specific district. Finally, we conduct experiments on Yelp data, and experimental results show that our proposed method outperforms the baseline methods and resolves the problem well.

title: Ontology Enhanced Sentiment Analysis of Financial Headlines
abstract: In an age where big data becomes more and more ubiquitous, there are still many domains and languages where insufficient data are available for model training. In those cases, encoding domain knowledge in an ontology can be an efficient way to enhance the performance of text mining algorithms. Furthermore, domain knowledge stored in an ontology is valuable for different problems within the same domain, while annotated data is often keyed to a specifically defined problem. In this work, we present a knowledge driven approach to predict sentiment on financial newspaper headlines for given company mentions. The text is linked to ontology concepts, and using the default reasoning capabilities ontologies offer, we are able to assess the sentiment of mentioned ontology concepts using class axioms that define sentiment for compositions of concepts. This allows us to, e.g., mark 'increasing profit' as positive but 'increasing debt' as negative. We show that the knowledge driven approach performs 7% better than the baseline in terms of cosine distance to the real values.

title: Bi Clique Mining for Change Tracking in Regulatory Compliance
abstract: Businesses need to adhere to certain regulations to remain compli ant. There are two situations when a business entity might have to deal with changing regulations. 1) A business wants to expand or move to a new geography and find itself subject to a slightly different set of regulations. 2) regulations themselves change over time and force the business to change its internal working to re main compliant. When a compliance officer is presented with a new regulatory document, he has to manually compare corresponding sentences between previous and the new version. In this paper, we propose a novel system to automatically report semantic changes or differences between two sentences by leverag ing two ideas 1) using deep parsing for word graph generation for the two sentences and 2) discovering bi cliques that reflect strong semantic connectedness between words of two sentences. We tag candidate nodes that reflect changes and then discover bi cliques to form phrase pairs that reflect some semantic change from the first to the second sentence. We show that deep parsing significantly outperforms other tech niques used for word graph construction for this task. We study the behavior of the performance of the proposed system varying the design thresholds.

title: Low Rank Matrix Completion over Finite Abelian Group Algebras for Context Aware Recommendation
abstract: The incorporation of contextual information is an important part of context aware recommendation. Many context aware recommendation systems adopt tensor completion to include contextual information. However, the symmetries between dimensions of a tensor induce an unreasonable assumption that users, items and contexts should be treated equally in a recommendation problem. In this paper, we address this problem by using matrices over finite abelian group algebra (AGA) to model context aware interactions between users and items. Specifically, we formulate context aware recommendation as a low rank matrix completion problem over AGA (MC AGA) and derive a new algorithm using the inexact augmented Lagrange multiplier method. We then test MC AGA on three real world datasets: one containing implicit feedback and two with explicit feedback. Experiment results show that MC AGA outperforms not only existing tensor completion algorithms but also recommendation systems with other context aware representations.

title: Tensor based Learning for Rumor aware Stock Movements
abstract: Recent studies in behavioral finance discover that emotional investors are affected by rumors, especially in the era of social media which fertilizes vibrant rumor creation and sharing. The challenge lies in how to quantify the influence of rumor on stock markets along with other market information. A common strategy in previous studies has been to concatenate the features of different information sources into one compound feature vector. In this article, we introduce a tensor based learning approach to capture the rumor based stock movements considering the joint impact of rumors and historical transaction data. It provides an efficient way to mingle the structure and unstructured data, and study their joint influence on market movements. Experiments on three year stock data of Growth Enterprise Market in China show that our approach outperforms the state of the art vector based methods.

title: DAEMON: A new dataset for Multi Task Dyadic Prediction in Recommendation Systems
abstract: We propose DAEMON, a new dataset for dyadic prediction that concerns the forecast of properties for the pairs constituted by users and items in recommendation systems. The dataset is based on the RecSys 2016 challenge for job recommendation and deals with the interesting and the more and more common situation of pairs of observations associated with multiple outputs.
