We analyse the corresponding learning problem, sometimes referred to as multi task learning in the literature, with a particular focus on a late fusion method that consists in learning each association separately and then combing them in order to take advantage of the redundant information contained in the different relationships. Further, we show that the multi task learning on DAEMON is effective for both classification and ranking tasks.

title: A Scalable Approach to Information Theoretic String Similarity Using a Guaranteed Rank Threshold
abstract: This paper describes two simple but powerful techniques for optimizing string similarity search. These techniques exploit the fact that string features such as character q grams display a Zipfian distribution and that high frequency features produce many low scoring candidates. The techniques provide a principled way to methodically eliminate such low scoring candidates without compromising search results which dramatically improves search performance. A search algorithm that exploits these techniques and uses a guaranteed rank threshold is described. Performance is measured on a collection of 4.9 million Wikipedia titles and a collection of 183,933 person names with average search times of 5 milliseconds and 1.5 milliseconds, respectively, on commodity hardware.

title: On Including the User Dynamic in Learning to Rank
abstract: Ranking query results effectively by considering user past behavior and preferences is a primary concern for IR researchers both in academia and industry. In this context, LtR is widely believed to be the most effective solution to design ranking models that account for user interaction features that have proved to remarkably impact on IR effectiveness. In this paper, we explore the possibility of integrating the user dynamic directly into the LtR algorithms. Specifically, we model with Markov chains the behavior of users in scanning a ranked result list and we modify LambdaMart, a state of the art LtR algorithm, to exploit a new discount loss function calibrated on the proposed Markovian model of user dynamic. We evaluate the performance of the proposed approach on publicly available LtR datasets, finding that the improvements measured over the standard algorithm are statistically significant.

title: A Lightweight Citation Recommendation Method Based on the Wisdom of Crowds
abstract: Searching for relevant articles from a large and ever growing number of papers has been challenging for researchers. Citation recommendation enables a fast and comprehensive literature search by automatically producing a list of relevant references given the input of an abstract or a full paper. Previous studies have developed many features relying on information about authors, co authors, article venues, and citing snippets, in an attempt to characterize and predict an authors potential citation choices. Based on topic modelling, we introduce a lightweight citation recommendation method that utilizes only two features, namely topical similarity and similar peers citation choices. The feature of similar peers citation choices exploits the wisdom of crowds embedded in the citation networks of academic articles. The underlying rationale is that prior citation choices made by similar articles have already incorporated various factors such as authors citing habits and the characteristics of authors and article venues. Experiments on the ACL Anthology Reference Corpus show that our retrieval model with two features achieves a similar level of accuracy as existing methods. However, our simple method significantly outperforms them in efficiency because it builds upon a much smaller set of readily available information (article abstracts and citation relationships only).

title: Finding Expert Authors in Financial Forum using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: The modern stock market is a popular place to increase wealth and generate income, but the fundamental problem of when to buy or sell shares, or which stocks to buy has not been solved. It is very common among investors to have professional financial advisers, but what is the best resource to support the decisions these people make? Investment banks, such as Goldman Sachs, Lehman Brothers, and Salomon Brothers, have dominated the world of financial advice for decades. However, due to the popularity of the Internet and financial social networks, such as StockTwits and Seeking Alpha, investors around the word have a new opportunity to gather and share their experiences. It is raises new questions: is the information these users provide trustworthy? How can we find the experts? In this paper, we seek to determine if neural network models can help us find the experts in a set of StockTwits tweets. We applied two neural network models doc2vec and convolutional neural networks to find top authors in StockTwits based on their messages. Our results showed that a convolutional Neural Network is the best model to predict such top authors in this data set.

title: On Fine Grained Geo Localisation of Tweets
abstract: The use of Twitter as a data source for monitoring real world events in cities has received much attention from the scientific community. However, the number of relevant geo tagged tweets available for a specific city remains insufficient to reliably perform analysis of urban areas, particularly for real time detection of small scale incidents and events. Thus, predicting the location of non geotagged tweets is an important yet challenging task, which can increase the sample of geo tagged data and help the analysis and decision making process. In this paper, we propose a location inference method that utilises a ranking approach combined with a weighted majority voting algorithm to refine the prediction using Twitter user credibility information. Using geo tagged tweets collected from Chicago (USA), our experimental results demonstrate that our method outperforms previous approaches and is capable of predicting 65.6\% of the evaluated tweets with 1.82 km of distance error, locating 78.9\% of them at less than 1 km of the real location.

title: Relevant Fact Selection for QA via Sequence Labeling
abstract: Question answering (QA) is a very important, but not yet completely resolved problem in artificial intelligence. Solving the QA problem consists of two major steps: relevant fact selection and answering the question. Existing methods usually combine the two steps to solve the problem. A major technique is to add a memory component to infer answers from the chaining facts. It is not very clear how irrelevant facts affect the effectiveness of these methods. In this paper, we propose to separate the two steps and only consider the problem of relevant fact selection. We used a graphical probabilistic model Conditional Random Field (CRF) to model the interdependent relationship among the chaining facts in order to select the relevant ones. In our experiments on a benchmark dataset, we are able to select correctly all relevant facts from 13 tasks out of 19 tasks (F scores of the rest of the 6 tasks range from 0.8 to 0.97). We also show that using our selector to pre select relevant facts can improve the performance of existing QA systems (e.g. MemN2N and LSTM).

title: Document Expansion Using External Collections
abstract: Document expansion has been shown to improve the effectiveness of information retrieval systems by augmenting documents' term probability estimates with those of similar documents, producing higher quality document representations. We propose a method to further improve document models by utilizing external collections as part of the document expansion process. Our approach is based on relevance modeling, a popular form of pseudo relevance feedback; however, where relevance modeling is concerned with query expansion, we are concerned with document expansion. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed model improves ad hoc document retrieval effectiveness on a variety of corpus types, with a particular benefit on more heterogeneous collections of documents.

title: Supervised methods for ranking relations in Web Search
abstract: In this paper we propose an efficient technique for ranking triples of knowledge base using information of full text. We devise supervised machine learning algorithms to compute the relevance scores for an item property pairs where an item can have more than one values. Such a score measures the degree to which an entity belongs to a type, and this plays an important role in ranking the search results. The problem is in itself new and not explored so much in the literature, possibly because of the heterogeneous behaviors of both semantic knowledge base and fulltext articles. The classifiers exploit statistical features computed from the Wikipedia articles and the semantic information obtained from the word embedding concepts. Our experiments are based on the frameworks as provided by WSDM cup 2017, which provides about 1k human judgments of person profession pairs. Evaluation shows that machine learning based approaches produce encouraging performance with the highest accuracy of 71%. The contributions of the current work are two fold, viz. we focus on a problem that has not been explored much, and show the usage of powerful word embedding features that produce promising results.

title: Graph based Ensemble Summarization for Microblogs
abstract: As microblogging sites have become important information sources, summarization of microblogs (tweets) is an important problem in IR. Considering that several summarization algorithms are already available, in this work, we investigate whether off the shelf summarization algorithms can be combined to produce good quality summaries. We propose EnGraphSum, a graph based ensemble summarization algorithm that can combine the outputs of several base summarization algorithms to produce summaries that are better than what is obtained from any of the individual base algorithms. To our knowledge, this is the first attempt towards ensemble summarization of microblogs.

title: Contextual Relatedness Filtering for Enhanced Feature Selection using Wikipedia: An Application on Cluster Labeling
abstract: Feature selection is an important component of information retrieval and natural language processing applications. It is used to extract distinguishing terms for a group of documents; such terms, for example, can be used for cluster labeling and multi document summarization. We present a new approach for finding contextual relatedness of terms to topics which can be used for enhancing feature selection quality by filtering out unrelated terms from the extracted feature list. Our approach automatically decides contextual relatedness of terms to topics using co occurrences of important terms (i.e. features) inside an external knowledge source, Wikipedia for our work. We evaluate our approach for cluster labeling problem on 20NG and ODP datasets, finding that it successfully detects relevancy information of terms to topics, thus filtering out irrelevant label candidates results in better cluster labeling quality.

title: Wavelet2vec: Wavelet Transform Representation for Text mining
abstract: Most text mining methods struggle to overcome obstacles of large scale and high dimensional data. In this paper, we propose a novel model, termed Wavelet2vec, which is based on wavelet transform to craft a significantly lower dimensional representation for text classification and clustering. The Wavelet2vec maps the text document as a numerical representation by converting them to Unicode signal/time series into a new space. The effectiveness and efficiency of our proposed approach are empirically investigated on three real world datasets. The experimental results reveal that Wavelet2vec outperforms a number of state of the art approaches for text classification task.

title: Context Driven Dynamic Product Ranking System for Fashion e commerce
abstract: Product discovery is a critical aspect in on line shopping, especially for fashion. Effective product discovery is key for providing a good user experience and driving purchases. Traditional approaches tackle this problem by providing a popularity based product listing overlayed with personalization basis the users browsing/purchase history. However, these approaches are typically static and don't respond to the users in session signals. Our work focuses on improving the product listing real time by detecting the user's context in session. We propose a context aware intelligent system for fashion e commerce which responds to user in session activity, dynamically re ranking the product listing to better match the users expressed intent thus helping him/her discover products quickly and effectively. Our system uses both historical co browsing data and current user's intent/context for determining the ranking of new products to be shown to the user. We showcase the performance of the proposed approach on historical sessions data from one of the top e commerce platforms.

title: Towards word embedding for duplicate bug report detection in software repositories
abstract: Software maintenance requires large scale bug reports filing. In order to avoid the same bug to be assigned to different developers, duplicate bug report detection is a crucial task in software maintenance. In this paper, we study the usage of neural language models for detecting duplicate bug reports in software repositories. We compare various state of the art neural language models to model bug reports. We also formulate LDA refined Word Embedding. Through our experiments on the real world dataset of Firefox project, we see that LDA refined Word Embedding performs better than the compared neural models for the task of duplicate bug report detection.

title: Detecting Positive Medical History Mentions
abstract: In medical practice, knowing the medical history of a patient is crucial for diagnosis and treatment suggestion. However, such information is often recorded in unstructured notes from doctors, potentially mixed with the medical history of family members and mentions of disorders for other reasons (e.g. as potential side effects). In this work we designed a scheme to automatically extract the medical history of patients from a large healthcare database. More specifically, we first extracted medical conditions mentioned using a rule based system and a medical gazetteer, then we classified whether such mentions reflected the patient's history or not. We designed our method to be simple and with little human intervention. Our results are very encouraging, supporting the potential for efficient and effective deployment in clinical practice.

title: Multiple Random Walks for Personalized Ranking with Trust and Distrust Relationships
abstract: Social networks with trust and distrust relationships has been an emerging topic in Information Retrieval, aiming at identifying users of trust when sharing information in social networks or purchasing products online. In this study we investigate how to generate accurate personalized rankings while considering both trust and distrust user relationships. This paper includes the following contributions, first we propose a trust and distrust propagation algorithm via multiple random walks to better capture the missing relationships between users in the signed network. Then, we introduce a regularization framework to account for the structural properties of the enhanced graph with the propagated relationships, as well as the user's trust and distrust preferences in the graph to produce his/her personalized ranking list. We evaluate the performance of the proposed approach on a benchmark dataset from Slashdot. Our experiments demonstrate the superiority of the proposed approach over state of the art methods that also consider trust and distrust relationships in the personalized ranking task.

title: Advanced Hidden Markov Models for Recognizing Search
abstract: Although cognitive IR approaches usually distinguish between different search phases, there are no automatic methods for recognizing these phases. In this paper, we use constrained Hidden Markov Models (HMM), for addressing this issue. Especially, we develop a hybrid form of HMM combining both discrete and continuous signal values, which improves the recognition process. Furthermore, we show how the new model can be used for predicting the time to the next relevant document, which is a prerequisite for the application of the interactive probability ranking principle.

title: Detecting Counterpart Entity Pairs across Time
abstract: Most search engines need users to input specific words to obtain useful results from the Web. However, this requirement is sometimes challenging for users who want to search for information regarding unknown words. It may be especially difficult to learn about the past without knowing suitable words, such as answering the question "Who was the counterpart of the Prime Minister of the UK in the Ottoman Empire in 1900?" We propose a novel search framework for finding counterpart relationships represented by entity pairs across time. This framework detects the counterparts by arithmetic operations as well as Word2Vec. To improve the accuracy, our framework groups news articles to develop context for entities. After embedding the entities into vector spaces built for all years, we map a given relationship to another vector space, then perform arithmetic operations. We show our algorithm outputs better results compared with simply applying Word2Vec.

title: Benchmarking community detection algorithms for uncovering stances
abstract: Stance detection systems often integrate social clues in their algorithms. While the influence of the social circles of users on stance is well known, there was no measure of how well state of the art community detection algorithms performed in terms of detecting like minded communities. We used Twitter's social interactions to compare the results of well known community detection algorithms on two datasets on the Scottish Independence Referendum and US Midterm Elections. Our results show that algorithms relying on information diffusion performs better for this task and confirm previous observations about retweets being better vectors of stance than mentions.

title: Emotional Social Signals for Search Ranking
abstract: A large amount of social feedback expressed by social signals (e.g. like, +1, rating) are assigned to web resources. These signals are often exploited as additional sources of evidence in search engines. Our objective in this paper is to study the impact of the new social signals, called Facebook reactions (love, haha, angry, wow, sad) in the retrieval. These reactions allow users to express more nuanced emotions compared to classic signals (e.g. like, share). First, we analyze these reactions and show how users use these signals to interact with posts. Second, we evaluate the impact of each such reaction in the retrieval, by comparing them to both the textual model without social features and the first classical signal (like based model). These social features are modeled as document prior and are integrated into a language model. We conducted a series of experiments on IMDb dataset. Our findings reveal that incorporating social features is a promising approach for improving the retrieval ranking performance.

title: Skill Translation Models in Expert Finding
abstract: Finding talented users on Stackoverflow can be challenging due to term mismatch between queries and content published on it. In this paper, we propose two translation models to augment a given query with relevant words. The first model is based on a statistical approach and the second is a word embedding model. Interestingly, the translations provided by these methods are not the same. Although the first model in most cases selects pieces of program codes as translations, the second model provides more semantically related words. Our experiments on a large dataset indicate the efficiency of both translation models.

title: A Metric for Sentence Ordering Assessment Based on Topic Comment Structure
abstract: Sentence ordering is a key component of verbal ability. It is also crucial for automatic text generation. While numerous researchers developed various methods to automatically evaluate the informativeness of the produced contents, the evaluation of readability is usually performed manually. In contrast to that, we present a self sufficient metric for sentence ordering assessment based on text topic comment structure. We show that this metric has high accuracy.

title: SERP User Behavior Prediction through Deep Multitask Learning
abstract: User behavior signals such as clicks are strong indicators used to measure a search engines performance. Many existing search algorithms focus on predicting users interactions, by optimizing a cost function for a single web document, given a query. Subsequently, a result set (list) is generated by ranking web documents with this score. However, the probability of user interaction with a web document on a Search Engine Result Page (SERP) depends on not just that web document in isolation, but also other documents/elements present on the SERP. Our approach focuses on predicting user behavior for a list of web documents by modeling the interdependencies between documents. In this paper, we propose a model, based on Multitask Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to predict user behavior for both individual web documents as well as the SERP.

title: Learning To Focus When Ranking Answers
abstract: One of the main challenges in ranking is embedding the query and document pairs into a joint feature space, which can then be fed to a learning to rank algorithm. To achieve this representation, the conventional state of the art approaches perform extensive feature engineering that encode the similarity of the query answer pair. Recently, deep learning solutions have shown that it is possible to achieve comparable performance, in some settings, by learning the similarity representation directly from data. Unfortunately, previous models perform poorly on longer texts, or on texts with significant portion of irrelevant information, or which are grammatically incorrect. To overcome these limitations, we propose the use of a novel attention mechanism for question answering, which helps the model learn on which words and phrases to focus, when building the mutual representation. We demonstrate ranking performance on several real world question answer ranking datasets, and provide visualization of the attention mechanism to offer more insights into how our models of attention could benefit ranking for difficult question answering challenges.

title: Citation metadata extraction via neural model based segment sequence labeling
abstract: Citation metadata extraction plays an important role in academic information retrieval and digital library. Current works on this task generally use rule based, template based or machine learning based approaches but these methods either rely on handcrafted features or are limited with domains. Meanwhile, neural network based models have shown strong ability in solving sequence labeling tasks. Citation metadata extraction can be considered as a typical sequence labeling task in which each word (or segment, depending on the granularity) is assigned with a label. In this paper, we propose an modified sequence labeling model for citation metadata extraction, called segment labeling. Instead of inference at word level, the input sequence is first segmented based on extracted features, and then segment features are computed to infer the label sequence of the segments. Based on the realistic situation that words in a citation string are usually organized in segments and words of the same segment belong to the label, this adaptation could make the model better suited for this task than common sequence labeling models. The model was trained on the data which were collected from BibTeX databases on the Web and annotated in a semi automatic manner. To evaluate our model's ability of generalization, we tested it on two public benchmark datasets of citation metadata extraction. Experiments show that our proposed model achieves best performance on both datasets.

title: Upper Bound Approximations for BlockMaxWand
abstract: BlockMaxWand is a recent advance on the Wand dynamic pruning technique, which allows efficient retrieval without any effectiveness degradation to rank K. However, while BMW uses docid sorted indices, it relies on recording the upper bound of the term weighting model scores for each block of postings in the inverted index. Such a requirement can be disadvantageous in situations such as when an index must be updated. In this work, we examine the appropriateness of upper bound approximation which have previously been shown suitable for Wand in providing efficient retrieval for BMW. Experiments on the ClueWeb12 category B13 corpus using 5000 queries from a real search engines query log demonstrate that BMW still provides benefits w.r.t. Wand when approximate upper bounds are used. Moreover, if the upper bound approximations are sufficiently tight, using these in BMW can provide efficiency gains w.r.t. Wand with exact upper bounds, in particular for queries of short to medium length.

title: A Collaborative Ranking Model for Cross Domain Recommendations
abstract: With the advent of social media platforms, generating high quality cross domain recommendations has become more and more important for users that express their preferences in heterogeneous domains. In this study, we propose a collaborative ranking model to generate cross domain recommendations. Given a target domain to generate the recommendations, we design an objective function aiming at performing push of the relevant items at the top of the list. Also, in our collaborative ranking model we propose a weighting strategy to control the influence of user preferences from auxiliary domains when producing the recommendation lists, as users may have different behaviours in multiple domains. Our experiments on ten cross domain recommendation tasks show that the proposed approach achieves high recommendation accuracy, compared to other state of the art methods.

title: Gaussian Embeddings for Collaborative Filtering
abstract: Most collaborative filtering systems, such as matrix factorization, use vector representations for items and users. Those representations are deterministic, and do not allow modeling the uncertainty of the learned representation. This can be useful when a user has a small number of rated items (cold start), or when there is conflicting information about the behavior of a user or the ratings of an item. In this paper, we leverage recent works in learning Gaussian embeddings and apply it to the task of recommendation. We show that this model performs well on three representative collections (Yahoo, Yelp and MovieLens) and analyze learned representations.

title: Detecting Controversies in Online News Media
abstract: Defining controversy as a public debate that divides society, this paper sets out to detect controversial news reports using online discussions as a source of information. We demonstrate that a combination of content and stylometric analysis yields useful signals for extracting disputed news articles. Moreover, we argue that a debate based approach can produce generic modelsopposed to the current state of the art, which largely depends on platform specific content or structure.

title: Query Performance Prediction using Word Embedding
abstract: A query performance prediction (QPP) approach automatically estimates the effectiveness of an IR system. The idea is to aggregate various pre retrieval features, such as query term ambiguity, and post retrieval features, such as retrieval scores, to quantify retrieval effectiveness of a query. Along with the nature of the collection, a major factor that makes it difficult for an IR system in retrieving relevant documents at top ranks for a given query, is the presence of ambiguous terms in the query. Instead of using collection statistics or external resources, such as the Wordnet, for the purpose of predicting word ambiguity, we propose a novel approach of applying word vector embedding. We argue that the ambiguity of a query term depends on the number of senses with which the other word vectors in the neighborhood of the query word vector, are associated. Each such sense is expected to form its own cluster comprising of words vectors associated with it. Using this clustering hypothesis, we argue that a query term is likely to be ambiguous if other words similar to it are uniformly associated with multiple senses, or in other words, the size of the clusters around the query word vector are uniform. We combine this pre retrieval QPP estimate with the state of the art post retrieval estimate, namely the Normalized Query Commitment (NQC) predictor by a linear combination. Our experiments demonstrate that the hybrid estimate significantly outperforms the NQC predictor in most standard topic sets.

title: How to Best Order Crowdsourced Relevance Judgement HITs
abstract: In this paper we study the effect on crowdsourced relevance judgement quality of the dominance of one class in the data they process. We aim at understanding if there is any positive or negative bias in workers seeing many negative examples in the identification of positive labels. To test our hypothesis, we design an experiment where crowd workers are asked to complete a batch of relevance judgement tasks presented in different orders. We repeat our experiment for different class distributions and orders. Our findings indicate that there is a significant improvement in the quality of relevance judgements when presenting to crowd workers relevant documents before the non relevant ones.

title: Salient Words Mining in Community Question Answering
abstract: Expert finding on Stackoverflow is a challenging task since there exists a term mismatch between queries and the published content of the community. In this study, we seek for addressing this challenge. In CQA communities such as Stackoverflow, the quality of an answer is directly proportional to its share of votes. By using Voteshare (i.e. an answer's share of votes) effect, we propose a model to expand a query to its salient translations. These words are the most noticeable ones that are mostly used by experts while rarely used by non experts. Our experiments on a large dataset evaluate the efficiency of the proposed model. Moreover, we focus on detecting advanced aspects of different topics in Stackoverflow. For this, we use a clustering method which differentiates the language of experts from the language of the others.

title: The Role of Pronouns to Sentiment Analysis in Online Health Communities
abstract: Analyzing sentiments of user posts in online health communities enables further investigations, e.g. of factors that affect the sentiment change. Since each person has his or her own personality and temporal emotional state, behavioral traits can be reflected in the persons writing style. Pronouns are function words, which often convey unique styling patterns into the texts. Drawing on a lexical approach to emotions, we conduct factor analysis on the use of pronouns in self description texts. Our analysis shows that the usage of pronouns has a remarkable effect on sentiment classification in online health communities. Moreover, we evaluate the use of pronouns in our domain and find it to be very different compared to standard English usage.

title: On the Construction of Suffix Arrays from Data Compressed by Parsing into Decreasing Sequences
abstract: This paper presents the data compression algorithm Monotone that is based on the parsing of the input data into the sequences of decreasing values. It is shown that the state of the art suffix array construction algorithm SA IS can be modified to operate on the output of the Monotone algorithm. The SA IS algorithm is linear time algorithm and it is based on the concept of induced sorting of LMS substrings. In this paper it is shown that if the input data are parsed into LMS substrings then the redundancy of the LMS substrings is rather low, the output alphabet is large and such parsing provides only a limited space for statistical compression. Instead we proposed the Monotone algorithm in which the output sequences are highly redundant, the output alphabet is small and we experimentally shown that in many cases it is possible to statistically compress the input data below the zero order entropy. We further show two additional data structures used in Monotone algorithm that allow introduction of repeating values in a suffix array.

title: Empirical Evaluations of Machine Learning Training Strategies: Is Active Learning Really Superior in Legal Document Review?
abstract: Machine learning is regularly applied in the legal arena because it can reduce the time and expense associated with the review of voluminous document populations. One form of machine learning Active Learning has drawn attention from the legal community because it offers the potential to make the machine learning process even more effective. The purpose of this paper is twofold: to question whether Active Learning actually is a superior learning methodology and to highlight the ways Active Learning can be most effective when it is utilized. Our observations from these experiments show Active Learning can effectively identify informative training documents quickly but that it becomes less effective over time depending on the strategy. This indicates that Active Learning may be best suited to initiate the predictive modeling process but not to continue through the entire document review.

title: Generating and Personalizing Bundle Recommendations on Steam
abstract: Many websites offer promotions in terms of bundled items that can be purchased together, usually at a discounted rate. Bundling may be a means of increasing sales revenue, but may also be a means for content creators to expose users to new items that they may not have considered in isolation. In this paper, we seek to understand the semantics of what constitutes a good bundle, in order to recommend existing bundles to users on the basis of their constituent products, as well the more difficult task of generating new bundles that are personalized to a user. To do so we collect a new dataset from the Steam video game distribution platform, which is unique in that it contains both traditional recommendation data (rating and purchase histories between users and items), as well as bundle purchase information. We assess issues such as bundle size and item compatibility, and show that these features, when combined with traditional matrix factorization techniques, can lead to highly effective bundle recommendation and generation.

title: Exploiting Gaussian Word Embeddings for Document Clustering
abstract: Every day, millions of documents in the form of articles, tweets, and blog posts are generated by Internet users. Many of these documents are not annotated with labels that would make the task of retrieving similar documents non trivial. The act of grouping similar un annotated documents together solely based on features extracted from their text is called document clustering. In a good assignment of documents to clusters, clusters ought to contain only those documents that are related. In this paper, we present a novel technique to cluster documents by exploiting the Gaussian word embeddings learned using word2gauss from said documents, and show, that our method generates coherent clusters that approach the performance of K means on Purity and Entropy scores while achieving higher recall as measured by Inverse Purity.

title: Neural Qantification for Twiter Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Is the population that is tweeting about the Oscars positively or negatively disposed towards the ``best movie''? The above question can be formulated as a quantification task where the objective is to infer an estimate of the proportion of the population belonging to a class (positive or negative) instead of predicting the sentiment of an individual tweet. In this paper we propose a novel formulation for quantification using recurrent neural networks with attention mechanisms that are trained to directly optimize quantification performance measures such as the Kullback Leibler Divergence (KLD). Our formulation and our proposed method NPRIDE offers several advantages (i) they directly optimizes for accurate population estimates without training to classify individual tweets; (ii) they offer the robustness quantification estimates have in the face of distributional drift; and (iii) our attention models provide insights about the words which effect the polarity of the tweets.

title: X DART: Blending Dropouts and Pruning for Efficient Learning To Rank
abstract: In this paper we propose X DART, a new Learning to Rank algorithm focusing on the training of robust and compact ranking models. Motivated from the observation that the last trees of MART models impact the prediction of only a few instances of the training set, we borrow from the DART algorithm the dropout strategy consisting in temporarily dropping some of the trees from the ensemble while new weak learners are trained. However, differently from this algorithm we drops permanently these trees on the basis of smart choices driven by accuracy measured on the validation set. Experiments conducted on publicly available datasets shows that X DART outperforms DART in training models providing the same effectiveness by employing up to 40% less trees.

title: Learning To Rank Documents by Learning To Rank Passages
abstract: We explore a few approaches of learning to rank documents using passage based information; specifically, utilizing learning to rank of passages. Our approaches are shown to substantially outperform a variety of baselines. Furthermore, the features we propose for ranking passages result in passage (focused) retrieval performance that transcends the state of the art.

title: Behavior based Community Detection in Enterprise Information Networks
abstract: Community detection in complex networks is a fundamental problem that has attracted much attention across various disciplines. Previous studies have been mostly focusing on the external interactions between different nodes (i.e., topology structure) in the network whereas largely ignoring the internal intricacies (i.e., non interactive behaviors) of each node. A pair of nodes without any interaction can still share similar internal behaviors. For example, in an enterprise information network, compromised computers that are remotely controlled by the same attacker often demonstrate similar abnormal behaviors even though they do not connect with each other. In this paper, we look into the problem of community detection in enterprise information networks, where the majority of the generated data are non interactive process level events inside each node/host. In particular, we propose a novel community detection approach to identify behavior based host communities in enterprise information networks, by capturing the behavioral patterns of each host purely based on large scale heterogeneous event data. We conduct experiments on a real enterprise information network to compare our proposed method with a couple of baselines. The results demonstrate the superior effectiveness of our solution across multiple popular metrics.

title: Explanatory Ad Hoc Entity and Relationship Summarization
abstract: For the extraction of information from very large document collections, multi document summarization approaches tend to fall short due to the involved amount of information, while knowledge extraction approaches are often too discriminative for exploratory purposes. In these settings, entity centric approaches can help to filter the relevant information in a preparatory step or to enable interactive explorations that support the user in an initial analysis of such a collection. In this paper, we discuss the tasks of entity summarization and relationship summarization that are aimed at such an interactive exploration. We introduce efficient ranking methods for sentence extraction that address these entity centric summarization tasks by leveraging entity and term relations in implicit network representations of large document collections.

title: Internal Knowledge Powered Relation Classification
abstract: The relation classification is playing a pivotal role in natural language processing (NLP) and relation extraction systems. In this paper, we propose an internal knowledge powered method that can be used in any neural network that is based on pairwise ranking loss function to do the task. The triple information obtained from the sentence and the corresponding relation label are named as internal knowledge in this work. In particular, we implement an internal knowledge powered convolutional neural network (IKP CNN) to encode the triple information into the relation classification procedure. We combine the knowledge graph embedding and convolutional neural network to finish the task instead of considering it as an ordinary classification task. Besides, we also construct a link between the relation and reversed relation, such as relation(entity_1,entity_2) and relation(entity_2,entity_1). Thus, we can enhance two relations in one sentence. Experiments on the SemEval 2010 Task 8 benchmark dataset show that our proposed method can efficiently improve the performance and the proposed IKP CNN model achieves a competitive or even better performance compared with the previous system without using external knowledge and the traditional NLP features. The performance can be potentially improved if our method can be combined with other effective networks, external knowledge, or NLP features.

title: Non negative Matrix Factorization meets Word Embedding
abstract: Document clustering is central in modern information retrieval applications. Among existing models, non negative matrix factorization (NMF) approaches have proven effective for this task. However, NMF approaches, like other models in this context, exhibit a major drawback, namely they use the bag of word representation and, thus, do not account for the sequential order in which words occur in documents. This is an important issue since it may result in a significant loss of semantics. In this paper, we aim to address the above issue and propose a new model which successfully integrates a word embedding model, word2vec, into an NMF framework so as to leverage the semantic relationships between words. Empirical results, on several real world datasets, demonstrate the benefits of our model in terms of text document clustering as well as document/word embedding.

title: A Contextual Approach to Dynamic Search and Topic Change
abstract: In this paper, we propose a unique approach to dynamic search that uses a LinUCB contextual bandit algorithm to automatically search topics and change queries when finished. The algorithm models actions that a user might utilize when querying a search engine, including the action of moving on to the next topic by completely changing the query, and uses the context surrounding the current state of the search to choose one action each iteration with which to interact with the search engine. By using a contextual approach to reinforcement learning to select an action at each iteration, this process fully automates the search from beginning to end, choosing both how to search the topic and how long to search for, leading to a more effective retrieval with varied numbers of queries for each topic. This experiment is conducted using the data from TREC 2016 Dynamic Domain Track. Our results show that using the context features of the current search iteration to select the next action in the search is an effective way to retrieve relevant documents and also that allowing the algorithm to decide how long to search each topic does not negatively affect the effectiveness of the search.

title: Predicting Shopping Behavior with Mixture of RNNs
abstract: We evaluate and compare two machine learning approaches for early prediction of shoppers behaviors by leveraging features from clickstream data generated during live shopping sessions. As a baseline, we use a mixture of high order Markov chain models to predict three possible outcomes: purchase, abandoned shopping cart, and browsing only. We then experiment with replacing the Markov chains in our mixture model with Recurrent Neural Networks. When sequences are truncated to 75% of their length, a relatively small feature set predicts purchase outcomes with an F measure of 0.80 and browsing only outcomes with an F measure of 0.98. We also investigate an entropy based decision procedure.

title: On Improving The Evaluation of Sample based Collection Selection: What We Missed in The Past
abstract: Federated Search, or Distributed Information Retrieval (DIR), is an IR research field driven by the need to satisfy information need on distributed heterogeneous collections. A good DIR system is defined by its ability to estimate a set of the most relevant collections based on a query. One of the approaches used to achieve this objective is the sample based approach. In sample based approach a collection selection algorithm is designed to use the so called Central Sample Index (CSI) to estimate the relevance of a collection. The CSI acts like a small search engine on the inside of a search engine. Current evaluation approach of CSI based collection selection algorithms relies only on multiple data sets to assess the performance of an algorithm. However, CSI consists of three major components: sampled documents (data set), search engine and retrieval method. We show advantages and shortcomings of the current evaluation approach. We propose that the creation of CSI in the evaluation process should also consider the choice of search engine and retrieval method. Our experiment results further strengthen our position.

title: The topological face of recommendation
abstract: Recommendation plays a key role in e commerce and in the entairtainment industry. The growing interest for algorithmic transparency motivates us in this paper to observe the results of recommendations, such as Youtube video recommendations, under the form of a graph. A capture under this form is usefull despite a limited exploration of the possible set of recommendations to a user. We thus illustrate the topology formed by successive recommentations to a Youtube user, provide its key characteristics, and show that one can learn from it, for instance to witness the knowledge of that user by the service. We then show that this graph view of the recommendations allows for asking the question of potential recommendation bias in online services, by analyzing the user recommendation topology. We propose a notion of recommendation coherence with regards to the topological proximity of recommended items (under the measure of items k closest neighbors, remainding the small world model). Finally, we illustrate this approach on a model and on a Youtube crawl, targeting the prediction of Recommeded for you links (i.e., biased or not by Youtube).

title: Term Proximity Constraints for Pseudo Relevance Feedback
abstract: Pseudo relevance feedback (PRF) refers to a query expansion strategy based on top retrieved documents, which has been shown to be highly effective in many retrieval models. Previous work has introduced a set of constraints (axioms) that should be satisfied by anyPRF model. In this paper, we propose three additional constraints based on the proximity of feedback terms to the query terms in the feedback documents. As a case study, we consider the log logistic model, a state of the art PRF model that has been proven to be a successful method in satisfying the existing PRF constraints. We show that the log logistic model does not satisfy the proposed constraints.We further modify it based on the proposed proximity based constraints. Experiments on four TREC collections demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed constraints. Our modiffication to the log logistic model leads to signifficant and substantial (up to 15%) improvements. Furthermore, we show that the proposed proximity based function outperforms the well known Gaussian kernel which does not satisfy all the proposed constraints.

title: 50 Shades of Bronze
abstract: In recent years, gathering relevance judgments through non topic originators has become an increasingly important problem in Information Retrieval. Relevance judgments can be used to measure the effectiveness of a system, and are often needed to build supervised learning models in learning to rank retrieval systems. The two most popular approaches to gathering bronze level judgments using non topic experts is through a controlled user study, or through crowdsourcing. However, re assessment comes with a cost the quality of the judgments can vary widely. In this work, we directly compare the reliability of judgments using three different types of bronze assessor groups. Our first group is a controlled lab group. In addition to the lab group (Lab), two different crowdsourcing groups were used. CF Document assessors were free to judge any number of documents for a topic, while CF Topic judges were required to judge all of the documents from a single topic, in a manner similar to the Lab group. Through our study, we found that Lab assessors exhibit a significantly higher inter rater score than CF Topic and CF Document when compared to a set of ground truth judgments, as well as when compared directly. These finding suggests that in the absence of ground truth data, agreement between assessors can be used to reliably gauge the quality of relevance judgments gathered from secondary assessors, and that controlled user studies are more likely to produce reliable judgments despite being more costly.

title: Neural Citation Network for Context Aware Citation Recommendation
abstract: The accelerating rate of scientific publications makes it difficult to find relevant citations or related work. Context aware citation recommendation aims to solve this problem by providing a curated list of high quality candidates given a short passage of text. Existing literature adopts bag of word representations leading to the loss of valuable semantics and lacks the ability to integrate metadata or generalize to unseen manuscripts in the training set. We propose a flexible encoder decoder architecture called Neural Citation Network (NCN), embodying a robust representation of the citation context with a max time delay neural network, further augmented with an attention mechanism and author networks. The recurrent neural network decoder consults this representation when determining the optimal paper to recommend based solely on its title. Quantitative results on the CiteSeer dataset consisting of 4,549,267 contexts and 855,735 papers reveal NCN cultivates a significant improvement over competitive baselines. Qualitative evidence highlights the effectiveness of the proposed end to end neural network revealing a promising research direction for citation recommendation.

title: A Study of SVM Kernel Functions for Sensitivity Classification Ensembles with POS Sequences
abstract: Freedom of Information (FOI) laws legislate that government documents should be opened to the public. However, many government documents contain sensitive information, such as confidential information, that is exempt from release. Therefore, government documents must be sensitivity reviewed prior to release, to identify and close any sensitive information. With the adoption of born digital documents, such as email, traditional sensitivity review processes are no longer suitable and there is a need for automatic sensitivity classification to assist digital sensitivity review. Support Vector Machine classifiers and Part of Speech sequences have both been separately shown to be promising techniques for sensitivity classification. However, sequence classification methodologies, and specifically SVM kernel functions, have not been fully investigated for sensitivity classification. Therefore, in this work, we present an evaluation of five SVM kernel functions for sensitivity classification using POS sequences. Moreover, we show that an ensemble classifier that combines POS sequence classification with text classification can significantly improve sensitivity classification effectiveness (+6.09% F2) compared with a text classification baseline, according to McNemar's test of significance.

title: Multi faceted Credibility aware Product Rating with Honest Reviews
abstract: Online reviews play a important role in influencing buyers' daily purchase decisions. However, fake and meaningless reviews, which cannot reflect users' genuine purchase experience and opinions, wide exist on the Web and pose great challenges to users in making the right choices. Therefore, it is desirable to build a fair model that evaluate the quality of products by distinguishing between the honest and dishonest reviews. To this end, we propose a framework for measuring the quality of products, which filters out fake and suspicious reviews using a predictive bilinear sparse model based on cross domain information and then builds a regression tree based scoring function for measuring genuine quality of products. Experimental results conducted on a real world review dataset show the effectiveness of our approach in delivering credible evaluations of products. Also, the proposed approach outperforms multiple baselines and can well handle new products with few reviews.

title: Income Prediction based on Tweet User's Temporal Orientation
abstract: Automatically estimating user's socio economic profile from language use in social media can unprecedentedly help social science research and various downstream applications ranging from business to politics. The current paper presents the first study where user cognitive structure is used to build a predictive model of income. In particular, we first develop a classifier using weakly supervised learning framework to automatically time tag tweets as past, present, or future. We quantify users overall temporal orientation based on their distribution of tweets and use it to build a predictive model of income. Our analysis uncovers correlation between future temporal orientation and income. Finally, we measure the predictive power of future temporal orientation on income by performing regression.

title: Heterogeneous model selection for multiscale time series forecasting
abstract: A computational experiment to select an optimal model requires consequent trials of models. Due to highly complex dependencies in the large set of multiscale time series, various forecasting models are in the competitive set to choose from. The paper investigates a problem of models selection. It proposes a new method to compare heterogeneous models and to select an optimal subset. This subset acts in ensemble to boost forecasting quality. The models are experts in the mixture. Their likelihood is the essential criterion to compare. A gating function computes the likelihood. The experiment uses linear model, ensemble of decision trees, SVM and gradient boosting as the experts. Multiscale sets of industrial and weather time series illustrate this method with application to the IoT.

title: Improving the Extraction of Mathematical Identifier Definitions using Machine Learning
abstract: The mathematical formulae contained in academic texts contribute significantly to the overall semantic content for that text. Especially in the STEM fields, large chunks of semantic information would be lost if formulae were to be ignored. To capture the semantics of mathematical formulae, it is essential to know the definitions of the involved identifiers. Mathematical information retrieval (MIR) systems can extract the definitions for mathematical identifiers, similarly to human readers, from the text surrounding a given formulae. In this paper, we develop an automatic evaluation framework, which is based on the NTCIR 11 Math Wikipedia dataset and the corresponding gold standard for identifier definition extraction. We compare known published approaches using this framework and develop a new approach which builds upon the previous work. The evaluation of our novel approach shows an increase in the identifier definition extraction precision from 16.43\% to 44.85\%, while increasing the recall from 22.26\% to 28.06\%.

title: KeyVec: Key semantics Preserving Document Representations
abstract: Previous studies have demonstrated the empirical success of word embeddings in various applications. In this paper, we investigate the problem of learning distributed representations for text documents which many machine learning algorithms take as input for a number of NLP and IR tasks. We propose a neural network model, KeyVec, which learns document representations with the goal of preserving key semantics of the input text. It enables the learned low dimensional vectors to retain the topics and important information from the documents that will flow to downstream tasks. Our empirical evaluations show the superior quality of KeyVec representations in two different document understanding tasks.

title: A Modular Analysis of Session Search Evaluation Metrics
abstract: Session search is a complex task. Information Retrieval (IR) systems need to consider multiple factors in returning and ranking documents. Multiple evaluation metrics have been proposed to measure the performance of IR systems in session search as comprehensively as possible. Issues coming out from the complexity of metrics include: what the similarities and differences are among these metrics, how each metric combines different factors, and how to achieve the optimal performance in different metric settings. In this paper, we addressed these problems by first conducting a modular analysis on common session search metrics, based on which we studied a fundamental question in session search: how to maximize a user's gain of information given the constraints on the user's effort/cost. Our research provides a new viewpoint of evaluation metrics and improvement of IR systems based on different metric settings.

title: Learning to filter tweet stream in real time
abstract: Twitter is characterized by the volume, velocity, and variety of the published information. Filtering and summarizing tweet stream for long ongoing events is a challenging task. To be effective, a trade off between pushing too many or too few tweets, and between the summary quality and the latency need to be achieved. While the proposed approaches are based mainly on the tweet content to discard irrelevant tweets regarding the event of interest, it is unclear how effective is the use of social signals in this task. In this paper, we propose to use machine learning method to build a binary classifier in which three categories of features are combined namely query dependent, tweet specifics and user account features. The experimental results show that the combination of social signals and query dependent features is able to classify correctly the majority of tweets with an accuracy higher than 90\%. Our experiments on TREC RTF 2015 and TREC RTS 2016 datasets have shown the effectiveness of learning to filter approach.

title: Entity Set Expansion via Knowledge Graphs
abstract: The entity set expansion problem is to expand a small set of seed entities to a more complete set of similar entities. It can be applied in applications such as web search, item recommendation and query expansion. Traditionally, people solve this problem by exploiting the co occurrence of entities within web pages, where latent semantic correlation among seed entities cannot be revealed. We propose a novel approach to solve the problem using knowledge graphs, by considering the deficiency of knowledge graphs. We design an effective ranking model based on the semantic features of seeds to retrieve the candidate entities. Extensive experiments on public datasets show that the proposed solution significantly outperforms the state of the art techniques.

title: Window Context Word Embedding Causes Topic Shifting; Exploit Global Context!
abstract: Exploitation of term relatedness provided by word embedding has gained considerable attention in recent IR literature. However, an emerging question is whether this sort of relatedness fits to the needs of IR with respect to retrieval effectiveness. While we observe a high potential of word embedding as a resource for related terms, the incidence of several cases of topic shifting deteriorates the final performance of the applied retrieval models. To address this issue, we revisit the use of global context (i.e. the terms co occurrence in documents) to measure the terms relatedness. We hypothesize that in order to avoid topic shifting among the terms with high word embedding similarity, they should also share relatively high global contexts. We therefore study the effectiveness of post filtering related terms by various global context relatedness measures. Experimental results show significant improvement in two out of three test collections tested, and support our initial hypothesis regarding the importance of considering global context in retrieval.

title: Optimizing Change Detection in Distributed Digital Collections
abstract: It is not unusual for digital documents to have problems associated with the persistence of links, especially when dealing with references to external resources. People keep track of various webpages of their interest using distributed digital collections and without possession of these documents; the curator cannot control how they change. In the current context, managing these distributed digital collections and getting notifications about varies changes have become a significant challenge. In this paper, we address the architectural aspects of change detection systems and present an optimized change detection architecture, including a web service and a browser plugin, along with an email notification service. We have performed an experimental study on our hybrid architecture for change detection in a distributed digital collection. The proposed method introduces a preliminary framework that can serve as a useful tool to mitigate the impact of unexpected change in documents stored in decentralized collections in the future.

title: A Sentiment Based Customer Review Summarization Method
abstract: Quickly understanding the opinions of customers from massive reviews has great importance for both individual and manufacturers. We design a sentiment based customer review summarization method that could extract typical reviews which represent the major opinions from massive customer reviews. The method contains two steps, the first step is to generate a candidate set using a sentiment based topic model and the second step is to use a ranking based sentence extraction methods based on the candidate set. The experiments performed on two datasets show the effectiveness of our method under both human evaluation and automatic evaluation.

title: An Efficient Medical Image Retrieval based on Specific Features
abstract: Facing the explosion in the amount of medical images, the image indexing and retrieval systems have seen an evolution to provide access to biomedical literature and satisfy the user information needs. Hence, several context based medical image retrieval approaches, such as text based, concept based, and specific feature based, have been appeared. In this paper, we investigate the performance of specific feature based retrieval according to both criteria: Efficiency and effectiveness. We exploit specific medical features into an indexing and retrieval process. Using two medical imageCLEF collections, we compare the performance of Specific feature retrieval with approaches from the literature and analyze where they are effective. Results show that using specific features is effective for retrieving images and more efficient for reducing time/space occupancy.

title: Convolutional Ranking in Community Question Answering
abstract: Convolutional Neural Networks have proven to be useful in a number of Natural Language Processing tasks. In this paper, we present three different convolutional models for Answer Selection and Similar Question Retrieval problems in community question answering in which we rank answers or questions with respect to a given question. Our three models are parallel, two channel, and joint channel models that essentially differ in terms of their encoding of convolutional representations. We further analyze the transferability of the convolutional models in question answering tasks. Experimental results show that our best model outperforms baselines and is robust against small and imbalanced training data. Furthermore, we show that transfer learning effectively deals with the problem of insufficient training data for some question answering tasks.

title: A Study of Quantum Language Model in Question Answering
abstract: Quantum theory, as a fundamental mathematical framework, has been shown to provide new theoretical insights to the development of advanced Information Retrieval (IR) models. Recently, Quantum Language Model (QLM), which takes the local term dependencies into consideration, has been developed and successfully applied to several typical IR tasks (e.g., ad hoc retrieval and session search). In this paper, we aim to broaden the theoretical and practical basis of QLM in light of the emerging Question Answering (QA) task. In QA, effectively measuring the similarity between a question and an answer is key, for which incorporating the global dependency information is also crucial. To address these issues, we first theoretically investigate variants of QLM based on a number of different quantum similarity/distance measures, and explore the intrinsic link between the quantum measures and a widely used similarity measure (i.e., word overlaps) in QA. Further, we propose an embedding based QLM (EQLM) with global dependency information. Experimental results on the TREC QA and WIKIQA datasets have verified our analysis and demonstrated that the proposed variants and extensions to QLM largely improve the performance of the word overlaps based and QLM based baselines.

title: Predicting Fashion Branding Effects Using User Generated Brand Network
abstract: The use of social media has increased company's interactions and communications with individuals. It not only increases the visibility of young designer fashion brands but also makes the competition even more fierce due to the proliferation of social media channels. Branding, activities that signal quality, status, and value of the brand, becomes a critical issue for fashion brands on social media. However, the branding effects of fashion brands on social media are under investigated in prior studies and are challenging to capture due to the domination of major national brands' marketing campaigns. In order to understand the branding effects among various types of fashion brands, this study examines and predicts the branding effects of fashion brands on a user generated brand network by using network analysis. Based on a data set with 707 users and 120K posts from Lookbook.nu, our initial findings demonstrate that both network information and brand preferences can improve our understanding of the choice of posting outfits with different brands.

title: Building Your Own Reading List Anytime via Embedding Relevance, Quality, Timeliness and Diversity
abstract: During every summer holidays, several editions of reading lists are recommended and emerged on mass media, e.g., New York Times, and BBC. However, these reading lists are built for whole people with general topics for some purposes. What if we expect the books of a specific topic at a specific moment? How to generate the requested reading list for our own automatically? In this paper, we propose a searching framework for building a topical reading list anytime, where the Relevance (between topics and books), Quality (of books), Timeliness (of popularities) and Diversity (of results) are embedded into vector representations respectively based on user generated contents and statistics on social media. We collected 8,197 real world topics from 198 diverse groups on Librarything.com. The proposed methods are evaluated on the topic collection and the public benchmarks Social Book Search 2012 2016 (SBS). Experimental results demonstrate the robustness and effectiveness of our framework.

title: A Neural Matching Model for Question Retrieval
abstract: Retrieving similar questions is a challenging problem in information retrieval, and it has significant importance in many applications in community question answering systems and search systems. In this paper, we propose a neural matching model for question retrieval under a general setting, where no question category or answer information is available. The proposed model uses a Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) layer for the long term dependency modeling in questions, and adopts Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for question representation learning based on the output of LSTM. Extensive experiments carried out on a publicly available dataset recently released by Quora show that our method can significantly outperform a variety of baselines, including a state of the art translation based language model (TRLM). Furthermore, when our neural matching model is integrated with basic term matching based retrieval models, larger gains can be achieved. As a further contribution, we also built a test collection with the Quora data, which is being made available to the community for further investigation of question retrieval.

title: A New Test of Cluster Hypothesis Using a Similarity based Hierarchical Co clustering Method
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new test of cluster hypothesis by applying a similarity based hierarchical co clustering method. The novelties of this work are threefold: (1) similarities output by different kernel functions are firstly used in cluster hypothesis test; (2) sparsifying similarities results in better retrieval efficiency for hierarchical clustering methods; and (3) being capable to discover the hierarchies inside and among co clusters, the tested method allows us to know the describing features of co clusters that are significantly relevant to a query. Employing the Optimal Cluster Search strategy, our experiments using linear kernel and Gaussian kernel demonstrate that retrieval effectiveness tends to be invariant to the sparsity of an input proximity matrix, revealing the fact of achieving the same effectiveness using at maximum 90\% less proximities. Furthermore, concerning retrieval effectiveness among clustering methods, our experiment supplements previous tests of cluster hypothesis, by adding Mcquitty, median and centroid methods in the test. We discover that complete, average and Ward methods are not always the dominant ones, as reported in past works. Instead, Mcquitty and median methods outperform the others in some cases.

title: On the geometry of narratives
abstract: After lying dormant for half a century, the interest in IR systems for automatic summarization and topic tracking is afoot again. As such systems can condense a story to its underlying storyline it could reduce an information overload. We examined publications for topic detection and tracking, and then formulated minimal requirements against which to assess these. The algorithms we studied fall short of one or more of these requirements. The paper therefore proposes a teqnique that at once generalizes the operative ingredient of previous systems and fulfills the formulated requirements. It does so by defining topics as high dimensional but sparse elements of a Grassmann manifold, and storyline as a trajectory connecting these elements. Geometric optimization (through Newton methods) then computes a best fit with respect to a stationary low dimensional story background. We found that random projections on the manifold are effective for discovering a storyline, while fulfilling the requirements.

title: Towards Understanding Cross cultural Crowd Sentiment using Social Media
abstract: Social media such as Twitter has been frequently used for expressing personal opinions and sentiments of users at different geographic places. In this paper, we propose a novel crowd sentiment analysis for fostering cross cultural studies. In particular, we aim to find similar meanings but different sentiments between social data such as tweets collected over diverse geographical areas. For this, we detect sentiments and topics of each tweet by applying the deep learning approach, and assign sentiments to each topic based on the sentiments of the corresponding tweets. This permits finding interesting cross cultural patterns by computing topic and sentiment correspondence. The proposed methods enable to analyze tweets from diverse geographical areas sentimentally in order to explore cross cultural differences. We evaluate the results of the proposed method on datasets derived from Twitter which are related to two countries: France and Italy.

title: IPC Based Information Retrieval for Patent Quality Classification
abstract: This study proposed a novel approach for patent information retrieval We attempt extract meaningful information from patent claims based on international patent classification (IPC). And, we want to map features relationship between IPCs and claims using text mining and natural language processing (NLP) techniques. First, we retrieve a set of keywords from descriptions of IPC according to these patents of training data in solar cell industry. These IPC based keywords are covered the industrial applications scope, and then, we compute the features mapping which have threes encoding such as binary, term frequency (TF) and average word embeddings. In our experimental results, the features mapping using IPC based keywords with patent claim data can be obtain more meaningful information and improved patent quality classification performance.

title: On the Effectiveness of Bayesian Network based Models for Document Ranking
abstract: Theoretical soundness and technical feasibility of treating the problem of document ranking in IR as an inference problem in Bayesian Networks, was studied in a recent research. A pilot framework was also proposed there. In this paper, we provide two implementations of the framework: BNBM25, the one based on BM25, and BNMATF, which is based on MATF, a state of the art ranking function. We empirically verify the effectiveness of these two implementations on several standard test collections. Positive, significant results are obtained. Potentials of this BN based framework in addition to its verified effectiveness are also discussed. As a result of the study, we believe that the technique is promising, worthy of further analysis and application.

title: A Non parametric Term Frequency Normalization Model for Probabilistic Information Retrieval
abstract: In probabilistic BM25, term frequency normalization is a key component. It is often controlled by parameters k1 and b, which are generally different and need to be optimized on each data set. In this paper, we assume and show empirically that term frequency normalization should be specific with query length in order to optimize retrieval performance. Following this intuition, we first propose a non parametric term frequency normalization with query length for probabilistic information retrieval, namely BM25NP. Then BM25NP is incorporated into the state of the art BM25 based models CRTER2 and LDA BM25, denoted as CRTER2NP and LDA BM25NP respectively. A series of experiments show that our proposed approaches BM25NP, CRTER2NP and LDA BM25NP are comparable to BM25, CRTER2 and LDA BM25 with the optimal b setting in terms of MAP on all the data sets.

title: ENCORE: External Neural Constraints Regularized Distant Supervision for Relation Extraction
abstract: Distant Supervision is a widely used approach for training relation extraction models. It generates noisy training samples by heuristically labeling a corpus using an existing knowledge base. Previous noise reduction methods for distant supervision fail to utilize information such as data credibility and sample confidence. In this paper, we proposed a novel neural framework, named ENCORE (External Neural COnstraints REgularized distant supervision), which allows an integration of other information for standard DS through regularizations under multiple external neural networks. In ENCORE, a teacher student co training mechanism is used to iterative distilling information from external neural networks to an existing relation extraction model. The experiment results demonstrated that without increasing any data or reshaping its original structure, ENCORE enhanced a CNN based relation extraction model for over 12\%. The enhanced model also outperforms the state of the art relation extraction method on the same dataset.

title: Impact of Replacement Policies on Static Dynamic Query Results Cache in Web Search Engines
abstract: Caching query results is an efficient technique for Web search engines. A state of the art approach named Static Dynamic Cache (SDC) is widely used in practice. Replacement policy is the key factor on the performance of cache system, and has been widely studied such as LIRS, ARC, CLOCK, SKLRU and RANDOM in different research areas. In this paper, we discussed replacement policies for static dynamic cache and conducted the experiments on real large scale query logs from two famous commercial Web search engine companies. The experimental results show that ARC replacement policy could work well with static dynamic cache, especially for large scale query results cache.

title: Interpretation of Node Representations
abstract: Recently there has been a large number of studies on embedding large scale networks such as word word, document document and user user graph into low dimensional, neighborhood and community aware representations. These embeddings have shown to perform exceedingly well for several NLP and IR applications such as document classification, recommendation, document author identification and named entity disambiguation. Though the performance of these embedding models have been better than traditional methods, little is known about what these representations encode, or why a particular node representation works better for certain tasks. Our work presented here constitutes the first step in decoding the black box of vector embedding of nodes by evaluating their effectiveness in encoding elementary properties of a node. Traditional feature engineering methods have exploited various elementary properties of node for high level applications such as node classification, node recommendation and node visualization. We believe that a node representation is effective for an application because it encodes the application specific elementary properties of nodes.
