To unpack the elementary properties encoded in a node representation, we evaluate the representations on the accuracy with which they can model each of these properties such as page rank, degree, closeness centrality, clustering coefficient, etc. We study three state of the art node representation models for three diverse tasks and graphs. Our analysis highlights that the proposed elementary property prediction tasks help in unearthing the important features responsible for the given node embedding model to perform well in a given downstream task.

title: Investigating Relations of Risk and Time Preference with Web Searching Behavior
abstract: During Web searching, a user issues queries and visits several Web pages expecting to make sense of the topics of interest. It is an individual's decision how to invest their limited resources, time and effort, to meet their information needs. Exploring the information space, searchers make decisions attempting to maximize the outcome and satisfaction, which is also affected by personal preferences, such as risk and time preferences. This work investigates how searchers' risk preference as well as time preference relate to their searching behavior: leave or stay. We measure two aspects of searching behavior using the framework of information foraging: distinct query and utilization ratio. Results of a user study with 31 participants suggest that: (1) risk averse people tend not to issue new queries; (2) short term impatient people do not want novel information while long term impatient want more; and (3) people behave differently with regard to risk aversion and time preference in assigned search and free search.

title: Topic specific Micropost Representation
abstract: We consider the problem of topic specific micropost representation in which we aim to encode microposts with arbitrary lengths into vectors of fixed length such that topically similar microposts are close in the vector space. Motivated by the recent success of recursive neural networks (RNNs) in word representation, we propose to utilize RNNs in conjunction with (word and author level) topic information to learn topic specific micropost representation. Our approach results in a more accurate language model and semantic representation of microposts. In particular, it reduce the perplexity of our best baseline language model by 5.2% and lead to more accurate tweet representation on different Twitter datasets.

title: Information Retrieval Model using Generalized Pareto Distribution and Its Application to Instance Search
abstract: We adopt the generalized Pareto distribution for the information based model and show that the parameters can be estimated based on the mean excess function. The proposed information retrieval model corresponds to the extension of the divergence from independence and is designed to be data driven. The proposed model is then applied to the specific object search called the instance search and the effectiveness is experimentally confirmed.

title: A Bag Of Entity based Information Retrieval: A Pilot Study
abstract: This paper investigates a new bag of entities representation for document ranking in ad hoc retrieval task. The improvements in entity linking systems result in the effective annotation of text with entities in a knowledge base (i.e. Wikipedia). The proposed learn to rank model utilizes the entity annotations, and the devised language model estimates the query/document similarity. The key point in bag of entity representation for ranking task is to simultaneously account for ambiguities in the entity linking process while retaining the bag of words similarity influence. Empirical evaluation on TREC Web Track collections demonstrates improvements over strong term based ranking baselines.

title: Towards Optimization of E Commerce Search: Formalization of Multiple Objectives in E Commerce Search
abstract: E Commerce (E Com) search is an emerging problem with multiple new challenges, including particularly the challenge of optimizing multiple objectives involving business metrics. Apart from maximizing relevance as in Web search, E Com search must also optimize two other critical metrics, i.e., the sell through rate (STR) and revenue. In this paper, we introduce and formalize the novel problem of optimizing E Com search for both STR and revenue, without hurting relevance of search results. We provide a formal denition of multiple objectives including Sell Through Rate (STR), Revenue Per Visit (RPV), and the discoverability to form a theoretical foundation for the development of effective E Com search algorithms that can optimize multiple objectives in E Com search. We sketch a novel epsilon explore Learning to Rank (e LTR) paradigm that can be integrated with the traditional LTR framework to explore new or less exposed items and discuss possible ways to evaluate e LTR.

title: Distant Supervision for Topical Classification of Tweets in Curated Streams
abstract: We tackle the challenge of topical classification of tweets in the context of analyzing a large collection of curated streams to deliver relevant content to users. Our approach is novel in applying distant supervision based on semi automatically identifying curated streams that are topically focused. These streams provide a source of labeled data to train topical classifiers that can then be applied to categorize tweets from more topically diffuse streams. Experiments on both noisy labels and human ground truth judgments demonstrate that our approach yields good topical classifiers essentially ``for free'', and that topic classifiers trained in this manner are able to dynamically adjust for topic drift as news on Twitter evolves.

title: Semiautomatic Post Hoc Analysis of A/B Tests
abstract: We present a semi automatic method for analyzing the results of A/B tests in information retrieval. Based on a set of evidence derived from a document ranking, an index, and a test collection such as relevance judgments, document lengths, query term frequencies, and more we test hypotheses about the relationships between a measure of effectiveness such as precision at 10 and basic features of documents. The results of these tests can tell us much more about the underlying reasons that explain how the modified system is performing differently than the baseline.

title: Predicting Information Seeking Intentions from Search Behaviors
abstract: It has been shown that people attempt to accomplish a variety of intentions during the course of an information seeking session, and there is reason to believe that these different information seeking intentions can benefit from system support tailored to each such intention. This paper is concerned with the problem of predicting the presence of such intentions during an information seeking session, through analysis of observable user search behaviors. We present results of a study of 40 participants working, each working on two different journalism tasks, which investigated how their search behaviors could indicate their intentions. Using 725 query segments captured from this study, our results demonstrate that information seeking intentions can be predicted with a simple classification model using a linear combination of search behavior features that can be logged with a browser plug in.

title: But is it Statistically Significant?
abstract: We analyze 5,792 IR conference papers published over 20 years to investigate how researchers have used and are using statistical significance testing in their experiments.

title: Generalized Mixed Effect Models for Personalizing Job Search
abstract: Job Search is a core product at LinkedIn which makes it essential to generate highly relevant search results when a user searches for jobs on Linkedin. Historically job results were ranked using linear models consisting of a combination of user, job and query features. This paper talks about a new generalized mixed effect models introduced in the context of ranking candidate job results for a job search performed on LinkedIn. We build a per query model which is populated with coefficients corresponding to job features in addition to the existing global model features. We describe the details of the new method along with the challenges faced in launching such a model into production and making it efficient at a very large scale. Our experiments show improvement over previous baseline ranking models, in terms of offline metrics (both AUC and NDCG@K metrics) as well as online metrics in production (Job Applies) which are of interest to us. The resulting method is more powerful and has also been adopted in other applications at LinkedIn successfully.

title: Behavioral Analysis of Long Surviving Arabic Content Polluters
abstract: We study the behavior of long lived eventually suspended accounts in social media through a comprehensive investigation of Arabic Twitter. With a threefold study of (i) the content these accounts post; (ii) the evolution of their linguistic patterns; and (iii) their activity evolution, we compare long lived users versus short lived, legitimate, and pro ISIS users. We find that these long lived accounts though trying to appear normal do exhibit significantly different behaviors from both normal and other suspended users. We additionally identify temporal changes that could support future discovery of these accounts who may be "hiding in plain sight".

title: A Sequence Model for Analyzing Spatial Patterns of Search Engine Results Page
abstract: This paper proposes a sequence model for analyzing relevance patterns on search engine results page (SERP). A 3rd degree polynomial curve was selected to fit the sequence model. The coefficients of the polynomial curve were extracted as the reduced representation of the sequences. K means clustering and a series of predictive models were applied on the coefficients to classify the SERP relevance patterns and predict user search behavior.

title: Twitter Demographic Classification using Deep Multi Modal Multi Task Learning
abstract: Twitter should be an ideal place to get a fresh read on how different issues are playing with the public, one that's potentially more reflective of democracy in this new media age than traditional polls. Pollsters typically ask people a fixed set of questions, while in social media people use their own voices to speak about whatever is on their minds. However, the demographic distribution of users on Twitter is not representative of the general population. In this paper, we present a demographic classifier for gender, age, political orientation and location on Twitter. We collected and curated a robust Twitter demographic dataset for this task. Our classifier uses a deep multi modal multi task learning architecture to reach a state of the art performance, achieving an F1 score of 0.89, 0.82, 0.86, and 0.68 for gender, age, political orientation, and location respectively.

title: Contextualizing Citations for Scientific Summarization using Word Embeddings and Domain Knowledge
abstract: Citation texts are sometimes not very informative or in some cases inaccurate by themselves; they need the appropriate context from the referenced paper to reflect its exact contributions. To address this problem, we propose an unsupervised model that uses distributed representation of words as well as domain knowledge to extract the appropriate context from the reference paper. Evaluation results show the effectiveness of our model by significantly outperforming the state of the art. We furthermore demonstrate how an effective contextualization method results in improving citation based summarization of the scientific articles.

title: Geo Social based m Closest Keywords Query Processing
abstract: As we enter a new Internet era with huge various mobile applications, more and more users would like to share geo location information under the context of social network apps. Such a scenario gives opportunities to make the combination of spatial computing and social computing meaningful. In this paper, we argue the current m closest keywords query is not sufficient for the requirement of the combination, due to lack of social dimension. We redefine the problem by adding social distance into measurement of places (locations), which makes the results reflecting friend relationship factors. Next, we propose an algorithm S2KESC, aims to find a circle with smallest diameter that encloses the places covering all query keywords and also satisfy the social distance constraint, and then we design 2 important procedures in S2KESC. For the future we will conduct experimental evaluation for S2KESC.

title: Information Retrieval Evaluation as Search Simulation: A General Formal Framework for IR Evaluation
abstract: We propose a general formal framework for evaluating IR systems based on search session simulation. We show that the traditional Cranfield evaluation method can be regarded as a special instantiation of the proposed framework where the simulated search session is a user sequentially browsing the presented search results and examining each of them in turn. Among the many benefits offered by the proposed framework are the possibilities of analytical examination of existing metrics to reveal any unreasonable assumptions and interpret them from a user's perspective and quantitative evaluation of arbitrary interactive retrieval systems with reproducible experiments.

title: A Joint Framework for Learning Role based Opinion Behaviors
abstract: Exploring the mechanism that explains how a user's opinion changes under the influence of his/her neighbors is of practical importance (e.g., for predicting the sentiment of his/her future opinion) and has attracted wide attention from both companies and researchers. Though various influence models have been proposed for opinion prediction, they never consider the social roles of users which summarize the abilities of users to influence others. In this work, we involve the social roles to build a more comprehensive model for understanding the opinion behaviors, and investigate the opinion behaviors by combining multi level influence between a user and his/her neighbors, including the user based influence and role based influence. A novel joint learning framework is proposed to learn the opinion prediction and social role detection in a unified model. The effectiveness of the proposed model is demonstrated through the experiments conducted on three Twitter datasets.

title: Structural Entity Aspects for Open domain Entity Ranking
abstract: The increased coverage of modern knowledge graphs, and resulting densification, poses two main issues for graph based entity ranking methods: The size of the graphs leads to computational challenges, and the presence of many non relevant edges diminishes the performance of eigenvector centralities, such as PageRank. We suggest a new way to construct knowledge graphs where edges are associated with text paragraphs, and use text retrieval to filter and weight the knowledge graphs.

title: Pseudo Relevance Query Performance Prediction for Information Retrieval
abstract: Techniques for estimating the effectiveness of an information retrieval system in the absence of relevance judgments, known as query performance prediction (QPP), generally work by associating some property of a query or its document result set with an evaluation metric like mean average precision. We propose a method of QPP that directly incorporates notions of relevance into the prediction process. To do this, we rely on the well known information retrieval technique of pseudo relevance feedback to approximate relevance judgments and to reformulate the query. Our experiments indicate that this approach is very effective at predicting query performance.

title: Search Support for the Comprehensive Collection of Related Research Papers using a Topic Analysis Technique
abstract: In an academic paper search, especially a search to confirm the originality of user's research, it is important that the search result includes almost all research papers related to a user's information needs. In this paper, we describe a support system for such comprehensive academic paper search. In such a search, non restrictive search terms are used to mitigate retrieval leakage. However, many non related research papers that do not satisfy the user's information needs are included in the search results when a user searches using such terms. Therefore, it is desirable to be able to support the task of deleting non related research papers. As a support method for identifying the research papers to be deleted, we propose an approach using Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA). First, topic analysis using LDA is performed for research papers' abstracts collected using search words. Then, the user select the topics related to his/her information needs from the topics generated by LDA. We regard that abstracts that do not include any selected topics are not related to the user's information needs and they are to be deleted. To investigate the effectiveness of this approach, we conducted the subject experiments using the NTCIR 1 and 2 datasets, and confirmed the effectiveness.

title: Optimizing Multi Page Search Results in Exploratory Search Tasks
abstract: Learning from user interactions has shown great promise in online optimization of ranking models for Web search. However, such models are currently leaned to optimize search results for one time queries. While many common search scenarios, such as exploratory search tasks, require search page navigation to be fully satis ed. For each result page, the search engine must resolve an exploration exploitation tradeoff; exploiting all user feedback obtained thus far to provide the user with documents maximizing the probability of relevance, or exploring the document space in order to find new aspects of the user information need. Therefore, we model the multi page exploratory search task as a sequential decision problem by using Markov decision process (MDP), and the optimal policy to solve the MDP, which specifies the best action to resolve exploration exploitation tradeoff in each state, is learned directly from user interactions. Evaluation based on the dataset of recent TREC dynamic domain track demonstrates that learning from user interactions can improve the performance of the entire session.

title: A Novel Contextual Stemming Algorithm for Microblogs
abstract: Stemming is an important step for improving retrieval performance by unifying different morphological variants of a word. We propose a context specific stemming algorithm for microblogs, based on word embeddings, which is capable of handling the informal, noisy vocabulary of microblogs. Experiments on TREC 2016 microblog dataset show that, the proposed stemmer enables significantly better retrieval performance than several state of the art stemming algorithms, for the same queries.

title: A Context Aware Approach for Detecting Worth Checking Claims in Political Debates
abstract: With the recent emergence of cases of false claims, rumors and fake news, there has been growing interest in fact checking. Investigative journalists and volunteers have been working hard trying to get to the root of a claim and to present solid evidence in favor or against it. Unfortunately, manual fact checking is very time consuming, and thus automatic methods have been proposed as a way to speed up the process. Yet, such methods still lag behind in terms of quality, and thus also of credibility in the eyes of the users, compared to what high quality manual checking by reputable sources can bring. Here, we work on a different way to speed up the process by detecting which claims are most worthy and thus should be prioritized for fact checking; yet, we leave the final decision to the investigative journalists. Despite its importance, this is a relatively understudied problem. Thus, we create a new corpus of political debates, containing statements that have been fact checked by nine reputable sources, and we train an SVM model that predicts which claims should be prioritized for fact checking, i.e., we model the problem as a ranking task. Unlike previous work, which has looked primarily at sentences in isolation, in this paper we focus on the context: interaction between the opponents, and reaction by the moderator and by the public. Our experiments show state of the art results, outperforming a strong rivaling system.

title: Crowdsourced App Review Manipulation
abstract: With the rapid adoption of smartphones worldwide and the reliance on app marketplaces to discover new apps, these marketplaces are critical for connecting users with apps. And yet, the user reviews and ratings on these marketplaces may be strategically targeted by app developers. In this paper, we investigate the use of crowdsourcing platforms to manipulate app reviews. We find that (i) apps targeted by crowdsourcing platforms are rated significantly higher on average than other apps; (ii) the reviews themselves arrive in bursts; (iii) app reviewers tend to repeat themselves by relying on some standard repeated text; and (iv) apps by the same developer tend to share a more similar language model: if one app has been targeted, it is likely that many of the other apps from the same developer have also been targeted.

title: Tree Ensemble Explainability
abstract: Complex machine learned models play an increasingly important role in modern technologies, consuming large amounts of data to provide a plethora of useful services. While these systems are highly effective, many of them are black boxes and give no insight into how they make the choices they make. Moreover, those that do often do so at the model level rather than the instance level. In this work, we present a method for deriving instance level explanations for tree ensemble models and examine its applications. Given tree ensemble models such as Random Forests and Boosted Trees are used across industry with great success, adding a level of insight simultaneously boosts modeler effectiveness and consumer trust.

title: Hybrid Deep Semantic Matrix Factorization for Tag Aware Personalized Recommendation
abstract: Matrix factorization has now become a dominant solution for personalized recommendation on the Social Web. To alleviate the cold start problem, previous approaches have incorporated various additional sources of information into the traditional matrix factorization models. These upgraded models, however, achieve only "marginal" enhancements on the personalized recommendation performance. Therefore, inspired by the recent development of deep semantic modeling, we propose a hybrid deep semantic matrix factorization (HDMF) model to further improve the performance of tag aware personalized recommendation by integrating the techniques of deep semantic modeling, hybrid learning, and matrix factorization. Experimental results show that HDMF significantly outperforms the state of the art baselines in tag aware personalized recommendation, in terms of all evaluation metrics, e.g., its mean reciprocal rank (resp. mean average precision) is 1.52 (resp. 1.66) times as high as that of the best baseline.

title: Word Sense Disambiguation using Wiktionary
abstract: In this paper, we present a new approach of using Wiktionary for the problem of Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD). The proposed framework includes the use of an online dictionary as corpus known as Wiktionary for training, the adapted LESK algorithm applied for WSD, and a multiple language perspective. Being well known and an open resource with a large number of relation types, Wiktionary provides multiple features that can be used to improve the task of WSD. We demonstrate the unique features we extract and report the performance compared to alternative models.

title: CitySearcher: A City Search Engine For Interests
abstract: We introduce CitySearcher, a vertical search engine that searches for cities when queried for an interest. Generally in search engines, utilization of semantics between words is favorable for performance improvement. Even though ambiguous query words have multiple semantic meanings, search engines can return diversified results to satisfy different users' information needs. But for CitySearcher, mismatched semantic relationships can lead to extremely unsatisfactory results. For example, the city Sale would incorrectly rank high for the interest shopping because of semantic interpretations of the words. Thus in our system, the main challenge is to eliminate the mismatched semantic relationships resulting from the side effect of the semantic models. In the previous case, we aim to ignore the semantics of a city's name which is not indicative of the city's characteristics. In CitySearcher, we use word2vec, a very popular word embedding technique to estimate the semantics of the words and create the initial ranks of the cities. To reduce the effect of the mismatched semantic relationships, we generate a set of features for learning based on a novel clustering based method. With the generated features, we then utilize learning to rank algorithms to rerank the cities for return. We use the English version of Wikivoyage dataset for evaluation of our system, where we sample a very small dataset for training. Experimental results demonstrate the performance gain of our system over various standard retrieval techniques.

title: Effectiveness of Word Embeddings in Tweet Classification
abstract: Word embedding techniques are being widely used as it is used in constructing continuous word vectors based on contexts in large corpuses. Both semantic and syntactic information of words are captured by word embedding so it can be used to compare word similarities which are widely needed in many IR and NLP tasks. Development of different word embedding techniques have been proposed such as word2vec by Mikolov et al. and doc2vec by Le and Mikolov. In this paper we study the effectiveness of word embeddings in tweet classification. We compared models generated from word2vec and doc2vec and found that doc2vec models performed better. Furthermore, we also compared results to state of the art approaches such as Support Vector Machine and Na{\"i}ve Bayes and found that word embeddings can attain better performance in tweet classification. In addition, we explored POS tagging and used it during the pre processing step with the aim to improve performance of models from word2vec. We show that such an approach could achieve higher performance. We also report the impact of variation of training size to the performance of models using word embeddings.

title: Recognizing and Investigating the Reasons for Question Deletion by Moderators in Community Q&A
abstract: Community question answering (CQA) sites have become major online venues where users can post questions to get answers that are more personalized than many other web resources. This advantage, however, can come with a price; some of the questions present in CQAs are found to be either irrelevant or unrelated to their askers actual needs. In a few cases, the questions are considered to be either inappropriate or deviant in nature. In such scenarios, the CQA community flag these questions as bad (inappropriate, irrelevant, spam, etc.). Once flagged, these posts are often deleted automatically or by the moderators of the CQA system. Therefore, it is valuable to identify the reasons a question may be considered bad in order to help askers revise their posts before publishing them, or outright rejecting them. In this paper, we propose a method in which a bad question can be detected via textual features. To accomplish this, we build a classifier that separates a good or a regular question from a bad or a going to be deleted question using textual features. Further, we propose a method to automatically detect the set of factors that contribute to a question being bad. We demonstrate that we can get about 70% accuracy in detecting whether a question is good or bad. Similarly, we also report decent results for precision, recall and F Measure to identify what factors contributed to a question being bad.

title: Cross Language Question Re ranking
abstract: We study how to find related questions in community forums when the language of the new questions is different from that of the existing questions in the forum. In particular, we explore the Arabic English language pair. We compare a kernel based system with a feed forward neural network in the scenario in which we have a large parallel corpus on which to train a machine translation system, bilingual dictionaries, and cross language word embeddings. We observe that both approaches degrade performance when working on the translated text, especially the kernel based system, which depends heavily on a syntactic kernel. We address this issue using a novel cross language tree kernel, which compares the original Arabic tree to the English trees of the related questions. We show that this kernel almost closes the performance gap to the monolingual system. On the neural network side, we exploit the parallel corpus to extract cross language embeddings used to represent the Arabic input and the English related questions in the same space. The results are also improved, but overall, the performance of the kernel system is superior to the neural network in this problem.

title: Open Relation Extraction for Support Passage Retrieval: Merit and Open Issues
abstract: Despite the success of entity retrieval tasks in IR, such an entity ranking is much more useful for a user if it comes along with human readable explanations of how those retrieved entities are connected to the information need. Relation extraction technology should aid in finding such support passages, especially in combination with entities and query terms. This work explores how the current state of the art in unsupervised relation extraction (OpenIE) contributes to a solution for the task, assessing potential, limitations, and avenues for further investigation.

title: Detecting Session Boundaries in Web Browsing
abstract: Nowadays online users browse the Internet to accomplish various tasks, such as planning for travel and checking recipes for cooking. Users generally use different online channels to accomplish a given task, from search websites to online forums. Through the web browser, it is common to observe that for example users switch from one task (travel) to another (recipe), and then resume (travel). It is crucial to support differentiating various user tasks within the user web browsing sessions. In this paper, we focus on detecting browsing session boundaries within the sequence of users web browsing logs. In our work, Boundary is defined as the given log entry at which a task switch occurs. By logging users visited pages and interactions within the web browser, we conduct a user study that explicitly asks the participants to segment their browsing logs. By mining many features within the web browsing logs, we exploit machine learning to train a classifier that can effectively detect the boundary, with an AUC of 0.94. Our work has shed light on the effectiveness of various mined features comprehensively and can be further exploited in many applications.

title: A Kernel Co occurrence based Rocchios Model for Pseudo Relevance Feedback
abstract: Rocchio's model is a classic query expansion method and it has been shown to be eective in boosting information retrieval performance. However, when selecting expansion terms, Rocchio's model does not consider the co occurrence relationship between a candidate term and a query term. Intuitively, terms which have a higher co occurrence degree with a query term are more likely to be related to the query topic. In this paper, we integrate a term's co occurrence information into Rocchio's model and propose a kernel co occurrence based Rocchio's model called KRoc. We use a Gaussian kernel function to measure a term's co occurrence relationship with a query term. A series of experiments are conducted and the experimental results show that our proposed KRoc model is eective and generally superior to strong baselines and state of the art approaches.

title: Generating Query Suggestions to Support Task Based Search
abstract: We address the problem of generating query suggestions to support users in completing their underlying tasks (which motivated them to search in the first place). Given an initial query, these query suggestions should provide a coverage of possible subtasks the user might be looking for. We propose a probabilistic modeling framework that obtains keyphrases from multiple sources and generates query suggestions from these keyphrases. Using the test suites of the TREC Tasks track, we evaluate and analyze each component of our model.

title: De duping URLs with Sequence to Sequence Neural Networks
abstract: Many URLs on the Internet point to identical contents, which increase the burden of web crawlers. Techniques that detect such URLs (known as URL de duping) can greatly save resources such as bandwidth and storage for crawlers. Traditional de duping methods are usually limited to heavily engineered rules. In this work, we propose a novel URL de duping framework based on sequence to sequence (Seq2Seq) neural networks. A single concise translation model can take the place of thousands of explicit rules. Experiments indicate that a vanilla Seq2Seq architecture yields robust and accurate results in detecting duplicate URLs. Furthermore, we demonstrate the efficiency of this framework in the real large scale web environment.

title: Addressing data sparsity in time series link prediction
abstract: Data sparsity is one of the core issues in future link prediction based on historical social network data. Sparsely distributed data often under estimate the model parameters, whereas over specified data over fits the estimation. This paper proposes two aggregation methods to estimate global parameters: (i) averaging, and (ii) Principal Component Analysis using Singular Value Decomposition. From various experimental observations over various dataset, it is evident that the proposed methods outperform the baseline methods.

title: Automating Relevance Banding in eCommerce Search using Click Model
abstract: eCommerce is burgeoning: in the past five years, both in the USA and the UK, eCommerce retail sales having overtaken brick and mortar stores for the first time. Search is a primary means for users engaging in eCommerce. eCommerce companies often perform laborious human intensive mappings of queries to various categories in their product taxonomiesa process called relevance banding. This is done in order to improve recall and precision of their search engines. In this paper, we propose fully automated alternatives to this manual process. We use statistical properties of the click model that is constructed using query click logs in order to automate this process. We propose two algorithmsprobability banding, and entropy bandingthat perform banding in a fully automated manner. In large scale A/B testing, our algorithms demonstrate considerable revenue and orders increase over the manual banding baseline. Our algorithms are now deployed at scale at CorpXa multibillion dollar eCommerce major.

title: Multi objective topic model for exploratory search in tech news
abstract: We develop an exploratory search technique based on probabilistic topic modeling to retrieve semantically relevant information. It transforms a long query into a bag of topics and retrieves documents by the topics instead of words. We use additive regularization of topic models (ARTM) in order to build a model that meets multiple objectives. Particularly, we enforce topics to be sparse, diverse, and interpretable. Besides, we incorporate meta data such as authors, tags, and categories into the model. We use the parallel online implementation of ARTM from the open source library BigARTM. We evaluate the search quality on two popular tech news media: techcrunch.com in English and habrahabr.ru in Russian. For evaluation we propose a technique which consists of two tasks for assessors. The first one is to find relevant tech news using any search utilities of their choice. The second one is to estimate the relevance of the documents retrieved by our search engine. We use the labeled data to determine the optimal number of topics and show that using meta data improves the search quality. Experiments show that assessors spend about 30 minutes for each query, while our engine produces immediate results providing better recall and comparable precision.

title: Graph Summarization for Entity Relatedness Visualization
abstract: In modern search engines, Knowledge Graphs have become a key component for knowledge discovery. When a user searches for an entity, the existing systems usually provide a list of related entities, but they do not necessarily give explanations of how they are related. However, with the help of knowledge graphs, we can generate relatedness graphs between any pair of existing entities. Existing methods of this problem are either graph based or list based, but they all have some limitations when dealing with large complex relatedness graphs of two related entity. In this work, we investigate how to summarize the relatedness graphs and how to use the dynamic summarization to assistant the users to retrieval target information from these graphs. We also implemented our approach in an online query system and performed thorough experiment evaluation. e results show that our method produces much better result than previous works.

title: Exploiting Legal Text Structures for Relevant Legal Text Retrieval
abstract: This paper presents an approach of exploiting legal structures for improving the performance of legal text retrieval systems. The approach deals with the challenge of usually long and complex legal texts. There are two aspects of legal texts that we opt to adapt for legal text retrieval systems: textual structure and logical structure. Textual structure is the way of organizing legal texts in multi level hierarchy. Logical structure is presented in legal texts as in which legal texts are composed of requisite and effectuation parts. From analyzing the structures, we decompose them into smaller information units. By decomposing the structures into smaller parts, our system performs more fine grain comparison of texts. We then train a ranking model with SVMRank and lexical features generated from the comparison on legal dataset for retrieval task. Experiments show the contribution of our approach for enhancing system performance.

title: Layout and Semantics: Combining Representations for Mathematical Formula Search
abstract: Math aware search engines need to support formulae in queries. Mathematical expressions are typically represented as trees defining their operational semantics or visual layout. We propose searching both formula representations using a three layer model. The first layer selects candidates using spectral matching over tree node pairs. The second layer aligns a query with candidates and computes similarity scores based on structural matching. In the third layer, similarity scores are combined using linear regression. The two representations are combined using retrieval in parallel indices and regression over similarity scores. For NTCIR 12 Wikipedia Formula Browsing task relevance rankings, we see each layer increasing ranking quality as measured by Bpref and nDCG scores.

title: Assessing Credibility in Community Question Answering Forums
abstract: We explore information credibility in community forums, in a setting in which the credibility of an answer posted in a question thread by a particular user has to be assessed. We motivate the problem and we create a publicly available dataset. We further perform preliminary experiments to rank user comments according to their credibility. We play with several features modeling the user, the answer, the question, the thread as a whole, and the interaction between them. Our initial experiments show that we can produce credibility scores leading to good answer rankings, thus supporting the use of this layer of information in practical applications.

title: Convolutional Neural Network with Pair wise Pure Dependence
abstract: Recently, it was shown that Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) could perform well on short text classification. CNN utilizes sliding windows for extracting features on a local block, while the long term dependency during words spanning windows and the global information of the sentence are ignored. We introduce Convolutional Neural Network with Pair wise Pure Dependence (CNN PPD) to effectively build a textual representation for combining the local short term dependency and global long term dependency. In CNN PPD, the Pair wise Pure Dependence(PPD), which is a kind of global dependency mined from the whole corpus and can not be conditionally factorized, is incorporated in CNN as the ultimate weight of partial convolution kernels. The experimental results show better performances than the baseline models.

title: Kullback Leibler Divergence Revisited
abstract: The KL divergence is the most commonly used measure for comparing language models in the language modeling framework to ad hoc document retrieval. We study the retrieval performance of using alternative divergence measures. Since the KL divergence is rank equivalent to a specific weighted mean, we also explore alternative weighted means. Our findings suggest that for sparse query language models (i.e., those with a small support), the KL divergence is not necessarily the best choice, especially for ranking documents in Web collections. For richer query language models, specifically, those induced using pseudo feedback, the KL divergence remains the most effective measure among those we study.

title: Recall Oriented Source Retrieval for Text Reuse Detection
abstract: The first step of each text reuse detection pipeline has to address the source retrieval problem: given a suspicious document, a set of candidate sources (from which text might have been reused) have to be retrieved via intelligently querying a web search engine. Within a second step, the retrieved candidate documents along become subject to text alignment with the suspcious document (in order to identify reused passages). Obviously, any true source of text reuse that is not retrieved during the source retrieval step reduces the recall of the reuse detector. I.e., source retrieval forms a recall oriented task, a fact that has been ignored in the past even among the expert groups: Although source retrieval ran as a shared task within the PAN lab at CLEF 2012 2015, only~2 of 20~participants managed to recall more than half the sources; yet the overall best recall achieved was still only~0.59. We propose a new approach that reaches a recall of~0.81 a massive performance gain of~37\%.

title: Hierarchical Topic Map Generation for Exploratory Browsing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel model for automatically generating topic map for a document corpus with no supervision. Given a collection of documents, we will generate a set of topics on the fly which will help the user to efficiently navigate through the corpus space and finally land upon the desired document. We leverage paradigmatic and syntagmatic relations between words to construct the hierarchy. We characterize each topic in the hierarchy by a single phrase. Our topic map captures the requirements of user while one navigates through the corpus space. Instead of a rigid tree structure, we define links on topic map such that they take user to next desired finer level based on the history of already visited nodes in the map. Experiments on DBLP titles datasets show that our topic map can be used very effectively and intuitively by the user to reach to the desired document.

title: Understanding and Predicting Usefulness Judgment in Web Search
abstract: Usefulness judgment measures the user perceived amount of useful information for the search task in the current search context. Understanding and predicting usefulness judgment are crucial for developing user centric evaluation methods and providing contextualize results according to the search context. With a dataset collected in a laboratory user study, we systematically investigate the effects of a variety of content, context, and behavior factors on usefulness judgments and find that while user behavior factors are most important in determining usefulness judgments, content and context factors also have significant effects on it. We further adopt these factors as features to build prediction models for usefulness judgments. An AUC score of 0.909 in binary usefulness classification and a Pearson's correlation coefficient of 0.694 in usefulness regression demonstrate the effectiveness of our models. Our study sheds light on the understanding of the dynamics of the user perceived usefulness of documents in a search session and provides implications for the evaluation and design of Web search engines.

title: Learning User Representations from Global Social Context for Improving Rumor Detection on Microblog Posts
abstract: Debunking fake information is important to keep social media a healthy environment. Recently, method using deep neural networks (DNNs) has achieved promising results in rumor detection on microblog posts. However, the DNN based model only considers the local content of the posts while ignoring the valuable user properties that can be obtained from the social context of propagation network. Intuitively, user traits especially conveyed by the users' connections and behaviors in the global context of propagation can provide crucial implications on information veracity. In this study, we attempt to learn user representations automatically using network embedding method, which are used to enrich the high level feature representation in DNNs and existing feature based methods for differentiating finer grained categories of rumors. Experimental results on two real world microblog datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms state of the art rumor detection methods with clear advantages on the learned user representations.

title: Dynamic Length Passage Scoring and Accumulated Passage Scoring for Document Retrieval in Ancient Chinese Literature
abstract: Information retrieval systems using vector space model like TF IDF and BM25 were well developed over decades. These algorithms performed well in ad hoc retrieval tasks that returns related document for users. At the same time, passage retrieval is another approach to return a small fraction of document that best matches to the user query. In the applications to find the descriptive mapping between source sentence and explanatory notes in ancient Chinese literature, available passage retrieval methods using fixed passage segments at the index time are not able to cope with the characteristic of written Chinese language. In this research, we propose a dynamic passage segmentation method, along with a passage scoring algorithm by four heuristic features. The algorithm is able to return best matching passages to the users. Also, we use the accumulated passage score as a document retrieval method. In comparison to the TF IDF/BM25 methods, the results showed that our method can improve precision at top most results using unigram, which provides fault tolerance capability to search Chinese literature with partial matching.

title: On the Interpretability of Rankings
abstract: Predictive models are omnipresent in automated and assisted decision making scenarios. But for the most part they are used as black boxes which output a prediction without understanding partially or even completely how different features influence the model prediction avoiding algorithmic transparency. Rankings are ordering over items encoding implicit comparisons typically learned using a family of features using learning to rank models. In this paper focus on how best can a system understand the model decisions made by a ranker in a post hoc model agnostic manner. We operate on the notion of interpretability based on explainability of rankings over an interpretable feature space. Consequently, we attempt to study how well does a subset of features, potentially interpretable, can explain the full model under different training sizes and algorithms. We do extensive experiments on the learning to rank datasets with 30k queries and report results that serve show in certain settings we can learn a faithful interpretable ranker.

title: Kernel Correspondence Analysis and Word Representation
abstract: We show linear correspondence analysis (LCA) is equivalent to defining a Gini index with appropriately scaled one hot encoding. Using this relation, we introduce nonlinear kernel extension of correspondence analysis. The extended correspondence analysis gives known analysis for categorical data and natural language processing by specializing kernels. We porpose supervised correspondence analysis (SCA) which is a special case of the kernel extension of correspondence analysis. We also show LCA avoiding catastrophic cancellation outperforms word2vec when training text data is not large and SCA outperforms word2vec and LCA when training data is large.

title: Open Source Repository Recommendation in Social Coding
abstract: Social coding and open source repositories have become more and more popular. Software developers have various alternatives to contribute themselves to the communities and collaborate with others. However, nowadays there is no effective recommender suggesting developers appropriate repositories in both the academia and the industry. Although existing one class collaborative filtering (OCCF) approaches can be applied to this problem, they do not consider particular constraints of social coding such as the programming languages, which, to some extent, associate the repositories with the developers. The aim of this paper is to investigate the feasibility of leveraging user programming language preference to improve the performance of OCCF based repository recommendation. Based on matrix factorization, we propose language regularized matrix factorization (LRMF), which is regularized by the relationships between user programming language preferences. Extensive experiments have been conducted on the real world dataset of GitHub. The results demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms five competitive baselines.

title: Venue Appropriateness Prediction for Personalized Context Aware Venue Suggestion
abstract: Personalized context aware venue suggestion plays a critical role in satisfying the users needs on location based social networks (LBSNs). In this paper, we present a set of novel scores to measure the similarity between a user and a candidate venue in a new city. The scores are based on user's history of preferences in other cities as well as user's context. We address the data sparsity problem in venue recommendation with the aid of a proposed approach to predict contextually appropriate venues. Furthermore, we show how to incorporate different scores to improve the performance of recommendation. The experimental results of our participation in the TREC 2016 Contextual Suggestion track shows that our approach beats state of the art strategies.

title: Improving Document Availability in Academic Facility
abstract: is paper provides a case study of improving availability for search ing documents in an academic facility. Every day we need some documents for our business in Center for Administration of In formation Technology (AIT) in Tokushima University1. AIT has been employing and operating Information Security Management System (ISMS)2 since 2014. ISMS requires to maintain Con den tiality, Integrity and Availability. Tokushima University places im portance on Availability. However, we were su ering from a time consuming problem to nd documents in the daily operation. We conducted a case study to put a full text search engine in an facility, considering the objective and e ciency about nding documents in the le server. In the process, we found document freshness is important to academic o ce workers for their job. And we as sessed the e ectiveness of a score in consideration of tf idf with document freshness. erefore, we made an improving an avail ability for nding documents using a full text search engine and some information retrieval techniques.

title: Traversing Linked Geospatial Data GeoNames in the Semantic Web
abstract: We take a look at the GeoNames gazetteer as a hub of Linked Geospatial Data. We examine quality and linkage characteristics to find out how well it allows the traversal of the Semantic Web and what issues may occur. Since many Semantic Web applications use GeoNames to ground location concepts, the availability of further outlinks from there into other resources such as DBpedia is a valuable factor. We examine different traversal scenarios originating with GeoNames and present findings related to link availability and distribution along language and geospatial dimensions and further discuss the role of cross lingual issues. Our findings show that up to 13\% of GeoNames populated places are linking into the Semantic Web, but that there are a number of additional links to local language versions that make it harder to traverse links in a default English language setting; that there are certain Web links not available through the RDF endpoints, and that there is a certain small bias in language and geospatial distribution. We propose approaches to address some of these issues, show the impact of these issues so they can partially be mitigated, and discuss options for future work.

title: Building Bridges across Social Platforms: Answering Twitter Questions with Yahoo! Answers
abstract: A tremendous number of questions are posted daily on microblogs. Some are rhetorical, and others seek real information needs. Among the latter ones, a large fraction remains unanswered. Several recent studies focused on identifying such questions, but providing useful answers is a natural next step that has not seen much attention. In this work, we investigate the ability to answer microblogs question by searching in a large community question answering website. To do so, we consider some transformations that the question has to go through, examine some proprieties of the answering platform, and study how to select among the various available configurations in a learning to rank framework.

title: Large Scale Goodness Polarity Lexicons for Community Question Answering
abstract: We transfer a key idea from the field of sentiment analysis to a new domain: community question answering (cQA). The cQA task we are interested in is the following: given a question and a thread of comments, we want to re rank the comments, so that the ones that are good answers to the question would be ranked higher than the bad ones. We notice that good vs. bad comments use specific vocabulary and that one can often predict the goodness/badness of a comment even ignoring the question, based on the comment contents only. This leads us to the idea to build a good/bad polarity lexicon as an analogy to the positive/negative sentiment polarity lexicons, commonly used in sentiment analysis. In particular, we use pointwise mutual information in order to build large scale goodness polarity lexicons in a semi supervised manner starting with a small number of initial seeds. The evaluation results show an improvement of 0.7 MAP points absolute over a very strong baseline, and state of the art performance on SemEval 2016 Task 3.

title: Session aware Information Embedding for E commerce Product Recommendation
abstract: Most of existing recommender systems assume that the user's visiting history can be constantly recorded, recommendation for anonymous users in the e commerce website has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we propose a novel deep neural network based method to address this kind of users, by leveraging user's multiple search behaviors within each session. Without relying on the user profile and previous historical records, we design a list wise ranking method to generate the recommendation based on a sequence of user behaviors within the session. A pre train method is also adopted to accelerate the model training. We conduct quantitative experiments on a recently published dataset. The evaluation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, which can outperform the typical state of the art recommendation methods.

title: Applying RadViz to Explore, Annotate and Classify Text Documents
abstract: Visualizing data is crucial in making various decisions such as what samples to use for building computational models or which attributes best capture the concepts reflected in the data and potentially influence the computational model representing it. To visualize high dimensional data, such as text, 2D graphical representations are often used, since they are easier to understand. Methods such as Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and t Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t SNE) have been successfully applied to project high dimensional data for visualization purposes. However, once the projections are derived, the connection to the attribute values in the data is lost, making it hard to reason about how these values influence the projection. Understanding this relationship is essential for many tasks, in particular, to create and refine a model of the data through learning a classifier. In this paper we propose a novel interactive framework that uses Radial Coordinate Visualization (RadViz) to explore text documents. RadViz enables visualization of projections while maintaining the context of the data: users can simultaneously visualize the attributes of the data and the data items. We propose extensions to this model as well as combine it with other visual representations and discuss how the resulting framework simplifies the identification of clusters, streamlines document labeling for learning a classifier, and helps users track how classifiers evolve as they are refined.

title: Query Expansion for Sentence Retrieval: Using Pseudo Relevance Feedback and Word Embedding Techniques
abstract: This work focuses on the task of sentence retrieval for non factoid queries. We explore Language Modelling (LM) and BM25 information retrieval (IR) models for sentence retrieval and apply query expansion techniques to address the vocabulary mismatch problem between query and answer sentences. We investigate two different query expansion approach for sentence retrieval: 1) pseudo relevance feedback (PRF), using Robertson terms selection, and 2)using word embeddings for performing query expansion. The experiments are done on WebAP data set developed using TREC GOV2 collection. The experimental results measured using P@10, NDCG@10 and MRR reveal that: 1) query expansion technique using PRF perform significantly better as compared to using just the retrieval model, 2) using word embeddings techniques for query expansion shows a small improvement over the baseline obtained using LM and BM25 retrieval models, but the difference is not significant. Further, we propose a 2 step approach which leverages the semantic representation of queries for enhancing pseudo relevance technique. The results using the 2 step model perform consistently better over the baseline and using just the PRF method. This work is a part of our ongoing investigation towards developing better web document summaries for different search tasks to support search interactions and users engagement effectively.

title: Neural Language Model for Query Auto Completion
abstract: Query auto completion (QAC) systems suggest queries that complete a user's text as the user types. Such queries are typically selected among previously stored queries, based on specific attributes such as popularity. However, queries cannot be suggested if a user's text does not match any queries in the storage. In order to suggest queries for previously unseen text, we propose a neural language model that learns how to generate a query from a starting text, a prefix. Specifically, we employ a recurrent neural network to handle prefixes in variable length. We perform the first neural language model experiments for QAC, and we evaluate the proposed methods with a public data set. Empirical results show that the proposed methods are as effective as traditional methods for previously seen queries and are superior to the state of the art QAC method for previously unseen queries.

title: Twitter Advertisement Outreach: Learning the Role of Aesthetics
abstract: Corporations spend millions of dollars on developing creative image based promotional content to advertise to their user base on platforms like Twitter. Our paper is an initial study, where we propose a novel method to evaluate and improve outreach of promotional images from corporations on Twitter, based purely on their describable aesthetic atributes. Existing works in aesthetic based image analysis exclusively focus on the atributes of digital photographs, and are not applicable to advertisements due to the influences of inherent content and context based biases on outreach. Our paper identifies broad categories of biases affecting such images, describes a method for normalizing to eliminate effects of those biases and score images based on their outreach, and examines the effects of certain handcrafted describable aesthetic features on image outreach. Optimizing on the describable aesthetic features resulting from this research is a simple method for corporations to complement their existing marketing strategy to gain significant improvement in user engagement on Twitter for promotional images.

title: Using Technical Knowledge Base to determine prerequisites
abstract: Learning about technical topics is a continuous process and is often difficult for both new students, as well as experienced researchers. The difficulty comes, in part, from the lack of pre requisite knowledge as well as context to study a given subject. In this paper, our goal is to return prerequisites for a topic of interest. We have automaticaly constructed a technical knowledge base and proposed techniques to use it to improve the performance of exisiting prerequisite prefer ence function RefD. Results on two sample query sets show improved precision by a factor of more than 1.5.

title: Integrating the Framing of Clinical questions via PICO into the Retrieval of Medical Literature for Systematic Reviews
abstract: The PICO process is a technique used in evidence based practice to frame and answer clinical questions. It involves structuring the question around four types of clinical information: Population, Intervention, Control or comparison and Outcome. The PICO framework is used extensively in the compilation of systematic reviews as the means of devising the search strategies used to retrieve studies for inclusion in the review. This paper evaluates how PICO annotations can be applied and integrated into retrieval to improve the screening of studies for inclusion in systematic reviews. The task is to increase precision while maintaining the high level of recall essential to ensure systematic reviews are representative and not biased. Our results showed that restricting the search strategies to match studies on the basis of PICO annotations does improve precision compared to a non PICO baseline (while maintaining similar recall). The implication of this study is that the development of search technologies based on these annotations can lead to both time and cost savings when compiling systematic reviews.

title: Seasonal Web Search Query Selection for Influenza Like Illness (ILI) Prediction
abstract: Influenza like illness (ILI) prediction from web search data is an important web analytics task, most notably popularised by Google Flu Trends. The basic idea is to use the frequency of queries in web search logs that are correlated with past ILI activity as features when predicting future ILI activity. One problem is that this approach leads to spurious correlations of non informative queries, which harm the quality of the resulting predictions. We present a novel solution to this problem: we model the seasonal variation of ILI activity and select queries that closely fit this seasonality. This selection is principled and produces predictions that are much more accurate than when not modelling seasonality (up to 11% reduction in root mean squared error) and efficient (notably fewer queries are used for the prediction).

title: Modeling Bidder Sequential Behaviors in Sponsored Search with Deep Inverse Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Sponsored search is a search advertising service that displays ads by holding online repeated auctions. In this market, advertisers participate in the auction as bidders and optimize their ad campaigns by sequential and interactive actions such as selecting relative keywords, changing bids, and so on. Modeling and understanding bidder behaviors are useful to improve auction mechanism design and evaluate the customer experience. Some previous works on this topic rely on overly strict assumptions or lacks understanding of bidders real motivation. In this paper, we propose an approach for interpreting and predicting sequential behaviors of bidders by formalizing it as an IRL (inverse reinforcement learning) problem. This method can reveal the utility function motivating the decisions and predict future behavior simultaneously by learning form observed historical sequences of different behaviors. The experimental results based on real sponsored search data validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in understanding advertisers behaviors.

title: Axiomatic Analysis to Model Term Discrimination Heuristic and Query Length
abstract: Number of terms in a query is a query specific constant that is typically ignored in retrieval functions. However, previous studies have shown that the performance of retrieval models varies for different query lengths, and it usually degrades when query length increases. A possible reason for this issue can be the high term redundancy in longer queries that makes it a challenge for the retrieval models to distinguish between the key and complementary concepts of the query. As a signal to understand the importance of a term, inverse document frequency~(IDF) can be used to discriminate query terms. In this paper, we propose a constraint to model the interaction between query length and IDF. Our theoretical analysis shows that current state of the art retrieval models, such as BM25, do not satisfy the proposed constraint. We further analyze the BM25 model and suggest a modification to adapt BM25 so that it adhere to the new constraint. Our experiments on three TREC collections demonstrate that the proposed modification outperforms the baselines, especially for verbose queries.

title: Timestamping Entities using Contextual Information
abstract: Wikipedia is the result of collaborative effort aiming to represent human knowledge and to make it accessible to the public. Many articles however lack key metadata information. For example, relatively large number of people have no information on their birth and death dates. We propose to estimate entitys lifetimes using link structure in Wikipedia. Our approach is based on propagating temporal information over links between Wikipedia articles.

title: Learning User Preference and Semantic Structure ofHeterogeneous Domains From User Curated Lists
abstract: List creation has become a popular way for online social network users to curate preferences. These lists capture a coherent semantic representation of the domain the list of items belong to. List curation can be seen as a way to capture fine grained topic specific item lists by users. List creation requires considerable effort on the part of community members of the domain, these lists can be user specific as well as community driven. Understanding and modeling user preferences expressed in these curated lists would help with diverse set of applications such as recommendations, user modeling, session understanding etc. This paper proposes generating semantic embedding of items based on a User ItemList Item graph using metawalks. In this work we mine the patterns generated by random walks in a heterogeneous information network to capture the semantic structure underlying these lists. We show how these semantic embeddings can be used for the tasks of List completion and List refinement. To empirically evaluate our approaches we perform experiments on a large collection of user lists curated on The Internet Movie Database (IMDb) and GoodReads.com, two popular community driven domains. Our approaches for the List completion task out performs nearest neighbour approaches for the List completion task.

title: Automatic Generation of Video Highlight with Title from Mass Interaction
abstract: As video content services explosively proliferate, both producers and consumers need short video clips that highlight the exciting scenes from the whole video content. However, it is not easy for editors to extract the summarized video segments, because it requires gathering the favorite video scenes and the appropriate titles, but it is labor intensive and not scalable. Though a few studies have looked into the video highlight generation problem of sports games based on Twitter, they have not focused on the diverse genres and the automatic title generation for the highlight scenes. In this work, we propose an automatic video summarization method that supports scene title synthesis from massive interaction data of the online community websites. We have designed our system that collects and analyzes chatting or online comments of users from YouTube, Twitch, sports video streaming websites, and a famous Korean web community. Our method detects the most favorite scenes with the peak of viewers' messages and generates the corresponding titles after dissecting the words and synthesizing the title sentences. From experiments of 100 video contents from four genres, we have shown that our proposal can summarize video streaming contents regarding drama, entertainment, sports and online game.

title: Multi Armed Bandits for Cluster based Active Search
abstract: We propose a multi armed bandits approach to perform active search in a collection of documents where the class of relevant instances has a very low prevalence. In this work we consider that the relevant documents are organized into groups that determine the importance of every document in the collection. We test our approach on the application of Technology assisted review.

title: Refining and Evaluating a Lucene based Search Tool for BaseKB Triples
abstract: Over the years, the National Institute of Standards and Technologys (NIST) Retrieval Group (RG) has been providing large test collections, common evaluation procedures, and organizing data challenge workshops to facilitate sharing of research results in search, natural language processing and related applications. The purpose of the Text Analysis Conference's Knowledge Base Population task (TAC KBP) is to fill knowledge bases from unstructured text and is tasked with mapping mentions of people, places, or things to the actual entities that they represent in a KB. Due to the vast size of such KBs, search tools are needed to explore them efficiently. This paper describes The development and evaluation of a Lucene based search tool for the BaseKB knowledge base, which contains more than a billion facts spanning over 40 million subjects and topics, such as people, places, organizations, as well as creative and artistic works. The overall objective was to improve functionality and efficiency including enhancing the format and structure of the outputted results. This paper describes how the code base and search output format was modified and refined to allow for ease of access and comprehension in future development, as well as how the original term frequencyinverse document frequency (TF IDF) method for improving the evaluation of the search outcomes was implemented and subsequently built upon to avoid issues arising due to the inherent ambiguity of certain entity names and the variability of the search tool ranking algorithm itself. The findings were that the: (i) functionality improved due to implementation of new features and results layout; (ii) type guess significantly improved search and could be implemented in future prototypes; and (iii) search speed could be further enhanced in the future through refinement of codes and through elimination of failed cases.

title: On the Use of an Intermediate Class in Boolean Crowdsourced Relevance Annotations for Learning to Rank Comments}
abstract: In many Information Retrieval tasks, the boundary between classes is not well defined, and assigning some document to a specific class may be complicated even for humans. For instance, a document which is not directly related to the user's query, may still contain relevant information. Similarly, in Question Answering, a passage may provide useful information, although it does not directly answer the question. In this scenario, an option is to define an intermediate class collecting ambiguous instances. Yet some natural questions arise: is this annotation strategy convenient? From a machine learning perspective, how should the intermediate class be treated? To answer these questions, we explored two community question answering datasets whose comments were originally annotated with three classes. We re annotated a subset of instances considering a binary \good vs \bad setting. Our main contribution is to show empirically that the inclusion of an intermediate class to assess Boolean relevance is not useful. Moreover, in case the data is already annotated with a 3 class strategy, the instances from the intermediate class can be safely removed at training time.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks and Convolution Kernels for L2R Answers
abstract: Recent work has shown that convolution tree kernels (CTKs) and convolutional neural networks (CNNs) obtain the state of the art in answer sentence reranking. Additionally, their combination in Support Vector Machines (SVMs) is promising as it can exploit the structural syntactic properties captured by CTK in synergy with the representation layers learned by CNNs. However, such layers are constructed according to a classification function, which is not directly exploitable in the preference ranking algorithm of SVMs. In this work, we define a new learning algorithm combining ranking with CTKs along with classification with CNNs. Our experiments on two well known and rather different datasets, WikiQA for answer sentence selection and SemEval Community Question Answering for comment selection, clearly show the benefit of our approach.

title: Semantically Enriched Markov Random Field Retrieval Model
abstract: Although retrieval models based on Markov Random Fields, such as Sequential Dependence Model (SDM), relax the bag of words assumption of standard probabilistic or language modeling based retrieval models by taking into account term dependencies in the form of bigrams, they do not address the vocabulary gap between queries and documents. In this paper, we presents Semantically Enriched Markov Random Field Retrieval Model, which addresses the vocabulary gap in retrieval models based on Markov Random Fields by incorporating semantically related terms based on distributed term representations (i.e. word embeddings). We adopt word embeddings to capture the semantic relationships between words, which is used to fill the vocabulary gap between query and collection documents, as well as to weigh unigrams and bigrams in SDM. Experiments on publicly available datasets demonstrate statistically significant improvement of our proposed method over state of the art baselines.

title: Theoretical Analysis of Interdependent Constraints in Pseudo Relevance Feedback
abstract: Axiomatic analysis is a well defined theoretical framework for analytical evaluation of information retrieval models. In axiomatic analysis, it is assumed that the constraints (axioms) are independent. In this paper, we revisit this assumption and hypothesize that there might be an interdependence relationship between the existing constraints. As a preliminary study, we focus on the pseudo relevance feedback (PRF) models that have been theoretically studied using the axiomatic analysis approach. In this paper, we introduce two novel interdependent PRF constraints which emphasize on the effect of existing constraints on each other. We further modify two state of the art PRF models, the log logistic and the relevance models, in order to satisfy the proposed constraints. Experiments on three TREC newswire and web collections demonstrate that the proposed modifications significantly outperform the baselines, in all cases.

title: Optimal parameter tuning for Microblog summarization
abstract: Summarizing microblogs is a non trivial task. In this paper we present a summarization system which filters Twitter feed based upon the user's information need. The system generates topic wise relevant and novel tweet summary or email digest which essentially summarizes the topic for a day. We use language models to design a summarization system where selection of smoothing techniques is critical. We studied the behaviour of parameters lambda and mu for JM smoothing and Dirichlet smoothing respectively. It was observed that expansion of the query is adversary affecting the result. The evaluation metrics nDCG@10 1 and nDCG@10 0 were used in this study.

title: The Dilution/Concentration Conditions for CLIR models
abstract: Inspired by the work in monolingual settings, we introduce in this paper the Dilution/Concentration (D/C) conditions to characterize good CLIR models from a theoretical perspective, based on direct intuitions under articial settings. The conditions, derived from rst principles in CLIR, generalize the idea of query structuring approach and, moreover, can be employed to direct the development of ecient CLIR models. We review state of the art CLIR models w.r.t. the conditions and conduct a series of experiments which conrm our theoretical development.

title: Automatic Catchphrase Identification from Legal Court Cases
abstract: Catchphrase identification from legal court documents is an important problem which has not been extensively studied. In this paper, we make an initial attempt to solve this problem. We propose a simple, unsupervised approach for extraction of catchphrases from real life court documents. We see that noun phrases or unigrams containing legal terms produce superior performance in MAP over a supervised state of the art baseline, when compared with ground truth catchphrases created by legal experts.

title: Exploration de traits pour la reconnaissance d'entites nommees du Francais par apprentissage automatique
abstract: Dans cet article, nous explorons divers traits proposes dans la litterature afin de fournir un detecteur d'entites nommees pour le Francais appris automatiquement sur le French Treebank. Nous etudions l'integration de connaissances en domaine, l'apport de la classification des verbes, la gestion des mots inconnus et l'integration de traits non locaux.
