Our work falls into this group, although certain ML methods (hybrid approach) play an important role in the process of evaluating our lexicons. The advantage of the lexicon based approaches is that the predictions of sentiment values (or class in case of classification) can be justified in terms of the number of sentiments bearing words, and thus fall into the category of explainable AI. However, many previous studies create general sentiment lexicons manually by extracting only adjectives from a text and assign a semantic orientation to the corresponding words. This makes the lexicon generation process laborious and time consuming. Also, the application of sentiment analysis is rapidly increasing to different domains, it is impractical to create a sentiment lexicon manually for every domain. Almatarneh et al., (2017) developed a method for automatically constructing sentiment lexicons using only two part of speech categories: adjectives and adverbs. The work of V.S. Subrahmanian et al. (2008) shows that the combination of adjective, verb and adverb increases the performance of the sentiment analysis task. Our work aims to develop a domain agnostic approach that automatically generates domain specific sentiment lexicon from any text associated with ratings (e.g., IMDB review). In addition, the approach creates sentiment lexicons from different combination of part of speech as shown in Table 1. The average accuracy results (MAE) among the different setting show that the combination of Adjective, Adverb and Verb has both higher performance in terms of mean absolute error (MAE), equal to 1.27, and a smaller number of lexicon entries. In the full paper, we will provide more details, including how we deal with less frequent words, which should obviously not appear in the lexicon, how the predictions are rescaled to minimize the error and provide a detailed report of the results. We have compared our approach with the automatic approach by Almatarneh et al., (2017), and ours has shown improved performance.

title: Aspect based sentiment analysis of conference review forms with LD enabled review criteria
abstract: Conference (or journal) review forms represent a particular kind of sentiment bearing documents, which has been to date left largely unexplored. Leveraging on the recent tendency towards open reviewing, as well as through collaboration with conference PC members and chairs, we obtained a multipart review corpus including a subset or a whole of anonymized conference reviews from four conferences. Furthermore, by a thorough manual analysis of the review forms and guidelines of eleven conferences (all from the semantic technology field, such as ISWC, ESWC, EKAW, K CAP, SEMANTiCS, etc.), we identified a set of generic review criteria (or, metrics), which we used as aspects in aspect based sentiment analysis of the review form texts. As a side activity, we also designed a provisional RDF ontology containing review related concepts such as ReviewMetrics, ReviewForm and ReviewFormField,and expressed the proposed set of aspects in RDF as instances of ReviewMetrics. The review form fields of a specific conference can be mapped on the generic aspects through a web application. A sentiment lexicon was then created specifically for the domain of conference paper reviews. A dictionary based sentiment lexicon analysis method was implemented and applied to a set of reviews from three different conferences. The first step of the lexicon construction method was the manual definition of a two level taxonomy, where the 1st level were the review criteria names and the 2nd level were 2 7 other terms: either synonyms of the review criteria or other obvious terms judged highly probable to appear in the respective portion of the review. In the second phase, noun phrases observed as frequently appearing in the given portions of the review, as well as frequent adjectives (as another typical sentiment ingredient), were automatically collected. 57 new terms were added to the lexicon in the second phase (a few other were removed via manual validation of the taxonomy). The results were then evaluated by comparing the numerical scores estimated by the algorithm with the numerical scores from the reviews. The outcome was then explored further by inspecting the accuracy of criterion identification and sentiment analysis on a sentence level. The precision of criterion identification was evaluated at 57.38% and the recall at 53.44%. As such, the error rate is quite high, however even the annotators had a substantial level of disagreement, initially diverging in their criterion labeling in over a third of the comments. This suggests that reconstructing the intended meaning of the review comments is a particularly difficult task even for human annotators. As regards the sentiment polarity, it was correct in over 75% of cases. This is an improvement on the result of a similar sentiment analysis carried out in a comparable study with focus on peer reviews of scientific publications, by Bucur et al. (from K CAP19). Their analysis algorithm only managed to reach an accuracy level of about 73% even though the sentiment analysis was not aspect based, which presumably made determining the sentiment easier. In particular, we observed that the polarity for a particular aspect expressed in a sentence may differ from the overall polarity of that sentence, provided the sentence covers multiple aspects of the review. Our algorithm is capable of being substantially improved when given the availability of a significantly larger dataset. This could help put together both a better aspect expression dictionary and a vast sentiment lexicon, the creation of which would heavily rely on the frequency of terms across reviews. Additionally, should a larger dataset be available, it would be possible to perform a more detailed exploration of the specifics of the language used in similar data, creating a more complex algorithm using the discovered knowledge. Another possible way to improve the results would be to put together specialized rules for the different criteria. For example, as comments about the presentation criterion often lead to false positives matches on other criteria, it would be possible to create a rule where criteria expression found in a sentence where there is also a match on presentation would be discarded. While there is already a two fold relationship between linked data and the presented research (the aspects are modeled via an RDF ontology and data, and the experiments were carried out on data from semantic technology conferences), the exploitation of linguistic LOD has not yet been tried. A very preliminary review of available LLOD resources indicates that those addressing sentiment analysis are often biased toward emotion analysis. The lexica developed in the project could possibly give rise to a complementary resource, which would rather target the sentiment (or, assessment polarity) expressed in a relatively emotion free and more rigorous language, as typically used in scientific reviews.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Hausa Tweets using English Translated Benchmark Sentiment Lexicon
abstract: Background: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is the identification and collection of peoples opinions conveyed in a text. SA is currently one of the most researched areas in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This is due to the continued need to identify and understand peoples opinions. The social media and the advancements in web technologies, beginning with the development of web 2.0 brought about research in SA. Early studies in SA are generally focused on basic classification of documents into positive, negative or neutral sentiments [1]. However, in later studies, more refined SA approaches were proposed focusing on the sentiment of individual aspects in the texts and the strength of the sentiments [2]. In recent studies, several applications of sentiment analysis have been explored. Notably, political prediction [3], disaster management [4], tourism [5], and healthcare management [6]. Purpose: Despite the numerous benefits of the SA, there are insufficient methods and very few studies on SA in many low resources languages. Most of the existing studies are on high resources languages, predominantly the English language. Hausa language is one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa. It has over 150 million speakers and is predominantly used in Northern Nigeria, Niger Republic, Chad, and many other West African countries. Yet, no available resources for sentiment analysis in Hausa language. Wan [7] proposed cross lingual sentiment analysis (CLSA) for low resource language. However, the success of the approach rely on an intermediary machine translation system between the two languages. In a similar study, Saif M. Mohammad et al. [8] have shown that Arabic sentiment analysis using automatically translated English sentiment lexicons produces good accuracy. Sentiment lexicon is one of the most important resources for sentiment analysis. It is a dictionary of sentiment bearing words together with their sentiment values. The lexicon can be used to classify texts into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments based on the sentiment words the text contains. This method of sentiment analysis is called the lexicon based sentiment analysis. Another method of sentiment analysis is the machine learning based SA where popular machine learning algorithms are trained to classify the text. Our work focused on lexicon based sentiment analysis using English translated sentiment lexicons. To this effect, we automatically translate sentiment lexicon from three widely use English sentiment lexicon. We also develop the first manually annotated sentiment corpus for Hausa language from social media

title: Towards Neural Schema Alignment for OpenStreetMap and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is one of the richest openly available sources of volunteered geographic information. Although OSM includes various geographical entities, their descriptions are highly heterogeneous, incomplete, and do not follow any well defined ontology. Knowledge graphs can potentially provide valuable semantic information to enrich OSM entities. However, interlinking OSM entities with knowledge graphs is inherently difficult due to the large, heterogeneous, ambiguous and flat OSM schema and the annotation sparsity. This paper tackles the alignment of OSM tags with the corresponding knowledge graph classes holistically by jointly considering the schema and instance layers. We propose a novel neural architecture that capitalizes upon a shared latent space for tag to class alignment created using linked entities in OSM and knowledge graphs. Our experiments performed to align OSM datasets for several countries with two of the most prominent openly available knowledge graphs, namely, Wikidata and DBpedia, demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the state of the art schema alignment baselines by up to 53 percentage points in terms of F1 score. The resulting alignment facilitates new semantic annotations for over 10 million OSM entities worldwide, which is more than a 400\% increase compared to the existing semantic annotations in OSM.

title: Reasoning Subevent Relation over Heterogeneous Event Graph
abstract: Subevent relation identification (SRI) is a challenging natural language processing task of great value for knowledge acquisition and reasoning. Given an event pair, previous work mainly defines SRI as a classification task and usually rely on hand crafted features extracted from a limited context. However, there are lots of evidence information in external knowledge bases which are not well explored by prior work but helpful for this task. To fill this gap, we propose to reason the subevent relation based on plentiful evidence information in addition to limited context features. Specifically, we notice that evidence information together with the input event pair can be organized into a heterogeneous event graph, which comprises various types of event relations. To facilitate this, we present a heterogeneous graph attention model with mix hop reasoning mechanism to reason subevent relation over heterogeneous event graph. In particular, our model allows nodes to capture more extensive and intact event knowledge by mixing feature representations of neighbors at multiple distances to aggregate information from diverse types of neighbors. Moreover, to explicitly model the hierarchical relations between event pairs and to improve the model consistency, we devise a novel hierarchy loss function for the proposed model. Our model is evaluated on two annotated datasets with subevent hierarchies: SeRI and HiEve. Experimental results show that our approach can outperform state of the art baseline methods. Further evaluation suggests that reasoning paths in the heterogeneous graph can regard as a reasonable explanation for the prediction result.

title: Out of Vocabulary Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Web Person Name Disambiguation
abstract: Web Person Name Disambiguation (WPND) is to group web pages according the individuals they refer to. It is particularly useful in Information Retrieval (IR) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Most state of the art systems use the Vector Space Model and clustering methods. However, these systems do not perform well in text information extraction and cross text association. In this paper, we explore the use of Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs) with out of vocabulary (OOV) triples to solve the problem of WPND. We propose a novel KGE model named TransOOV, which projects KGE in the word vector space and represents the uncertainty of OOV entities and relations by multidimensional Gaussian distribution. It fully utilizes and structurally understands semantic information. The main idea is to combine defined triples provided by external Knowledge Graphs (KGs) with OOV triples extracted from unstructured text for TransOOV training. Then, we define the similarity calculation and clustering methods. We validate our model with the state of the art systems on WePS datasets. The results show that our model is superior to the baselines. In addition, compared with other KGE models, TransOOV solves the problem of embedding OOV triples into KGs, and achieves the best results on WPND, OOV link prediction and triple classification.

title: WikiCSSH: Extracting and Evaluating Computer Science Subject Headings from Wikipedia
abstract: Hierarchical domain specic classication schemas (or subject heading vocabularies) are often used to identify, classify, and disambiguate concepts that occur in scholarly articles. In this work, we develop, apply, and evaluate a human in the loop work ow that first extracts an initial category tree from crowd sourced Wikipedia data, and then combines community detection, machine learning, and hand crafted heuristics or rules to prune the initial tree. This work resulted in WikiCSSH; a large scale, hierarchically organized vocabulary for the domain of computer science (CS). Our evaluation suggests that WikiCSSH outperforms alternative CS vocabularies in terms of vocabulary size as well as the performance of lexicon based key phrase extraction from scholarly data. WikiCSSH can further distinguish between coarse grained versus fine grained CS concepts. The outlined work ow can serve as a template for building hierarchically organized subject heading vocabularies for other domains that are covered in Wikipedia.

title: Can we assess research using open scientific knowledge graphs? A case study within the Italian National Scientific Qualification
abstract: The need for open scientific knowledge graphs is ever increasing. While there are large repositories of open access articles and free publication indexes, there are still few free knowledge graphs exposing citation networks, and often their coverage is partial. Consequently, most evaluation processes based on citation counts rely on commercial citation databases. Things are changing thanks to the Initiative for Open Citations (I4OC, https://i4oc.org) and the Initiative for Open Abstracts (I4OA, https://i4oa.org), whose goal is to campaign for scholarly publishers to open the reference lists and the other metadata of their articles. This paper investigates the growth of the open bibliographic metadata and open citations in two scientific knowledge graphs, OpenCitations COCI and Crossref, with an experiment on the Italian National Scientific Qualification (NSQ), the National process for University Professor qualification which uses data from commercial indexes. We simulated the procedure by only using such open data and explored similarities and differences with the official results. The outcomes of the experiment show that the amount of open bibliographic metadata and open citation data currently available in the two scientific knowledge graphs adopted is not yet enough for obtaining results similar to those provided using commercial databases.

title: Frame Semantics for Social NLP in Italian: Analyzing Responsibility Framing in Femicide News Reports
abstract: We propose using a FrameNet based approach for analyzing how socially relevant events are framed in media discourses. Taking femicides as an example, we per form a preliminary investigation on a large dataset of news reports and event data covering recent femicides in Italy. First, we revisit the EVALITA 2011 shared task on Italian frame labeling, and test a recent multilingual frame semantic parser against this benchmark. Then, we experiment with specializing this model for Italian and perform a human evaluation to test our models real world applicability. We show how FrameNet based analyses can help to identify linguistic constructions that background the agentivity and responsibility of femicide perpetrators in Italian news.

title: Supervised learning approach for section title detection in PDF scientific articles
abstract: The majority of scientific articles is available in Portable Document Format (PDF). Although PDF format has the advantage of preserving layout across platforms it does not maintain the original metadata structure, making it difficult further text processing. Despite different layouts, depending on the applied template, articles have a hierarchical structure and are divided into sections, which represent topics of specific subjects, such as methodology and results. Hence, section segmentation serves as an important step for a contextualized text processing of scientific articles. Therefore, this work applies binary classification, a supervised learning task, for section title detection in PDF scientific articles. To train the classifiers, a large dataset (more than 5 millions samples from 7,302 articles) was created through an automated feature extraction approach, comprised by 17 features, where 4 were introduced in this work. Training and testing were made for ten different classifiers for which the best F1 score reached 0.94. Finally, we evaluated our results against CERMINE, an open source system that extracts metadata from scientific articles, having an absolute improvement in section detection of 0.19 in F1 score.

title: Abjad Numerals Recognition in Medieval Arabic Mathematical Texts based on Bi directional LSTM CRF Model
abstract: Abjad numerals, also called hisab al jumal, is a numeral system based on the twenty eight letters of Arabic. In ancient Arabic mathematics, all problems and solutions sentences were completely expressed in natural language. There was no mathematical symbolism. This is the first algorithmic approach that explore the use of a Bi directional Long Short Term Memory (Bi LSTM) network with a conditional random field (CRF) layer to automatically analyze and recognize Abjad numerals in mathematical expression in medieval Arabic mathematical texts. Since that the numerological calculation of hisab al jumal contain no ambiguity, we also translate hisab al jumal terms detected in the previous step which written out in natural language to modern numeral system. Experimental results on the Hj Tagged Corpus demonstrate that the proposed methods is efficient in correctly classifying mathematical components (such as numerical constants, hisab al jumal numbers, mathematical operation..etc), where it achieves an F1 score of 98.1%.

title: Pedestrian safety analysis using Time Petri Nets and Non monotonic Logic: Theoretical Foundations
abstract: In this article we attempt to analyze the accident risk of crossing pedestrians. For this purpose, we develop a Petri nets model for the vehicle pedestrian infrastructure interaction. The proposed Petri nets model is then translated into non monotonic logic using a fragment of the normal theory of defaults logic theory. Thus, knowing if a state can be reached in the accessibility graph of the associated Petri net, will be expressed by a non monotonic proof process derived from defaults logic theory. The risk of pedestrian crossing behavior is modeled from some crossing scenario. The effects of spaces per ception and behaviors' temporality, on their risk of crossing were analyzed using Time Petri Nets. Thus, the Petri temporal model translation to defaults logic is given to allow the formal pedestrians' safety analysis.

title: A Reinforcement Learning based Stabilization Module for Airplane Flight with Q Learning
abstract: In recent years, there have been many advances in the field of reinforcement learning (RL). RL algorithms have achieved human master abilities in games such as go, chess, etc. The capabilities of RL algorithms have also now been tested in the automated transportation field for self driving cars. In this paper we apply reinforcement learning models to simulated airplane flight. In particular, we develop and test a reinforcement learning based methodology for airplane stabilization. In essence, through reward functions and Q learning based modeling, we analyze and evaluate how a simulated Cessna 172 can learn to stabilize itself while in flight. Our results show that, after training, the airplane learns to maintain a stable course and attitude. We perform the analysis on X plane 11 which is a realistic flight simulator. Results of the analysis are presented and discussed.

title: The importance of signal pre processing for machine learning: The influence of Data scaling on a driver identification classification problem
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms have overtaken the attention of the scientific community for their important capabilities and their over the top results. However, the excessive focus on hyperparameters and the models architectures made the pre processing step often neglected. In spite of its importance, it represented a weak point for most of the machine learning applications as well as a blind spot in many research studies. In this paper, we will demonstrate through a CAN Bus vehicle data based driver identification case study, the importance of testing the use of different methods of data scaling and normalization while demonstrating their role in improving the performance of several Machine Learning algorithms.

title: How knowledge driven class generalization affects classical machine learning algorithms for mono label supervised classification
abstract: Beyond class imbalance and the sample size per class, this research paper studies the effect of knowledge driven class generalization on the accuracy of classical machine learning algorithms for mono label classification. We apply our analysis on five classical machine learning models (Perception, Support Vectors, Random Forest, K nearest neighbors, and Decision Tree) to classify a set of animal image files generated from Wikimedia Commons, a large scale repository of free images. Thanks to our analysis, we found that the accuracy rates of mono label classification models, mainly Support Vectors and K nearest neighbors, are affected by class generalization. The increasing or decreasing behavior of accuracy rates is driven by the settings of the classification categories and the generalization. The analysis of class generalization should be useful to understand the limitations of classical machine learning algorithms and to fuel debates about the improvement of classical models and supervised classification evaluation methods within the framework of Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

title: Learning Activity Matters When Gamifying It
abstract: Motivational affordances used in gamification can enhance the motivation of a learner by increasing the perceived value of the activity. However, such an effect is dependent upon the level of pre existing motivation towards the learning activity and on the persons view of these affordances as interesting or valuable. Therefore, it is necessary to create methods that can make the decisions for gamifying learning more systematic. In this context, this paper is examining the suitability of the Expectancy Value Cost Scale as an instrument for estimating the potential motivational value towards a learning activity, which can make the targeted effects of its gamification more predictable.

title: Automatic Searching of Deep Neural Networks for Medical Imaging Diagnostic
abstract: Medical imaging diagnosis is the most assisted method to help physicians diagnose patient diseases using different imaging test modalities. But Imbalanced data is one of the biggest challenges in the field of medical imaging. To advance this field, this work proposes a framework that can be used to find the optimal DNN architectures for a database with the challenge of imbalanced datasets. In our paper, we present an open source framework for automatic deep neural network search for medical imaging diagnosis.

title: Optimization of Electronically Scanned Conformal Conical Antenna Array Synthesis Using Artificial Neural Network Algorithm
abstract: Studying of mechanically steerable antennas has been considered the subject of feature research. To decrease the cost of the mechanical system and to enhance the steering potentials of the radar applications, we suggest renewing any mechanical antenna components with an electronically controlled 3D or Conformal Conical Antennas arrays. 3D antenna arrays can be readily fabricated with existing manufacturing technologies and offer considerable interests in terms of the 3 D steerable radiation beam, size, directivity, HPBW, and SLL reduction. In this paper, we have elaborated the neural networks method based beamforming that will be employed to the array pattern synthesis for three dimensional (3D) Conformal Conical Antenna arrays. This procedure authorizes to model and to optimize the antenna arrays system, by acting on various parameters of the array and taking into account planned general criteria. The goal is then to develop a feedforward neural network with supervised learning that approximates the following array patterns function. It explains how to introduce the basic principles of artificial neural network (ANN), some fundamental networks are examined in detail for their ability to solve simple pattern synthesis problem in conical antenna arrays. This fact increases the complexity of the problem under consideration and fitting the neural network models, such as training function, architecture, and parameter that would improve and result in more accuracy about input output relations. Then, the used neural technique showed its effectiveness in improving performance using the identified conformal conical isotropic antenna arrays

title: Improved chemical reaction optimization for distributed flexible job shop problem with transportation times
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a variant of the Distributed Flexible Job shop Scheduling Problem in which they introduced the transportation time as an additional constraint. The Distributed Flexible Job shop Scheduling Problem with transportation times (DFJSPT), that we study in this work, consists on each operation can be executed on one of the available machines and this in a set of geographically distributed factories. Each factory has a set of machines on which a set of jobs must be executed and the transport of jobs between machines is made by one or several transport robots. The DFJSPT combine three NP Hard problems: The problem of assigning jobs to machines, the distribution problem of jobs to factories and the robot routing problem. In this paper, we study the DFJSPT with a single robot in each factory and we propose an improved chemical reaction optimization metaheuristic to solve it in order to minimize the makespan. We tested our approach on two different categories of instances that we designed on purpose, the first category is composed of instances of flexible job shop scheduling problem with transportation times to which we have integrated the constraints of jobs distribution between factories, the second category is composed of instances of distributed and flexible job shop scheduling problem to which we have integrated the constraints of Transportation times.

title: what can do a deep learning based approach on sentiment analysis?
abstract: In recent years, online video content has gained a lot of popularity and exponential growth. Thus, understanding the Quality of Experience (QoE) perceived by end users of video streaming services is crucial for both network operators and service providers. However, it is not trivial to ensure an adequate QoE because QoE is multidisciplinary. Thus, user experience is affected by various influencing factors (e.g., context factors, human factors, and system factors), and it is still challenging to identify the QoE key influencing factors. To address these challenges, we focused on improving the performance of QoE estimation models by exploiting valuable human and context information (users comments provide important information). In this paper, we employ the Long Short Term Memory algorithm to process users comments and classify them into a negative and positive comments. Specific features from the application level, user level, and context level are fed into the convolutional neural network and artificial neural network for further processing to estimate QoE. The proposed approach is evaluated with standard evaluation metrics, such as accuracy and loss.

title: An Exact Algorithm for A Multi Period Inventory Routing Problem with Lateral Transshipment
abstract: In a supply chain, inventory is the main source of costs for a company. The idea of reducing logistics costs is therefore to control inventory costs, which are essentially the inventory holding cost and the transportation cost. One of the most used models to solve these two problems jointly is the Inventory Routing Problem (IRP), which will be the subject of this study. This paper deals with the case of a deterministic demand from a set of customers to a single supplier with a single vehicle that will be used to replenish them for a single product type over a finite planning horizon. Our paper will first analyse the impact of increasing supplier lead times on network costs. Then, we will study the effects of using the lateral transshipment (LT) technique on the overall network cost. In this paper, we developed a mathematical model and solved it by an exact method. The obtained results will show that LT is an effective tool capable of improving the total network cost and balancing the customers' inventory level.

title: Traffic Sign Recognition approach based on Haar Cascade and Deep learning
abstract: Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) systems can instantly assists drivers directly or through Automated Driving Systems (ADS) to improve the driving process and to avoid road accidents, which are incremental and dangerous for human life. In order to develop a TSR system, various methods can be used, first, based on detecting and extracting the candidate regions of the road sign and then classify them according to their predefined classes. The challenge of TSR system is to recognize road signs with the highest possible accuracy and the shortest processing time. In this paper, we first study different Traffic Sign Detection and Traffic Sign Classification methods aiming to choose the best ones in terms of accuracy. Then, we propose a new real time approach, based on Haar like Cascade technique for the detection step and on a deep learning model (which we called DeepSL) for the classification step. In order to validate the efficiency of our pipeline, we choose speed limit road signs images from the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset to achieve real tests. Obtained results show a good acceptable accuracy rate (95%) after two training time for the recognition of speed limit road signs.

title: A comparative study on the importance of each face part in facial gender recognition via convolutional neural networks
abstract: Nowadays, gender recognition systems are very important in several fields such as security, human machine interaction, surveillance and targeted advertising. However, many factors, such as makeup and disguise, can affect recognition and extend the processing time. Our research revolves around this issue. This is a comparative experimental study of the significance of each part of the face (eyes, mouth, nose) in the gender facial recognition via convolutional neural networks (CNN). As a first step our goal is to find the most crucial part of the face in order to determine the most important part in the gender recognition. The used method was tested on the UTKFace dataset and the preliminary results confirm that the eyes contain the most discriminating information regarding gender identification. We achieve a classification accuracy of 92% for eyes, 91% for mouth and 89% for nose. Then we propose a second study on the degree of importance of the eyes for both genders by training the system using only eyes. We achieve a classification accuracy of 99% for eyes of men and 99% for eyes of women.

title: The impact of Weather and Panel characteristics Features on Photo voltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: Solar energy intermittency is causing an enormous problem in smart grid management, the energy needed is not always meet due to the unequal dispatchability during the day. So, accurate solar energy forecasting becomes a necessity to satisfy the demand. During this work, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was deployed within brute force search algorithm to pick the category (categories) of features that fit the model accurately using data generated from photo voltaic (PV) plants installed in Eugene, Oregon within weather data of the same location. Several combinations were tested and evaluated using two error measures to conclude that plane of array irradiance and predetermined panel characteristics are the most effective features to attain good accuracy.

title: Agent Architecture for Pedestrian's Crowd in Public Places: Combination of Individual and Cooperative Reasoning
abstract: A major problem in a crowd evacuation is rescuing frightened and trapped people. This paper presents a decision making process based on a combination of individual and social cooperative reasoning to evacuate people during a crowd evacuation. Specifically, we propose to evacuate crowds by modeling the social cooperative behaviors of multi agent systems. In this context, cooperative reasoning contributes to the collaboration between agents to find missing data in a multi variable environment. Cooperative reasoning allows agents to exchange information and reach an agreement in order to exit quickly and safely. Experimental results showed that cooperative reasoning combined with individual reasoning has a great impact on final decision and can lead to a successful evacuation with a percentage of 90.

title: Verbal Aggressions Detection in Mexican Tweets
abstract: Verbal aggressions are a struggle that a great number of social media users have to face daily. Some users take advantage of the anonymity that social media give them and offend a person, a group of people, or a concept. The majority of proposals which pretend to detect aggressive comments on social media handle it as a classification problem. Although there are a lot of techniques to face this problem in English, there are a lack of proposals in Spanish. In this work, we proposed to use several Spanish lexicons which have a collection of words that have been weighted according to different criteria like affective, dimensional, and emotional values. In addition to them, estructural values, word embeddings and one hot codification were taken into account. The combination of these features proved to be a novel proposal because competitive scores were obtained when this model was applied over a dataset which contains Mexican Spanish tweets that are labeled as aggressive and non aggressive.

title: Co Comment Network: A novel approach to construct social networks within Reddit
abstract: This work analyzes the online Reddit comment posts and proposes a novel approach to construct a social network automatically within Reddit that connects users of it. The investigation reveals that users tend to form links to others who have a mutual interest in interacting with some topics or posts. This mutual interest among users can make connections among them in the network. This study shows that Reddit contains a large, strongly connected core of high degree nodes, surrounded by many small clusters of low degree nodes which the authors define as the Co Comment network. One of the important research focuses is to examine whether the networks built from the Reddit comments show the desirable social network properties, e.g., power law distribution, small world effect, and clustering coefficient properties. Results obtained from the experiment confirm that the Co Comment network conforms to social network properties. The authors also discover communities within the Co Comment network and verify them to validate the constructed network.

title: Automatic Knowledge Graph Construction over Efficient Information Extraction Networks
abstract: Knowledge graph construction (KGC) aims at constructing a knowledge graph from enormous amounts of unstructured sources. Once unstructured information is stored in a graph structured format, it becomes easier to access and utilize. In this paper, we propose a automatic knowledge graph construction method based on an efficient contextual model, which is composed of layered convolutional neural networks (CNN) and attention based bidirectional LSTM layers. The model achieves similar performance compared to the RoBERTa (pre trained model) but is time conserving and is more lighter than this kind of pre trained model. In addition, we propose a framework to enrich the constructed KG with external high quality sources using relation linking. The refined KG is visualized based on Neo4j. Our experiments highlighted that our method achieved a few points of amelioration that can be readily applied to other similar domain fields.

title: Spa P Transformer: Sparse self attention model of R Sinusoidal positional encoding based on text classification
abstract: The emergence of Transformer and its derivative models brings new opportunities to tasks of NLP (Natural Language Processing). Transformer is not only a separate model, but also the core of different text task systems. Therefore, Transformer has become an important component of many powerful models, such as BERT. However, Transformer is not without defects. Researchers are still puzzled by the huge amount of computation generated in the process of self attention. Especially in long text data sets. We propose Spa R Transformer based for long text classification. Compared with Transformer, the performance and running time of Spa R Transformer have been significantly improved. In order to solve the long tail problem of attention, we first query the main attention, and then select the most important related attention to replace the overall attention according to the confidence score. At the same time, we update the positional encoding to provide relative location information for the model. In long text dataset IMDB, Spa R Transformer improves the accuracy and F1 score of Transformer by 4.5%.

title: Secure Evaluation of SPARQL Aggregate Queries over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
abstract: We focus on the setting where multiple data providers independently store knowledge graphs over some ontology. Each data providers graph may contain temporal data (e.g., timestamped smart meter consumptions) as well as sensitive personal data (e.g., age, income, number of persons in the household). We propose SEAK, a framework for Secure Evaluation of SPARQL Aggregate queries over temporal Knowledge graphs. The core ideas behind SEAK are: (1) push as much computations as possible directly in an off the shelf SPARQL query engine, which allows benefiting from the existing SPARQL features (including SPARQL star for querying timestamped data), and (2) exchange only encrypted graphs to hide the potentially sensitive data from the server performing the group by and aggregation; to this purpose, we jointly rely on several cryptographic schemes: AES, order preserving encryption, and Paillier additive homomorphic encryption. We implemented SEAK on top of Apache Jena. To show the feasibility and scalability of SEAK, we performed a large scale empirical evaluation using an RDF encoding of a real world dataset provided by the Irish Social Science Data Archive (ISSDA) Commission for Energy Regulation (CER).

title: Distributed Query Processing and Reasoning over Linked Big Data
abstract: Enormous quantities of structured and unstructured data on the Web and the need to extract and derive useful knowledge from such data make Semantic Web and Big Data Technology explorations of paramount importance. Open semantic web data created using standard protocols (RDF, RDFS, OWL) consists of billions of records in the form of data collections called ``linked data". With the ever increasing linked big data on the Web, it is imperative to process this data with powerful and scalable techniques in distributed processing environments such as MapReduce. There are several distributed RDF processing systems, including SemaGrow, FedX, SPLENDID, PigSPARQL, SHARD, SPARQLGX, that are developed over the years. However, there is a need for computational and qualitative comparison of the differences and similarities among these systems. In this paper, we extend a previous comparative analysis to a diverse study with respect to qualitative and quantitative analysis view, through experimental approach for these distributed RDF systems. We examine each of the selected RDF query systems with respect to the implementation set up, system architecture, underlying framework, and data storage of the systems. We used two widely used RDF benchmark datasets, namely LUBM and WatDiv. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance in terms of query adaptability and query processing time for different queries. The results of the experiments in this study show that SemaGrow distributed system performed more efficiently compared to FedX and Splendid, even though in smaller queries the former performed slower.

title: Recurrent Graph Convolution Network for Rumor Detection
abstract: The development of social media has provided an ideal platform for sharing information, but it has also become a hotbed for rumor posting and spreading. Existing rumor detection methods mainly look for clues from the textual content, static propagation structures. However, previous work does not fully use users' information while ignoring the dynamic change of the propagation structure. Therefore, this paper proposes a rumor detection model based on the dynamic propagation structure called Recurrent Graph Convolutional Network (Re GCN). We construct a more informative post representation based on the post's textual content and the user's information. Then, we construct a dynamically changing propagation structure representation by dividing rumor propagation into multiple stages and capture the dynamically changing propagation features by Bi Directional Recurrent Neural Networks (Bi RNN) and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). Finally, the rumors are classified by fusing the information at each stage through the attention mechanism. Experimental results on two real world datasets show that the proposed method has significant improvement compared to the state of the art benchmark methods.

title: QuatRE: Relation Aware Quaternions for Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: We propose a simple yet effective embedding model to learn quaternion embeddings for entities and relations in knowledge graphs. Our model aims to enhance correlations between head and tail entities given a relation within the Quaternion space with Hamilton product. The model achieves this goal by further associating each relation with two relation aware rotations, which are used to rotate quaternion embeddings of the head and tail entities, respectively. Experimental results show that our proposed model produces state of the art performances on well known benchmark datasets for knowledge graph completion.

title: Exploring Relevance and Coherence for Automated Text Scoring using Multi task Learning
abstract: With the explosive growth of the information on the Internet, the evaluation of the quality and credibility of web content has become more important than ever before. In this work, we focus on the quality assessment of texts. Recently, various methods have been proposed for the automated text scoring task and obtained competitive results. However, few studies have focused on both relevance and coherence, which are two important factors in evaluating text quality. To improve the scoring task, we propose two auxiliary tasks using negative sampling and integrate them into a multi task learning framework. The first auxiliary task is relevance modeling and the other one is coherence modeling. We evaluate our model on the Automated Student Assessment Prize (ASAP) dataset. Experimental results show that our model achieves higher Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) scores with an improvement of 1.5% on average.

title: Inductive Knowledge Enhanced Recommender Systems Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: In recent years there has been growing interest in exploiting knowledge graphs (KGs) for improving the accuracy, diversity, and interpretability of recommendation results. Existing recommender systems supporting KGs, however, only work in transductive settings, where predictions are only made for users and items seen during training; furthermore, existing inductive systems, which are able to make predictions involving unseen objects, do not support KGs. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that is effective in inductive settings, and which can seamlessly incorporate large scale KGs to enhance the quality of recommendations. Our results show that our system, while being more general than the baselines, is able to outperform them on the restricted cases to which the baselines are applicable.

title: Trigger GNN: A Trigger Based Graph Neural Network for Nested Named Entity Recognition
abstract: Nested named entity recognition (nested NER) aims to identify the entity boundaries and recognize categories of the named entities in a complex hierarchical sentence. Some works have been done using the character level, word level, or lexicon level methods. However, such researches ignore the role of the complementary annotations. To bridge the gap, we investigate a trigger based graph neural network (Trigger GNN) approach to leverage the nested NER. We posit that the entity triggers (one of the complementary annotations) can add in complementary supervision signals on the whole sentences and thus help the model to learn and generalize more efficiently. Experiments show that the Trigger GNN is cost effective and efficient on four public NER datasets, and it can effectively alleviate the nested NER.

title: Semantic Path Guided Graph Neural Network for Heterogeneous Graph Embedding
abstract: Heterogeneous graph embedding is to embed rich semantics and structural information of a heterogeneous graph into low dimensional node representations. Most existing methods define multiple meta paths to capture the heterogeneity and rich semantic information in the heterogeneous graph. However, it is a non trivial task to learn effective heterogeneous graph embedding for meta path based models because of three major challenges: (1) ignore node content features; (2) learn limited semantic information if the meta paths can be considered alone; (3) lack of certain explanation when assigning different weighting values for normalizing neighbors of the target node via the attention mechanism. To address these issues, we propose a novel model \underline{Sem}antic \underline{Path} Guided \underline{G}raph \underline{N}eural \underline{N}etwork (SemPathGNN) to further boost the final performance of the task. Specifically, in order to deal with node heterogeneity in the heterogeneous graph, we first leverage node content transformation to encapsulate input heterogenous node attributes. We then construct a joint sampling strategy from a semantic path based structure perspective to extract complex semantics and structural information and guide the neighbor selection in the heterogeneous graph, while a similarity based importance computation strategy is introduced to measure weighting values between the target node and its specified semantic path based neighbors. Moreover, to further generate preliminary embedding of the target node by aggregating feature messages from these semantic path based neighbors. Finally, SemPathGNN combines messages via cross semantic path based structure aggregation built upon the attention mechanism to obtain the final embedding for each node in the graph. Experiments conducted on four datasets from different domains for node classification and node clustering demonstrate that SemPathGNN achieves more accurate prediction results as compared to several state of the art baselines.

title: Enhancing Sequential Recommendation via Decoupled Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Sequential recommendation can capture dynamic interest patterns of users based on user interaction sequences. Recently, there has been interest in integrating the knowledge graph (KG) into sequential recommendation. Existing works suffer from two main challenges: a) representing each entity in the KG as a single vector can confound heterogeneous information about the entity; b) triple based facts are modeled independently, lacking the exploration of high order connectivity between entities. To solve the above challenges, we decouple the KG into two subgraphs, namely CRoss user Behavior based graph and Intrinsic Attribute based graph (Crbia), depending on the type of relation between entities. We further propose a CrbiaNet based on the two subgraphs. First, CrbiaNet obtains behavior level and attribute level semantic features from these two subgraphs independently by different graph neural networks, respectively. Then, CrbiaNet applies a sequential model incorporating these semantic features to capture dynamic preference of the users. Extensive experiments on three real world datasets show that our proposed CrbiaNet outperforms previous state of the art knowledge enhanced sequential recommendation models by a large margin consistently.

title: Relational Graph Convolutional PonderNet for Entity Classification in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Despite the vast amount of information encoded in knowledge graphs, information about the class affiliation of entities remain often incomplete. Neural networks, in particular Graph Convolutional Neural Networks, have been shown to be effective predictors to complete information about the class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs. However, these models do not learn the class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs incorporating the complexity of the task, which negatively affects the prediction capabilities of the models. To address this problem, we introduce Relational Graph Convolutional PonderNet, an end to end network that learns the prediction of class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs within a Markov process. The number of computational steps is learned during training using a geometric distribution. At the same time, the loss function combines insights from the field of evidential learning. As a result, the model generalizes to graphs of varying complexity and is thus effective in terms of both training time tailored to complexity and prediction accuracy. The experiments show a strong performance improvement over existing models. Based on the chosen hyperparameters for the geometric distribution, the expected number of computation steps can be adjusted to improve efficiency during training.

title: Neural Expert Finding
abstract: An expert finding system allows one to find individuals who have expertise in certain fields or domains. However, most of the expert finding systems, based on document based topic modeling or keyword search methods, are limited in their capability to encode contextual knowledge from natural language. This paper presents Neural Expert Finder (NEF), a novel method that explores neural models to learn contextual expert representations utilizing research interests and academic publication titles. NEF uses a transfer learning approach based on transformer encoder networks to leverage the rich semantic and syntactic patterns of language encoded in pre trained language models (PLMs). To fine tune the language models, we propose a self supervised learning approach utilizing contrastive factual text sequences formulated from raw structured data. For experimentation, we build a new benchmark dataset for expert finding named SGComp, curated from experts university and Google Scholar profiles. Our empirical evaluation methods demonstrate that the proposed method can learn effective contextual representations and identify experts most relevant to specific research areas. In addition, we utilise SGComp and three domain specific public datasets to compare NEF against ExpFinder nVSM, a state of the art (SOTA) system in expert finding and demonstrate consistent improved performance with the neural learning paradigm of NEF.

title: Predicting the Acceptability of Atomic Candidate OWL Axioms
abstract: Candidate axiom scoring is the task of assessing the acceptability of a candidate axiom against the evidence provided by known facts or data. Being able to accurately score candidate axioms is a prerequisite for automatic schema or ontology induction, but can also be useful for ontology and/or knowledge graph validation. Accurateaxiom scoring heuristics are often heavy to compute, which is a big problem if one wants to exploit them in iterative search methods like level wise generate and test or evolutionary algorithms, where large numbers of candidate axioms need to be scored. We tackle the challenge of learning a surrogate predictive model of the score of candidate axioms that is fast to execute yet accurate enough to be used in such settings. For this purpose, we leverage a semantic similarity measure extracted from the subsumption hierarchy of an ontology. We prove that the method proposed in this paper is able to learn the acceptability labels of candidate OWL axioms with high accuracy, and that it can do so for multiple types of OWL axioms.

title: KIR: A Knowledge enhanced Interpretable Recommendation Method
abstract: With the popularization of the Internet and the development of information technology, information data has shown explosive growth, and the Recommendation System (RS) is of great significance for screening effective information and improving the efficiency of information acquisition. The existing recommendation methods can improve the accuracy of the recommendation results to a certain extent, but the interpretation of the recommendation results is insufficient and difficult to satisfy the desire of some users to understand the recommendation basis due to the lack of interpretability. For this reason, the Knowledge Graph (KG) is introduced as auxiliary information of the RS and calculates the importance of entity and relation in the KG to users, and use these as the basis for the recommendation. First, item categories are introduced to enhance the impact on user preferences. Second, an Attention Mechanism (AM) is proposed to distinguish users interests in different contextual entity relation sets in the KG. Finally, multiple feature information is input into the Convolutional Neural Net work (CNN) to extract users preferences. The experimental results prove that the model has a certain improvement in the accuracy of the recommendation effect, and at the same time, it can better explain the reasons for the recommendation.

title: Handling Out Of Vocabulary words in Question Answering on Knowledge Bases
abstract: Accessing the large volumes of information available in public knowledge bases might be complicated for those users unfamiliar with the SPARQL query language. Automatic translation of questions posed in natural language in SPARQL has the potential of overcoming this problem. Existing systems based on neural machine translation are very effective but easily fail in recognizing words that are Out Of the Vocabulary (OOV) of the training set. This is a serious issue while querying large ontologies. In this paper, we combine Named Entity Linking, Named Entity Recognition, and Neural Machine Translation to perform automatic translation of natural language questions into SPARQL queries. We demonstrate empirically that our approach is more effective and resilient to OOV words than existing approaches by running the experiments on Monument, QALD 9, and LC QuAD v1, which are well known datasets for Question Answering over DBpedia.

title: A Geospatial Join Optimization for Federated GeoSPARQL querying
abstract: We present a join optimization method for federated linked geospatial data. This optimization targets within distance queries in cases where the shapes that are compared are served from different sources of the federation. This operation is computationally expensive, because it cannot be answered from the spatial index of any of the individual data sources in the federation. Our optimization augments the subqueries prepared for each source with additional restrictions on topological relations that must be satisfied and that (a) can be answered from the spatial index of the individual data sources; (b) do not change the semantics of the query. We evaluate our optimization on data and queries derived from a real world workflow over land usage data. Evaluation shows that our optimization substantially improves query processing time.

title: An Analysis of Links in Wikidata
abstract: Wikidata is becoming one of the most prominent open knowledge graphs on the Web. Relying on a community of users with different expertise, this cross domain knowledge graph is directly related to other data sources. This paper investigates how far Wikidata is connected to other sources in the Linked Data ecosystem. We adapt a previous definition of ontology and instance links to the terminological part of the Wikidata vocabulary and perform an analysis of the links in Wikidata to external datasets and ontologies from the Linked Data ecosystem. As a side effect, this reveals insights on the ontological expressiveness of meta properties used in Wikidata. The results of this analysis show to what degree Wikidata is already topologically central to the Linked Data ecosystem and how the Wikidata ontology connects and reuses existing ontologies on the Web.

title: TempCaps: A Capsule Network based Embedding Model for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs store the dynamics of entities and relations during a time period. In real world scenarios, typical temporal knowledge graphs often suffer from incomplete dynamics with missing facts. Hence, modeling temporal knowledge graphs to complete the missing facts is an important task. In this paper, we tackle the temporal knowledge graph completion task by proposing TempCaps, which is a Capsule network based embedding model for Temporal knowledge graph completion. TempCaps models temporal knowledge graphs by introducing a novel dynamic routing aggregator inspired by capsule networks. Specifically, TempCaps builds entity embeddings by dynamically routing retrieved temporal relation and neighbor information. Experimental results demonstrate that TempCaps reaches state of the art performance for temporal knowledge graph completion. Additional analysis also shows that TempCaps is efficient.

title: Knowledge Graph Entity Type Prediction with Relational Aggregation Graph Attention Network
abstract: Most of the knowledge graph completion methods focus on inferring missing entities or relations between entities in the knowledge graphs. However, many knowledge graphs are missing entity types. The goal of entity type prediction in the knowledge graph is to infer the missing entity types that belong to entities in the knowledge graph, that is, (entity,entity type=?). At present, most knowledge graph entity type prediction models tend to model entities and entity types, which will cause the relations between entities to not be effectively used, and the relations often contain rich semantic information. To utilize semantic information contained in the relation when performing entity type prediction, we propose a method for entity type prediction based on relational aggregation graph attention network (RACE2T), which consists of an encoder relational aggregation graph attention network (FRGAT) and a decoder (CE2T). The encoder FRGAT uses the scoring function of the knowledge graph completion method to calculate the attention coefficient between the entities and the relation entity pairs in its neighborhood. This attention coefficient will be used to aggregate the information of relations and entities in the neighborhood of the entity to exploit the information of the relations. The decoder CE2T is designed based on convolutional neural network, which models the entity embeddings output by FRGAT and entity type embeddings, and performs entity type prediction. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper is superior to state of the art methods.

title: Union and Intersection of all Justifications
abstract: We present new algorithms for computing the union and intersection of all justifications for a given ontological consequence without first computing the set of all justifications. Our goal is to use these sets to explain the consequences and, if needed, repair them. Through an empirical evaluation, we show that our approach behaves well in practice for expressive description logics. In particular, the union of all justifications can be computed much faster than with existing justification enumeration approaches.

title: Exploring the impact of literal transformations within Knowledge Graphs for Link Prediction
abstract: Knowledge graphs encode knowledge relevant for many applications, but in many cases they are inherently incomplete. Thus, Link Prediction methods have been proposed to infer new triples in order to complete a given Knowledge Graph. Usually, such Link Prediction methods ignore literals in spite of the fact that literals can express useful information about entities not encoded in relations. The existing methods that do incorporate literal information (e.g. LiteralE) do so by modifying the model and loss function. However, it would be desirable if any link prediction method could use literals. Thus, we propose a new approach that relies on graph transformations which transform literals in such a way that existing Link Prediction algorithms can leverage the literal information. In particular, we define three transformations and evaluate them in comparison to the state of the art approaches. In most cases, the additional triples induced by our transformations lead to a performance increase and even state of the art performance can be reached when comparing against LiteralE. Our approach can be seen as a new baseline for encoding literal information into relational triples for Link Prediction.

title: RDFtex: Knowledge Exchange between LaTeX based Research Publications and Scientific Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SciKGs) aim to integrate scientific knowledge in a machine readable manner. For populating SciKGs, research publications pose a central source of scientific knowledge. Hence, the goal is to represent both contextual information, i.e., metadata, and contentual information, i.e., original contributions like definitions and experimental results, of research publications in SciKGs. However, typical forms of research publications like the traditional papers cannot be easily integrated into SciKGs. Furthermore, they do not support making direct use of the rich information SciKGs provide. To tackle this, the present paper proposes RDFtex, a framework that enables (1) the import of contributions represented in SciKGs to facilitate the preparation of LaTeX based research publications and (2) the export of original contributions to facilitate their integration into SciKGs. We demonstrate the frameworks functionality using the example of the present paper itself since it was prepared with RDFtex and its currently implemented features.

title: Deep Correlation based Concept Recommendation for MOOCs
abstract: The current course recommendation in massive open online courses (MOOCs) usually ignores students interests in some certain type of knowledge concepts, resulting in low completion of most courses. Therefore, it requires a concept recommendation to help students accurately choose courses in MOOCs. In this paper, we propose Deep Correlation based Concept Recommendation (DCCR) for MOOCs. It gathers the interactive information obtained by different entities through meta paths in MOOCs and extracts the semantic information of knowledge concepts. To deeply capture the correlation information among users, a multi relation graph is built to generate the correlation features which aggregates the abundant information under different meta paths. Then through the graph convolutional neural networks, entity embeddings of users and knowledge concepts are generated. Additionally, a novel fusion function is designed to get the final joint representations reasonably. By verifying on two public datasets, experiments show that DCCR outperforms the state of the art methods.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Refinement Operators in ALC
abstract: Refinement operators have been successfully applied to class expression learning on RDF knowledge graphs. However, state of the art models based on refinement operators often have to explore a large number of class expressions to find an adequate solution for a given learning problem. Arguably, the reliance of state of the art models on myopic heuristic functions contributes to this limitation. In contrast, deep reinforcement learning provides effective means to address myopia by estimating discounted cumulative future rewards. In this work, we leverage deep reinforcement learning to accelerate class expression learning in ALC by proposing DRILL a novel class expression learning approach that uses a convolutional deep Q learning model to steer its search. We evaluate DRILL on 4 benchmark datasets by using 390 learning problems. Our experiments suggest that DRILL converges to goal states at least 2.7 times faster than state of the art models on all learning problems. The results of our statistical significance test confirms that DRILL converges to goal states significantly faster (p value <1%) than state of the art models on all benchmark datasets. To foster reproducible research, we provide an open source implementation of DRILL, including pretrained models, training and evaluation scripts.

title: Comparative Research in Stream Reasoning
abstract: The diverse research efforts in recent years in the area of stream reasoning (SR) led to a wide range of SR engines. However, the lack of standardization and the diverse choices in SR, e.g., tuple driven vs. time driven engines, stream level vs. graph level entailment, streaming all results vs. newly derived ones, mean that real comparability among the engines is hardly given. A first step towards achieving comparability and standardization is the RSP QL model, implemented in the RSP4J framework, which allows for describing and formalizing the semantics of SR engines. In this work, we quantify the in use importance of several key performance indicators (KPIs) and features based on the results of a survey. We then compare SR engines along these KPIs with the CityBench and the CSRBench oracle. Our analysis of SR systems shows that the two RSP4J implementations C SPARQL2.0 and YASPER outperform the well known C SPARQL implementation both in terms of performance and configurability. Our comparison against a naive SR extension of the incremental reasoning engine RDFox shows that SR engines still have potential for improvement. Only when it comes to great system loads, the SR engines stay ahead of RDFox because they start dropping input triples to prevent an overload. Finally, we propose a unifying interface for SR benchmarks meant to ease future benchmarking efforts, especially for RSP4J based engines.

title: Popularity Prediction on Online Content with Fusion of Text and Trend History SubGraph Neural Network
abstract: The popularity prediction of online contents has been an important task in many fields such as advertising, recommendation system, public opinion analysis. Most methods mainly use the own information of text, user, and trend history (TH) of online contents to predict future popularity. However, these methods ignore the relations between online contents. The relations can be taken as external factors for prediction in some degree, which is important and hard to capture. Graph neural network (GNN) is an excellent method to extract the relations. But how to construct graph as external factors and how to get the feature representation of nodes efficiently in GNN are two key problems for prediction popularity. In order to solve these problems, we propose a method named Fusion of Text and Trend SubGraph Neural Network (FTSGNN) in this paper. Firstly, text subgraphs and TH subgraphs instead of the global graph are constructed in FTSGNN. The two kinds of subgraphs are constructed with the texts and TH in each sliding window, respectively. Only online contents within the sliding window is used for constructing subgraphs, which is more efficient. Secondly, deep graph infomax (DGI), which is an unsupervised method, is introduced in FTSGNN to obtain the feature embeddings of each online context easily. Finally, these feature embeddings and TH of online contents are fused to train the model for prediction. Experiments on the Sina Weibo dataset show that FTSGNN obtains better accuracy and efficiency than the method only with TH, which improves MSE from 0.402 to 0.226 and MAPE from 0.283 to 0.242 with text and 2 hours' TH.

title: Refining Large Identity Graphs using the Unique Name Assumption
abstract: The Unique Name Assumption (UNA) supposes that two terms with distinct IRIs from the same dataset do not refer to the same real world entity. The UNA has been used to refine identity graphs: if the UNA is true, then identity links (e.g. those with relation owl:sameas) between two entities defined by the same dataset can be considered erroneous. While this works on a small scale, it has not been validated on the scale of large integrated knowledge graphs, such as the LOD cloud, which contain data from many different sources. We propose a concrete definition of the UNA with tolerance towards exceptions, namely the internal UNA (iUNA). We compare our definition with existing definitions with respect to some real world datasets. Based on the iUNA, we propose an algorithm to identify erroneous links in an identity graph of half a billion triples extracted from the LOD Cloud. The algorithm employs an SMT solver and takes advantage of the latter's ability to efficiently reason over equality and remove a minor amount of links. Finally, we demonstrate how additional information can improve the accuracy of such refinements.

title: Text Enhanced Relational Context Hyperbolic Graph Convolution Network for Link Prediction
abstract: Knowledge graph (KG) embeddings learn low dimensional representations of entities and relations and can be used for knowledge graph completion task. There exists a lot of hierarchical relations in the knowledge graph, but the hierarchical data in the knowledge graph are not well utilized. Besides, existing knowledge representation learning models lack effective utilization of entity semantic information contained in textual information of entities. Finally, the context information of relation often plays an important role in relation representation, but the existing model does not make full use of it. Therefore, we proposes a Text Enhanced Relational Context Hyperbolic Graph Convolution Network (TRHGCN) for link prediction, which makes full use of the context information of relations and text description of entities to represent the relations and entities in knowledge graph. TRHGCN model utilize the hyperbolic space, which can better excavate the hierarchical structure of the knowledge graph. Link prediction experiments are carried out on FB15K 237, WN18RR, NELL 995 dataset. The results demonstrate that TRHGCN is significantly outperforms existing state of the art methods on benchmark models such as CompGCN and ConvE, and our model performs better on hierarchical relations.

title: Supervised Knowledge Aggregation for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: We explore data driven rule aggregation based on latent feature representations in the context of knowledge graph completion. For a given query and a collection of rules obtained by a symbolic rule learning system, we propose end to end trainable aggregation functions for combining the rules into a confidence score answering the query. Despite using latent feature representations for rules, the proposed models remain fully interpretable in terms of the underlying symbolic approach. While our models improve the base learner constantly and achieve competitive results on various benchmark knowledge graphs, we outperform current state of the art with respect to a biomedical knowledge graph by a significant margin. We argue that our approach is in particular well suited for link prediction tasks dealing with a large multi relational knowledge graph with several million triples, while the queries of interest focus on only one specific target relation.

title: A Human in the Loop Approach for Personal Knowledge Graph Construction from File Names
abstract: Knowledge workers' personal and work related concepts (e.g. persons, projects, topics) are usually not sufficiently covered by knowledge graphs. Yet, already handmade classification schemes, prominently folder structures, naturally mention several of their concepts in file names. Thus, such data could be a promising source for constructing personal knowledge graphs. However, this idea poses several challenges: file names are usually noisy non grammatical text snippets, while folder structures do not clearly define how concepts relate to each other. To cope with this semantic gap, we include knowledge workers as humans in the loop to guide the building process with their feedback. Our semi automatic personal knowledge graph construction approach consists of four major stages: domain term extraction, ontology population, taxonomic and non taxonomic relation learning. Machine learning models and a rule based system immediately learn from user feedback and predict new A Box statements. We conduct four expert interviews from different domains in an industrial scenario to evaluate our approach. Results show that file systems may serve as a suitable source and, combined with our approach, already yield useful personal knowledge graphs with moderate effort spent.

title: Certainty is the easy path: expressing without asserting named graphs
abstract: Knowledge in most scholarly disciplines is characterised by diverse degrees of certainty. Asserting such statements in RDF is hindered by the correct representation of uncertain or evolving aspects (due to e.g., ignorance, changes of opinion, disagreements, challenges, etc.). In this article we examine and discuss the need and usefulness of expressing without asserting (EWA) arbitrary claims as RDF named graphs. We describe how most of the currently existing approaches (e.g., reification, n ary relationships, N3, RDF*, etc.) seem to treat non asserted statements more as a side effect, rather than a design issue on its own right, and how the semantics of RDF 1.1 named graphs does not effectively contribute to the task. We propose a solution, called Conjectures to express statements whose truth value is not specified, and therefore cannot be asserted, regardless of the semantics chosen for named graphs among the many available. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing it with prior attempts.

title: Expressive Scene Graph Generation using Commonsense Knowledge Integration for Visual Understanding and Reasoning
abstract: Scene graph generation aims to capture the semantic elements in images by modelling objects and their relationships in a structured manner, which are essential for visual understanding and reasoning tasks including image captioning, visual question answering, visual storytelling and image retrieval. The existing scene graph generation approaches provide limited performance and expressiveness for higher level visual understanding and reasoning. This challenge can be mitigated by leveraging commonsense knowledge, such as related facts and background knowledge, about the semantic elements in scene graphs. In this paper, we propose the integration of diverse commonsense knowledge about the semantic elements in scene graphs to generate rich and expressive scene graphs using a heterogeneous knowledge source that contains commonsense knowledge consolidated from seven different knowledge bases. The graph embeddings of the object nodes are used to leverage their structural patterns in the knowledge source to compute similarity metrics for graph refinement and enrichment. We performed experimental and comparative analysis on the benchmark Visual Genome dataset using the standard metric, in which the proposed method achieved a higher recall rate (R@K = 29.89, 35.4, 39.12 for K = 20, 50, 100) as compared to the existing state of the art technique (R@K = 25.8, 33.3, 37.8 for K = 20, 50, 100). The qualitative results of the proposed method in a downstream task of image generation showed that more realistic images are generated using the commonsense integrated scene graphs. These results depict the effectiveness of commonsense knowledge integration in improving the performance and expressiveness of scene graph generation for visual understanding and reasoning tasks.

title: EaT PIM: Embedding and Transforming Procedural Instructions for Modification
abstract: Cooking recipes are a type of procedural instructions, which provide a stepwise description of how to complete a task.
