title: Skin Cancer Diagnosis Enhancement through NLP and DNN based Binary Classification
abstract: In the present work we intend to enhance the diagnosis of skin cancer by applying Natural Language processing and Machine Learning techniques to a specific classification problem. Our experimentation with different architectures yielded noteworthy results over a specific corpora of medical notes. Using a BoW/TF IDF representation of the corpus and a 1 dimensional Convolutional Neural Network(CNN1D) architecture we achieved an F1 measure of 0.91.

title: Improved Sentiment Analysis Performance using Hand crafted Negation Features
abstract: The Sentiment Analysis task holds a spotlight in the NLP community. Some of the most important questions are about what features to consider when modeling the phenomenon, and, despite important advances, this question is not fully answered. This work focuses on the influence of negation for polarity detection in Spanish sentiment analysis. We extracted "negation features" from SFU ReviewSP NEG corpus, a dataset annotated with negation structures.Throughout extensive experiments, we illustrated how the usage of negation features benefit the models performance achieving state of the art results in SFU ReviewSP NEG corpus, by a simple extension of the bag of words baseline that also leverages the interpretability of negation features in the negation structures. Moreover, we include recent language model in our experiments, in order to contrast the capability of these hand crafted features versus automatic inferred features by modern deep learning models.

title: Path Planning Method for Navigation and Exploration with Drones using the 3D RRT Algorithm
abstract: . In the past few years, drone development has opened doors to new application areas giving us the chance to carry sensors onto more complex environments, such as cities and forests, in which there are proximity conditions of considerable size that could be categorized as highly dangerous. In this context, the path planning method is commonly used in robotics applications to find a valid sequence to move the drone to a target point. This method aims to find the shortest path length and obtain a safe trajectory avoiding collisions with obstacles. To achieve this objective, we present a novel path planning method for navigation and exploration with drones based on a 3D version of the RRT algorithm. The proposed algorithm developed in Python have two principal contributions, first are used a box model to encapsulate obstacles to avoid collisions and a dynamic range bias for the sampling, and, a giving orientation technique is employed on the exploration steps to reduce the number of computational operations and processing time when is obtained a valid path. Simulations results are performed to validate the algorithm using different scenarios and 3D obstacles randomly located. The results illustrated that the 3D RRT algorithm finds a valid path avoiding obstacles with benefits on computational cost and better processing time

title: Exploratory Data Analysis for the Automatic Detection of Question Paraphrasing in Collaborative Environments
abstract: Internet searches are a daily occurrence, but we must be aware that more than one person searches the same topic with different words, this is called paraphrasing. Paraphrasing involves syntactic changes and the overlapping of words, linked to the rules of the language in which we work. The identification is a problem of great importance for natural language processing (NLP), especially paraphrasing in questions with the same intention. In addition, it has been found that for the study of similarities, some features are not taken into account, which makes the identification yield lower results, by not taking into account some relationships of interest between the data. In this paper, we address the problem of automatic paraphrase identification in the Quora Question Pair (QQP) dataset, paying special attention to the shape of the data through exploratory data analysis (EDA), This is in order to ensure that the identification methods are properly implemented to obtain better results than those that do not, as well as to compare different deep neural network methods in collaborative environments where resources are more limited.

title: Robust Control of a Quadrotor UAV Applied to the Transport and Delivery of Kits.
abstract: This work addresses the problem of controlling the transport of a load from one point to another via cable through a quadrotor, eliminating the oscillation generated by the suspended load. Robust non linear control is featured, which asymptotically stabilises the desired quadrotor position while simultaneously limiting load swing and aligning it to the vertical position of the inertial reference frame. The proposed control scheme considers the dynamics generated by the suspended load to generate the control law. Unlike the approaches used in the scientific literature, no feedback is needed on the dynamics of the suspended load; an extended state observer estimates these dynamics. The simulation results show that the proposed control can be helpful for the safe transport of the payload. Numerical simulations are shown that demonstrate the effectiveness controller.

title: Data Integration for the Evaluation of Cancer Evolution in Mexico through Data Visualization.
abstract: Cancer is the third cause of death in Mexico, one of the chronic degenerative diseases that has grown the most throughout the territory. This document describes a system that allows the integration and deployment of a unified data repository on cancerology in Mexico from public access sources generated by units specialized in cancer treatment and follow up. Data mining techniques allow the data repository integration for analyzing the cancer panorama in Mexico. The project involves cleaning processes, integration, selection, and transformation of data in a preprocessing stage, for further analysis and presented through a graphical interface. The primary objective is to generate an application that analyzes the evolution and spread of cancer in Mexico in recent years using data science techniques.

title: Convolutional and dense ANN for cloud kinetics fore casting using satellite images
abstract: Intermittency of solar radiation over earth surface due to cloud presence poses a great challenge for power production at photovoltaic fields. Predic tion of cloud kinetics may help to deal with variations of energy produc tion and their compensation to satisfy electricity demand. Nowadays, there are huge amounts of satellite information available about clouds at most re gions of the world. That information could be useful to characterize cloud kinetics and to calculate solar radiation ahead of time. In this paper, we propose two methods to predict cloud kinetics by using artificial neural networks (ANN) and satellite images. First method is mainly graphical and uses a convolutional ANN to predict the cloud satellite image at time k+1 from the set of previous n cloud satellite images. Then, the cloud position vector, that represents the predicted image, is obtained. Second method is mainly numerical and uses a dense ANN to directly predict the cloud posi tion vector at time k+1 from the set of previous m position vectors of satel lite images. The predicted cloud position vectors are compared to the real ones when the corresponding satellite image becomes available. Time series of predicted cloud position and velocity vectors are compared through the RMSE index to quantify the precision of predictions. We find that even though both methods offer a short term forecasting with good accuracy, the method using dense ANN provides more accurate results though its perfor mance should be checked under less simplified assumptions.

title: A Hybrid Hyperheuristic Approach for the Containership Stowage Problem Considering the Ship Stability
abstract: In this work we face the Containership Stowage Problem, also referred to as Master Bay Planning Problem (MBPP) in the literature. MBPP is an NP hard combinatorial optimization problem that consists in finding the best plan to load a set of containers into a set of available locations in the containership, subject to several structural and operational constraints. This problem is really difficult to solve and very import in the context of maritime port logistics. Since it is a practical decision making problem with high complexity and challenging instances, a hybrid hierarchical approach is developed in this paper. Our algorithmic proposal couples a heuristic procedure with a perturbative hyperheuristic. The validation of the proposed approach is performed by solving pseudo randomly instances available in the literature. The computational results show the efficiency of the proposed hybrid hierarchical algorithm when comparing with the reference results from the literature.

title: Mathematical optimization model for raw sugar unloading delay from harbor to storage silos
abstract: In this paper, we are introducing a mathematical model to describe the process of unloading the whole bulk carrier ship's raw sugar cargo, imported by a Company, to be stored in storage silos at the Casablanca refinery. The main point is to optimize the duration of the bulk carrier ship's stay at the Casablanca harbor's deck. First of all a mathematical formula is elaborated to describe the real life process of unloading the whole bulk carrier ship's cargo using a set of inequalities. An algorithm is then proposed to optimize the duration of the bulk carrier ship's stay at the Casablanca harbor's deck which is combining "branch and bound" and "tabu search" methods. The results found are very encouraging since it was possible to minimize the unloading delay from 10 days currently observed to 5 days as well as the scenarios found using the mathematical model were actually applicable in reality.

title: Time Series Prediction of Pregnant Women with COVID 19 in Mexico
abstract: This study focuses on the prediction of the daily number of pregnant women infected with SARS CoV 2 in Mexico. In particular, we developed a Fuzzy Time Series Model (FTSM) from 910 historical observations. The accuracy of the proposed model was measured by the well known Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) index. Specifically, our FTSM obtained a RMSE value of 34.45 units. This indicates that the forecasted values fit relatively well the real data. Thus, taking into account the empirical evidence, we conclude that the values forecasted by our FTSM are really close to the real values and could be helpful in medical decision making.

title: An Intelligent Human Activity Recognizer for Visually Impaired People using Deep Learning Technique
abstract: With the advancement of artificial intelligence and computer vision, assistive devices for visually impaired people is an active research area for the last decade. People with visual disabilities face challenges in the detection and recognition of various human actions which leads to a lack of confidence and constant dependency while performing daily routine activities. The objective of this research is to recognize and classify different human actions based on the position and posture of their body. In this research, captured video is processed for human pose estimation by extracting 2D body skeleton using OpenPose method. The extracted body points further to the process for feature extraction using pre trained VGG 19 CNN which classifies the human actions using an SVM classifier. Furthermore, the proposed method integrates with a voice enabled feature to deliver instructions on classified human activities. The proposed deep learning method is to train and test using three different dataset (a) Weizmann dataset for gesture based human actions, (b) Kinetics dataset for interaction based human actions, and (c) CK+ dataset for behaviour based human actions. The accuracy for classification of different human actions reached to 93.08\%, 95.03\%, and 93.12\% and the F1 score reached 93.59\%, 95.19\% and 93.66\%, respectively. These results indicate the significance of the proposed method for the assistance of visually impaired people.

title: The role of the number of examples in Convolutional Neural Networks with Hebbian Learning
abstract: Both synaptic plasticity rules (the so called Hebbian rules) and Convolutional Neural Networks are based on or inspired by well established models of Computational Neuroscience about mammal vision. There are some theoretical advantages associated with these frameworks, including online learning in Hebbian Learning. In the case of Convolutional Neural Networks, such advantages have been translated into remarkable results in image classification in the last decade. Nevertheless, such success is not shared in Hebbian Learning. In this paper, we explore the hypothesis of the necessity of a wider dataset for the classification of mono instantiated objects, this is, objects that can be represented in a single cluster in the feature space. By using 15 mono instantiated classes, the Adam optimizer reaches the maximum accuracy with fewer examples but using more epochs. In comparison, Hebbian rule BCM demands more examples but keeps using real time learning. This result is a positive answer to the principal hypothesis and enlights how Hebbian learning can find a niche in the mainstream of Deep Learning.

title: Diachronic Neural Network Predictor of Word Animacy
abstract: Distinction between animate and inanimate is a fundamental issue of cognition and language. The paper considers the problem of automatic recognition of animacy in the Russian language. We propose a recognizer that is based on the analysis of co occurrence with the most frequent words and is trained on data from the Russian subcorpus of Google Books Ngram. The obtained recognition accuracy of animacy is 94.3% on the test sample. We also consider the application of the trained recognizer to diachronic data. The performed analysis shows that high recognition accuracy can be obtained even using the data extracted from the corpus for one single year. This allows one, firstly, to diachronically investigate changes in perception of words for which variability of animacy/inanimacy is observed. Secondly, the considered examples show that change in perception of an object as animate or inanimate can serve as a marker of semantic change and, in particular, emergence of new meanings of a word denoting this object. This makes the recognizer a good tool for studies of language evolution.

title: Takagi Sugeno Type Neuro Fuzzy System Model based Fault Diagnostic in Photovoltaic System
abstract: Exposing photovoltaic installations to the outdoors for a long time leads to various breakdowns. Accurate and quantitative diagnosis of defect severity is vital for decision making given the cost of defect removal. In this paper, a Takagi Sugeno type neuro fuzzy approach for the detection, identification and location of faults in solar photovoltaic systems is proposed. Then, an algorithm for optimizing the structure of the neuro fuzzy model is developed, in order to improve the convergence capacity, resolve the influence of random parameters on the predictive performances, and to reduce both the number of synaptic weights and membership functions. This approach accurately detects, identifies and locates photovoltaic faults based on measurements of fault current, photovoltaic voltage, irradiance level, temperature and weather. Various fault scenarios are experimentally verified and validated in a large scale solar photovoltaic power plant in order to demonstrate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed approach.

title: Sequential Models for Sentiment Analysis: A Comparative Study
abstract: Sentiment analysis has been a focus of study in Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks in recent years. In this paper, we propose the task of analysing sentiments using five sequential models and we compare their performance on a Twitter dataset. We used the bag of words, as well as the tf idf, and the Word2Vec embeddings, as input features to the models. The precision, recall, f1 and accuracy scores of the proposed models were used to evaluate the models performance. The Bi LSTM model with Word2Vec embedding performs the best against the dataset, with an accuracy of 84%.

title: A Nudge to the Metrobus in the Metropolis of La Laguna: Towards an Intelligent Mobility System
abstract: We present a perspective of an important projecto called Metrobus de la Laguna, we present the critical reality of this project. This perspective its motivated of an important project called Metro bus de la Laguna, we present the critical reality and offer a Nudge strategy with a collaborated project proposal with key stakeholders of the project. e present a perspective of an important project called Metrobus de la Laguna, we present the critical reality and offer a Nudge strategy with a collaborated project proposal with key stakeholders of the project.

title: Product Localization using a voice recognition assistant in a retail company with 4 branches located in Aguascalientes
abstract: Implementation of IoT devices through voice recognition to help older adults, new customers and new employees to locate a product among 1,200 products in a retailing company. After implementing this Assistant, using the data collected, the retail company will apply data mining techniques to improve sales rearranging the products.

title: Use of cellular automata to determine habitat vulnerability under uncertainty of an ecological stronghold and its impact on the carbon footprint
abstract: Use of a cellular automaton that models the behavior of the species and collect information to help protect wildlife in order to monitor its population. implement algorithms that model factors that affect it so we can be able to prevent while also making predictions based on a set of rules established.

title: PREDICTIVE MODEL WITH ALGORITHM RNA TO DETERMINING VARIABLES IN WASTEWATER POLLUTION
abstract: This research sought the validation of water quality variables prediction through supervised learning neural network algorithm developed in Phyton programming language. For its testing, the algorithm was applied to a wastewater database whose result indicated the predictive variables of water quality in accordance with international standards. Afterwards, the obtained variables were compared with existed predictor variables found in a previous research, which analyzed the same wastewater database through a process called data mining. The obtained comparation results validated the algorithm with a precision result of 99.2 % according to the reliability matrix.

title: Graph exploration guided by provenance in seismology: design and query expressions
abstract: This position paper analyses data and meta data modelling challenge to provide curated collections that can be easy to explore. Data exploration can be done considering data provenance to give insight into the conditions in which data are collected (i.e., by which type of devices, labelled by which human/synthetic agents, etc.). We focus on seismic geophysics data curation and exploration because we believe these tasks depend highly on the knowledge domain. The discussion about possible solutions is driven by the hypothesis that graphs can be well adapted data models to represent, explore and analyse seismic data. Given that data curation is done by human agents, provenance is an essential meta data to be added to seismic data. We show how this provenance can guide curation and exploration.

title: Towards a High Level Framework for Scalable Similarity Join Computation Using MapReduce and LSH
abstract: Similarity joins are widely used in several application domains and are recognized to be among the most useful data processing and analysis operations. Similarity joins retrieve all data pairs whose distances are less than a predefined threshold $\lambda$. Implementing an efficient computation of similarity joins on large volumes of data is a difficult task especially for non specialists. In this article, we present a generic framework for processing similarity joins using the MapReduce model and Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) functions. This framework can be used with different types of data since the user provides only the distance definition and the LSH family adapted to its data. Then our framework generates an implementation based on our MapReduce similarity join programs allowing to reduce the number of comparisons as well as the communication costs which improves the data processing time on large scale systems. The experiments on set and trajectory similarity joins show very good performance results.

title: Evaluation of Semantic Parsing Frameworks for Automated knowledge base construction
abstract: Semantic parsing a sub field of natural language understanding, translates natural language utterances into detailed representations of their meaning. Though numerous meaning representation frameworks exist, none has been universally accepted. The current paper provides a comparative study for the most promising semantic representations of text, taking into account parsers, performance, extensibility, available corpora, and other aspects used for automated construction of a knowledge base for commonsense reasoning. In parallel, a corpus was constructed, and experiments were conducted to capture the linguistic attributes essential for automated reasoning.

title: Storing Feature Vectors in Relational Image Data Warehouses
abstract: An image data warehousing also manipulates image data represented by feature vectors and attributes for similarity search. In this paper, we study the impact of storing feature vectors on the performance of analytical queries extended with a similarity search predicate over images. We consider applications that manipulate huge data volumes. Thus, we use the Spark framework as support. Experimental results showed that depending on the query characteristics and the data warehouse design, the difference in performance was up to 86.23\%. Based on these results, we propose guidelines for storing feature vectors in relational image data warehouses.

title: Downtown Walkability as a Contribution to Environmental Sustainability
abstract: Rapid urbanization has turned urban mobility into one of the biggest challenges for modern cities. Particularly in downtown of medium and large cities, it encourages a fierce competition for the use of the public spaces among pedestrian, individual motorized transport, public transport resulting in accidents, congestion, increasing costs and travel time, and contributing to the issue of environmental pollution. Taking the theme walkability as a contribution to social, economic, and environmental sustainability this work takes walking as a form of mobility in an urban center and develops a methodology for helping citizen who arrive at downtown bus terminals to reach points of interest. The main objective is to offer better routes, for a social class coming from peripheral neighborhoods, to access essential public services. In determining the best walking route, three macros indicator are defined: Environment indicator, representing physical characteristics of the walking environment; Comfort indicator, represented by visual attractiveness and local comfort; and Safety indicator representing public and personal security. Promethee multicriteria method, is employed to determine the best routes connecting points of Origin (Urban Terminal) to public service points in the urban center of Campinas. As a contribution the implementation of best routes by local government will provide the urban center with walking space that meets the citizen requirement.

title: How to automatically build an ontology from unconstrained texts?
abstract: Ontologies are essential in many domains, but their use is limited by the cost of their development. This paper considers the problem of automatic ontology construction, and proposes an overview of the techniques and tools available to address the different tasks required to meet this challenge.

title: Automatic classification of stigmatizing articles of mental illness: the case of Portuguese online newspapers
abstract: The stigma related to mental health continues to be present in online newspapers, where mental diseases are often used metaphorically to refer to entities or situations outside the context of mental health and psychiatry. Considering that the manual analysis of this problem requires a great deal of human effort and time, this project explores the implementation of Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing techniques for the task of automatically classifying stigmatizing articles with references to the mental disorders of schizophrenia and psychosis. This work is implemented in Portuguese online news articles, collected from the Arquivo.pt repository, a public repository of archived Portuguese web pages, and can be adapted to other languages or similar problems. Nine machine learning and deep learning algorithms were implemented to perform the presented task, most of them yielding results with accuracy and precision above 90%. In addition, the automatic detection of topics present in the articles was also performed, through topic modeling with the top2vec model, which allowed concluding that the stigmatization of mental health occurs, essentially, in the topics of Economics and Politics. The experimental results confirm the existence of stigma in Portuguese newspapers (52% of the 978 articles collected) and the effectiveness of the use of Artificial Intelligence models for its detection. Additionally, a set of 978 articles collected and manually classified with the classes ["stigmatizing", "literal"] is obtained.

title: Portuguese Man of War Image Classification With Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: Portugueseman of war(PMW)isagelatinousorganismwith long tentacles capable of causing severe burns, thus leading to negative impacts on human activities, such as tourism and fishing. There is a lack of information about the spatio temporal dynamics of this species. Therefore, the use of alternative methods for collecting data can con tribute to their monitoring. Given the widespread use of social networks and the eye catching look of PMW, Instagram posts can be a promis ing data source for monitoring. The first task to follow this approach is to identify posts that refer to PMW. This paper reports on the use of convolutional neural networks for PMW images classification, in order to automate the recognition of Instagram posts. We created a suitable dataset, and trained three different neural networks: VGG 16, ResNet50, and InceptionV3, with and without a pre trained step with the ImageNet dataset. We analyzed their results using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score metrics. The pre trained ResNet50 network presented the best results, obtaining 94% of accuracy and 95% of precision, recall, and F1 score. These results show that convolutional neural networks can be very effective for recognizing PMW images from the Instagram social media.

title: A Multiplex Network framework based Recommendation Systems for Technology Intelligence
abstract: Network Science has become a flourishing interest in the last decades as we witness the Big Data explosion in many fields including, social science, biology and engineering. Technology Intelligence aims at surveying the prolific production of information and recent studies have identified their multiplex nature as a very important aspect to understand various aspects of information. However, the interplay between multiplexity and controllability of these networks is challenging. This paper aims to describe a flexible framework for a recommendation system, based on multiplex networks in the context of technological development. We detail the important characteristics of the multiplex network that is of interest to us, and show the advantages of this approach over the matrix approaches common in the literature.

title: Relation extraction from clinical cases for a knowledge graph
abstract: We describe a system for automatic extraction of semantic relations between entities in a medical corpus of clinical cases. It builds upon a previously developed module for entity extraction and upon a morphosyntactic parser. It uses experimentally designed rules based on syntactic dependencies and trigger words, as well as on sequencing and nesting of entities of particular types. The results obtained on a small corpus are promising. Our larger perspective is transforming information extracted from medical texts into knowledge graphs.

title: Privacy Operators for Semantic Graph Databases as Graph Rewriting
abstract: Database sanitization allows to share and publish open (linked) data without jeopardizing privacy. During their sanitization, graph databases are transformed following graph transformations that are usually described informally or through ad hoc processes. This paper is a first effort toward bridging the gap between the rigorous graph rewriting approaches and graph sanitization by providing basic generic graph rewriting operators to serve as a basis for the construction of sanitization mechanisms. As a proof of concept, we formalize two operators, blank node creation and weighted relation randomization, using an algebraic graph rewriting approach that takes into account semantic through the equivalent of Where and Except clauses. We show that these operators can be used to achieve pseudonymity and local differential privacy. Both operators and all related rewriting rules are implemented using the Attributed Graph Grammar System (AGG), providing a concrete tool implementing formal graph rewriting mechanisms to sanitize semantic graph databases.

title: Should I Stay or Should I Go: A New Reasoner for Description Logic
abstract: We present the Emi reasoner, based on a new interpretation of the tableau algorithm for reasoning with Description Logics with unique performance characteristics and specialized advantages. Emi turns the tableau inside out, solving the satisfiability problem by adding elements to expressions rather than adding expressions to element node labels. This strategy is inspired by decidable reasoning algorithms for Horn Logics and EL++ that run on a loop rather than recursive graph based strategies used in a tableau reasoner. Because Emi solves the same problem there will be a simple correspondence with tableaux, yet it will feel very different during execution, since the problem is inverted. This inversion makes possible many unique and straightforward optimizations, such as paralellization of nearly every part of the reasoning task, concurrent ABox expansion, and localized blocking techniques. Each of these optimizations contains a design trade off that allows Emi to perform extremely well in certain cases and not as well in others, often reversing the observed efficiency trends present in common tableaux implementations. Our initial evaluations show that even a naive implementation of Emi is performant with popular Java reasoners such as Hermit, Pellet, and jFact.

title: Enriching Relation Extraction with OpenIE
abstract: Relation extraction (RE) is a sub discipline of information extraction (IE) which focuses on the prediction of a relational predicate from a natural language input unit (such as a sentence, a clause, or even a short paragraph consisting of multiple sentences and/or clauses). Together with named entity recognition (NER) and disambiguation (NED), RE forms the basis for many advanced IE tasks such as knowledge base (KB) population and verification. In this work, we explore how recent approaches for open information extraction (OpenIE) may help to improve the task of RE by encoding structured information about the sentences' principal units, such as subjects, objects, verbal phrases, and adverbials, into various forms of vectorized (and hence unstructured) representations of the sentences. Our main conjecture is that the decomposition of long and possibly convoluted sentences into multiple smaller clauses via OpenIE even helps to fine tune context sensitive language models such as BERT (and its plethora of variants) for RE. Our experiments over two annotated corpora, KnowledgeNet and FewRel, demonstrate the improved accuracy of our enriched models compared to existing RE approaches. Our best results reach 92% and 71% of F1 score for KnowledgeNet and FewRel, respectively, proving the effectiveness of our approach on competitive benchmarks.

title: Evaluating Prompt based Question Answering for Object Prediction in the Open Research Knowledge Graph
abstract: There is a large body of emerging work investigating the prompt based training of pre trained or fine tuned transformer language models obtained from large scale text corpora of general knowledge, in the context of effectively applying these models on a new genre of text created in low resource settings. Prompt based construction of training instances has shown to be effective in the generalization of pre trained or fine tuned models' probabilistic parameters toward transferability in resource scarce settings. This work, for the first time, reports results on adopting prompt based training of transformers for scholarly knowledge graph object prediction. The work is unique in the following two main aspects. 1) It deviates from the other works proposing entity and relation extraction pipelines for predicting objects of a scholarly knowledge graph. 2) While other works have tested the method on text genera relatively close to the general knowledge domain, we test the method for a significantly different domain, i.e. scholarly knowledge, in turn testing the linguistic, probabilistic, and factual generalizability of these large scale transformer models. We find that (i) per expectations, transformer models when tested out of the box underperform on a new domain of data, (ii) prompt based training of the models achieve performance boosts of up to 40% in a relaxed evaluation setting, and (iii) testing the models on a starkly different domain even with a clever training objective in a low resource setting makes evident the domain knowledge capture gap offering an empirically verified incentive for investing more attention and resources to the scholarly domain in the context of transformer models.

title: Augmentation of Instance Data for the Identification of Ontological Elements enabling Natural Language Search in Graph Databases
abstract: The storage and representation of knowledge is becoming increasingly important. However, an essential step is to be able to easily query relevant knowledge. Resource Description Framework (RDF) based query languages enable very precise access possibilities. However, most people have little to no knowledge about query languages and the underlying database schemas. In this regard, Natural Language Querying is a vibrant research area that seeks to bridge the gap between an unstructured question and a structured query. Nevertheless, many existing approaches do not generalize well to multiple domains and may require handcrafted rules, manual customization, or large amounts of annotated training data. This paper proposes the Augementation for Identification based Natural Language Search (A4I NLS) system, which formulates all subtasks required to evaluate an unstructured question as machine learning based classification tasks. The relevant training data for the classifications is to be generated automatically from the instance data stored in the existing knowledge graph. The developed system shows promising results on a large knowledge graph.

title: Price based Learning for Explainable Reasoning in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Knowledge Graphs represent real time data which is constantly growing with the addition of new information. To respond to the changes in data and make useful inferences, there is a need for dynamic algorithms which can adapt to the evolving graphs and give interpretable and explainable reasoning. The state of the art neural networks and embedding based methods suffer from interpretability of their decisions as they learn from latent vector representation. While the path based methods logically parse the queries to provide traceable reasoning, they are based on static templates of data which limits their use for dynamic graphs. Also most of the current methods rely on offline training and are not capable of continuous learning from new data. In this research work, we propose the use of a new class of auction algorithms for evolving knowledge graphs to perform data analysis tasks like question answering, link prediction and making recommendations. These algorithms use a new parameter called node prices to guide the search for the path and dynamically update the prices based on a set of defined rules. The prices also provide the means to 'transfer knowledge'. In particular, our results show that reusing the learned prices from previous searches, as initial prices for subsequent related searches can significantly reduce the number of iterations. We also discuss some use cases from industry where our method can be useful.

title: Uncovering the semantics of PD patients movement data collected via off the shelf wearables
abstract: In Neurodegenerative Diseases (ND) such as the Parkinson Disease (PD), wearable sensors are used to collect movement (kinetic) data for analysis and assessment of patients symptoms, not only in clinical conditions, but also during Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). Data collected through sensors embedded in wearable devices, such as smartwatches, need to be semantically described in a commonly agreed, explicit and formal way, to become interoperable, and interlinked with other related data collected in personal health records (PHR) e.g., patients Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRIs), medical prescriptions, medical advice, etc. Such an integrated and unified view of personal health data provides health specialists with decisive knowledge, decreasing their efforts to constantly assess patients condition via traditional methods. The objectives of this study are to collect movement data of PD patients through wearables, analyze them to uncover their semantics, and then use such semantics to semantically annotate data in a formal and explicit way that their interlinking with other related heterogenous data will be facilitated. The aim is to utilize those semantics in health specialists services such as live analytics, decision support, and high level critical alerts recognition. In this work, the integration of unobtrusive wearable technology for health monitoring is emphasized, collected data are analyzed for uncovering their semantics, and formal semantic models are examined for their suitability to be reused, and extended, for the semantic annotation the collected movement data.

title: Knowledge Graph Injection for Aspect Based Sentiment Classification
abstract: Since the increase of Web reviews of products and services, Aspect Based Sentiment Classification (ABSC) has become more important to determine the sentiment of online opinions. Useful information extracted from these reviews can then be used by companies themselves, but can also be applicable by consumers. In the recent literature on ABSC, hybrid methods, which combine knowledge based and machine learning approaches, are becoming more popular as well. However, in this work, instead of following a two step procedure, we attempt to improve the model accuracy by proposing to directly inject the information from a domain ontology in a state of the art neural network model, more precisely LCR Rot hop++. Furthermore, by using soft positioning and visible matrices we aim to prevent that the injected knowledge hinders the semantics of the original sentences. To evaluate the accuracy of our model, LCR Rot hop ont++, we use the standard SemEval 2015 and SemEval 2016 datasets for ABSC. We conclude that knowledge injection in the neural network is effective for sentiment classification, especially if the amount of labeled data is limited.

title: Explainable Phenotype Centric Drug Repurposing via Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Biomedical knowledge graphs encode domain knowledge as biomedical entities and relationships between them. Such rich sources support the use of automated methods for the discovery of novel research hypotheses, e.g. the repurposing of a known drug. In reinforcement learning based multi hop reasoning, an agent is trained to walk the graph of biomedical knowledge from disease to compound. Walked paths can serve as explanations for predictions, but the challenge of discovering meaningful paths remains. We hypothesise that additional background knowledge such as a known disease drug pair can reduce the number of reasoning paths, so that the agent can learn faster and from a more meaningful subset. In this work, we propose to constrain the agents policy guided walks through a novel reward function that exploits knowledge about a diseases symptoms (i.e. phenotypes) encoded as instantiated logical rules. We assess the impact of contextual knowledge in a quantitative and qualitative evaluation, and aim at measuring: (i) the effect training with context has on the reasoning paths, and (ii) the effect of using context for explainability purposes, measured in terms of plausibility, novelty, and relevancy. Results indicate that learning with contextual knowledge significantly increases coherence between diseases and discovered multi hop reasoning paths, without affecting the interpretability for the domain experts.

title: Language Model based Entity Alignment in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Entity Alignment (EA) is the task of identifying equivalent entities present in multiple Knowledge Graphs (KGs). It is a significant step in improving the quality of KGs and thereby crucial for downstream applications, e.g., question answering and recommendation. To accomplish this, many embedding based EA approaches have been proposed that consider the triple information and attributes together with the entity names, descriptions, and neighbourhood information. Additionally, most of the existing baseline models require a set of aligned entities or triples as seeds for training. However, this paper proposes a novel EA approach that uses contextual Large Language Models (LLMs) on textual information primarily on entity names from the source and target KGs. This paper proposes a supervised as well as an unsupervised entity alignment approach. An adversarial learning strategy to learn the mapping of the source and target embedding spaces without supervision is presented. The model has been evaluated on benchmark datasets which demonstrates that the proposed approach outperforms most of the baseline models for the SRPRS datasets.

title: Mapping and Cleaning Open Commonsense Knowledge Bases with Generative Translation
abstract: Structured knowledge bases (KBs) are the backbone of many knowledge intensive applications, and their automated construction has received considerable attention. In particular, open information extraction (OpenIE) is often used to induce structure from text. However, although it allows high recall, the extracted knowledge tends to inherit noise from the sources and the OpenIE algorithm itself. Besides, OpenIE tuples contain an open ended, non canonicalized set of relations, making the extracted knowledge's downstream exploitation harder. In this paper, we study the problem of mapping an open KB into the fixed schema of an existing KB, specifically for the case of commonsense knowledge. We propose to approach the problem by generative translation, i.e., by training a language model to generate fixed schema assertions from open ones. Experiments show that this approach occupies a sweet spot between traditional manual, rule based, or classification based canonicalization and purely generative KB construction like COMET. It produces higher mapping accuracy than the former, while avoiding the association based noise of the latter. We make the code and the generated data publicly available.

title: Towards Executing Knowledge Graphs on Blockchain using Graph Based Imperative Code Generation
abstract: Smart contracts, deployed on blockchains, can automate decision logic found in legal contracts, organizational rules, or guidelines such as clinical practice guidelines. High level decision logic tends to be encoded by domain experts or knowledge engineers, using high level domain formalisms such as Symboleo (legal contracts) or PROforma (clinical), or more general purpose, rule based formalisms such as Notation3 (N3) or SWRL. Manually implementing this decision logic as smart contracts, using an imperative blockchain language, requires technical expertise that is typically beyond the skillset of these stakeholders. At the same time, due to restrictions of certain platforms, such as blockchain, it is difficult to directly deploy engines for executing high level decision logic. We target the translation of high level decision logic, encoded by a Knowledge Graph (KG) with N3 rules and a domain ontology, into an imperative programming language. Currently, targets include Solidity, for use on the Ethereum blockchain; and JavaScript, for general web based deployments. Although many limitations must currently be placed on input KG, we believe this is a first step towards making KG executable on blockchain and other platforms without the need for resource intensive execution engines. Our use case targets KGs that encode clinical decision logic pertaining to diabetes.

title: CLUE: A Context based Method for Labeling Unobserved Entities in Sequential Data
abstract: Sequential data is commonly found in industrial applications such as self driving cars and smart manufacturing. Obtaining high quality, labeled sequence data for training machine learning models is an expensive and arduous task in such applications. Using prior knowledge for augmenting existing data/labels has been a recent focus within the machine learning community. In this paper, we investigate a specific type of label augmentation that enhances sequential data with additional labels for entities (i.e., objects and events) that have gone unobserved and, therefore, unlabeled in existing datasets. To address this issue, we present CLUE, a simple, general purpose method in which sequential data is represented as a knowledge graph (KG) and analyzed to infer the unobserved entities (UEs). This inference leverages Piaget's theory of object continuity, a well known theory in psychology, to determine if entities are present yet unobserved. Using autonomous driving as the application domain, we demonstrate the applicability of this method for augmenting driving scenes in two benchmark datasets Pandaset and NuScenes that include complex urban driving situations. Our investigation finds that CLUE was able to augment 12.49% and 38.51% of driving scenes with +8.24% and +18.5% additional labels for UEs in Pandaset and NuScenes, respectively. Interestingly, CLUE showed significant improvements in labeling entities that occur at the tail end of the entity frequency distribution (i.e., entities that are rarely observed).

title: Expertise Modeling in the Context of Emergency Management
abstract: It is crucial for emergency management organizations to have rapid access to relevant experts who can advise and assist following a disaster. To improve expert mining and recommendation capabilities, creating a knowledge graph that links experts to their corresponding topics of expertise and other sources of relevant information is a natural choice to capture an integrated network of people and a rich taxonomy of expertise. In this paper, we present an ontology for modeling experts, their expertise topics and relations between them, and their spatiotemporal scoping. We go on to discuss the primary conceptual components and how they can be instantiated, then present overarching examples related to emergency management operations. The ontology synthesizes three different ways to characterize an expert, based on a) identifiable academic expertise; b) voluntary engagements, work related responsibilities or experience; and c) organization specialization or affiliation.

title: Comparative Research in Stream Reasoning
abstract: The diverse research efforts in recent years in the area of stream reasoning (SR) led to a wide range of SR engines. However, the lack of standardization and the diverse choices in SR (e.g., tuple driven vs. time driven engines, streaming all results vs. newly derived ones, ...) mean that real comparability among the engines is hardly given. A first step towards achieving comparability and standardization is the RSP QL model, implemented in the RSP4J framework, which allows for describing and formalizing the semantics of SR engines. To further advance the state of the art in comparative research of stream reasoning, we first present the results of a survey to quantify the in use importance of several key performance indicators (KPIs) and features. We then compare SR engines along these KPIs with the CityBench and the CSRBench oracle. Our analysis shows that the two RSP4J implementations C SPARQL2.0 and YASPER outperform the well known C SPARQL implementation in terms of performance and configurability. Our comparison against a naive SR extension of the incremental reasoning engine RDFox shows that SR engines still have potential for improvement. To avoid a costly integration of engines into several different benchmarking environments, we finally present a unifying interface, already aligned with the CityBench and CSRBench, for benchmarking SR engines.

title: Cobalt: A Content Based Similarity Approach for Link Discovery over Geospatial Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Data integration and applications across knowledge graphs(KGs) rely heavily on the discovery of links between resources within these KGs. In an increasing number of cases, geospatial data is being represented using the Linked Data standards. The vector geometry used to characterize the resources contained within these knowledge graphs presents a challenge for link discovery approaches, which have to deal with millions of point sets containing billions of points. In this paper,we tackle this challenge by proposing Cobalt, a topological relations discovery approach based on the content measures combined with R Tree indexing. Our experiments showed that Cobalt is able to speedsup the topological relation discovery over geospatial KGs up to15104 order of magnitude while maintaining an F Measure between 70% and 90%

title: Optimizing SPARQL Queries with SHACL
abstract: We propose a set of optimizations that can be applied to a given SPARQL query, and that guarantee that the optimised query has the same an swers under bag semantics as the original query, provided that the queried RDF graph validates certain SHACL constraints. Our optimizations exploit the relation ship between graph patterns in the SPARQL queries and the SHACL constraints that describe those patterns in the RDF graph. We prove the correctness of these optimizations.

title: Combining Temporal Reasoning Formalisms and Empirical Semantic Drifts
abstract: The encoding and exploitation of semantics has been gaining popularity, as exemplified by the uptake of logic based knowledge graphs (KGs) and embedding based Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques. However, the semantics of terms in a domain are usually considered in a non dynamic manner, rather than a proper reflection of how they evolve over time. Although domain updates can be checked for consistency and used in logical inferences, after an update is applied, no further consideration is given to which information is new and which already existed. Understanding and applying semantic evolution can have profound implications in a number of applications, including question answering, data quality assurance, and knowledge completion. However, while a number of methods have been proposed to track dynamic semantics, there is a paucity of approaches to effectively combine these to better monitor and incorporate their evolution. We describe a generally applicable definition of semantic evolution to address the impact of domain updates as events in stationary semantics. Our work combines temporal reasoning as an analytical approach for the modeling of causal relations between events and effects with semantic drifts as an empirical approach for quantifying the impact of domain updates. We demonstrate how the weaknesses of each individual approach are addressed and how their interaction can improve the representation of semantic evolution.

title: Join Ordering of SPARQL Property Path Queries
abstract: SPARQL property path queries offer a succinct way to write complex navigation queries on RDF knowledge graphs. However, their evaluation remains difficult because they involve the execution of transitive closures. As a result, many property path queries time out when executed on public online RDF knowledge graphs. A common way to improve execution time is to find a good join order. While the join order problem has been widely studied for basic graph pattern SPARQL queries, it remains largely unexplored when considering the presence of a path pattern in the query. In this paper, we present a novel approach capable of discovering good join orders for property path queries. Our approach relies on sampling to estimate the cost of join orders with path patterns. In experiments with the latest Wikidata Benchmark, we show that 40\% of path queries are affected by the join ordering problem. With our proposal, without changing the underlying engine, we can speed up the evaluation of property path queries by at least a factor of 6 on BlazeGraph, just by finding better join orders.

title: Refining Large Integrated Identity Graphs using the Unique Name Assumption
abstract: The Unique Name Assumption (UNA) supposes that two terms with distinct identifiers from the same knowledge base do not refer to the same real world entity. UNA can be used to detect errors in large integrated knowledge bases. For example, some identity link can be erroneous if they are in a path that connects two entities (that refer to different real world objects) defined in the same knowledge base. For large knowledge bases, however, the UNA does not always hold due to redundant IRIs that captures various encoding, languages, namespaces, versions, letter cases, etc. UNA can still be useful for identifying erroneous links provided good adaption to the exceptions. For this, we propose a concrete definition of the UNA with tolerance towards multiple exceptions, namely the internal UNA (iUNA). To compare iUNA and other variants of UNA, we propose a generic algorithm that can be used for refinement. The algorithm employs an SMT (Satisfiability Modulo Theory) solver and takes advantage of the latter's ability to efficiently reason over equality. For evaluation, we identify erroneous links in an identity graph of half a billion triples extracted from the LOD Cloud. Finally, we compare our algorithm using iUNA against the Louvain algorithm.

title: Structural Bias in Knowledge Graphs for the Entity Alignment Task
abstract: Knowledge Graphs (KGs) have recently gained attention for representing knowledge about a particular domain and play a central role in a multitude of AI tasks like recommendations and query answering. Recent works have revealed that KG embedding methods used to implement these tasks often exhibit direct forms of bias (e.g., related to gender, nationality, etc.) leading to discrimination. In this work, we are interested in the impact of indirect forms of bias related to the structural diversity of KGs in entity alignment (EA) tasks. In this respect, we propose an exploration based sampling algorithm, SUSIE, that generates challenging benchmark data for EA methods, with respect to structural diversity. This exploration based sampling method requires setting the value of a single hyperparameter, which affects the connectivity of the generated KGs. Using our sampling, we demonstrate that state of the art EA methods, like RREA and RDGCN, exhibit different robustness to structurally diverse input KGs.

title: Abuse Classification for Heterogeneous Natural Language Text using Federated Learning
abstract: The commenting spaces on online social media have become the foreground for abusive content, trolling, and cyberbullying over the last few years. Recent developments in automated learning approaches prompt the use of context for uncovering insights and identifying offensive content online. However, managing the huge amounts of data that are continually posted online makes it difficult for training at a centralized location. Thus, in this paper, we develop a novel Fed Hate framework for identifying abusive content among monolingual, code mixed, and code switched diversed Hindi English text. We use BiLSTM based Fed Hate model, which runs across a federated client server architecture utilizing various heterogeneous data sets downloaded from shared tasks on abuse detection. Our experimental findings indicate that the Fed Hate framework is more effective than the traditional centrally trained learning model and achieves an average classification accuracy of 80\% for each client machine. Additionally, we supervised the system level analysis, including CPU GPU monitoring among available resources for our proposed experimental setup.

title: Generating gradual self explanatory SHACL constraints from expert knowledge and probabilistic reasoning
abstract: The Shape Constraint Language (SHACL) has been defined by the W3C to answer the rising need of controlling and assessing the quality of the ever growing knowledge bases using specific constraints encoded as shapes. However, these can be complex to define. In this paper, we propose a method to automatically generate SHACL constraints from a knowledge base and expert knowledge. We present a formalization allowing the learning of a causal probabilistic model, from which explaining rules are extracted and translated as constraints for assessing the quality of the knowledge base and detecting odd facts. We introduce two kinds of SHACL constraints: descriptive and reasoning, to permit a better assessment of the quality of both the current knowledge base and possible new data to be integrated from other sources.

title: Document level Event Extraction via Efficient Multi Scale Feature Extraction Framework with Set Prediction
abstract: The aim of document level event extraction (DEE) task is to identify the event types present in a given document and extract their corresponding event arguments. This is crucial for providing structured information in various natural language processing tasks. Unlike sentence level event extraction, DEE involves extracting events and event arguments from one or more events that may be scattered throughout the document. In this paper, we propose a multi scale feature extraction framework with set prediction for efficient extraction of structured events from a document in a parallel manner. Our approach uses non autoregressive decoder to generate events in parallel, and employs two efficient aggregation strategies to capture latent information. To obtain event arguments, we treat the matching process as a set prediction task, which can be solved using the Hungarian algorithm. Empirical results on the DEE ChFinAnn dataset demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing state of the art method in the challenging DEE task. Our dataset and code will be available on the github.

title: Formalization of Component Oriented Question Answering Systems using Petri Nets and its RDF Driven Component Definition
abstract: One of the approaches for building Question Answering systems is based on utilizing a Service Oriented Architecture. The services (or components) are dedicated to performing one of the downstream tasks such as named entity disambiguation, relation linking, etc. The components are combined in a Question Answering pipeline to reach the overall goal of answering a natural language question. While processing a question, conceptually, the components generate and store data structures that are used further in the process. As the number of available components grows rapidly, one needs to establish a formal model and machine readable description to simplify the process of building Question Answering pipelines and therefore the whole system. In this paper, we introduce a formal definition of the component for Question Answering systems. The behavioral semantics is based on the Coloured Petri Nets. Therefore, from the components' semantics, real world systems can be orchestrated while ensuring that the system is executable. Hence, the presented component descriptions are enabling the developers to search for compatible components and consequently automatically create executable Question Answering systems.

title: Entity Linking with Out of Knowledge Graph Entity Detection and Clustering
abstract: Entity Linking is relevant to several downstream tasks like question answering, knowledge graph population, or general knowledge extraction. An often neglected part of entity linking is the possibility of encounters with entities that do not exist in a target knowledge graph yet. While there are a few recent works focusing on this problem, they mainly employ full text knowledge bases or rely on external information. However, these resources are not available in most use cases. In this work, we rely only on information in a knowledge graph and assume to not have any external information available. To analyze the problem of identifying and disambiguating entities not yet in the knowledge graph, we propose a silver standard benchmark dataset encompassing texts from 1999 to 2022. Based on our novel dataset, we develop an initial approach using pre trained language models and knowledge graph embeddings without the need for a parallel full text corpus. We show that the detection of entities not in the target knowledge graph can be improved by simulating them during training. Furthermore, knowledge graph information in the form graph embeddings is of advantage when clustering out of knowledge graph entities.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Structural Information from Knowledge Graphs on Entity Linking
abstract: Previous work in the field of entity linking has made great strides in using different types of knowledge, whether explicit or implicit, to benefit disambiguation quality. However, the effects of using different levels of structural information have rarely been systematically studied. In this paper, we explore and evaluate different ways of using structural knowledge graph information to maximize its qualitative information benefits specifically for the entity disambiguation task. We compare four entity disambiguation models that incorporate varying degrees of topological graph structure, and find that a higher degree of topological graph structure (e.g., in the form of contextualized embeddings) does not necessarily provide an advantage for the disambiguation task. On the contrary, precomputed embeddings trained on the entire knowledge graph and inherently representing the global topological structure outperform previous state of the art models in our evaluation with a margin of 1.7% on Wikidata disamb and a F1 score of 94.0%. We use and analyze entity type data for filtering before disambiguation, identifying previous research results on the relevance of type information. This results in a time savings of 20 30\% in simple disambiguation situations and suggests potentially greater benefits for complex systems. Overall, our analyses show that different types of information more than one might suspect are important for entity linking.

title: Knowledge Graph Enhanced Neural Query Rewriting
abstract: The main task of an e commerce search engine is to semantically match the user query to the product inventory and retrieve the most relevant items that match the users intent. This task is not trivial as often there can be a mismatch between the users intent and the product inventory for various reasons, the most prevalent being: (i) the buyers and sellers use different vocabularies, which leads to a mismatch; (ii) the inventory doesnt contain products that match the users intent. To build a successful e commerce platform it is of paramount importance to be able to address both of these challenges. To do so, query rewriting approaches are used, which try to bridge the semantic gap between the users intent and the available product inventory. Such approaches use a combination of query token dropping, replacement and expansion. In this work we introduce a novel Knowledge Graph enhanced neural query rewriting in the e commerce domain. We use a relationship rich product Knowledge Graph to infuse auxiliary knowledge in a transformer based query rewriting deep neural network. Experiments on two tasks, query pruning and complete query rewriting, show that our proposed approach significantly outperforms a baseline BERT based query rewriting solution.

title: Knowledge Graph Completeness: a Definition and Assessment Centered on an Information Need
abstract: Over the last few years, driven by the growth of open data and e governments, there has been an increasing demand for transparency as well as accountability. These two concepts require particular information to be easily accessible, most common being the creator, the license, the modification dates, etc. According to us, the expression of such specific information need is central to the definition of these two concepts. This leads us to consider their assessment as a particular case of completeness, one aspect of data quality. In order to make the approach applicable to any case requiring information, this paper first formalizes the notion of information need based on a hierarchical structure. Then it defines completeness of a knowledge graph with respect to an information need. This enables to take into account preferences of the users which can vary significantly. The proposal is used to define a first measure of accountability of a knowledge graph, which enables to evaluate several RDF graphs of the linked open data. It appears that most of them do not provide accessible metadata about themselves. The others get various accountability results, including good ones, showing that linked data can be very suitable for accountability and more broadly transparency.

title: Integrating Knowledge Graph embedding and pretrained Language Models in Hypercomplex Spaces
abstract: Knowledge graphs, such as Wikidata, comprise structural and textual information in order to represent knowledge. For both kinds of information, dedicated approaches for graph embedding and language models learn patterns that allow for predicting novel structural knowledge. Some approaches have further integrated learning and inference with both types of information, but could not fully exploit the interaction of structural and textual information. We propose an approach that builds on existing strong representations of the graphs and texts, and we use hypercomplex algebra to model the interactions between (i) graph structural information and (ii) various different textual representations. More specifically, we suggest Dihedron and Quaternion modeling with 4*D dimensional hypercomplex numbers to integrate four different representations, namely structural knowledge graph embeddings, word level representations (e.g. Word2vec and FastText), sentence level representations (using a sentence transformer) and document level representations (using FastText or Doc2vec). Our unified framework based on the hypercomplex algebra scores the plausibility of labeled edges via Hamilton and Dihedron products, thus modeling pairwise interactions between any two of the four different representations. Extensive experimental evaluations on standard benchmark datasets shows the superiority of our two new models using abundant textual information in addition to sparse structural knowledge to enhance performance in link prediction tasks.

title: LitKGE: Improving numeric LITerals based Knowledge Graph Embedding models
abstract: Knowledge Graphs consist of a set of triples where a triple is a link between either two entity nodes (relational triple) or an entity node and a literal node (attributive triple). Similar to relational triples, attributive triples also provide semantics that could benefit the task of link prediction (LP) on KGs. Hence, some embedding based LP methods have been introduced in the past which leverage both kinds of triples. This paper introduces an approach named LitKGE where literals (specifically numerical literals) are further exploited to improve the task of LP by making implicit information that is present in the KG explicit. This is performed by generating property paths starting from an entity node leading to a literal node and considering the path as a feature for the entity. The features are then incorporated with existing LP or Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) methods. LitKGE is evaluated on three standard LP datasets, namely FB15K 237, YAGO3 10, and LitWD48K. The results indicate that LitKGE outperforms the existing KGE models which use numerical literals.

title: Automatically Inserting Emojis in Responses for Open Domain Emotion Controllable Dialogue Generation
abstract: With the development of emotional dialogue generation, the quality of automatic dialogue systems is getting higher and higher. Most existing works express emotions through plain texts only, which is not enough to represent the true emotion. Emojis, a cenozonic expression, have been used widely on the Internet. Emojis are not only more intuitive, but also more accurate in expressing emotions. In this paper, we endeavor to design an automatic emojis inserted open domain emotion controllable dialogue generation system EREI (Emotional Response with Emoji Inserted) to compensate for the deficiency of plain text expression. Specifically, we devise two modules, the emoji selector to track, quantify, calculate and select emojis and the type selector to classify the sentences according to the analysis of semantic representations. Both of the two components are combined and work together to help our model generate responses with contextual emojis and thus enrich the message contents. It is worth noting that our emojis inserted in the replies are not simply in line with the emotions, but also with people's habits and the characteristics of contemporary. Experimental results demonstrate that our model can produce appropriate emojis and vivid emotional responses.

title: TRack Entities to Preserve CONtext (TREPCON): A Transformer based approach to create a fully contextualized goal oriented dialogue system
abstract: End to end goal oriented dialogue systems face multiple challenges in incorporating knowledge graphs to generate valuable answers. Incorporating application domain knowledge into the generation process by accessing available knowledge has been shown to be a promising approach. For selecting the knowledge that is relevant for the generation of the correct answer, two main techniques proved their effectiveness when being used: (1) Achieving context sensitivity by including the entire history of the current dialogue into the generation process and (2) Static preselection of a likely relevant subset of the available knowledge. In this paper, we discuss the shortcomings of a static preselection approach and propose an approach based on entity tracking as a way of dynamic knowledge selection. Our approach allows for preserving the integrity of the conversation better than other techniques that statically merge knowledge graph information and dialogue history. Furthermore, we propose encoding the knowledge graph triples with informative key value representations and leveraging a transformer based approach to encode the knowledge to train the model to achieve context sensitivity to the entire dialogue when generating KG entities. Our TREPCON model consistently improves BLEU and entity F1 scores compared to eight state of the art approaches.

title: Towards a Knowledge Engineering Methodology for Flexible Robot Manipulation in Everyday Tasks
abstract: In the last decade, there have been great advancements in household robotics, enabling robots to autonomously accomplish household tasks including the preparation of dishes. These robots are typically pre programmed or trained for specific tasks only, and can not fulfill new requests. We hypothesize that this lack of flexibility in fulfilling new ad hoc task requests could be overcome by a knowledge based approach that allows robots to build upon and reuse existing knowledge to infer how to address a new task or carry out an already known task on a new object. Towards this goal, we propose a knowledge based methodology that leverages the knowledge that already exists on the Web to construct a manipulation relevant ontology that supports robots in reasoning on how to manipulate a specific object. The ontology comprises information about object dispositions and affordances as well as a taxonomy that decomposes a complex task into atomic steps. As a proof of concept for our approach, we construct a food cutting ontology that is assembled by importing and linking to knowledge from relevant ontologies in addition to extracting and semantically enhancing knowledge from unstructured Web sources. We demonstrate how robots can query the ontology and translate the contained information into action parameters. We further evaluate the feasibility of the created ontology by simulating the exemplary task of ``Quartering an apple" in a virtual environment.

title: Comparison of Knowledge Graph Representations for User Consumption Scenarios
abstract: With the wide adoption of knowledge graphs, multiple representation models have gained popularity beyond the original RDF model. However, there is currently no consensus about which of these representations is optimal for different user profiles and scenarios. In this work, we analyze the fitness of popular knowledge graph representations, i.e., Standard Reification, N Ary relations, Wikidata qualifiers, and RDF star, for consumption scenarios of three representative user profiles: knowledge explorers, knowledge engineers, and data scientists. We compare the accessibility for knowledge explorers through a user study with dedicated browsing interfaces. Considering the requirements of knowledge engineers, we investigate the query building suitability of different representations through a user study, and we compare query performance through queries on both synthetic and real world datasets. We measure the impact of the representation model choice for data scientists on the popular task of link prediction with graph embedding models. Our experiments suggest that Qualifiers and RDF star are better suited to support use cases of knowledge explorers and engineers, while Standard Reification models perform most consistently for data science inference tasks. The differences between the representation models largely depend on the properties of the queries and the data. We make our resources available to support future work to further improve the understanding of these representations and their role in real world scenarios.

title: Scalable Prediction of Atomic Candidate OWL Class Axioms Using a Vector Space Dimension Reduced Approach
abstract: Scoring candidate axioms or assessing their acceptability against known evidence, is essential for automated schema or ontology induction and can also be valuable for ontology and knowledge graph validation. However, traditional methods for accurately scoring candidate axioms are often computationally and storage expensive, making them impractical for use with larger ontologies. In this work, We propose a scalable method to predict the scores/labels of atomic candidate OWL class axioms of different types. The method relies on a semantic similarity measure derived from the ontological distance between concepts in a subsumption hierarchy, as well as feature selection for vector space dimension reduction. We train a machine learning model using our reduced vector space, encode new candidates as a vector, and predict their scores. Extensive tests that covered a range of ontologies of various sizes and multiple parameters and settings were carried out to investigate the effectiveness and scalability of the method.

title: Probabilistic Shapes Constraint Language
abstract: The Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL) is a W3C recommendation which allows to represent constraints in RDF ~shape graphs~ , and validate RDF data graphs against these constraints. A SHACL validator produces a validation report which result is false for a shape graph as soon as there is at least one node in the RDF data graph that do not conform the shape. This boolean result of the validation of an RDF data graph against an RDF shape graph is not suitable for discovering new high potential shapes from the RDF data. In this paper, we propose a probabilistic framework to accept shapes with a realistic proportion of nodes in an RDF data graph that does not conform to it. Based on this framework, we propose an extension of the SHACL validation report to express a set of metrics including the generality and likelihood of shapes and we define a method to test a shape as a hypothesis test. Finally, we present the results of experiments conducted to validate a test RDF data graph against a set of shapes.

title: Transformer based Semantic Relation Typing for Knowledge Graph Integration
abstract: More and more knowledge graphs (KGs) are generated in various domains. Applications using more than one KG require an integrated view on those KGs, which, in the first place, requires a common schema or ontology. Merging schemas requires not only equivalence mappings between classes, but also other semantic relations, like subclass, superclass etc. In this paper, we introduce a TaSeR, a Transformer based model for Semantic Relation Typing, which is able to decide which type of relation holds between two given classes. We experiment with different blocking approaches to generate the candidate set of class pairs. The approach can differentiate between equivalent class, sub /superclass, part of/has part, related, and no relation at all. With the latter outcome, it is not only possible to refine given class alignments but also filter incorrect correspondences. For the evaluation, a new measure is introduced which credits for proximal matches.

title: Semantically Constitutive Entities in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Knowledge graphs are repositories of facts about a world. Each fact or triple involves how a head entity is related to a tail entity. In this work, we seek to distill the set of entities or nodes in a knowledge graph into a specified number of constitutive nodes, whose embeddings would be retained. Intuitively, the remaining accessory nodes could have their original embeddings forgotten, and yet reconstitutable from those of the retained constitutive nodes. The constitutive nodes thus represent the semantically constitutive entities, which retain the core semantics of the knowledge graph.
