We propose a formulation as well as algorithmic solutions to minimize the reconstitution errors. The derived constitutive nodes are validated empirically both in quantitative and qualitative means on four publicly accessible knowledge graphs. Experiments show that the selected semantically constitutive entities outperform those selected based on structural properties alone.

title: Connecting FoodOn to a Wikidata Subgraph through Federated SPARQL Queries
abstract: Data sets involving food frequently are of interest across multiple cultural contexts. Many ontologies and vocabularies related to food are monolingual. Enriching ontologies and vocabularies with multilingual data is useful for extending access to a resource to wider audiences. The WikiFCD knowledge base of food composition data includes mappings to Wikidata and to FoodOn, a widely used ontology for food. In this paper we describe a sample of six food items from WikiFCD as the basis for an exploration of strategies for sourcing multilingual labels from projects of the Wikimedia Foundation. We present five subgraphs of data related to food items sourced from Wikidata, Wikipedias and WikiFCD. We describe the advantages and disadvantages of each subgraph. Each subgraph can be quickly retrieved from the Wikidata Query Service SPARQL endpoint or the SPARQL endpoint of WikiFCD. These strategies could be adapted to other domains seeking to enrich their data with multilingual labels.

title: Entity Linking for KGQA Using AMR Graphs
abstract: Entity linking is an essential part of analytical systems for question answering on knowledge graphs (KGQA). The mentioned entity has to be spotted in the text and linked to the correct resource in the knowledge graph (KG). With this paper, we present our approach on entity linking using the abstract meaning representation (AMR) of the question to spot the surface forms of entities. We re trained an existing AMR model with automatically generated training data. Based on this model, we extract surface forms and map them to an entity dictionary of the desired KG. For the disambiguation process, we evaluated different options and configurations on QALD 9 and LC QuaD 2.0. The results of the best performing configurations outperform existing entity linking approaches in part significantly.

title: Customized Concept Weighting: A Neural Network Approach
abstract: The aim of concept weighting in knowledge graphs is to characterize the importance of each concept in a specific domain, and to determine its selective power. This is particularly useful for data analysis tasks. Existing works on concept weighting mainly exploit either the graph's structure or the frequency of the concept in the data instances. These works provide concepts weights independently form the considered analysis task. We argue that these weights should vary according to the targeted task, and we introduce a neural network based approach which computes concept weights using regression on a customized multi layered structure. The loss function used in the approach is specified according to a given labelling of the elements in the considered dataset. In this paper, we present the principles of our weighting approach and we report on some experiments showing its effectiveness on real data extracted from the national library of France describing the documents' conservation histories.

title: REGNUM: Generating Logical Rules with Numerical Predicates in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Mining logical rules from a knowledge graph (KG) can reveal useful patterns for predicting facts, curating the KG, and identifying trends. However, many rule mining systems face challenges when working with numerical data because numerical predicates can take a large number of values, leading to a huge search space. In this work, we present REGNUM, a system that addresses this issue by generating rules with numerical constraints. REGNUM extends the body of rules mined from a KG by using supervised discretization of numerical values with decision trees to increase the confidence of the rules without sacrificing significance. Our experimental results show that the numerical rules have a higher overall quality than the parent rules and are effective at making better predictions.

title: Classifying sequences by combining context free grammars and OWL ontologies
abstract: This paper introduces a pattern to formalise context free grammars in OWL and how to use it for sequence classification. The proposed approach and existing methods are compared and discussed based on their complexity as well as their pragmatic applicability with examples in the music domain.

title: Decentralised Contract Conclusion on the Web Architecture a Gap Analysis
abstract: We investigate how contracts can get concluded by agents via the Web architecture. While other fields of research such as multi agent systems or e commerce have investigated different aspects of the problem, the peculiarities of the Web architectures pose specific challenges. We identify different aspects of the problem, discuss how different aspects of the problem are tackled in different communities, and propose a synthesis for the Web architecture, which builds on Social Linked Data (Solid), ie. HTTP based interaction between agents with WebIDs, where messages are described in RDF.

title: Overlay Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have become increasingly popular for their ability to capture complex relationships within graphs. However, a significant limitation of GNNs is their inability to capture long range relevant neighbors. This paper introduces Overlay Graph Neural Networks (OGNNs) to address this challenge. OGNNs are based on the combination of one or more overlay layers taking as input the graph and a node feature matrix, either available or derivable by analyzing the graph. Each overlay layer combines base embeddings learned by considering node features and short range node neighbors with overlay embeddings computed by projecting nodes with similar features close in an overlay space and then aggregating overlay neighbor nodes via a sliding window attention mechanism. Base and overlay embeddings are combined to capture nodes immediate and global context in a graph. We evaluate OGNNs in a node classification task using various benchmarks and show that OGNNs achieve state of the art results with the advantage of being easily portable to any existing GNN model.

title: Extraction of Fine grained Semantic Event Representations from Transformers
abstract: Major societal events, such as military conflicts and political elections, often have a complex nature and give rise to many related events. Knowledge graphs utilise event ontologies to represent these events and their characteristics. However, current event extraction approaches mainly focus on extracting coarse grained event classes and relations and fail to capture fine grained semantic event representations. To address this limitation, we propose SERT (Semantic Event Representations from Transformers), a method for extracting fine grained events, their classes, and relations from text using a target event ontology. SERT employs a two step process: i) multilabel event classification and ii) relation extraction based on a sequence to sequence transformer. Our experiments demonstrate that SERT outperforms state of the art event extraction baselines in event classification and relation extraction by 9 and, respectively, 11 percentage points according to the macro F1 score.

title: NASTyLinker: NIL Aware Scalable Transformer based Entity Linker
abstract: Entity Linking (EL) is the task of detecting mentions of entities in text and disambiguating them to a reference knowledge base. Most prevalent EL approaches assume that the reference knowledge base is complete. In practice, however, it is necessary to deal with the case of linking to an entity that is not contained in the knowledge base (NIL entity). Recent works have shown that, instead of focusing only on affinities between mentions and entities, considering inter mention affinities can be used to represent NIL entities by producing clusters of mentions. At the same time, inter mention affinities can help to substantially improve linking performance for known entities. With NASTyLinker, we introduce an EL approach that is aware of NIL entities and produces corresponding mention clusters while maintaining high linking performance for known entities. The approach clusters mentions and entities based on dense representations from Transformers and resolves conflicts (if more than one entity is assigned to a cluster) by computing transitive mention entity affinities. We show the effectiveness and scalability of NASTyLinker on NILK, a dataset that is explicitly constructed to evaluate EL with respect to NIL entities. Further, we apply the presented approach to an actual EL task, namely to knowledge graph population by linking entities in Wikipedia listings, and provide an analysis of the outcome.

title: Research on numerical knowledge representation method for mixed knowledge graph
abstract: In recent years, knowledge graphs have been widely used in various fields. This paper focuses on the mixed numerical and discrete knowledge graphs (mixed KG) in the field of industrial manufacturing. Through the knowledge graph embedding method, entities and relations are represented in a low dimensional continuous vector space. However, most of the existing research only deals with the discrete association between entities and relationships, while research on numerical entities is still rare. Therefore, this paper proposes three numerical entity knowledge representation methods (NumKRs) to effectively represent numerical entities. These three methods explore the representation of digital entities from different ways of data statistics, character semantics, and discretization. The experimental results show that the NumKRs effectively improve the performance of link prediction tasks between three different KGE methods, TransE, DisMult, and RotatE, and achieve state of the art results on the complex product dataset containing numerical and discrete entities.

title: iSummary: Workload based, Personalized summaries for Knowledge Graphs
abstract: The explosion in the size and the complexity of the available Knowledge Graphs on the web has led to the need for efficient and effective methods for their understanding and exploration. Semantic summaries have recently emerged as methods to quickly explore and understand the contents of various sources. However, in most cases, they are static, not incorporating user needs and preferences, and cannot scale. In this paper, we present iSummary, a novel, scalable approach for constructing personalized summaries. As the size and the complexity of the Knowledge Graphs for constructing personalized summaries prohibit efficient summary construction, in our approach we exploit query logs. The main idea behind our approach is to exploit knowledge captured in existing user queries for identifying the most interesting resources and linking them, constructing as such high quality, personalized summaries. We present an algorithm with theoretical guarantees on the summarys quality, linear in the number of queries available in the query log. We evaluate our approach using three real world datasets and several baselines, showing that our approach dominates other methods in terms of both quality and efficiency.

title: A Semantic Similarity Scoring Ontology based approach to support interoperability for IoT enabled applications
abstract: IoT data has the potential to be utilized in many domain specific applications to enable smart sensing in areas that were not initially covered during the conceptualization phase of these applications. Typically, data collected in IoT scenarios serve a specific purpose and follow heterogeneous data models and domain specific ontologies. Therefore, IoT data could not easily be integrated to domain specific applications as it requires ontology alignment of diverse data models with the end application. This poses a big challenge to semantic interoperability during the integration of IoT data into a pre established system. In this line, the alignment process is cumbersome and challenging for an ontology engineer, since it requires shortlisting manually the relevant ontologies that could be aligned to the IoT data to align each term used in IoT data with the concepts defined in the domain specific ontologies. In this paper, we propose a solution that supports the alignment process by utilizing Natural Language Processing (NLP) and semantic web technologies. Our novel solution proposes a Data and Information Interoperability Model (DIIM) based Semantic Similarity Score Ontology (S3O) that automatically identify the relevant terms used in Internet of Things (IoT) data and ontologies and stores the similarity scores among terms based on various similarity algorithms. We showcase our solution by aligning IoT sensor data with water domain specific ontologies.

title: Notation3 as an Existential Rule Language
abstract: Notation3 Logic (N3) is an extension of RDF which allows the user to write rules introducing new blank nodes to RDF graphs. Many applications, like for example ontology mapping, rely on this feature as blank nodes used directly or in auxiliary constructs like reification are omnipresent on the Web. However, the use of blank nodes in rule heads often impairs the performance of N3 reasoners. On the other hand, there are many engines like for example VLog or Vadalog developed for existential rules. These are optimised for these kinds of constructs but do not directly support Semantic Web rule formats. In this paper we investigate the relation between Notation3 rules with blank nodes in their head and existential rules. We define a subset of N3 which excludes special constructs of the language and built in functions. We provide a direct mapping from this subset to existential rules which preserves and reflects equivalence of N3 formulas. This mapping is then employed in practise to compare the performance of the N3 reasoners EYE and Cwm on N3 rules to VLog on the mapped counterparts. By using the existential rule reasoner on rules relying on blank node introduction we could severely decrease reasoning times while this was not the case for rule sets lacking this feature. With our implementation we enable the Semantic Web community to directly benefit from the recent findings in existential rule reasoning.

title: Data Augmented Knowledge Graph Completion via Pre trained Language Models
abstract: Knowledge graphs provide significant assistance for many artificial intelligence tasks, but they are usually incomplete. Techniques for knowledge graph completion can improve the coverage of Knowledge Graphs (KGs) by inducing new facts. Traditional methods for completion use structural representations in embedding space, but textual information can also be helpful. Recently, pre trained language models have shown impressive performance on natural language processing tasks. KG BERT is a pre trained language model that is used for knowledge graph completion and achieves appealing performance. However, KG BERT struggles when the number of facts is inadequate. We consider the inadequacy of data for various relations and the compensation for sparsity via data augmentation. We propose two knowledge graph data augmentation methods to generate facts with novel relations. Specifically, multi hop relations between two entities are extracted to form multi hop facts, and implicit relations are generated by Horn rules. Moreover, we find multi hop facts are useful for few shot learning scenario. Our system improves the performance of KG BERT regarding the accuracy of the link prediction task. The experimental results demonstrate that our models make significant enhancements for KG BERT and outperform the state of the art systems on knowledge graph completion benchmarks (e.g., WN18RR and UMLS).

title: HintMiner: Automatic Question Hints Mining From Q\&A Web Posts
abstract: Users often need ask questions and seek answers online. The Question Answering (QA) forums such as Stack Overflow cannot always respond to the questions timely and properly. In this paper, we propose HintMiner, a novel automatic question hints mining tool for users to help them find answers. HintMiner leverages the machine comprehension and sequence generation techniques to automatically generate hints for users' questions. It firstly retrieve many web Q\&A posts and then extract some hints from the posts using MiningNet. The MiningNet is a neural encoder decoder model based on the transformer and copying mechanisms. We have evaluated HintMiner on 60,000 Stack Overflow questions. The experiment results show that the proposed approach is effective. For example, HintMiner achieves an average BLEU score of 36.17\% and an average ROUGE 2 score of 36.29\%. Our tool and experimental data are publicly available. \footnote{\url{https://github.com/AnonymousAuthor2013/HintMiner}}.

title: "GraphQL will rewrite the Semantic Web'' A promise not yet kept
abstract: When Facebook publicly released the GraphQL framework in 2015, experts in the Semantic Web community had the feeling that it would rewrite the semantic web. This article revises the usage of GraphQL in the Semantic Web by performing a systematic literature review to verify if and to what extent this promise has been kept. We looked for academy and enterprise solutions published as peer reviewed contributions on Scopus, ACM Digital library, and IEEE Explore, and developers' contributions publicly available on GitHub. As a result, it demonstrates that the academy, enterprises, and developers have experimented with using GraphQL for authoring Semantic Web based solutions, accessing Knowledge Graphs, integrating or replacing SPARQL, or as a SPARQL proxy. However, GraphQL still requires time to gain an official and standard role in the Semantic Web. We summarise the potentialities and the limitations to guarantee a wider diffusion of GraphQL in the Semantic Web community.

title: OPPO: An Ontology for Describing Fine Grained Data Practices in Privacy Policies of Online Social Networks
abstract: Privacy policies outline the data practices of Online Social Networks (OSN) to comply with privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA. However, privacy policies often do not explicitly or not sufficiently mention the data practices of an OSN. Prior works have developed frameworks and ontologies for checking non compliance between policies and regulations, but they are limited to identifying data practices at very coarse levels. Towards the goal of better understanding to what extent privacy policies comply with regulations, this paper develops a conceptual model of the concepts and relations needed to describe data practices in greater detail. We formally capture the model as an OWL ontology. To illustrate our models generality and extendability, we identify and analyze data practices and security mechanisms in more detail and encode these details as extensions to the general ontology. We populate the complete ontology with data from a sample privacy policy Telegram, and then evaluate its internal and external consistency, adherence to best practices in ontology design, and ability to express and answer sample questions about the privacy policies.

title: SEEK: Two stage Text summarization using semantics aware and external knowledge
abstract: Text summarization aims to extract important information from a given document, which is a challenging, but an important task in natural language processing. In this paper, we put forward a novel semantics aware mechanism (SAM) to capture the global semantics of the document, which collects the latent topics in the document to assist with text summarization task. On the other hand, to enhance topical expression and build the relationship between entities, we attempt to jointly generate summarization with both semantics aware mechanism and external knowledge. We raise a new structured model, Semantics Aware Text Summarization Using External Knowledge(SEEK), which generates the summarization with two stages(capture phase and enhancement phase). For better evaluating text summarization models, we define a human evaluation criterion TS(Topic Similarity) to measure global semantics. Our experimental results on benchmark datasets outperform state of the art summarization models.

title: Relational Message Aggregation for Inductive Link Prediction with Entity Type Constraints
abstract: Inductive link prediction, in which entities unseen during training may appear in the testing phase, has been shown to be promising to complete the constantly updated knowledge graphs (KGs). Existing methods mainly use relational message aggregation to predict missing links by generating relational subgraphs and extracting logical structures. However, many methods focus on edge information and obtain entity features through adjacent edges, which is not friendly to sparse KGs. In this work, we consider semantic descriptions of entities and propose etRAN, a novel relational message aggregation model with entity type constraints. etRAN can choose techniques to obtain entity types under different description information, and then combine edge structures and entity types to form relational paths. Therefore, our model can generate logic rules that contain both structured and semantic information. In the aggregation phase, we consider the importance of different relation paths by using an attention mechanism. Specifically, we incorporate prior knowledge into type constraints and embed them into adjacent relations for weight assignment. Our experimental results show improvement in whether large or tiny datasets and the progress is more evident on sparse knowledge graphs. It indicates that our model is capable of KGs with limited relational message. We also combine our model with embedding based methods to represent the entity type. Then we separate the combined models in ablation experiments, and the results show that the combined models outperform their individual counterparts.

title: Common Sense Knowledge based Zero Shot Relationship Retrieval for Generalized Scene Graph Generation
abstract: Scene graphs are structured, symbolic representations of images that model objects as nodes and relationships between objects as edges in a graph. They are widely used in visual reasoning tasks such as visual question answering, image retrieval, image captioning, multimedia event processing, etc. Existing scene graph generation methods struggle to handle unseen visual relationships, as they rely on crowdsourced training datasets with a highly imbalanced distribution of visual relationships in which more meaningful and expressive visual relationships are underrepresented. Moreover, collecting and collating sufficient training samples for all visual relationships in the real world is nearly impossible. This challenge can be alleviated via a zero shot approach coupled with rich, diverse common sense knowledge. We propose a zero shot relationship retrieval method based on heterogeneous knowledge graphs that capture the maximum diversity of common sense knowledge among other knowledge sources. The proposed method detects objects in the image and retrieves relationships from the common sense knowledge graph relevant to and shared among each pair of objects based on structural and semantic similarity in the embedding space. Then, the redundant and irrelevant triplets are discarded and the scene graph of the image is constructed. We performed an extensive experimental and comparative analysis of the proposed method on the Visual Genome benchmark dataset using the standard evaluation metrics. The proposed method surpassed the previous state of the art method with a considerable improvement of over 10% in the zero shot recall rate, i.e. zR@K increased from 22.22 to 24.47 for K=100, thus demonstrating its effectiveness for generating generalized scene graphs.

title: Multi level Deduplication in Knowledge Graphs: A Self Organizing Neural Network Approach
abstract: A knowledge graph (KG) constructed initially based on an unstructured source of document may contain redundant information. Eliminating such redundancy in KG is necessary to reduce the required storage resources and improve the graph interpretability. However, such redundancy may involve complex interconnecting nodes and edges such that simply deduplicating every individual node is insufficient or even leading to catastrophic lost of meaningful information. Most existing methods for deduplication in KG are still focused on individual entities based on the assumption that they can be considered as redundant if they are similar or identical, but rarely look at the context of how they are related to one another in the KG. In this paper, a new KG deduplication method is presented that detects redundancies spanning from single duplicated edges to long branching paths of nodes and relations in the graph. The deduplication process is conducted iteratively in multiple levels by combining representation learning and a novel clustering method based on a multi channel self organizing neural network to obtain the graph structural model associated with its complex redundant paths. Designed to encode multi modal patterns, the neural network combines the embedding vector representation with the contexts from related entities in the graph to effectively distinguish redundant information from the non redundant ones. Experimental studies are conducted to evaluate the proposed method against different complexities of redundancy in KGs with different clustering methods. It is demonstrated that the combination of iterative graph embeddings with multi level clustering by the neural network can effectively deduplicate complex redundancies in KG compared against state of the arts clustering algorithms.

title: Ontological modeling of sequences for Modern Greek derivation
abstract: In the present article, we explore ontological models about sequences in order to test them towards a Modern Greek (MG) morphological example. Among the explored models are rdf:List and rdf:Seq, URI based and number based patterns, the Sequence Ontology Pattern (SOP) or more holistic initiatives such as the Ordered List Ontology (OLO), the Collections Ontology (CO) and the ORE specification. After presenting the related morphological framework by analyzing MG indicative word sequence patterns, a common lexical example is represented by each one of the aforementioned models to evaluate their suitability according to specific benchmarks. These include entity analysis, item indexing and size of a sequence, ordering semantics, model usability and lightweightness. Conclusively, we opt for the CO as the most fine grained, referenced and axiomatized model, which we also use to express indicative SPARQL Query Expansion (QE) cases, despite the heaviness that the amount of constituent items would entail.

title: Query Optimization for Ontology Mediated Query Answering
abstract: Ontology mediated query answering (OMQA) consists in asking database queries on first order logic (FOL) knowledge bases (KB); a KB is a database (a set of facts) on which an ontology (a set of deductive constraints) holds. The main OMQA technique is FOL rewritability: each query asked on a KB is reformulated w.r.t. the KB's ontology so that the relational evaluation of this reformulated query on the KB's database computes the correct answers. Crucially, because this technique compiles ontology constraints into queries, reformulated queries may be complex and their optimization is the crux of efficiency. In this paper, we devise a novel, general OMQA optimization framework for FOL rewritability of queries asked on datalog+/ , description logic, existential rules, OWL or RDF/S KBs. Our contributions are threefold. First, we revise the original definition of FOL rewritability in order to enable simpler (contained) reformulated queries with the same answers, which can be evaluated faster. Second, we provide a generic algorithm that computes such simpler reformulated queries from the ones computed by any off the shelf algorithm for FOL rewritability. Finally, we experimentally show on a well established benchmark that our optimized reformulated queries significantly improves OMQA performance in general, up to several orders of magnitude!

title: Enhancing Pre trained Language Models via Mutual Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Knowledge completion systems rely on pre trained language models (PLM) to overcome the efforts needed to build and continuously update knowledge bases (KB). Current state of the art models solve this task following a retriever reader framework, where the system first filters documents and then extracts or generates the answers following evidence. PLMs show great performance as part of the knwledge completion pipeline, either as a retriever or as a reader. In this paper, we formulate an original cooperative pre training procedure and enhance PLM to address entities on knowledge completion tasks. We show that integrating manually annotated and rich information about entities from KBs into neural language representation models leads to a global improvement of the candidates. We explore a new direction by mutually training PLM and KB representation models via knowledge distillation. We argue that the textual corpus and KB represent two distinct and complementary spaces for knowledge intensive tasks. Training them via a dynamic environment, where roles interchange between teachers and students, leads to an improved ability to process entities and competitive results on two standard datasets for slot filling, namely T REx and zsRE.

title: Declarative RDF Graph Construction: Materialization or Virtualization?
abstract: RDF graphs are commonly derived from (semi )structured data by applying a set of mapping rules. RDF graph construction is performed by either materializing an RDF graph and storing it into a triplestore, or virtualizing the RDF graph by translating SPARQL queries into the query language of the underlying data sources. The choice between materialization or virtualization of an RDF graph is often based on experience or preference as there are no studies yet that provide sufficient evidence to decide on when to materialize or virtualize an RDF graph. On one hand, a large number of RDF construction engines were proposed optimizing the RDF construction in terms of performance, and they were compared among each other. On the other hand, the few virtualization systems that exist nowadays were only compared to triplestores. In this paper, we investigate the impact of data, mapping rules, and queries on materialization and virtualization through synthetic and real data benchmarks. Virtualization requires less time to answer a query if the number of records increases but imposes restrictions on query expressivity. Materialization performs better and ensures answers for complex queries and mapping rules, and becomes as good or even better than virtualization if the RDF loading into the triplestore is excluded. We identify bottlenecks and opportunities for improvements, enable more informed decisions, and open the way towards hybrid systems.

title: Neural Class Expression Synthesis
abstract: Many applications require explainable node classification in knowledge graphs. Towards this end, a popular ``white box'' approach is class expression learning: Given sets of positive and negative nodes, class expressions in description logics are learned that separate positive from negative nodes. Most existing approaches are search based approaches generating many candidate class expressions and selecting the best one. However, they often take a long time to find suitable class expressions. In this paper, we cast class expression learning as a translation problem and propose a new family of class expression learning approaches which we dub neural class expression synthesizers. Training examples are ``translated'' into class expressions in a fashion akin to machine translation. Consequently, our synthesizers are not subject to the runtime limitations of search based approaches. We study three instances of this novel family of approaches based on LSTMs, GRUs, and set transformers, respectively. An evaluation of our approach on four benchmark datasets suggests that it can effectively synthesize high quality class expressions with respect to the input examples in approximately one second on average. Moreover, a comparison to state of the art approaches suggests that we achieve better F measures on large datasets. For reproducibility purposes, we provide our implementation as well as pretrained models in our public GitHub repository at https://github.com/fosterreproducibleresearch/NCES

title: Evaluating Language Models for Knowledge Base Completion
abstract: The rapid growth of knowledge raises the need for constant updates to existing knowledge bases (KBs) a time consuming, manual task, hindering scale of current knowledge bases. Recently, language models (LMs) have been proposed for unsupervised knowledge extraction from large scale text sources such as Wikipedia. In this work, we investigate the idea of automated KB completion from text sources using LMs. Realistic evaluation of KB completion with prior knowledge extraction benchmarks is problematic since they provide curated subject sets and sample already existing facts from KBs. Therefore, in this work, we introduce a novel, more challenging benchmark dataset and a methodology tailored for realistic assessment. Specifically, our dataset, dubbed WD Known, is an unbiased random sample of Wikidata, containing 3.9 million existing facts (in contrast to only 34k in LAMA). For the evaluation of facts non existent in the KB, we extract plausible subject relation pairs with non existent objects in the KB. Using the LM on these facts, we obtain actual novel facts, previously unknown to the KB. Since the ground truth of these answers is unknown, we perform a human evaluation. Our key finding is that biases in dataset conception of previous benchmarks lead to a systematic overestimate of LM performance for KB completion. However, our results also reveal knowledge areas of LMs. We, for example, perform significant completion of Wikidata on relation \textit{nativeLanguage} by a factor of ~21 (from 260k to 5.8M) at 82% precision. Moreover, we find LMs can build surprisingly strong generalization capabilities: even on relations where most facts were not directly included in the LM training data, prediction quality is high enough for allowing KB completion. We open source the novel benchmark including data, code and method for follow up research.

title: Evaluating Continuous Basic Graph Patterns over Dynamic Link Data Graphs
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the problem of evaluating Basic Graph Patterns (BGP, for short, a subclass of SPARQL queries) over dynamic Linked Data graphs; i.e., Linked Data graphs that are continuously updated. We consider a setting where the updates are continuously received through a stream of messages and support both insertions and deletions of triples (updates are straightforwardly handled as a combination of deletions and insertions). In this context, we propose a set of in memory algorithms minimizing the cached data for efficiently and continuously answering main subclasses of BGP queries. The queries are typically submitted into a system and continuously result the delta answers while the update messages are processed. Consolidating all the historical delta answers, the algorithms ensure that the answer of each query is constructed at any given time.

title: Recommendations Become Even More Useful: Multi task Extension of Scientific Collaborations Forecasting
abstract: Prediction of collaborations between scientists is a well known challenge that could be interpreted as the forecasting of links' emergence in co authorship graphs. The recent success of graph neural networks allowed to achieve supreme performance in this task, especially in comparison with early approaches based on node level similarity score utilization. However, the aggregation of additional information from adjacent structures for the needs of this task is still underdeveloped up to the present moment. In this paper, we introduce a novel end to end pipeline for the assessment of scientific collaborations based on the aggregation of data from both citation graphs and co authorship networks. As another crucial feature, we have developed the domain specific multi task extension of the classic link prediction task and deployed the model as a web service, which could serve as a basis for further industrial implementation.

title: Double Graph Based Feature Fusion for Document level Named Entity Recognition
abstract: Most named entity recognition models are used to process each sentence within a document. However, these models do not make full use of document information to predict entity. Existed document level NER only considered character level and word level features while ignoring the importance of document level features. To address this problem, we introduce a double graph based feature fusion model for document level named entity recognition. Firstly, word level embeddings and character level embeddings are concatenated to encode with BiLSTM. Secondly, word level graphs and sentence level graphs are constructed and node update strategies are used to update node embeddings. Finally, word node and sentence node embeddings are concatenated to feed into a sequence labeling model to predict entities. Experimental results show that our model in F1 achieves 92.12\% and 88.19\% on CoNLL 2003 and DocRED datasets, respectively.

title: A Scalable Database for Syntactic and Lexical Resources
abstract: Natural language generation from ontologies is a recurrent topic but yet the proper connection between semantic properties and their verbalization in a natural language is often insufficient or simply left to external components. We present a novel database engine tailored specifically for storing syntactic rules as well as lexical entries for natural language generation. The engine supports an unlimited number of languages which are moreover linked via an abstract syntax making it easier to generate content in several languages simultaneously. Dynamic addition and removal of data is possible. Transactions ensure the data integrity and enforce single writer multiple readers exclusion policy. The writer does not block the readers.

title: Explainable Integration of Knowledge Graphs using Large Language Model
abstract: Linked knowledge graphs build the backbone of many data driven applications such as search engines, conversational agents and e commerce solutions. Declarative link discovery frameworks use complex link specifications to express the conditions under which a link between two resources can be deemed to exist. However, understanding such complex link specifications is a challenging task for non expert users of link discovery frameworks. In this paper, we address this drawback by devising NMV LS, a language model based verbalization approach for translating complex link specifications into natural language. NMV LS relies on the results of rule based link specification verbalization to apply continuous training on T5, a large language model based on the Transformer architecture. We evaluated NMV LS on English and German datasets using well known machine translation metrics such as BLUE, METEOR, ChrF++ and TER. Our results suggest that our approach achieves a verbalization performance close to that of humans and outperforms state of the art approaches.

title: Subsumption Prediction on E Commerce Taxonomies
abstract: Taxonomy plays a key role in e commerce, categorising items and facilitating both search and inventory management. Concept subsumption prediction is critical for taxonomy curation, and has been the subject of several studies, but they do not fully utilise the categorical information available in e commerce settings. In this paper, we study the characteristics of e commerce taxonomies, and propose a new subsumption prediction method based on the pre trained language model BERT that is well adapted to the e commerce setting. The proposed model utilises textual and structural semantics in a taxonomy, as well as the rich and noisy instance (item) information. We show through extensive evaluation on two large scale e commerce taxonomies from eBay and AliOpenKG, that our method offers substantial improvement over strong baselines.

title: Memory Net: Generalizable Common Sense Reasoning over Real World Actions and Objects
abstract: We address the problem of situated reasoning of artificial agents (AA) in human like environments. In particular, we want the AAs to reason about so called action patterns in a real world human environment: e.g., which tools can be used for a certain action, which actions can be performed with certain tools and objects, and so on. This should occur in a situated way, i.e., always referring to concrete instances in a real world environment. For this purpose, we develop a representational concept based on knowledge graphs. We consistently populate a large scale knowledge graph (Memory Net) with densely interrelated everyday concepts, common sense action patterns, and environment information. We then propose an inference mechanism that uses semantic proximity by approximate subgraph matching, which allows broad semantic generalization. As a proof of concept, the system is compared with human data and a state of the art neural language model based machine learning approach, responding tool questions in a home environment setting. The results show that the Knowledge Graph approach is able to generalize well for this type of tasks, with considerable benefits in terms of applicability in variable, incremental and interactive settings.

title: New Workflow for Reusing Ontologies Based on Requirements Semantic Similarities
abstract: One of the cornerstones of many ontology engineering methodologies is the reuse of ontologies in order to save development time and rely on fragments of knowledge that have been already validated through use. While approaches to ontology reuse have gained traction during the past twenty years, there is still a dearth of practical solutions that allow developers to easily assess how suitable a candidate ontology is to be reused for a new set of requirements. This paper proposes a novel process, to be embedded in existing ontology engineering methodologies, that determines a set of candidate ontologies to be reused on the grounds of the similarity between the requirements of the new ontology being developed and those of an existing set of potential candidates, e.g. ontologies in an ontology portal. We illustrate the proposed method by means of a use case and evaluate its accuracy with the support of a domain expert. These preliminary results confirm that the proposed approach can identify ontologies with similar requirements to those of an ontology under development and that, therefore, have the potential to be reused (at least in part). Furthermore, we discuss the challenges that need to be addressed in order to support ontology developers in easily exploiting a list of candidate ontologies for reuse.

title: Characterizing Nexus of Similarity within Knowledge Bases
abstract: Similarities between entities daily occur in many real world scenarios. In more than a century, researchers in different fields have proposed a range of approaches to measure the similarity between entities. More recently, inspired by "Google Sets", considerable academic and commercial efforts have been devoted to expanding a given set of entities with new similar ones. As a result, existing approaches nowadays are able to take into account properties shared by entities, hereinafter called nexus of similarity. Accordingly, machines are largely able to deal with both similarity measures and set expansions. To the best of our knowledge, however, there is no way to characterize nexus of similarity between, namely identifying them nexus in a formal and comprehensive way so that they are both machine and human readable; moreover, there is no clear consensus on how to assess existing approaches when entities are weakly similar. As a first step towards filling these gaps, the paper aims to complement existing methods by proposing a formal semantics to deal with nexus of similarity. To do that, we develop a novel logic based framework to formally and automatically characterize nexus of similarity between tuples of entities within a knowledge base.

title: Two view Graph Neural Networks for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: We present an effective GNN based knowledge graph embedding model, named WGE, to capture entity and relation focused graph structures. Given the knowledge graph, WGE builds a single undirected entity focused graph that views entities as nodes. WGE also constructs another single undirected graph from relation focused constraints, which views entities and relations as nodes. WGE then proposes a GNN based architecture to better learn vector representations of entities and relations from these two single entity and relation focused graphs. WGE feeds the learned entity and relation representations into a weighted score function to return the triple scores for knowledge graph completion. Experimental results show that WGE outperforms competitive baselines, obtaining state of the art performances on seven benchmark datasets for knowledge graph completion.

title: SMARTER: Hierarchical Graph Summarization for Progressive Query Processing
abstract: Graph summarization techniques are well established in several research areas, leading to many benefits, such as volume and storage reduction, interactive visualization, noise elimination, and query speedup. Despite this, semantic graph summarization approaches have not yet achieved an optimal trade off between accuracy and performance. In this paper, we introduce SMARTER, a hierarchy based semantic graph summarization technique and show its flexibility and efficiency for query processing. By adding typing information to the summary, we build quotient summaries on top of RDF graphs, allowing summarization according to the levels of the graph's structural hierarchy. As such, the obtained graph summaries can be used for progressive query processing, leading to evaluate a query progressively from coarse grained levels until fine grained ones, thus striking a balance between accuracy and performance. The extensive experimental study on real world graph datasets, with varied query workloads, show the effectiveness and the efficiency of SMARTER, on both exact and progressive query answering.

title: Co Driven Recognition of Chinese Semantic Entailment via the Fusion of Transformer and HowNet Sememes Knowledge
abstract: Chinese semantic entailment recognition aims to detect and judge whether the semantics of two Chinese sentences are consistent and whether there is entailment relationship. However, the existing methods usually face the challenges of chinese synonyms, polysemy and difficulty to understand long texts. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a co driven Chinese semantic entailment recognition method based on the fusion of Transformer and HowNet sememes knowledge. The experimental results on financial and multi semantic interpretation data sets such as BQ, AFQMC, PAWSX, etc. show that, compared with lightweight models such as DSSM, MwAN, DRCN, and pretraining models such as ERNIE, this model can not only effectively improve the accuracy of Chinese semantic implication recognition (by 2.19%, 5.57% and 6.51% compared with the DSSM, MwAN and the DRCN model on the BQ dataset), control the number of model parameters (about 16M), but also adapt to long text implication recognition scenarios of more than 50 words.

title: Heterogeneous Graph Interaction based Event Extraction with Attentional Position Embeddings
abstract: Document level event extraction has become one of the important research directions in natural language processing, which aims to extract the complete event arguments from the whole document. However, existing models cannot fully utilize contextual semantic relations and sequential information in complex document level scenarios, failing to mine the relational facts between multiple sentences and arguments. To address the above problems, we propose a heterogeneous graph interaction event extraction model fusing positional embedding and attention matrix called GPAIT. Firstly, contextual semantic relationships are enhanced between entities by constructing entity attention relationship matrix; Secondly, the attention matrix is combined to rectify the representation of heterogeneous graphs; Finally, positional embedding is fused into graphs to build a graph convolutional neural network that can better capture semantic sequential relationships. Experiments on ChFinAnn and COVID 19 News show that GPAIT outperforms other document level event extraction methods in terms of F1 by 1.2% and 3.6% respectively.

title: ProductE: Embedding Temporal Knowledge Graphs in a Product Space of Heterogeneous Geometric Subspaces
abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs represent temporal facts (s, p, o, tau ) relating a subject s and an object o via a relation label p during a time interval tau . Temporal knowledge graphs may exhibit static temporal patterns at distinct points in time and dynamic temporal patterns between different timestamps. For example, a friendship relation between six students might exhibit a static temporal pattern corresponding to a 6 clique at the time of their enrolment but change to two static temporal patterns of disjoint triangles after their graduation. The change from a 6 clique to two triangles can be described as a dynamic structural temporal pattern of subgroup formation. In order to learn a rich set of static and dynamic temporal patterns and apply them for inference, several embedding approaches have been suggested in the literature. However, as they all resorted to single underlying embedding spaces, their capability to model all kinds of temporal patterns was severely limited by having to adhere to the geometric property of their one embedding space. We lift this limitation by an embedding approach that maps temporal facts into a product space of several heterogeneous geometric subspaces with distinct geometric properties, i.e. Complex, Dual and Split complex spaces. In addition, we propose two temporal attention mechanisms. The temporal relational attention mechanism captures various relations with different degrees of temporality. The temporal geometric attention mechanism fuse information from different geometric subspaces according to the captured relational and temporal information. Experimental results on standard temporal benchmark datasets favorably evaluate our approach against state of the art model.

title: RDF star2Vec: RDF star Graph Embeddings for Data Mining
abstract: Knowledge graph embedding (KGE) is used in machine learning tasks such as node classification and link prediction and is an important research topic in the semantic web community. RDF star introduces quoted triple (QT), which is a triple used as the subject or object of another triple, and also can use a QT for the compositional entities of another QT. Hence, RDF star can represent recursive hyper relational KGs that contain nested structures. However, existing KGE models cannot adequately learn the semantics of QTs and entities because they do not consider complex RDF star graphs containing QT QT relations and multi leveled nested QTs. In this paper, we propose RDF star2Vec, a novel KGE model for RDF star graphs, which introduces graph walk methods that allow probabilistic transition between a QT and its compositional entities. The feature vectors of QTs, entities and relations are obtained from the generated sequences using the structured skip gram model. Furthermore, we provide a dataset and benchmarking framework for data mining tasks of complex RDF star graphs to facilitate developing and evaluating KGE models for RDF star. Evaluation experiments showed that RDF star2Vec outperformed recent extensions of RDF2Vec in classification, clustering, entity relatedness, and QT similarity tasks.

title: Open domain Taxonomy Induction with Structure Optimization
abstract: Taxonomies provide hierarchical knowledge to assist various downstream applications, recommendation systems, web search, and question answering. However, due to the comprehensive coverage and tangled links of open domain sources, the generated taxonomies still suffer from a sub optimal structure. One of the essential manifestations is that the granularity of ``siblings is inconsistent, and there are still potential hierarchical relationships between these nodes. An iterative taxonomy induction framework based on distant supervision is proposed to alleviate this problem. First, we extract high quality seed taxonomy by pattern matching with the external knowledge base. Second, we enrich the semantic coverage of the seed taxonomy by considering the insertion order when using the distributional model. As the core component of our framework, we further detect the potential is a pairs between ``siblings by learning a contrastive model of fine grained hierarchical relationships. Finally, we utilize error detection to ensure the accuracy of the taxonomy. Experiments on this and several public benchmarks verify the effectiveness of our approach.

title: TunA: Tunable Query Optimizer for Web APIs and User Preferences
abstract: To answer queries many query processors combine different SPARQL sources, e.g., various knowledge bases (KBs) or APIs. RESTful Web APIs are rarely the focus of those systems as they come with many limitations, such as not being able to process SPARQL queries. Additionally, most existing approaches optimize their query plans only for performance, even though users often have additional preferences regarding coverage, reliability, or currency. In addition, data is often provided with different levels of quality so that not all sources should be trusted equally. In this paper, we therefore present TunA a query engine that is able to combine RESTful Web APIs and local RDF KBs in the form of triple stores while tuning its (query) plans towards user preferences. Erroneous information from Web APIs is detected using hierarchical agglomerative clustering. Our evaluation shows that TunA outperforms current state of the art systems and is less vulnerable to erroneous information, even in settings where only unreliable sources are available.

title: Transformer Based Entity Extractor for Intelligence and Security Informatics
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of closed domain information extraction (IE) for intelligence and security informatics domain. We propose a BERT based model to identify entities that are undetermined by standard NERs. We approach the problem of IE as a) text classification and b) named entity recognizer. We conduct our experiments on incident summaries present in Global Terrorism Database (GTD). We apply BERT based transformer encoder models for both tasks, revealing the advantages of using pre trained models that can be fine tuned for domain specific tasks to achieve significantly good results. We also propose an annotation enrichment algorithm for NER to address the challenges of poorly labelled instances. The results reveal that despite the class imbalance, our model gives an average classification precision of 80% for targettype, attacktype, weapontype and recognizes the entities (gname, place, and target) with an average precision of 88%.

title: Embedding $\mathcal{ALC}$ ontology for symbol grounding
abstract: The symbol grounding problem is a challenge in the field of Artificial Intelligence and Cognitive Science that concerns the question of how words or symbols in a language get their meanings and what meaning they really are, or how they can be connected to the objects or ideas they represent. Current RDF(S) based ontology embedding approaches have achieved notable success in solving the symbol grounding problems like link prediction and ontology population. However, they cannot handle complex situations requiring higher level knowledge due to the lack of expressive definitions of the symbols to be grounded. OWL based ontology embedding approaches have thus been developed, with current attempts stopping at embedding $\mathcal{EL}$++ ontologies, which are limited in the expressive power available for specifying concepts, relationships, and logical statements though. In this paper, we advance this line of work to the language of $\mathcal{ALC}$, a more expressive description logic that allows for the specification of a wider range of concepts and relationships, and in particular, we propose differentiable fuzzy $\mathcal{ALC}$ (DF $\mathcal{ALC}$) as a general $\mathcal{ALC}$ ontology embedding approach to address the variable symbol grounding problem. DF $\mathcal{ALC}$ injects an $\mathcal{ALC}$ ontology into neural models through differentiable concepts and role embeddings, where a hierarchical loss is defined to revise the grounding learned by the neural model based on the semantics of fuzzy $\mathcal{ALC}$. As simply capturing the semantics of the grounding by maximizing satisfiability according to the semantics of fuzzy $\mathcal{ALC}$ does not reasonably correct grounding, we further define a rule based loss for DF $\mathcal{ALC}$ which models revision rules in learning. Experimental results show that unsupervised learning with DF $\mathcal{ALC}$ represented ontology and rule based loss improves the performance of image object detectors ($\uparrow$2.35\% F1), even in the low resource case.

title: Sedenion valued Embeddings in Knowledge Graph Fact Validation
abstract: Knowledge graph embedding research has mainly focused on learning real and complex valued vector representations for knowledge graphs. Few recent works suggested the benefits of quaternion and octonion valued representations in the link prediction task. Such models can be framed as models learning in 1 ,2 ,4 and 8 dimensional Cayley Dickson algebras. In this work, we propose learning knowledge graph embeddings in the 16 dimensional Cayley Dickson algebra over real numbers, i.e., learning sedenion valued representations. We evaluate this approach on two widely used benchmark datasets on the tasks of link prediction and fact validation. The evaluation results suggest that while our sedenion based embeddings SedE do not perform well in the link prediction task, they outperform QMult on both datasets and QuatE on one while achieving a similar performance on the other dataset. We provide our implementation of this approach at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/sedenion embeddings C0E4/, and datasets, pre trained models and evaluation data at https://figshare.com/s/97fa4c9c21bae16189ca.

title: Why Just RDF Triples? An Abstraction of the Declarative Mapping Process for Knowledge Graph Construction
abstract: Several approaches for RDF knowledge graph construction have been proposed in recent years and declarative mapping languages have risen as the most maintainable and reproducible solution. Different requirements led to the proliferation and evolution of mapping languages and the corresponding processors for their execution. However, focusing exclusively on the extension of languages or the enhancement of processors is not sufficient for the global optimisation of the entire mapping process. In this paper, we propose a reference abstraction of the declarative mapping process and its decomposition into its main building blocks, taking into consideration both the definition and the execution of mappings. We also employ this abstraction to define a generic conversion process between different data representations and we provide a prototypical implementation of a generalised data converter. Finally, the proposed prototype is evaluated both qualitatively, considering a set of common challenges in the knowledge graph construction process, and quantitatively, considering performance and scalability.

title: A 2D Entity Pair Tagging Scheme for Relation Triplet Extraction
abstract: It is essential for large scale knowledge graph construction to extract relation triplets composed of entity pairs and relations from unstructured texts. Although recent researches have made considerable progress in joint extraction of entities and relations, they are still confronted with some problems. Specifically, existing methods usually decompose the task of relation triplet extraction into several subtasks or different modules, which inevitably suffers from error propagation or poor information interaction. In this paper, a novel end to end relation extraction model named 2DEPT is proposed, which can effectively address the problems mentioned above. The proposed model comprises a 2D entity pair tagging scheme that provides a simple but effective decoding method and a token pair classifier based on scoring which determines whether a token pair belongs to the specific relationship. Besides, extensive experiments on two public datasets widely used by many researchers are conducted, and the experimental results perform better than the state of the art baselines overall and deliver consistent performance gains on complex scenarios of various overlapping patterns and multiple triplets. The source code and dataset are available at: https://github.com/Oliverstars/Code42DEPT.

title: Predicting the Acceptability of Atomic Candidate OWL Class Axioms
abstract: The task of evaluating the fitness of a candidate axiom against known facts or data is known as candidate axiom scoring. Being able to accurately score candidate axioms is a prerequisite for automatic schema or ontology induction, but can also be useful for ontology and/or knowledge graph validation. Accurate axiom scoring heuristics are often heavy to compute, which is a big problem if one wants to exploit them in iterative search methods like level wise generate and test or evolutionary algorithms, where large numbers of candidate axioms need to be scored. We tackle the challenge of learning a predictive model as a surrogate to reasoning, that predicts the acceptability score of candidate class axioms, that is fast to execute yet accurate enough to be used in such settings. For this purpose, we leverage a semantic similarity measure extracted from the subsumption hierarchy of an ontology. We prove that the method proposed in this paper is able to learn the acceptability labels of candidate OWL class axioms with high accuracy and that it can do so for multiple types of OWL class axioms.

title: GETT QA: Graph Embedding based T2T Transformer for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
abstract: In this work, we present an end to end Knowledge Graph Question Answering (KGQA) system named GETT QA. GETT QA uses T5, a popular text to text pre trained language model. The model takes a question in natural language as input and produces a simpler form of the intended SPARQL query. In the simpler form, the model does not directly produce entity and relation IDs. Instead, it produces corresponding entity and relation labels. The labels are grounded to KG entity and relation IDs in a subsequent step. To further improve the results, we instruct the model to produce a snippet of the KG embedding for each entity. The snippet enables a finer search for disambiguation purposes. We find that T5 is able to learn the KG embedding snippets without any change of loss function, improving KGQA performance. As a result, we report strong results for LC QuAD 2.0 and SimpleQuestions Wikidata datasets on end to end KGQA over Wikidata.

title: Repairing EL ontologies using weakening and completing
abstract: The quality of ontologies in terms of their correctness and completeness is crucial for developing high quality ontology based applications. Traditional debugging techniques repair ontologies by removing unwanted axioms, but may thereby remove consequences that are correct in the domain of the ontology. In this paper we propose an interactive approach to mitigate this for EL ontologies by axiom weakening and completing. We present the first approach for repairing that takes into account removing, weakening and completing. We show different combination strategies, discuss the influence on the final ontologies and show experimental results. We show that previous work has only considered special cases and that there is a trade off, and how to deal with it, involving the amount of validation work for a domain expert and the quality of the ontology in terms of correctness and completeness. We also present new algorithms for weakening and completing.

title: Topic Modeling for Short Texts via DMM with Topic Word Correlation
abstract: Inferring diverse and coherent latent topics from short texts is a critical and fundamental task of topic models. Existing topic models incorporate external knowledge to improve the coherence of topic modeling, and Generalized Polya Urn (GPU) scheme is another desired option to promote similar words under the same topic during the topic inference process. However, knowledge enhanced or GPU guided topic models learn coherent topics by enforcing hard and word independent rules that similar words should have the same promotional contribution in all topics, which is questionable in that similar words of one topic are not necessarily of equal importance for another topic. In this paper, we propose a Topic Modeling for Short Texts via DMM with Topic Word Correlation (TWC DMM), which leverages subtle topic word correlation into Dirichlet Multinomial Mixture (DMM) and introduces a novel Boost Generalized Polya Urn (BPU) model with Irrelevancy Filtering mechanism. Access to the relationship of similar words to the topic permits the creation of an intelligent topic modeling algorithm that utilizes the knowledge in a soft and topic aware manner to mine more coherent and diverse topics over five comparison models on three real world short text datasets.

title: Co FT: Effective Fine tuning for Pretrained Language Model via Adding Collaborator
abstract: Dialogue understanding is a common application in many online webs, which recognizes the intents of customers via utterance classification. The state of the art methods finetune a pretrained language model (PTLM) on a task specific dataset, which is sub optima because it makes the PTLM forget the knowledge learned in pretraining. To address it, we propose an effective finetuning method (Co FT) via adding collaborators for PTLM. Instead of finetuning the whole PTLM, we add an extra collaborator utterance encoder (CoUE). The CoUE consists of independent tokenizer and network weights, which can be implemented via rich flexible network architectures. We aggregate the features extracted by PTLM and the CoUE, and then feed them to the intent predictor (a feed forward classifier) for dialogue intent recognition. Given a domain specific dataset, we only update the weights of CoUE via a 2 stage training method. Our experiments show that Co FT outperforms the PTLM finetuning method and achieves 78.43\% f1 score. Besides, Co FT also shows a good capacity in the few shot learning.

title: Activity Recommendation for Business Process Modeling with Sequence to Sequence Models
abstract: Activity recommendation in business process modeling is concerned with suggesting suitable labels for a new activity inserted by a modeler in a process model under development. Recently, it has been proposed to represent process model repositories as knowledge graphs, which makes it possible to address the activity recommendation problem as a knowledge graph completion task. However, existing recommendation approaches are entirely dependent on the knowledge contained in the model repository used for training. This makes them rigid in general and even inapplicable in situations where a process model consists of unseen activities, which were not part of the repository used for training. In this paper, we avoid these issues by recognizing that the semantics contained in process models can be used to instead pose the activity recommendation problem as a set of textual sequence to sequence tasks. This enables the application of transfer learning techniques from natural language processing, which allows for recommendations that go beyond the activities contained in an available repository. We operationalize this with an activity recommendation approach that employs a transformer based sequence to sequence model at its core, and uses the representations of process knowledge as structured graphs combined with the natural language based semantics of process models. In an experimental evaluation, we show that our approach considerably outperforms the state of the art in terms of semantic accuracy of the recommendations and that it is able to recommend and handle activity labels that go beyond the vocabulary of the model repository used during training.

title: A Recursive Evaluation of SPARQL Queries Accelerates Class Expression Learning
abstract: Over 100 billion RDF assertions are found on the Web. RDF knowledge bases are hence first class citizens of the Web. Consequently, machine learning on the Web entails machine learning on RDF knowledge bases. Class expression learning based on refinement operators is a promising family of explainable machine learning approaches for RDF knowledge bases. However, most implementations of this paradigm fail to scale to the large knowledge bases found on the Web. One common bottleneck of these implementations is the retrieval function. This work address this drawback in ALC by providing a recursive execution mechanism for SPARQL queries. We implement this strategy into a triplestore to enable it to efficiently answer retrieval queries in ALC under the closed world assumption. We evaluate our approach on four popular benchmark datasets for machine learning in ALC. Our results suggest that our approach is between 3 and 50 times faster than the state of the art.

title: ATMiner: Mining Approximate Functional Dependencies on Transactional Graphs
abstract: Mining dependencies on graphs is an important step to improve the data quality of graphs in rule based graph repairing methods, it is defined as finding all graph functional dependencies (GFDs) that appear frequently in graphs. Most existing work focuses on mining functional dependencies or a single graph and ignores the impact of noisy data. In this paper, we proposed ATMiner, a novel framework for mining approximate functional dependencies on transactional graphs. First, we formlized approximate functional dependency on transactional graphs (TGAFD), which is a class of data quality rules imposing topological and relaxed attribute dependency constraints on transactional graphs. Then,we developd an algorithm for discovering TGAFDs, referred as ATMiner. ATMiner is made up of three parts: graph patterns mining, graph patterns matching, and dependencies discovery. Furthermore, we propose a graph dataset generator based on graph dependencies that can be used to demonstrate the validity of the graph dependency discovery algorithms. At last, we verifed the efficiency of ATMiner and emploved the found TGAFDs to detect inconsistent errors in real life and synthetic datasets.

title: A Comparative Study of Publicly Accessible Tools for Logic based Module Extraction
abstract: Extracting a module from an ontology is a fundamental technique in ontology engineering, with the usefulness of reducing the hardness of creating, maintaining, understanding, reusing, and reasoning an ontology. It deals with reducing an ontology to a module to cover a specific subject domain. This paper focuses on currently publicly accessible module extraction tools that are grouped into subset module extraction and rewritten module extraction (aka uniform interpolation). We give a comparative study of these tools for the computational complexity of extracting modules and the quality of solutions returned by these tools on two benchmark datasets. Furthermore, we investigate the interrelations between subset module extraction and rewritten module extraction: subset module extraction is an optimization technique for rewritten module extraction in order to improve the performance of subset module extraction; theoretically, a subset module can be obtained from a rewritten module by keeping track of the axioms in the original ontology that contribute to axioms in the rewritten module. We present sound evidence that, in most cases, subset modules are much larger than rewritten modules; but subset module extraction is much computationally easier than rewritten module extraction. There is no significant evidence that subset module extraction can improve the performance of rewritten module extraction.

title: Generalized Role Hierarchies in DLR
abstract: We present an extension of the n ary description logic DLR with generalized role hierarchies, and prove the usual reasoning problems over this system decidable. It captures most of the features of OWL DL, with n ary relations. We discuss an application to ontology alignment, and propose that complex alignment creates a need for n ary description logic.

title: Peuplement d'ontologie a partir de petites annonces immobilieres
abstract: Le peuplement d'ontologie a partir de textes vise a transformer du contenu textuel en assertions ontologiques. Cela permet d'obtenir une representation structuree du contenu d'un texte et d'automatiser sa comprehension. Cet article traite d'une approche de peuplement automatique d'une ontologie a partir de petites annonces immobilieres. Celle ci s'appuie a la fois sur une analyse textuelle et une analyse des connaissances du domaine. Des experimentations, realisees sur des annonces francaises de ventes de maisons, sont discutees et donnent des resultats encourageants.

title: Connexions et relations
abstract: Dans cet article, nous poursuivons la definition dune espece dontologies baptisees ontologies epistemiques en caracterisant la nature des entites complexes quelles representent. Parmi celles ci figurent les propositions et evenements (dans la sphere mentale) et les etats de choses (dans la sphere physique). Pour rendre compte de leur structure, nous faisons appel a la figure ontologique de la connexion. Dans larticle, nous privilegions letude des etats de choses, que nous identifions a des connections internes (liant les objets et processus a leurs qualites) et a des connections externes (entre objets et processus). De telles connexions sont recurrentes et nous en avons connaissance sous la forme de types, ou liens generaux, de connexion. Nous definissons ces liens generaux de connexion comme une espece de relations.

title: Graphes de Connaissances et Ontologie pour la Representation de Donnees Immobilieres Issues dAnnonces en Texte Libre
abstract: Nous decrivons nos premiers travaux sur la conception dune ontologie et dun graphe de connaissances pour la representation des donnees immobilieres issues dannonces. Nous identifions plusieurs scenarios motivants a partir des donnees extraites afin de justifier notre modelisation. Puis nous proposons une modelisation pour representer les donnees spatiales incertaines et leurs geometries dans un graphe de connaissances

title: Modelisation des ingredients de remedes issus de pharmacopees arabes medievales dans une base de donnees graphe
abstract: Cet article presente le travail de modelisation engage dans le cadre d'un projet interdisciplinaire, dont le but est d'etudier les remedes decrits dans les pharmacopees arabes medievales. Les informations extraites d'un texte ancien, traduit en anglais, ont ete representees dans une base de donnees graphe, en utilisant la plateforme Neo4j. Cette etude de cas a mis en evidence plusieurs problemes de modelisation, notamment pour la representation d'ingredients qui sont des sous parties de plantes et dont l'appellation comporte des ambiguites. L'article detaille ces problemes et les solutions apportees.

title: Construction d'un graphe de connaissance a partir des annotations manuelles de textes de zoologie antique
abstract: Ce travail est realise dans le cadre de lIRN Zoomathia qui vise letude de la transmission des savoirs zoologiques de lAntiquite au Moyen Age. Dans ce contexte, un pre mier travail dannotation manuelle de lHistoire Naturel le de Pline lAncien sur la zoologie antique (livres 8 11) en utilisant des concepts rassembles dans le thesaurus The Zoo a ete realise par des specialistes de lAntiquite. Ce pendant, ces annotations ont ete realisees avec des com mentaires Word, ce qui rend complexe lexploitation de ces connaissances par les chercheurs epistemologues, histo riens et philologues dans leur travail danalyse de ces textes anciens. Dans cet article, nous presentons notre approche de transformation de ces annotations manuelles en graphe de connaissance RDF permettant lintegration et linterro gation des connaissances extraites dans le but daider les chercheurs dans leur travail danalyse de ces textes et de la transmission des connaissances a travers eux. Afin de valider la pertinence du modele et le graphe de connais sance, nous avons recueilli aupres dun expert du domaine un ensemble de questions de competences que nous avons traduites en SPARQL pour y repondre en interrogeant le graphe de connaissance produit.

title: Ameliorer la FAIRisation des donnees meteorologiques a l'aide de la ressource lexicale INMEVO
abstract: Rendre les jeux de donnees meteorologiques FAIR est un enjeu crucial pour la recherche scientifique. Le modele dmo core permet, pour les donnees tabulaires, d'expliciter la semantique des colonnes en les reliant a des concepts d'ontologies de domaine. Ces concepts etant generalement peu ou pas documentes, nous proposons (1) d'enrichir dmo core afin de pouvoir associer aux colonnes leurs definitions issues d'une ressource lexicale, et (2) de generer une telle ressource, a partir du Vocabulaire Meteorologique International de l'Organisation Mondiale de Meteorologie.

title: Prevention et auto reeducation de pathologies osteoarticulaires assistees par intelligence artificielle
abstract: Les pathologies osteo articulaires et tout particulierement les lombalgies ou les entorses de cheville sont un enjeu de sante publique. Les donnees decrivant limpact des traitements sur levolution des pathologies sont insuffisantes pour imaginer un processus dauto apprentissage. Nous avons donc concu une application basee, notamment, sur des regles de consensus medicales capable de generer des seances dexercices adaptees a la pathologie du patient et a son evolution. Nous avons retenu une approche qui, partant de lentorse de cheville, a pu etre generalisee a 12 pathologies et a donne lieu a une application operationnelle. Recovup, issue de ces travaux, est disponible sous forme de WebApp (https://recovup.com).

title: CubicWeb as a Service : un service pour la publication sur le Web de donnees liees
abstract: La publication de donnees RDF, suivant les 5 etoiles du Linked Open Data, devient de plus en plus systematique.
