abstract: TBE: Acne vulgaris is a skin condition which occurs frequently within the population. Important step in diagnosing the condition is grading the severity of the case. For this purpose dermatologists often use different grading scales and criteria. To aid this grading process, the usage of deep learning algorithms has been proposed by multiple authors. This paper explores the usage of deep learning algorithms on two separate datasets, one of which is reinforced with bounding boxes for acne.

title: Physicochemical compatible motifs in proteins sequences.
abstract: In the branch of biochemistry there is the problem of identifying motifs made up of amino acid sequences, the identification of motifs is important since from these it is possible to define a set of properties that characterize proteins, such as their functionality, their structure 3D, its origin, etc. The search for motifs is considered a complex problem, since depending on the number of amino acids that make up the motif, it will be the number of possible different motifs that can be generated. To search for these motifs, a methodology divided into 3 phases was applied. The objective of the first phase was to obtain a set of subsequences of variable size with a high conservation index, for the second phase a set of artificial motifs was obtained that, through a genetic algorithm, maximize the physicochemical compatibility of the amino acids of the motifs, in the third phase it was sought that the artificial motifs existed in a group of proteins, in order to identify areas of interaction between the protein in its 3D structure. The artificial motifs found by the methodology help experts for the modeling of protein structures in 3D and the identification or better classification of protein subsequences.

title: Towards an interpretable model for automatic classification of endoscopy images
abstract: Deep learning strategies have become the mainstream for computer assisted diagnosis tools development since they outperform other machine learning techniques. However, these systems can not reach their full potential since the lack of understanding of their operation and questionable generalizability provokes mistrust from the users, limiting their application. In this paper, we generate a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) using a genetic algorithm for hyperparameter optimization. Our CNN has state of the art classification performance, delivering higher evaluation metrics than other recent papers that use AI models to classify images from the same dataset. We provide visual explanations of the classifications made by our model implementing Grad CAM and analyze the behavior of our model on misclassifications using this technique.

title: Parametric estimation of a RC servomotor using evolutionary algorithms
abstract: In the present work, an evolutionary algorithm is proposed to estimate the numerical values of the coefficients in a second order dynamical model of an RC servomotor. The estimated values for this model were validated using a commercial servomotor. A comparison of models between classical estimation techniques and the results from the evolutionary algorithm is given. The evolutionary algorithm is applicable for estimating parameters of the dynamic model of a servomotor where only the bounds of the parameters are known, and the measurement of the input and output signals of the servomotor is available.

title: Meibomian glands characterization using Intelligent systems
abstract: Analysis of the morphology of the meibomian glands from keratograph images is used for the diagnosis of dry eye and other dysfunctions in ophthalmology. A reliable analysis requires years of experience in the area, and usually this is made manually. This is the reason to propose an automatic algorithm using image processing and supported by a fuzzy expert system to characterize the health status of a meibomian gland. Results give by proposed system are comparable to those give by expert of the area.

title: Towards a textual mechanics: A preliminary approach
abstract: In the last years, the development of continuous distributed vector representations of words made possible a plethora of models, algorithms, and new applications in the field of Natural Language Processing. Besides the evident benefits of this breakthrough, there is much to uncover from these representations. In this paper, we present the concept of textual mechanics as an attempt to understand textual properties, characteristics, and relationships in textual documents. Here we will present the idea of textual mass, volume, and density. Using these concepts we will utilize the MegaLite corpus to understand the idea of synthesis and expressiveness in three different roman languages Spanish, French, and Portuguese.

title: Gathering, integration and preprocessing of data in educational data mining
abstract: Learning environments generate data that can be analyzed through educational data mining to obtain knowledge that helps to improve these tools. Data gathering, integration, and preprocessing are the first steps on the way for building a dataset that is appropriate for the job. Instruments to gather data must often be built, and it is common to have more than one data source. The present work presents the conformation of an educational data set, exposing the stages of design and development of tools to gather data, data gathering and integration, data cleaning and preprocessing, and data set conformation. The study carried out for data gathering consists of three data sources: Student performance data at a university, data from the application of some scales and data from a mathematical logic course using the MateLog system.

title: Reversible image authentication scheme with tampering reconstruction based on very deep super resolution network
abstract: Reversible image authentication (RIA) involves a data hiding process in which watermarks are imperceptibly embedded into an image to protect it against tampering attacks. If a marked image is not tampered, then watermarks can be erased from the marked image and the original cover image is obtained without distortion. Watermarks can be enhanced with recovery information for reconstruction of tampered image regions. However, due to embedding capacity limitations, recovery information must be strategically selected to obtain better image reconstruction quality. To address this issue, very deep super resolution (VDSR) network is used in the reconstruction phase of the proposed scheme. Sparse signal representations of down scaled image blocks are obtained to apply compressed sensing theory and obtain the reference values used as recovery information. Experimental results indicate that our scheme outperforms previous state of the art methods in terms of reconstructed images quality while reducing time complexity in sparse signal approximation phase as a result of dealing with down scaled image blocks.

title: Cooperative Chaotic Exploration with UAVs Combining Pheromone Dispersion and Hopfield Chaotic Neural Network
abstract: Currently, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) or Drones have been presented as new tools for terrain exploration in multiple applications and various objectives. UAV exploration has challenges in how the vehicle scans the environment, which must be a fast, safe and complete scan. This paper presents some mobility models previously developed for chaotic exploration with multiple UAVs, which is called cooperative exploration. The main mobility model is based on pheromone dispersion used in the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm. In addition, we propose some modifications to these models by introducing the Hopfield Chaotic Neural Network dynamics to generate the chaotic behavior and improve the performance in the coverage of the explored area. Likewise, simulation results are presented in exploring an area size of 50m X 50m with 2 UAVs.

title: An improved Estimation of Distribution Algorithm for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming Problems: EDAIImv
abstract: In a mixed integer nonlinear programming problem, integer restrictions divide the feasible region into discontinuous feasible parts with different sizes. Evolutionary Algorithms (EAs) are usually vulnerable to being trapped in larger discontinuous feasible parts. In this work, an improved version of an Estimation of Distribution Algorithm (EDA) is developed, where two new op erations are proposed. The first one establishes a link between the learning based histogram model and the epsilon constrained method. Here, the constraint violation level of the epsilon constrained method is used to explore the smaller discontinuous parts and form a better statistical model. The second operation is the hybridization of the EDA with a mutation operator to generate offspring from both the global distribution information and the parent information. A benchmark is used to test the performance of the improved proposal. The results indicated that the proposed approach shows a better performance against other tested EAs. This new proposal solves to a great extent the influence of the larger discontinuous feasible parts, and improve the local refinement of the real variables.

title: Comparison between SVM and DistilBERT for multi label text classification of scientific papers aligned with sustainable development goals
abstract: The scientific articles identification with the 17 sustainable development goals of the UN 2030 Agenda is a valuable task for research and educational institutions. Finding an efficient and practical multi label classification model using machine or deep learning remains relevant. This work refers to the performance comparison of a text classification model that combines Label Powerset (LP) and Support Vector Machine (SVM) against a transfer learning language model such as DistilBERT in 5 different imbalanced and balanced dataset scenarios of scientific papers. A proposed classification process was implemented with performance metrics, which have confirmed that the combination LP SVM continues to be an option with remarkable results in multi label text classification.

title: Machine Learning based Decision Making in Evolutionary Multiobjective Clustering
abstract: Clustering is an important optimization problem which is at the core of many data mining and machine learning applications. Evolutionary multiobjective clustering algorithms optimize multiple partition quality criteria simultaneously, producing a set of trade off solutions in a single execution. How can a final solution be selected from this set of candidate trade offs? Decision making is concerned with such a task, acknowledging that obtaining a single solution may represent the ultimate goal in practice. Given the limitations of current techniques, we explore a novel approach to decision making: tackling this task as a supervised learning problem. Our approach attempts to learn from the decision making process in example (training) problems, with the aim of later applying the learned model to lead the identification of final solutions in new applications. In this paper, we present preliminary results on the evaluation of this proposal. Our experiments include comparisons with respect to a set of decision making approaches from the literature and consider a collection of synthetic clustering problems with diverse characteristics. The results obtained are promising, highlighting the relevance of devising alternative decision making strategies, the effectiveness of our proposal, and motivating further research on this matter.

title: Retrieval based Statistical Chatbot in a Scientometric domain
abstract: The scope of this research work is to integrate a statistical ontology model of scientometric indicators in a chatbot. Building a chatbot requires the use of Natural Language Processing (NLP) as a capability for recognizing users' intent and extracting entities from users' questions. We proposed a method for recognizing the requested indicator and transforming the question expressed in natural language into a query to the semantic model. The chatbot and the ontology model represent a novel framework that can answer questions about Scientometric Indicators. The chatbot is evaluated in terms of Goal Completion Rate (GCR). It measures how many questions the chatbot answered correctly and identifies intent and entity extraction correctly. The second evaluation approach of the chatbot is a survey that focuses on usability, the strictness of language variations, chatbot comprehension, correlation in chatbot responses, and user satisfaction.

title: Towards the monitoring of violent events in social media through visual information
abstract: Violence is a latent threat for individuals, this is an even more concerning issue in Latin American cities. The detection and monitoring of events reported in social media could help to build maps of zones with incident of violent events. This could eventually lead to the automatic generation of risk maps which could be of great help to users and even authorities. This paper aims to detect violent incidents reported in social media using visual information only. While most of the related work focuses on the text modality, the goal of this paper is to assess the feasibility of detection when only visual information is available. CNN based feature extraction and standard classification models are implemented and evaluated in a recently released corpus. Experimental results show that distinguishing images depicting violent events is feasible, but the fine grain recognition of categories is still an open problem.

title: Hyperactivity Recognition from children with ADHD combining machine learning and electroencephalographic signal analysis
abstract: The main objective of the study is to develop a pattern recognition of the electroencephalographic signal activity of children with Attention Deficit and Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) differentiating between 3 different mental states which are : Attention, Neutral and Hyperactive and also to find which classification technique is better suited for this task. There is no study found in the literature which emphasizes or establishes a pattern related to hyperactivity in children with ADHD, most of the papers found work with the mental state of attent, the differentiation between children with ADHD and Non ADHD or differences between medicated children against placebo meds and their effects over their attention and their schools performance. Since there is no database available related to hyperactivity, we had to create one of our own. We conducted an inductive mental state process with a group of 6 children equally balanced between the number of boys and girls from the age range 8 11 years old, the sessions took place individually with the approval of at least one of their parents. The induction process included 3 stages per mental state with a 15 minute duration each, for the mental state of attention one half of the time the children worked on an activity related from a program of intelligence development called overlaying images on paper; and the other half of the time, they worked on a digital version of this activity that we developed called Superfig. The neutral activity induction was made through with a guided meditation focusing primarily on their breathing and for the hyperactivity induction the children worked with a fractal music sound as they tried to follow the rhythm of the beats that they were listening to, while wearing an 13 electrode EEG what was monitoring their alpha, beta, theta and gamma electrical brain waves pattern, with a total amount of registries above 2 million. Once gathered all the data, it was submitted to a profound data analysis making a strong emphasis over the pattern related to hyperactivity through the electrical brain activity, discovering an important alpha wave pattern in the parietal cortex on the electrodes P7 and P8 , this last one had a drastically decremented relationship value over P7. Which was observed after treating the data creating the correlation matrix and the covariance matrix which came to our attention noticing some Atypical values. After, all data was submitted through different automatic classification techniques which were Desticion Trees, Knearest known Neighbors, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Neuronal Networks. The best results obtained were from the Neuronal Networks; this last one, gave better results with an Accuracy = 0.874, F1 score = 0.933 and a Precision of 1.00.

title: A proposition of the inconsistency measure through qualitative reasoning
abstract: In this paper, a methodology for the measurement of inconsistency in a belief system is proposed.

title: Authentication in sensors and data for IoT decentralized applications using blockchain
abstract: The irruption of the Internet of Things (IoT) has yielded many benefits for organizations streamlining complicated task evolving our current industry into a more automated and scalable one. At the same time, repetitive activities inherent to current society have been seamlessly changed to bring new habits, commodity and different manners of work. As other technology adoptions, IoT has also introduced unforeseen security risks, requiring substantial organizational proposals to mitigate these issues. One of the main drawbacks of industry implementations of IoT is to authenticate sensors and data flows in the network. In this work, the proposed decentralized application was mounted on the Rinkeby testnet. In this environment sensors, actuators and smart devices were registered for later being authenticated in the network to avoid impersonation of the nodes. The functional tests of the proposed decentralized application were carried out using a prototype made of low cost sensors which produces data that is accessible, immutable and secure.

title: Automating the heuristic based solver generation for microelectronic thermal management problems
abstract: The Microelectronic Thermal Management Problem (MTMP) is now more present in our daily life than before, mainly when the thermal polluting crypto farms appear the sight. Several alternatives are available to solve this problem, for example, microchannel heat sinks, plate fin heat sinks, and heat pumps. No matter the device or structure, there is always an inherent optimisation problem related to the effective practical implementation of these mechanical devices. The literature is plenty of astonishing techniques dealing with that highly nonlinear problem; many of them, metaheuristics, comprise reliable and flexible alternatives. Nevertheless, there is no free lunch. For that reason, in this work, we implement a hyper heuristic algorithm to solve the so called Metaheuristic Composition Optimisation Problem (MCOP) in the MTMP context. So, we achieve an intelligent system capable of generating specialised metaheuristics that deal with MTMP instances. Our results show that the proposed methodology is feasible and flexible to tackle several variations of the same problem. In most of the comparative cases, our methodology reaches comparable results to those reported in the literature.

title: RBF Neural Network Based on FT Windows for Auto Tunning PID Controller
abstract: The weighted function windows are used in many areas as signal analysis and application systems. In addition, the weighted functions are broad uses in filter design where different windows allow to choose different filter characteristics. The most common individual window types are rectangular, Hanning, Flat Top, and Keiser Bessel. This paper presents the Flat Top Windows (FTW) applied to control systems where the FTW are used as activation functions on a radial basis neural network (RBF). Contrary to the "traditional" FT weighted function windows, where time windows limit the information, this paper proposes new ones that, including new parameters, allow translation and dilation of the window. Additionally, these new parameters are updated using a gradient descent algorithm.

title: Improving artefact detection in endoscopic video using a real time ensemble method
abstract: In this contribution, we use an ensemble deep learning method for combining the prediction of two individual detectors (i.e., YOLOv4 and Yolact) with the aim to detect artefacts in endoscopic images. This ensemble strategy enabled us to improve the robustness of the individual models without harming their real time computation capabilities. We demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach by training and testing the two individual models and various ensemble configurations on the Endoscopic Artifact Detection Challenge dataset. Extensive experiments show the superiority, in terms of mean average precision, of the ensemble approach over the individual models and previous works in the state of the art.

title: A comparison of tiny nerf versus spatial representations for 3d reconstruction
abstract: Neural rendering has emerged as a powerful paradigm, offering many benefits over classical rendering by using neural networks to reconstruct surfaces, represent shapes, and novel view synthesis, either for objects or scenes. In this neural rendering, the environment is encoded in a neural network. We believe that these new representations can be used to codify the scene for a mobile robot. Therefore, in this work, we perform a comparison between a multi layer perceptron (that encodes the neural rendering) and other volume representations that are commonly used as maps in robotics, such as voxel maps, point clouds, and triangular meshes. The target is to know the advantages and disadvantages of neural representations. The comparison is made in terms of spatial complexity and processing time to obtain a model. Experiments show that neural representations require three times less memory space compared to other representations. In terms of processing time, the multi layer perceptron takes about six times more to compute the model.

title: Implementation of lightweight deep learning models VGG 16, VGG 19, ResNet50, Xception, MobileNet and MobileNetV2 for classification of COVID 19 and different classes.
abstract: In the course of the pandemic, a variety of works have been developed, which implement convolutional neural networks for the classification of COVID 19 and other classes; when performing an analysis of these models, it was observed that the results obtained by these models are uncertain, because the authors of these models manifest results with the metrics of Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1 Score; during the evaluation and training stage, not considering subjecting the network to test by means of sets of images not processed by the network. In this work, the implementation of the Convolutional Neural Networks VGG 16, VGG 19, ResNet50, Xception, MobileNet and MobileNetV2 was performed; for the analysis of chest X ray images of patients with COVID 19 and conditions not caused by this disease. Eleven publicly available image sets from GitHub, Mandeley and Kaggle platforms were implemented. Different preprocessing techniques were applied; first the image normalization technique was applied, which consists of excluding images, where hospital equipment, personal objects, informative labels of the radiography and reduced sharpness are present in the lung area; then, cropping, rotation and resizing editing was performed to the remaining images. Consequently, Balance Contrast Enhancement Technique (BCET), Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE), Gamma correction, normalization technique and CLAHE and Histogram Equalization (HE) filter were applied to this new set. Accuracy, Precision, Recall and F1 Score metrics were used to quantitatively measure the classification performance of both models. The best result was obtained with the VGG 16 model implementing the CLAHE filter, presenting 82.61% Accuracy, 83.74% in Precision, 82.61% in Recall and 82.46% in F1 Score, implementing 2,002 images for training, 667 for validation and 667 for testing.

title: Red Light/Green Light: a lightweight algorithm for, possibly fraudulent, online behavior change detection
abstract: Telecommunications services have become a constant in people's lives. This has inspired fraudsters to carry out malicious activities causing economic losses to people and companies. Early detection of signs that suggest the possible occurrence of malicious activity would allow analysts to act in time and avoid unintended consequences. Modeling the behavior of users could identify when a significant change takes place. Following this idea, an algorithm for online behavior change detection in telecommunication services is proposed in this paper. The algorithm gets its name from the popular Red Light/Green Light children's game, as it works similarly to the person who starts out as ``guardian'' in the game. The proposed algorithm was evaluated over two data sets related to mobile phone calls and Short Message Service (SMS). The experimental results show that the new algorithm can identify behavioral changes related to unforeseen events. In addition, a case study on real SMS messages dataset is presented. Here, the proposed algorithm successfully identified several users associated with malicious activities.

title: GA AF: A Passive Filter Design Tool
abstract: Circuit design commonly follows one of two possible paths: the establishment of device values on a preset topology or the design of "blank sheets"; which involves the creation of a device without topological constraints. Naturally, the second path involves a higher level of knowledge and complexity; however, being unconstrained, the possibility of finding novel and efficient designs is also increased. This paper presents an evolutionary tool for the design of passive analog filters whose efficiency is comparable to classical design methodologies such as Butterworth and Chebyshev. The performance of the filters obtained by the tool is validated by using SPICE simulation software without the need to adjust the device values. The tests developed on low pass and high pass filters show that the tool builds filters of different topologies, adjusting the order of the filters obtained according to the requirements of the design specifications. Some of the filters obtained by the tool exhibit third order behavior.

title: White Blood Cell Classification Using One Stage Object Detector
abstract: White blood cells are a fundamental part of the immune system which protect human body against infections and diseases. The complete blood count is a routine analysis that provides doctors information about the patient. Monitoring the immune system, allows doctor to select preventive treatments against disease such as anemia and leukemia. Furthermore, doctors can make better decisions in the medicine administration. The complete blood count relies in a rigorous observation of a blood sample through a microscope; the accuracy of the result depends on the expertise and time of the analyst. Laboratories uses expensive and complex flow cytometry based machines for blood cell counting. In this paper it is presented a novel vision based method using convolutional neural networks for white blood cell detection and classification. The results show the proposed method outperforms the handcrafted techniques as well as the CNN based models found in the literature.

title: Detection of Tomato Ripening Stages using Yolov3 tiny
abstract: One of the most important agricultural products in Mexico is the tomato (Solanum lycopersicum), which occupies the 4th place as the nationally most produced goods. Therefore, it is necessary to improve its production. One way to achieve that, it is to build automatic systems that detect, classify and keep track of the fruit. So, in this paper, we address the task of designing a computer vision system to detect tomatoes at different ripening stages. To solve the problem, we use a neural network based model for tomato classification and detection. Specifically, we use the YOLOv3 tiny model. To train it, we perform two grid searches testing several combinations of hyperparameters to obtain promising results. Our experiments showed an f1 score of 89.99% in the localization and classification of ripening stages in a custom dataset.

title: Double pack: A Grey Wolf Optimizer ensemble
abstract: Solution quality is a major aspect in nature inspired algorithms. To this end, we propose an ensemble based on the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), considering the advantages of this algorithm. The ensemble, named DP GWO, generates a population that is divided into two packs (sub populations). These packs are evolved independently for a number of iterations. Afterwards, the evolved packs are merged again into a single population, which is evolved only once. This ensemble was compared against five algorithms (ABC, PSO, GWO, Hybrid genetic swarm, and SARA 1) using seven classical optimization problems. Although all the algorithms are competitive, the DP GWO ensemble showed better results on average and also over 30 runs in the majority of the test problems.

title: Program Synthesis and Natural Language Processing: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: This paper reports a systematic literature review on program synthesis from natural language. The objective of the study was to analyze the relevant works published in the last five years, in order to identify trends and areas of opportunity. Four data sources were chosen (IEEE, ACM, Springer and Elsevier) from where a total of 8 papers, both from journals and conference proceedings, were selected. Those papers propose solutions aimed for end users or novice programmers, taking as inputs natural languages queries and producing as output expressions in different programming languages, such as boolean, DSL or Java. The methods for program synthesis go from those that hard code the rules for translating an expression in natural language to code, to those that learn the rules from input output pairs

title: Portfolio Selection using Artificial Intelligence Techniques in the Mexican Stock Exchange
abstract: Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) techniques in the portfolio selection problem has shown high potential for performance improvement. Even a slight improvement in the portfolio selection problem can produce significant profit for investors. This thesis project proposes an evaluation scheme using a combination of AI techniques to create portfolios for the Mexican Stock Exchange. The portfolio selection problem is divided into two stages: stock selection and portfolio optimization. In the stock selection stage, we use three labeling strategies, one of them proposed by us, to train supervised machine learning classifiers, including Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forests (RF), Neural Networks (NN), and PBC4cip. The classifiers perform a binary classification to filter stocks with a high potential to achieve positive returns for the next month. In the optimization stage, we use and adapt to the context a state of the art multi objective genetic algorithm (NSGA III) to find solutions that set the participation weights for each stock. From the efficient frontier (Pareto front), we consider three portfolios for evaluation performance: maximum return (GA max return), minimum risk (GA min risk ), and average risk (GA avg risk ). For comparison purposes, we also made portfolios using all stocks and baseline optimizers; equally weight distribution (1/N), maximum Sharpe ratio (max Sharpe), and minimum risk (min risk) using analytical methods. The portfolios are created using national and international stocks that trade on the Mexican Stock Exchange. We implement an evaluation scheme that finds the combination of a set of AI techniques that produce the portfolios with better performance according to three different investor profiles: aggressive, conservative, and moderate. The portfolios are evaluated monthly from December 2019 to December 2020 using the return, risk, and Sharpe ratio as objective goals. The proposed historical and t+1 labeling strategy produced higher average returns using every classifier and optimization technique. Portfolios with the highest returns were produced by SVM and NN classifiers and GA max return optimizer, while PBC4cip and GA min risk created portfolios with the lowest risk. The results achieved have higher returns than the risk free interest rate in Mexico (CETES) and S&P 500 and S&P/BMV IPC indexes.

title: Automated web annotator of biomedical entities in Spanish language
abstract: In Natural Language Processing (NLP) and supervised machine learning, the scarcity of labeled corpora results in poor performance of machine learning models. In the medical domain, there are also fewer labeled corpora in Spanish than in English. In this research we propose a method to identify biomedical entities in clinical text in the Spanish language, through automatic translation and word alignment, for which we translate the source text (Spanish) to the target text (English), then we label the target text with automatic labelers of biomedical entities, to finally project the biomedical entities of the target text to the text spans that correspond in the source text by means of a word alignment generated in the translation process. This is done with the objective of annotating the source text with English language tools (automatic annotators). As a result, an efficient method capable of processing and annotating biomedical entities in the Spanish language with high precision is obtained, since it integrates several automatic annotators in a single web system.

title: Multi Modal Sensor Fusion for Bolivian Sign Language Recognition
abstract: Sign language recognition systems allow hearing impaired people to communicate with the general public by extracting patterns from visual and/or sensor data. However, this technology has not been fully developed for the Bolivian sign language, for which only static gesture recognition was investigated. Although many state of the art sign language recognition approaches would also fit the Bolivian case, open data about it is almost non existent. Consequently, we propose a dataset with 1440 video sequences of 20 dynamic gestures and their respective features: body and hand keypoints, hand segments and optical flow. Inspired by the great successes of sensor fusion approaches, we propose an architecture to recognise dynamic gestures of the Bolivian Sign Language by assembling three CNN based models. The proposed architecture achieves an average accuracy ranging from 85% to 95%, using 10 cross validations.

title: Pursuing the Deep Learning based Classification of Exposed and Imagined Colors from EEG
abstract: EEG based brain computer interfaces are systems aiming to integrate disabled people into their environments. Nevertheless, their control could not be intuitive or depend on an active external stimulator to generate the responses for interacting with it. Targeting the second issue, a novel paradigm is explored in this paper, which depends on a passive stimulus by measuring the EEG responses of a subject to the primary colors (red, green, and blue). Particularly, we assess if a compact and feature extraction independent deep learning method (EEGNet) can effectively learn from these EEG responses. Our outcomes outperformed previous works focused on a dataset composed of EEG signals belonging to 7 subjects while seeing and imagining three primary colors. The method reaches an accuracy of 45% for exposed colors, 43% for imagined colors, and 35% for the six classes. Last, the experiments suggest that EEGNet learned to discover patterns in the EEG signals recorded for imagined and exposed colors, and for the six classes, too.

title: Chatbot for Depression Detection with Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Due to the pandemic SARS COV2, the World Health Organization reported a paralysis in mental health services by 93%. Depression is one of the most dan gerous mental disorders since it can leave people disabled or even lead them to suicide, which is why it is proposed to develop a virtual assistant of first attention to emotional health that will guide a conversation of close interaction, applying the Beck depression inventory. This system identifies and qualifies the level of depression in the user, incorporating voice recognition with the mixed model: Hidden Markov Neural Networks (HMM ANN) to take user input data, a nat ural language processing model to give context to the input data system and a de cision tree diagram to guide the interaction with the user, resulting from the inte gration of these subsystems a platform with a user friendly design that favors us ability and voice to voice interaction with the users. people.

title: A hybrid methodology based on CRISP DM and TDSP for the execution of preprocessing tasks in Mexican environmental laws
abstract: This article focuses, on the one hand, on showing some techniques applied during the preprocessing of texts represented by environmental law documents, as a previous work to the analysis of a set of them. The need to carry out this type of analysis is due to several factors such as: the large number of existing legislative documents such as laws, programs, regulations, etc., the modifications that are made to the legal system due to social changes, and especially, to those contradictions that may arise between one or more laws. On the other hand, certain tasks of the CRISP DM methodology were addressed and, specifically, for the data preparation phase in the generic tasks of selection, cleaning, transformation and formatting. This was done using the NLTK library text preprocessing techniques of tokenization, segmentation, denoising and normalization. Among the most remarkable results is an instantiation between CRISP DM, TDSP and experiment planning methodologies, oriented to the preprocessing of Mexican federal environmental laws. In addition, this article shows a comparative analysis of the PyPDF2 and Pdfplumber libraries for the extraction of text in pdf format to plain text. This analysis is accompanied by the measurement of memory and execution time with the intention of scaling these tests with a larger number of documents and preprocessing tasks.

title: News Intention Study and Automatic Estimation of its Impact
abstract: Since the invention of the Internet, and with the rise of social networks, information is available to all users quickly and in large quantities. One of the main sources of information on social networks is news. Among the possible options available for users to give their opinion, comments and for the purposes of this work, tweets are the main tool of expression. For this reason, tweets are the object of study of this work. The content of these opinions is highly emotionally charged. By analyzing users comments about a news item, it is possible to determine its polarity and in turn use it as an indicator of the controversiality of the news. Controversiality tells us how the news affected its consumers, since if the responses are highly controversial it means that the readers opinions differed greatly, and that there was no common agreement on the news. Since there was no consensus in the responses, it can be inferred that there was a heated discussion in the comments. These heated discussions are striking because they indicate which types of news generate more conflicts among readers and which do not.

title: Evaluation of a New Representation for Noise Reduction in Distant Supervision
abstract: Distant Supervision is a relation extraction approach that allows automatic labeling of a dataset. However, this labeling introduces noise in the labels (e.g., when two entities in a sentence are automatically labeled with an invalid relation). Noise in labels makes difficult the relation extraction task. This is precisely one of the main challenges of this task. Until now, the methods that incorporate a previous noise reduction step do not evaluate the performance of this step. This paper evaluates the noise reduction using a new representation obtained with autoencoders. In addition, it was incoporated more information to the input of the autoencoder proposed in the state of the art to improve the representation over which the noise is reduced. Also, it was proposed three methods to select the instances considered as real. As a result, it was obtained the highest values of the area under the ROC curves using the improved input combined with state of the art anomaly detection methods. Moreover, the three proposed selection methods significantly improve the existing method in the literature.

title: Techniques for generating language learning resources: a system for generating exercises for the differentiation of literal and metaphorical context
abstract: Automatic generation systems for language learning, as well as computer assisted language learning (CALL) systems, have evolved in general according to the demands of teachers and students. For those systems, it is important to review Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques aimed at that task, considering other disciplines such as Computational Sciences, Computational Linguistics and Creativity for teaching and learning other languages. This work is twofold. First, it presents an effort to review the main characteristics, methods and techniques used for its implementation, relevance and profitability of the systems developed in recent years; considering the importance to develop the abilities to recognize literal use of language as well as its non literal use, particularly metaphorical expressions in the natural process of learning a new language. For the second part, it presents a system that, based on the Trofi dataset (Gao G.,2018) , is able to generate different exercises to strengthen the students abilities to read and recognize the use of some verbs in literal and non literal contexts.

title: Studying Special Operators for the Application of Evolutionary Algorithms in the Search of Optimal Boolean Functions for Cryptography
abstract: The role of Boolean functions in modern cryptography has triggered the necessity of developing methods to construct them with adequate properties, such as balancedness and high nonlinearity making them more resistant to a variety of cryptanalytic attacks. Research into the construction of weightwise perfectly balanced Boolean functions using Evolutionary Algorithms is scarce but encouraging (e.g., [1]). In this work, we first investigate the effect on an evolutionary algorithms performance when using a penalty function against the solution using the repairment method. Second, we focus on the effect of problem specific crossover operators (e.g., those used on [2]), and particularly proposing a novel one free of solution repairs to preserve balancedness. The results obtained suggest that an adequate penalty factor and the use of specifically designed evolutionary operators are able to efficiently find Boolean functions with perfect balancedness and high nonlinearity, as desired.

title: Musical Composition using a Genetic Algorithm, Emotional Musical Theory and Machine Learning
abstract: This work proposes a mathematical model for computer aided music composition as a multi objective optimization problem. This work aims to create a framework to automatically generate a set of songs with two melodies by combining a genetic algorithm with machine learning. Musical patterns were studied [8, 3, 9, 1] to simplify them and apply them for the construction of the optimization model. This work uses recent emotional music theory to construct the optimization problem [6]. Three conflicting objective functions represent the desired characteristics of the melody to be created: (1) song happiness, (2) song minimalism, and (3) song genre. Two of these objectives are analytically designed, fulfilling well studied features like those in [5, 10, 6]. The third objective function was developed using a machine learning model like in [2, 4, 11]. The software JSymbolic is used [7] for extracting features in real time and getting the score with the machine learning model trainer in the present work. The results obtained by this work can be listened to by test examples presented in a video format. References 1. Bertin Mahieux, T.: Large Scale Pattern Discovery in Music. title: A vision based method for the detection of social interactions in co located spaces
abstract: Collaborative learning (CL) is an educational approach that assumes that learning is improved by successful socialization processes, designed to enhance the creation of meaningful knowledge. This means groups of learners working together to achieve some educational goals, immersed in a context of collective order called Social Shared Regulation of Learning (SSRL) [1]. Through SSRL, group members set up rules that control individual and collective actions, and provides a communal background to the educative process. Since SSRL is a underlying process, it is usually evaluated in terms of observables or measurables, like behavior (what the learners do) [2], [3]. However despite some advances, evaluation of SSRL is still a challenge for CL researching [4]. Traditional methods to assess SSRL include self reporting, or video based reporting, which involve a high content of subjectivity [5]. This work presents a novel application of computer vision and artificial intelligence techniques for automatic evaluation of SSRL [6]. Social behavior is specified by an interaction model used in groupware development, named MARS [7]. This interaction model is used to define participants, social roles, group activities, and pattern of movements that must be detected by vision techniques. Thus, SSRL is not viewed solely as the coordination of physical interactions between learners, but it includes social context provided by MARS. Both physicial activity detection and social information are used to infer SSRL knowledge, by means of Fuzzy Temporal Logic rules. The potency of this method is showed analyzing video recordings of an observational study, where participants were asked to design collectively a WEB interface. Analysis under this method were compared with analysis obtained by a traditional method to assess SSRL. The results of the comparison are promising, as they show good agreement between both analyses.

title: Data Stream Mining for Dynamic Student Modeling
abstract: Data Stream Mining (DSM) has become a research topic of greater interest in recent years. Its goal is to extract knowledge and hidden patterns from continuous data streams. In e learning systems, a large amount of data is generated from the interaction of the student with the system in the form of data streams, which nature or distribution changes over time. DSM techniques are able to incrementally analyze this kind of data, by creating models that adapt their structure on the fly. In this context, an interesting feature to model is the academic performance of students. In this paper, a methodology for dynamic student modeling using DSM classifiers is proposed. For this, the Students Academic Performance database, available on Kaggle, was used. Six DSM classifiers were implemented in MOA: Naive Bayes, Hoeffding Tree, Hoeffding Adaptive Tree, OzaBag, OzaBagADWIN, and Adaptive Random Forest. For the evaluation, the prequential error method, the Kappa statistic, and the execution time were used. The results obtained show that the Naive Bayes classifier generates the best results in terms of accuracy and execution times.

title: Explainable Machine Learning and Genetic Algorithms with a Case Study on Enhancement of Satisfaction in Time Use in Academic Settings
abstract: A strategy is presented in which accurate explainable machine learning models based on decision trees are used to generate both new avenues of research into the realities represented in the training datasets, and combined with metaheuristics such as genetic algorithms can also be used to investigate the minimum changes needed for some datapoints to become classified in a more desirable class, or to generate a more desirable regression value according to a decision maker. A case study is put forward in which decision trees are trained with a dataset with 30 at tributes, that are mostly about time use, to classify users into having or not satis faction with their time use in academic settings. Then genetic algorithms are used to find suggestions of minimum change or cost to move instances of users from absence to presence of satisfaction in time use in academic settings.

title: DISCRIMINATION BETWEEN COVID 19 & PNEUMONIA ON DIGITAL CHEST CT SCANS IMPLEMENTING A CONVOLUTIONAL NERURONAL NETWORK
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) in 2020 declared a pandemic caused by the coronavirus (COVID 19) that originated in Wuhan, China, which has caused thousands of victims, infecting millions worldwide. This virus presents symptoms similar to those of a common flu such as: cough, fever, fatigue and dyspnea, to mention a few, when an infected person exhales or emits respiratory particles containing the virus, it can spread rapidly to a person, who can deposit these particles on their eyes, mouth or nose. There are two types of tests to verify that a person has been infected, one of which is a reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT PCR) and antigen test, which, because of their materials and processing, can take time to give a positive or negative result, which is why with the help of artificial intelligence along with Machine Learning (ML) techniques can create a clinical tool to help detect better and in turn effective, the virus in the lungs. In the present work with the help of chest X ray images as a dataset having 3616 images for both classes, an implementation of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is proposed for the timely detection of patients with COVID 19, which is implemented a pre trained neural network named VGG16, which with training can achieve optimal accuracy for classification (COVID, PNEUMONIA), which will be displayed on a web page, using Flask, to be a friendly interface, and easy to use focused on the medical sector, being programmed in Python programming language, can help save resources and time for effective detection of the virus that currently affects society.

title: Unification of Source Code Re use Similarity Measures
abstract: Since any computer program is created from source code, it is relatively easy to create new programs from other authors. Automatic source code re use detection is useful to protect the inventions behind a computer program, but also to recover similar programs in a free software context that can be re used to create new programs. First, the methods for detecting the source code re use apply individual similarity measures to both source codes (the original and the suspect) to obtain the similarity of specific characteristics. After that, the information is combined in different ways to determine whether it is a re use case. For this problem, we propose an evolutionary approach to obtain the relevance of each individual similarity measure, but also, propose a unified method to combine the strengths of the individual similarity measures for increasing the recovery accuracy. Using a standard dataset in the experimentation, we obtain three new individual similarity systems that outperform their original systems and a new unified system that obtains the best result.

title: Feature selection by angle correlation for the detection of involuntary human activities using a body sensor network and machine learning classifiers
abstract: People are capable of performing activities with voluntary movements, such as lying down, sitting down, running or walking, however, there are activities with involuntary movements such as those that are the product of epileptic seizures (FIA). Using a body sensor suit, signals from inertial sensors were acquired and processed to obtain statistical characteristics. Using an algorithm based on the correlation of angles between features, it was shown that using certain signals favored the recognition of human activities and made it possible to identify which features and modules are not necessary by contrasting models.

title: Generation, optimization and validation of prototypes using an evolutionary approach
abstract: Prototype Generation (PG) methods seek to generate a subsample of prototypes that has the ability to classify the Test Sample (TS) with similar or better accuracy to the Training Sample (TS). The prototype subsample must be smaller than the Training Sample. PrG methods only use the TS to generate the prototype subsample. In addition, most PG methods will only improve the results for the NN rule. PG methods do not adapt prototypes to the classification problem. The methods do not allow the incorporation of a different metric and a classifier that makes use of the NN rule to evaluate prototypes. As a result, the prototypes generated are not adapted to the classification problem. To try to solve the problem found, a Genetic Algorithm (GA) was proposed that allows us to find the best possible solution within a space of solutions. The AG was combined with a KNN classifier and two evaluation metrics to generate the prototypes. To generate the first prototypes, the traditional genetic algorithm and a KNN classifier were used, with three general steps that are the initialization, generation, and validation of the prototype subsample. It was demonstrated that the proposed method generates representative prototypes for EM with different number of patterns, number of features, and number of classes, without import the imbalance between classes

title: Application of Neural Networks for the prediction of particulate pollutant PM10 in an industrial area
abstract: Due to the immense importance of environmental pollution today, it directly affects the health of all living beings because it is the leading cause of respiratory diseases. In the city of Nogales Sonora, the primary source of environmental pollution are the emissions generated by the industrial sector, being the PM10 pollutant because it is small particles that can be entered the body through the respiratory tract, turning it into a dangerous pollutant that can generate various damages to health. Predicting the concentrations of this pollutant can significantly help to take preventive measures such as alerting the affected population or even taking preventive actions to reduce pollutant emissions. This paper proposes a PM10 pollutant concentration prediction model that uses meteorological variables such as wind direction, wind speed, temperature, and relative humidity, together with PM10 pollutant concentrations. For this purpose, a database with historical records and SQL sentences is created to automate the validations dictated by the rules for automatic validation environments. We implemented a Multilayer Perceptron Backpropagation type model to predict the pollutant concentration in the next hour. To validate the proposed model, we implemented Mean Square Error (MSE), the Root of Mean Square Error (RMSE), and the Absolute Mean Error (MAE). We obtained the best result with a multilayer Perceptron architecture with two hidden layers, a learning rate of 0.01, and the sigmoid type activation function, using 8474 training patterns and 1695 patterns for testing.

title: Comparative Analysis of Clustering Methods for Fuzzy Classifiers Simplification
abstract: One problem of fuzzy systems for classification tasks is the exponential growth of rule generation, which translates into excessively long processing times. Different proposals in the literature address this problem through exhaustive rule reduction techniques, which achieve competitive results compared to conventional classifiers by reducing their computational complexity as well. This paper presents a comparative analysis among several clustering methods used to identify the structure of fuzzy classifiers, avoiding the use of exhaustive rule search algorithms and then the differential evolution algorithm is applied to improve their performance. The results show that the Gaussian Mixture Model is the most suitable clustering technique to identify the structure of fuzzy classifiers, since it provides the corresponding fuzzy model with highly competitive classification performance compared to other state of the art methods.

title: Automatic identification of suicidal ideation in texts using cascade classifiers
abstract: According to the 2021 World Health Organization report, suicide is a universal phenomenon that causes about 703,000 deaths per year, being among the first five causes of unnatural death. This event mainly affects young people between 15 and 29 years old, who are also the main users of social networks and the Internet. It is noteworthy that these digital platforms play a dual role in suicide issues, on the one hand, by allowing access to dangerous sites that can provide pro suicide information and, on the other hand, by allowing clues of suicidal ideations to be detected through shared content. This study presents a computational method based on a cascade classification that firstly detects the distribution of latent emotions in text and uses this output to identify signs of suicidal ideation. Our proposed method shows that the cascade architecture proves to be more robust than direct classification when there are no explicit signs of suicidal ideation. In addition, unlike direct classification, the cascade classification approach automatically provides information about the emotions that influence a person with suicidal thoughts.

title: CESAMMO: Categorical Encoding by Statistical Applied Multivariable Modeling
abstract: Categorical attributes are present in datasets used in machine learning (ML) tasks. Since most ML algorithms only accept numeric inputs, categorical instances must be converted to numbers. There are different encoding techniques to accomplish this task. During this conversion, it is important to preserve the underlying pattern in the dataset. Otherwise, there may be a loss of information that can negatively affect the performance of supervised learning algorithms. In this paper, we present an encoding technique based on finding those numbers or codes that preserve the relationship between the categorical attribute and the other variables of the dataset. We solved six supervised classification problems using the proposed technique with five different ML algorithms. Additionally, we compare the performance of the proposed technique with other ten encoding techniques. We found that the proposed technique outperforms the most commonly used encoding techniques for certain trained ML algorithms. On average, CESAMMO remained within the top 5 techniques in terms of performance of the 12 encoders tested.

title: Web crawler and classifier for news articles
abstract: In this work we present a crawler that collects news articles and a classifier that identifies the section that these articles belongs to. Due to the large number of available sources of information, a tool for gathering and filter news articles about specific interests it is necessary. For instance, a person might be interested in news about sports or science and it could be necessary to check several web sites to finally obtain these kind of news. Therefore, in this work we propose a web application that uses a crawler to automatically collect news articles from different websites, then a classifier determines the section of each news article and finally the news articles that match the section of interest are displayed in the web application.

title: Sentiment Analysis in the Rest Mex challenge
abstract: In this paper, we describe the participation of the ESCOM Artificial Intelligence group in the Rest Mex 2022 forum for the Sentiment Analysis task. The objective of the task was to create a model capable of predicting the polarity of the sentiment expressed by a tourist's opinion, as well as the type of attraction visited. For this task, we followed two different approaches: a lexicon based approach and a Machine Learning approach. In the lexicon based approach, we use a dictionary with words that have a numerical value that specifies the association with some emotions or attractions. We trained a logistic regression model for the Machine Learning approach to predict sentiment polarity and attractions. Our proposal obtained a combined score for both tasks of 0.85, which is only 0.03 points away from the best reported result.

title: How to construct the symmetric cycle of length 5 using Hajos construction with an adapted Rank Genetic Algorithm
abstract: We successfully adapted a rank based genetic algorithm to solve the problem of finding the symmetric cycle of length 5 from the complete symmetric digraph of order 3, using only Hajos construction, that is, directed Hajos join and identifying non adjacent vertices, a problem posed by Bang Jensen et. al. in 2020.

title: Heart Failure Disease Prediction Using Machine Learning Models
abstract: Heart failure disease affects 26 million people worldwide and it has a lower survival rate than breast or prostate cancer. An early diagnostic of the disease is very important for prevention and possible treatment. In this work, we propose using machine learning models to predict the probability of developing a heart failure disease in a patient. We compare two machine learning models over a public dataset of risk factors and patients' clinical features. After a comparative analysis, we find that a logistic regression model can predict 87% of the cases on the data base. After that, we implement an easy web application for heart failure disease prediction. We anticipate that applying this model hospitals will be able to reduce their patient admission due to heart failure disease and patients will be able to reduce their risk and avoid all the implicit costs.

title: Determination of Hazardous Asteroids Using Machine Learning
abstract: Potentially Hazardous Asteroid, or PHA, are near Earth asteroids with a minimum orbital intersection distance of 0.05 AU or less with the Earth. This distance is roughly one twentieth of the Earth Sun mean distance, and it is thought to be the biggest conceivable orbital perturbation within a 100 year time frame that might result in a collision. This work proposes to build a machine learning model that can be used to provide a preventive forecast that confirms which asteroid are harmful to the Earth and which are not. After an analysis of a public dataset in asteroid and comparing four machine learning models, we found that the XGBoost model performs with 98% of accuracy. We use this model to find the most relevant features in the dataset, and we validated this information with the literature.

title: Machine Learning Model of Digital Transformation Index for Mexican Households
abstract: Digital transformation refers to the change in all aspects of human society by the adoption of digital technologies. Different methodologies and measurements have been proposed to determine the level of digital transformation in regions or countries. In this work, we propose the creation of a digital transformation index for Mexican households using machine learning models for digital transformation measurement analysis and estimation. We include three dimensions in terms of the information and communication technologies infrastructure, availability of services, and usage. We also use a public dataset from the Mexican government to build and train three machine learning models. Experimental results validate that our methodology can deliver a digital transformation measurement using machine learning models consistently with 84% of accuracy and 84% of F1 score. We also prototype a simple web application using the best machine learning model found. We anticipate that measuring the digital transformation in companies, governments, and households allows better decisions in business intelligence and public policy.

title: The analysis of modern approaches of semantic parsing
abstract: Semantic parsing has recently gotten a lot of press in the community. Even though many neural modelling attempts have considerably improved performance, the data scarcity problem still exists. In semantic parsing, modelling apparent logical regularities is critical, making it challenging for neural networks to obtain high outcomes without task specific previous knowledge. This article will introduce critical views on modern approaches to semantic parsing, namely preliminary data preparation, modification, and a unique framework for infusing prior information into a model. We will demonstrate all relevant previous work and approaches designed to increase the accuracy model in neural networks. Also, an overview on how to generate a high precision synchronous context free language from the training data captures essential conditional independence aspects encountered in semantic parsing. The model is then taught about these structural properties using datum from this language to train a sequence to sequence recurrent network (RNN) model with an attention based coping mechanism. We will consider the possible ways to improve the accuracy of our recurrent network model on three semantic parsing data sets, resulting in new state of the art performance on the standard data set for models with similar supervision.

title: A novel Machine Learning method applied to the forecast of a Stock Market Index
abstract: The present paper recalls the aim of the ongoing work of applying the Artificial Organic Networks (AON) machine learning framework, to develop a new algorithm capable of generating a prediction for a stock market index, based on the Index Tracking Problem (ITP); thus, a conception of a new AON arrangement is needed. Pursuing this main goal, a first approach toward the definition of a new topology is presented, stating some general ideas along with the following discussion. Finally, we offered some preliminary results related to these main notions, considering the employment of a multiple non linear regressive (MNLR) model, to build an AON structure; the relative error obtained along the experiments was of the order of 1x10\textsuperscript{ 2}.

title: Credit Risk Models in the Mexican Context Using Machine Learning
abstract: The Default Rate is related to the period of the economic cycle in which they are observed, during expansion periods of the economy the default rate tends to be lower. But in contraction periods, the default rate tends to increase and this could be a risk for the stability of a countrys economy. Therefore, it is important to monitor the perspective of the economy in case it is expected to decrease or have abrupt movements. This work aims to identify the economic variables that determine the default rate of the Mexican Financial System and to find a machine learning model that forecasts the default rate. For this, we aggregate a dataset based on three official Mexican sources that compile data from 2013 to 2022, including the COVID 19 pandemic time frame. Then, we propose the analysis using two machine learning models. After the analysis, the results confirm that the artificial neural networks model shows better predictive power for the default rate values. We also implement an easy to use web application to estimate the default rate based on three simple variables. We anticipate this work might help on estimating the default rate and might impact on the strategic policies in the Mexican economy.

title: Neural Networks Based Optimization of Energy Losses in Power Grids of Kazakhstan
abstract: This article is focused on the main problem of power grid facilities in Mangystau region high level of depreciation of the assets of oil enterprises. Operation of mostly outdated equipment, moreover, in non optimal conditions, sometimes not depending on power transmission companies, creates significant value of technological losses of electric power in this equipment. The paper presents the results of modelling the parameters of the electrical system in the Matlab package using neural networks, which shows the relationship between the parameters of the optimal system and the system under study. A comparison with the results of analytical modelling is made. The correspondence of the optimization of the system to the target values obtained for the optimal replacement schemes of the receivers is shown.

title: Considerations in the Incremental Hypervolume Algorithm of the WFG
abstract: The hypervolume indicator (HV) has been subject of a lot of research in the last few years, mainly because its maximization yields near optimal approximations of the Pareto optimal front of a multi objective optimization problem. This feature has been exploited by several evolutionary optimizers, in spite of the considerable growth in computational cost that it is involved in the computation of HV as we increase the number of objectives. Some years ago, the Walking Fish Group (WFG) implemented a new version of the incremental hypervolume algorithm, named IWFG 1.01. This implementation is the fastest reported to date for determining the solution that contributes the least to the HV of a non dominated set. Nevertheless, this new version has gone mostly unnoticed by the research community. We believe that this is due to an error in the source code provided by the authors of this algorithm, which appears when coupling it to a multi objective evolutionary algorithm. In this paper, we describe this error, and we propose a solution to fix it. Moreover, we illustrate the significant gains in performance produced by IWFG~1.01 in many objective optimization problems (i.e., problems having three or more objectives), when integrated into the \textit{S} Metric Selection Evolutionary Multi Objective Algorithm (SMS EMOA).

title: Functions of similarity and dissimilarity and correlation for the domain of probability distributions
abstract: Similarity and dissimilarity measures are often highly requested in areas such as Recommender Systems, Machine Learning, Data Mining, Neural Networks, etc. However, when specifying the domain we have that these are used on the domain of real numbers, but these can also be used in other domains, such as probability distributions, in this paper the properties that fulfill the similarity and dissimilarity measure are explained on the domain of probability distributions, and new functions of similarity, dissimilarity and correlation are developed that will be used specifically for this domain.

title: Classification of flood warnings applying a convolutional neural network
abstract: The effects of climate change create climatic temporal imbalances that favor the development of hydrometeorological phenomena and cause socioeconomic damage when they occur. In the absence of EWS and dedicated monitoring stations, the effectiveness of a CNN model is tested to interpret and label information on the climatic conditions of the Misantlas river basin and its surroundings, regarding to the flood hazard level. Aiming to classify rainfall events in the region using information collected through 3 weather stations around the region: northern zone of Veracruz, specifically the municipality of Misantla. Neural networks can maximize the use of information collected by weather stations, providing a safer environment in the event of floods, and having a positive effect on the preservation of human activity. The information provided allows to label data as VERDE, AMARILLO and ROJO with more than 95% accuracy, performing better when working with a large number of validation data, but also shows a slowdown during the integration of larger training data sets.

title: Machine Learning Techniques in Credit Default Prediction
abstract: Digital transformation after the pandemic is a must if a company wants to survive in a highly competitive environment. Machine Learning (ML) applications are no strangers to Digital Transformations, and banks are looking for ways to improve efficiency by means of similar technologies. In this work, we propose a machine learning model for predicting the credit default using the LendingClub public dataset. The accepted loans include data ranging from 2007 to 2017. For this purpose, we implement support vector machines and logistic regression models. The results showed that support vector machines is a high accurate model (93%) for predicting the credit default.

title: Ventilator Pressure Prediction Using a Regularized Regression Model
abstract: The mechanical ventilation is one of the most frequent methods used in Intensive Care Units (ICUs) to improve the breathing of patients. During the early days of the COVID 19 pandemic, the use of mechanical ventilators has been crucial. In this work, we propose to build a Lasso regression model based on lung simulators for predicting the airway pressure in the respiratory circuit of ventilators while breathing. We model the whole breathing process in two separate states. After that, we analyze the feature importance in the regression model to better understand the ventilator pressure prediction. We anticipate this model would help improving the patient's health and overcoming the cost barrier of new methods for mechanical ventilators.

title: Cardiovascular Disease Detection Using Machine Learning
abstract: The detection of Cardiovascular Diseases (CVDs) prematurely is of great interest for the Healthcare Industry. According to the World Health Organization, heart diseases represent 32% of global deaths by 2019. In this work, we propose building an interpretable machine learning model to detect CVDs. For this, we use a public dataset consisting of over 320~thousand records and 279~features. We explore the performance of three well known classifiers and we build them using hyper parameter techniques. For interpretability, feature relevance is tested. After the experimental results, we found Random Forest to performed the best with 94% of accuracy and 81% of area under the ROC curve. We also implement an easy web application as a tool for detecting CVDs using relevant features information.

title: A bibliometric review of methods and algorithms for generating corpora for learning vector word embeddings
abstract: Natural Language Processing (NLP) problems are among the hardest Machine Learning (ML) problems due to complex nature of the human language. Introduction of word embeddings improved the performance of ML models on various NLP tasks as text classification, sentiment analysis, machine translation, etc. Word embeddings are real valued vector representations of words in a specific vector space. Producing quality word embeddings that are then used as input to downstream NLP tasks is important in obtaining a good performance. To accomplish it, corpora of sufficient size is needed. Corpora may be formed in a multitude of ways, including text that was originally electronic, transcripts of spoken language, optical character recognition, and synthetically producing text from the available dataset. The study provides the most recent bibliometric analysis on the topic of corpora generation for learning word vector embeddings. The analysis is based on the publication data from 2006 to 2022 retrieved from Scopus scientific database. A descriptive analysis method has been employed to obtain statistical characteristics of the publications in the research area. Results of the systematic analysis show the evolution of the field over the time and highlights influential contributions to the field. It is believed that compiled bibliometric review could help researchers get knowledge of the general state of the scientific knowledge, its descriptive features, patterns, and insights in order to systematically design their studies.

title: Design of a Decision Support System to improve fertilser application for Winter Wheat in the UK and Spain: A case study.
abstract: Fertiliser application is critical when improving yield in agriculture, the correct and optimal usage has a significant effect in crop development. The proper usage of fertiliser not only helps with the crop's growth and yield but also has an impact on the field's health for future crops. In this paper a comparative study of fertiliser utilisation for winter wheat in both the UK and Spain is conducted. While Winter Wheat can grow in a variety of climates, the crop's response to different fertilisers and its application rates relies on a variety of variables (soil types, weather, elevation, etc.) and differs in both countries. Based on the conducted study, we then built a DSS to help farmers in both countries improve fertiliser usage by analyzing and comparing the best practices for the winter wheat crop and having the system recommend different options. A simple web based DSS is developed and an empirical analysis is conducted to test the DSS, the results of the analysis is presented and future work is discussed.

title: A NLP DNN Automated Method for Bilingual News Tweets Virality Classification
abstract: As more governments, companies and organizations turn to Social Media for, both, creating more impact and influence in society, and for listening to the living pulse of public opinion, a method for virality classification becomes more relevant. Our research has produced an automated method for the collection, labeling, training and classification of News Tweets as viral or non viral, this method improves over our previous research by generalizing the classification of tweets in multiple languages using a single RNN LSTM configuration, also it automates the process so no human intervention is needed, but human supervision, on line and forensic analysis is enabled. This approach creates the opportunity for experts of other disciplines to use the method through a Mobile Web App enabling transdisciplinary research. Our method produces classifications across multiple languages with an F1 Score in a consistent range from 0.82 to 0.86. The examples provided in this work are from Spanish and English News Tweets.

title: Design of a soft mood sensor for food recommendation using Deep Learning
abstract: The analysis of emotions and moods in people allows us to know, among many things, tastes, which allows us to offer personalized products or services. This article shows a way of detecting and classifying people's moods using selfie photographs for subsequent use in restaurant dish recommenders. For this solution we propose to make use of two neural networks; the first one will be used for the detection of Action Units (AU) present in the works of Paul Ekman, and a second neural network to classify the correct mood once the AUs have been previously detected and classified.

title: Video Surveillance of Beehives using Computer Vision and IoT
abstract: Different animal species beneficial to the environment and human beings face imminent extinction due to different types of problems. The preservation of these species for the survival of humans and ecology is necessary. To preserve species, it is necessary to identify diseases and pests, through surveillance and observation by man. The honey bee (apis melifera) is an endangered specie, and its care and preservation are already necessary. The Llano Aguascalientes region, Mexico faces problems of the extinction of this specie.
