abstract: Enormous quantities of structured and unstructured data on the Web and the need to extract and derive useful knowledge from such data make Semantic Web and Big Data Technology explorations of paramount importance. Open semantic web data created using standard protocols (RDF, RDFS, OWL) consists of billions of records in the form of data collections called ``linked data". With the ever increasing linked big data on the Web, it is imperative to process this data with powerful and scalable techniques in distributed processing environments such as MapReduce. There are several distributed RDF processing systems, including SemaGrow, FedX, SPLENDID, PigSPARQL, SHARD, SPARQLGX, that are developed over the years. However, there is a need for computational and qualitative comparison of the differences and similarities among these systems. In this paper, we extend a previous comparative analysis to a diverse study with respect to qualitative and quantitative analysis view, through experimental approach for these distributed RDF systems. We examine each of the selected RDF query systems with respect to the implementation set up, system architecture, underlying framework, and data storage of the systems. We used two widely used RDF benchmark datasets, namely LUBM and WatDiv. Furthermore, we evaluate the performance in terms of query adaptability and query processing time for different queries. The results of the experiments in this study show that SemaGrow distributed system performed more efficiently compared to FedX and Splendid, even though in smaller queries the former performed slower.

title: Recurrent Graph Convolution Network for Rumor Detection
abstract: The development of social media has provided an ideal platform for sharing information, but it has also become a hotbed for rumor posting and spreading. Existing rumor detection methods mainly look for clues from the textual content, static propagation structures. However, previous work does not fully use users' information while ignoring the dynamic change of the propagation structure. Therefore, this paper proposes a rumor detection model based on the dynamic propagation structure called Recurrent Graph Convolutional Network (Re GCN). We construct a more informative post representation based on the post's textual content and the user's information. Then, we construct a dynamically changing propagation structure representation by dividing rumor propagation into multiple stages and capture the dynamically changing propagation features by Bi Directional Recurrent Neural Networks (Bi RNN) and Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN). Finally, the rumors are classified by fusing the information at each stage through the attention mechanism. Experimental results on two real world datasets show that the proposed method has significant improvement compared to the state of the art benchmark methods.

title: QuatRE: Relation Aware Quaternions for Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: We propose a simple yet effective embedding model to learn quaternion embeddings for entities and relations in knowledge graphs. Our model aims to enhance correlations between head and tail entities given a relation within the Quaternion space with Hamilton product. The model achieves this goal by further associating each relation with two relation aware rotations, which are used to rotate quaternion embeddings of the head and tail entities, respectively. Experimental results show that our proposed model produces state of the art performances on well known benchmark datasets for knowledge graph completion.

title: Exploring Relevance and Coherence for Automated Text Scoring using Multi task Learning
abstract: With the explosive growth of the information on the Internet, the evaluation of the quality and credibility of web content has become more important than ever before. In this work, we focus on the quality assessment of texts. Recently, various methods have been proposed for the automated text scoring task and obtained competitive results. However, few studies have focused on both relevance and coherence, which are two important factors in evaluating text quality. To improve the scoring task, we propose two auxiliary tasks using negative sampling and integrate them into a multi task learning framework. The first auxiliary task is relevance modeling and the other one is coherence modeling. We evaluate our model on the Automated Student Assessment Prize (ASAP) dataset. Experimental results show that our model achieves higher Quadratic Weighted Kappa (QWK) scores with an improvement of 1.5% on average.

title: Inductive Knowledge Enhanced Recommender Systems Using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: In recent years there has been growing interest in exploiting knowledge graphs (KGs) for improving the accuracy, diversity, and interpretability of recommendation results. Existing recommender systems supporting KGs, however, only work in transductive settings, where predictions are only made for users and items seen during training; furthermore, existing inductive systems, which are able to make predictions involving unseen objects, do not support KGs. In this paper, we propose a novel approach that is effective in inductive settings, and which can seamlessly incorporate large scale KGs to enhance the quality of recommendations. Our results show that our system, while being more general than the baselines, is able to outperform them on the restricted cases to which the baselines are applicable.

title: Trigger GNN: A Trigger Based Graph Neural Network for Nested Named Entity Recognition
abstract: Nested named entity recognition (nested NER) aims to identify the entity boundaries and recognize categories of the named entities in a complex hierarchical sentence. Some works have been done using the character level, word level, or lexicon level methods. However, such researches ignore the role of the complementary annotations. To bridge the gap, we investigate a trigger based graph neural network (Trigger GNN) approach to leverage the nested NER. We posit that the entity triggers (one of the complementary annotations) can add in complementary supervision signals on the whole sentences and thus help the model to learn and generalize more efficiently. Experiments show that the Trigger GNN is cost effective and efficient on four public NER datasets, and it can effectively alleviate the nested NER.

title: Semantic Path Guided Graph Neural Network for Heterogeneous Graph Embedding
abstract: Heterogeneous graph embedding is to embed rich semantics and structural information of a heterogeneous graph into low dimensional node representations. Most existing methods define multiple meta paths to capture the heterogeneity and rich semantic information in the heterogeneous graph. However, it is a non trivial task to learn effective heterogeneous graph embedding for meta path based models because of three major challenges: (1) ignore node content features; (2) learn limited semantic information if the meta paths can be considered alone; (3) lack of certain explanation when assigning different weighting values for normalizing neighbors of the target node via the attention mechanism. To address these issues, we propose a novel model \underline{Sem}antic \underline{Path} Guided \underline{G}raph \underline{N}eural \underline{N}etwork (SemPathGNN) to further boost the final performance of the task. Specifically, in order to deal with node heterogeneity in the heterogeneous graph, we first leverage node content transformation to encapsulate input heterogenous node attributes. We then construct a joint sampling strategy from a semantic path based structure perspective to extract complex semantics and structural information and guide the neighbor selection in the heterogeneous graph, while a similarity based importance computation strategy is introduced to measure weighting values between the target node and its specified semantic path based neighbors. Moreover, to further generate preliminary embedding of the target node by aggregating feature messages from these semantic path based neighbors. Finally, SemPathGNN combines messages via cross semantic path based structure aggregation built upon the attention mechanism to obtain the final embedding for each node in the graph. Experiments conducted on four datasets from different domains for node classification and node clustering demonstrate that SemPathGNN achieves more accurate prediction results as compared to several state of the art baselines.

title: Enhancing Sequential Recommendation via Decoupled Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Sequential recommendation can capture dynamic interest patterns of users based on user interaction sequences. Recently, there has been interest in integrating the knowledge graph (KG) into sequential recommendation. Existing works suffer from two main challenges: a) representing each entity in the KG as a single vector can confound heterogeneous information about the entity; b) triple based facts are modeled independently, lacking the exploration of high order connectivity between entities. To solve the above challenges, we decouple the KG into two subgraphs, namely CRoss user Behavior based graph and Intrinsic Attribute based graph (Crbia), depending on the type of relation between entities. We further propose a CrbiaNet based on the two subgraphs. First, CrbiaNet obtains behavior level and attribute level semantic features from these two subgraphs independently by different graph neural networks, respectively. Then, CrbiaNet applies a sequential model incorporating these semantic features to capture dynamic preference of the users. Extensive experiments on three real world datasets show that our proposed CrbiaNet outperforms previous state of the art knowledge enhanced sequential recommendation models by a large margin consistently.

title: Relational Graph Convolutional PonderNet for Entity Classification in Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Despite the vast amount of information encoded in knowledge graphs, information about the class affiliation of entities remain often incomplete. Neural networks, in particular Graph Convolutional Neural Networks, have been shown to be effective predictors to complete information about the class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs. However, these models do not learn the class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs incorporating the complexity of the task, which negatively affects the prediction capabilities of the models. To address this problem, we introduce Relational Graph Convolutional PonderNet, an end to end network that learns the prediction of class affiliation of entities in knowledge graphs within a Markov process. The number of computational steps is learned during training using a geometric distribution. At the same time, the loss function combines insights from the field of evidential learning. As a result, the model generalizes to graphs of varying complexity and is thus effective in terms of both training time tailored to complexity and prediction accuracy. The experiments show a strong performance improvement over existing models. Based on the chosen hyperparameters for the geometric distribution, the expected number of computation steps can be adjusted to improve efficiency during training.

title: Neural Expert Finding
abstract: An expert finding system allows one to find individuals who have expertise in certain fields or domains. However, most of the expert finding systems, based on document based topic modeling or keyword search methods, are limited in their capability to encode contextual knowledge from natural language. This paper presents Neural Expert Finder (NEF), a novel method that explores neural models to learn contextual expert representations utilizing research interests and academic publication titles. NEF uses a transfer learning approach based on transformer encoder networks to leverage the rich semantic and syntactic patterns of language encoded in pre trained language models (PLMs). To fine tune the language models, we propose a self supervised learning approach utilizing contrastive factual text sequences formulated from raw structured data. For experimentation, we build a new benchmark dataset for expert finding named SGComp, curated from experts university and Google Scholar profiles. Our empirical evaluation methods demonstrate that the proposed method can learn effective contextual representations and identify experts most relevant to specific research areas. In addition, we utilise SGComp and three domain specific public datasets to compare NEF against ExpFinder nVSM, a state of the art (SOTA) system in expert finding and demonstrate consistent improved performance with the neural learning paradigm of NEF.

title: Predicting the Acceptability of Atomic Candidate OWL Axioms
abstract: Candidate axiom scoring is the task of assessing the acceptability of a candidate axiom against the evidence provided by known facts or data. Being able to accurately score candidate axioms is a prerequisite for automatic schema or ontology induction, but can also be useful for ontology and/or knowledge graph validation. Accurateaxiom scoring heuristics are often heavy to compute, which is a big problem if one wants to exploit them in iterative search methods like level wise generate and test or evolutionary algorithms, where large numbers of candidate axioms need to be scored. We tackle the challenge of learning a surrogate predictive model of the score of candidate axioms that is fast to execute yet accurate enough to be used in such settings. For this purpose, we leverage a semantic similarity measure extracted from the subsumption hierarchy of an ontology. We prove that the method proposed in this paper is able to learn the acceptability labels of candidate OWL axioms with high accuracy, and that it can do so for multiple types of OWL axioms.

title: KIR: A Knowledge enhanced Interpretable Recommendation Method
abstract: With the popularization of the Internet and the development of information technology, information data has shown explosive growth, and the Recommendation System (RS) is of great significance for screening effective information and improving the efficiency of information acquisition. The existing recommendation methods can improve the accuracy of the recommendation results to a certain extent, but the interpretation of the recommendation results is insufficient and difficult to satisfy the desire of some users to understand the recommendation basis due to the lack of interpretability. For this reason, the Knowledge Graph (KG) is introduced as auxiliary information of the RS and calculates the importance of entity and relation in the KG to users, and use these as the basis for the recommendation. First, item categories are introduced to enhance the impact on user preferences. Second, an Attention Mechanism (AM) is proposed to distinguish users interests in different contextual entity relation sets in the KG. Finally, multiple feature information is input into the Convolutional Neural Net work (CNN) to extract users preferences. The experimental results prove that the model has a certain improvement in the accuracy of the recommendation effect, and at the same time, it can better explain the reasons for the recommendation.

title: Handling Out Of Vocabulary words in Question Answering on Knowledge Bases
abstract: Accessing the large volumes of information available in public knowledge bases might be complicated for those users unfamiliar with the SPARQL query language. Automatic translation of questions posed in natural language in SPARQL has the potential of overcoming this problem. Existing systems based on neural machine translation are very effective but easily fail in recognizing words that are Out Of the Vocabulary (OOV) of the training set. This is a serious issue while querying large ontologies. In this paper, we combine Named Entity Linking, Named Entity Recognition, and Neural Machine Translation to perform automatic translation of natural language questions into SPARQL queries. We demonstrate empirically that our approach is more effective and resilient to OOV words than existing approaches by running the experiments on Monument, QALD 9, and LC QuAD v1, which are well known datasets for Question Answering over DBpedia.

title: A Geospatial Join Optimization for Federated GeoSPARQL querying
abstract: We present a join optimization method for federated linked geospatial data. This optimization targets within distance queries in cases where the shapes that are compared are served from different sources of the federation. This operation is computationally expensive, because it cannot be answered from the spatial index of any of the individual data sources in the federation. Our optimization augments the subqueries prepared for each source with additional restrictions on topological relations that must be satisfied and that (a) can be answered from the spatial index of the individual data sources; (b) do not change the semantics of the query. We evaluate our optimization on data and queries derived from a real world workflow over land usage data. Evaluation shows that our optimization substantially improves query processing time.

title: An Analysis of Links in Wikidata
abstract: Wikidata is becoming one of the most prominent open knowledge graphs on the Web. Relying on a community of users with different expertise, this cross domain knowledge graph is directly related to other data sources. This paper investigates how far Wikidata is connected to other sources in the Linked Data ecosystem. We adapt a previous definition of ontology and instance links to the terminological part of the Wikidata vocabulary and perform an analysis of the links in Wikidata to external datasets and ontologies from the Linked Data ecosystem. As a side effect, this reveals insights on the ontological expressiveness of meta properties used in Wikidata. The results of this analysis show to what degree Wikidata is already topologically central to the Linked Data ecosystem and how the Wikidata ontology connects and reuses existing ontologies on the Web.

title: TempCaps: A Capsule Network based Embedding Model for Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs store the dynamics of entities and relations during a time period. In real world scenarios, typical temporal knowledge graphs often suffer from incomplete dynamics with missing facts. Hence, modeling temporal knowledge graphs to complete the missing facts is an important task. In this paper, we tackle the temporal knowledge graph completion task by proposing TempCaps, which is a Capsule network based embedding model for Temporal knowledge graph completion. TempCaps models temporal knowledge graphs by introducing a novel dynamic routing aggregator inspired by capsule networks. Specifically, TempCaps builds entity embeddings by dynamically routing retrieved temporal relation and neighbor information. Experimental results demonstrate that TempCaps reaches state of the art performance for temporal knowledge graph completion. Additional analysis also shows that TempCaps is efficient.

title: Knowledge Graph Entity Type Prediction with Relational Aggregation Graph Attention Network
abstract: Most of the knowledge graph completion methods focus on inferring missing entities or relations between entities in the knowledge graphs. However, many knowledge graphs are missing entity types. The goal of entity type prediction in the knowledge graph is to infer the missing entity types that belong to entities in the knowledge graph, that is, (entity,entity type=?). At present, most knowledge graph entity type prediction models tend to model entities and entity types, which will cause the relations between entities to not be effectively used, and the relations often contain rich semantic information. To utilize semantic information contained in the relation when performing entity type prediction, we propose a method for entity type prediction based on relational aggregation graph attention network (RACE2T), which consists of an encoder relational aggregation graph attention network (FRGAT) and a decoder (CE2T). The encoder FRGAT uses the scoring function of the knowledge graph completion method to calculate the attention coefficient between the entities and the relation entity pairs in its neighborhood. This attention coefficient will be used to aggregate the information of relations and entities in the neighborhood of the entity to exploit the information of the relations. The decoder CE2T is designed based on convolutional neural network, which models the entity embeddings output by FRGAT and entity type embeddings, and performs entity type prediction. The experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper is superior to state of the art methods.

title: Union and Intersection of all Justifications
abstract: We present new algorithms for computing the union and intersection of all justifications for a given ontological consequence without first computing the set of all justifications. Our goal is to use these sets to explain the consequences and, if needed, repair them. Through an empirical evaluation, we show that our approach behaves well in practice for expressive description logics. In particular, the union of all justifications can be computed much faster than with existing justification enumeration approaches.

title: Exploring the impact of literal transformations within Knowledge Graphs for Link Prediction
abstract: Knowledge graphs encode knowledge relevant for many applications, but in many cases they are inherently incomplete. Thus, Link Prediction methods have been proposed to infer new triples in order to complete a given Knowledge Graph. Usually, such Link Prediction methods ignore literals in spite of the fact that literals can express useful information about entities not encoded in relations. The existing methods that do incorporate literal information (e.g. LiteralE) do so by modifying the model and loss function. However, it would be desirable if any link prediction method could use literals. Thus, we propose a new approach that relies on graph transformations which transform literals in such a way that existing Link Prediction algorithms can leverage the literal information. In particular, we define three transformations and evaluate them in comparison to the state of the art approaches. In most cases, the additional triples induced by our transformations lead to a performance increase and even state of the art performance can be reached when comparing against LiteralE. Our approach can be seen as a new baseline for encoding literal information into relational triples for Link Prediction.

title: RDFtex: Knowledge Exchange between LaTeX based Research Publications and Scientific Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SciKGs) aim to integrate scientific knowledge in a machine readable manner. For populating SciKGs, research publications pose a central source of scientific knowledge. Hence, the goal is to represent both contextual information, i.e., metadata, and contentual information, i.e., original contributions like definitions and experimental results, of research publications in SciKGs. However, typical forms of research publications like the traditional papers cannot be easily integrated into SciKGs. Furthermore, they do not support making direct use of the rich information SciKGs provide. To tackle this, the present paper proposes RDFtex, a framework that enables (1) the import of contributions represented in SciKGs to facilitate the preparation of LaTeX based research publications and (2) the export of original contributions to facilitate their integration into SciKGs. We demonstrate the frameworks functionality using the example of the present paper itself since it was prepared with RDFtex and its currently implemented features.

title: Deep Correlation based Concept Recommendation for MOOCs
abstract: The current course recommendation in massive open online courses (MOOCs) usually ignores students interests in some certain type of knowledge concepts, resulting in low completion of most courses. Therefore, it requires a concept recommendation to help students accurately choose courses in MOOCs. In this paper, we propose Deep Correlation based Concept Recommendation (DCCR) for MOOCs. It gathers the interactive information obtained by different entities through meta paths in MOOCs and extracts the semantic information of knowledge concepts. To deeply capture the correlation information among users, a multi relation graph is built to generate the correlation features which aggregates the abundant information under different meta paths. Then through the graph convolutional neural networks, entity embeddings of users and knowledge concepts are generated. Additionally, a novel fusion function is designed to get the final joint representations reasonably. By verifying on two public datasets, experiments show that DCCR outperforms the state of the art methods.

title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Refinement Operators in ALC
abstract: Refinement operators have been successfully applied to class expression learning on RDF knowledge graphs. However, state of the art models based on refinement operators often have to explore a large number of class expressions to find an adequate solution for a given learning problem. Arguably, the reliance of state of the art models on myopic heuristic functions contributes to this limitation. In contrast, deep reinforcement learning provides effective means to address myopia by estimating discounted cumulative future rewards. In this work, we leverage deep reinforcement learning to accelerate class expression learning in ALC by proposing DRILL a novel class expression learning approach that uses a convolutional deep Q learning model to steer its search. We evaluate DRILL on 4 benchmark datasets by using 390 learning problems. Our experiments suggest that DRILL converges to goal states at least 2.7 times faster than state of the art models on all learning problems. The results of our statistical significance test confirms that DRILL converges to goal states significantly faster (p value <1%) than state of the art models on all benchmark datasets. To foster reproducible research, we provide an open source implementation of DRILL, including pretrained models, training and evaluation scripts.

title: Comparative Research in Stream Reasoning
abstract: The diverse research efforts in recent years in the area of stream reasoning (SR) led to a wide range of SR engines. However, the lack of standardization and the diverse choices in SR, e.g., tuple driven vs. time driven engines, stream level vs. graph level entailment, streaming all results vs. newly derived ones, mean that real comparability among the engines is hardly given. A first step towards achieving comparability and standardization is the RSP QL model, implemented in the RSP4J framework, which allows for describing and formalizing the semantics of SR engines. In this work, we quantify the in use importance of several key performance indicators (KPIs) and features based on the results of a survey. We then compare SR engines along these KPIs with the CityBench and the CSRBench oracle. Our analysis of SR systems shows that the two RSP4J implementations C SPARQL2.0 and YASPER outperform the well known C SPARQL implementation both in terms of performance and configurability. Our comparison against a naive SR extension of the incremental reasoning engine RDFox shows that SR engines still have potential for improvement. Only when it comes to great system loads, the SR engines stay ahead of RDFox because they start dropping input triples to prevent an overload. Finally, we propose a unifying interface for SR benchmarks meant to ease future benchmarking efforts, especially for RSP4J based engines.

title: Popularity Prediction on Online Content with Fusion of Text and Trend History SubGraph Neural Network
abstract: The popularity prediction of online contents has been an important task in many fields such as advertising, recommendation system, public opinion analysis. Most methods mainly use the own information of text, user, and trend history (TH) of online contents to predict future popularity. However, these methods ignore the relations between online contents. The relations can be taken as external factors for prediction in some degree, which is important and hard to capture. Graph neural network (GNN) is an excellent method to extract the relations. But how to construct graph as external factors and how to get the feature representation of nodes efficiently in GNN are two key problems for prediction popularity. In order to solve these problems, we propose a method named Fusion of Text and Trend SubGraph Neural Network (FTSGNN) in this paper. Firstly, text subgraphs and TH subgraphs instead of the global graph are constructed in FTSGNN. The two kinds of subgraphs are constructed with the texts and TH in each sliding window, respectively. Only online contents within the sliding window is used for constructing subgraphs, which is more efficient. Secondly, deep graph infomax (DGI), which is an unsupervised method, is introduced in FTSGNN to obtain the feature embeddings of each online context easily. Finally, these feature embeddings and TH of online contents are fused to train the model for prediction. Experiments on the Sina Weibo dataset show that FTSGNN obtains better accuracy and efficiency than the method only with TH, which improves MSE from 0.402 to 0.226 and MAPE from 0.283 to 0.242 with text and 2 hours' TH.

title: Refining Large Identity Graphs using the Unique Name Assumption
abstract: The Unique Name Assumption (UNA) supposes that two terms with distinct IRIs from the same dataset do not refer to the same real world entity. The UNA has been used to refine identity graphs: if the UNA is true, then identity links (e.g. those with relation owl:sameas) between two entities defined by the same dataset can be considered erroneous. While this works on a small scale, it has not been validated on the scale of large integrated knowledge graphs, such as the LOD cloud, which contain data from many different sources. We propose a concrete definition of the UNA with tolerance towards exceptions, namely the internal UNA (iUNA). We compare our definition with existing definitions with respect to some real world datasets. Based on the iUNA, we propose an algorithm to identify erroneous links in an identity graph of half a billion triples extracted from the LOD Cloud. The algorithm employs an SMT solver and takes advantage of the latter's ability to efficiently reason over equality and remove a minor amount of links. Finally, we demonstrate how additional information can improve the accuracy of such refinements.

title: Text Enhanced Relational Context Hyperbolic Graph Convolution Network for Link Prediction
abstract: Knowledge graph (KG) embeddings learn low dimensional representations of entities and relations and can be used for knowledge graph completion task. There exists a lot of hierarchical relations in the knowledge graph, but the hierarchical data in the knowledge graph are not well utilized. Besides, existing knowledge representation learning models lack effective utilization of entity semantic information contained in textual information of entities. Finally, the context information of relation often plays an important role in relation representation, but the existing model does not make full use of it. Therefore, we proposes a Text Enhanced Relational Context Hyperbolic Graph Convolution Network (TRHGCN) for link prediction, which makes full use of the context information of relations and text description of entities to represent the relations and entities in knowledge graph. TRHGCN model utilize the hyperbolic space, which can better excavate the hierarchical structure of the knowledge graph. Link prediction experiments are carried out on FB15K 237, WN18RR, NELL 995 dataset. The results demonstrate that TRHGCN is significantly outperforms existing state of the art methods on benchmark models such as CompGCN and ConvE, and our model performs better on hierarchical relations.

title: Supervised Knowledge Aggregation for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: We explore data driven rule aggregation based on latent feature representations in the context of knowledge graph completion. For a given query and a collection of rules obtained by a symbolic rule learning system, we propose end to end trainable aggregation functions for combining the rules into a confidence score answering the query. Despite using latent feature representations for rules, the proposed models remain fully interpretable in terms of the underlying symbolic approach. While our models improve the base learner constantly and achieve competitive results on various benchmark knowledge graphs, we outperform current state of the art with respect to a biomedical knowledge graph by a significant margin. We argue that our approach is in particular well suited for link prediction tasks dealing with a large multi relational knowledge graph with several million triples, while the queries of interest focus on only one specific target relation.

title: A Human in the Loop Approach for Personal Knowledge Graph Construction from File Names
abstract: Knowledge workers' personal and work related concepts (e.g. persons, projects, topics) are usually not sufficiently covered by knowledge graphs. Yet, already handmade classification schemes, prominently folder structures, naturally mention several of their concepts in file names. Thus, such data could be a promising source for constructing personal knowledge graphs. However, this idea poses several challenges: file names are usually noisy non grammatical text snippets, while folder structures do not clearly define how concepts relate to each other. To cope with this semantic gap, we include knowledge workers as humans in the loop to guide the building process with their feedback. Our semi automatic personal knowledge graph construction approach consists of four major stages: domain term extraction, ontology population, taxonomic and non taxonomic relation learning. Machine learning models and a rule based system immediately learn from user feedback and predict new A Box statements. We conduct four expert interviews from different domains in an industrial scenario to evaluate our approach. Results show that file systems may serve as a suitable source and, combined with our approach, already yield useful personal knowledge graphs with moderate effort spent.

title: Certainty is the easy path: expressing without asserting named graphs
abstract: Knowledge in most scholarly disciplines is characterised by diverse degrees of certainty. Asserting such statements in RDF is hindered by the correct representation of uncertain or evolving aspects (due to e.g., ignorance, changes of opinion, disagreements, challenges, etc.). In this article we examine and discuss the need and usefulness of expressing without asserting (EWA) arbitrary claims as RDF named graphs. We describe how most of the currently existing approaches (e.g., reification, n ary relationships, N3, RDF*, etc.) seem to treat non asserted statements more as a side effect, rather than a design issue on its own right, and how the semantics of RDF 1.1 named graphs does not effectively contribute to the task. We propose a solution, called Conjectures to express statements whose truth value is not specified, and therefore cannot be asserted, regardless of the semantics chosen for named graphs among the many available. We evaluate the effectiveness of our approach by comparing it with prior attempts.

title: Expressive Scene Graph Generation using Commonsense Knowledge Integration for Visual Understanding and Reasoning
abstract: Scene graph generation aims to capture the semantic elements in images by modelling objects and their relationships in a structured manner, which are essential for visual understanding and reasoning tasks including image captioning, visual question answering, visual storytelling and image retrieval. The existing scene graph generation approaches provide limited performance and expressiveness for higher level visual understanding and reasoning. This challenge can be mitigated by leveraging commonsense knowledge, such as related facts and background knowledge, about the semantic elements in scene graphs. In this paper, we propose the integration of diverse commonsense knowledge about the semantic elements in scene graphs to generate rich and expressive scene graphs using a heterogeneous knowledge source that contains commonsense knowledge consolidated from seven different knowledge bases. The graph embeddings of the object nodes are used to leverage their structural patterns in the knowledge source to compute similarity metrics for graph refinement and enrichment. We performed experimental and comparative analysis on the benchmark Visual Genome dataset using the standard metric, in which the proposed method achieved a higher recall rate (R@K = 29.89, 35.4, 39.12 for K = 20, 50, 100) as compared to the existing state of the art technique (R@K = 25.8, 33.3, 37.8 for K = 20, 50, 100). The qualitative results of the proposed method in a downstream task of image generation showed that more realistic images are generated using the commonsense integrated scene graphs. These results depict the effectiveness of commonsense knowledge integration in improving the performance and expressiveness of scene graph generation for visual understanding and reasoning tasks.

title: EaT PIM: Embedding and Transforming Procedural Instructions for Modification
abstract: Cooking recipes are a type of procedural instructions, which provide a stepwise description of how to complete a task. When cooking, it can sometimes be desirable to substitute ingredients that are used in the recipe for purposes like avoiding allergens, replacing a missing ingredient, or exploring new flavors. This can more generally be framed as a problem of identifying valid modifications in procedural instructions, which is challenging as it requires an understanding of how entities and actions in the instructions interact to produce the final result. In this paper, we introduce a methodology to (1) parse instructions, using natural language processing tools and domain specific ontologies, to generate flow graph representations and (2) train an embedding model which captures the intuition that intermediate outcomes in a flow graph are the result of combining all entities involved in each step of the instructions. Our embedding strategy aggregates nodes and dynamically computes intermediate results within the flow graphs, which requires learning embeddings for significantly fewer nodes than typical graph embedding models. Our methods show strong performance compared to recent approaches in both generating flow graphs and using those flow graphs to identify missing ingredients in recipes.

title: An Analysis of the Reproducibility Crisis in the Web of Data
abstract: The problem of reproducibility, also referred to as the reproducibility crisis, is an ongoing problem in data driven science. The highly connected decentral Web ob Ontologies represents the backbone for semantic data. With the aid of DBpedia Archivo an online ontology interface and open augmented archive we analyze and quantify reproducibility issues. Archivo uses several fully automated ontology discovery mechanisms that run each week and have turned Archivo which contains more than 1,400 ontologies into one of the most exhaustive and recent ontology archives. Daily checks for new ontology versions and automated tests monitor the evolution and availability of a huge portion of the ontologies used in the LOD cloud and allow to get a picture of the state of affairs on a global scale.

title: Effects of Structural Information from Knowledge Graphs on Entity Linking
abstract: Prior work in the domain of entity linking has made great strides by utilizing various kinds of knowledgewhether explicit or implicitto the benefit of disambiguation quality. Nevertheless, the effects of using different levels of structural information are rarely studied systematically. In this paper, we examine and evaluate different ways to exploit structural knowledge graph information in order to maximize its qualitative informativeness benefit specifically for the entity disambiguation task. We start by comparing four entity disambiguation models incorporating different degrees of topological graph structure and find that greater degrees hereof (e.g. in the form of local subgraph based embeddings) do not necessarily benefit the disambiguation task. On the contrary, pre computed embeddings trained on the whole knowledge graph, inherently representing global topological structure, outperform previous state of the art models in our evaluation by a margin of 1.68 % onWikidata Disamb with a 94.03 % F1 score. Second, we leverage and analyse entity type data for pre disambiguation filtering, supporting prior research findings to type information relevance. This leads to time savings of 2030 % in an already basic disambiguation setting, hinting at potentially greater benefits for complex systems.

title: Beyond Accuracy: Informativeness and Credibility to Promote Reliable Information over Misinformation
abstract: The COVID19 crisis has shown that people decisions about health related issues could be easily affected by fake news and conspiracy theories, which can endanger human lives or results in financial loss. In this paper we propose DeepCheck a retrieval based system that aims to provide users with useful and credible information in response to healthrelated queries. The proposed approach explore new methods to identify the Informativeness and Credibility of information and promote them over other relevance dimensions, as indicators of the quality of retrieved documents. DeepCheck efficiently determines the informativeness of documents using Bert and T5. Then assess the credibility of the informative document in supporting or dissuading the initial query using Natural Language Inference model. By comparing with state of the art algorithms, extensive experiments show the effectiveness of DeepCheck in terms of accuracy up to 4%. Further ablation study has shown that informativeness and credibility have interlinked concepts that should be deployed together to promote the reliable information over misinformation.

title: S2CTrans: Building a bridge from SPARQL to CYPHER
abstract: Knowledge graph is an important cornerstone of the development of artificial intelligence. Its underlying storage is mainly based on two data models: RDF and property graph. However, there are great differences in semantic representation and processing logic between RDF model query language represented by SPARQL and property graph query language represented by CYPHER. These differences cause difficulties in graph pattern matching and solution modification transformation, which makes it a great challenge to achieve efficient translation from SPARQL to CYPHER while preserving the original semantics. Therefore, in order to promote the interoperability of knowledge graph query language and make SPARQL suitable for querying property graph, it is necessary to study the translation from SPARQL to CYPHER. In this paper, we use graph relational algebra to prove the feasibility of SPARQL to CYPHER translation. Based on this discovery, we propose S2CTrans framework, which realizes the translation from SPARQL to CYPHER on the premise of preserving the original semantics. Experiments on BSBM datasets show that S2CTrans can translate most SELECT queries in SPARQL1.1 specification into type safe CYPHER statements, and maintain the consistency of the results.

title: Siamese Hybrid Graph Neural Network model for Short Text Similarity
abstract: Abstract. The semantic comparison of short texts is an essential aspect of Natural Language Processing (NLP). Due to the language irregularities, sparse and noise, short texts do not necessarily contain as much semantic as longer clean texts. The representation learning for short texts is a challenging issue. To address the issue, many approaches are proposed based on sequence and knowledge. However, the sequence based methods do not capture semantic similarity beyond a trivial level, and the knowledge based methods call for large numbers of computational resources as well as external knowledge. In this paper, we study in particular how to represent short texts efficiently and accurately. We propose a new method based on Graph Neural Network (GNN) and attention mechanism to calculate the short text similarity. To the end, we develop a new architecture called Siamese Hybrid Graph Neural Network model for Short Text Similarity (SHGN) with multi dimensional message passing and graph progressive learning mechanism. Extensive evaluations are conducted on two benchmark datasets: STS B and SICK, where SHGN outperforms the the best baseline by 0.6% for STS B and 1.4% for SICK.

title: Ontology Based GraphQL Server Generation for Data Access and Integration
abstract: In a GraphQL Web API, the GraphQL schema defines the types of objects that can be queried, and a GraphQL resolver is responsible for querying relevant underlying data sources. Thus, we can expect to use GraphQL for not only data access but data integration if the GraphQL schema reflects the semantics of data from multiple data sources, and the GraphQL resolver can obtain data from underlying data sources and structure the data according to the GraphQL schema. However, there does not exist a semantics aware approach to employ GraphQL for data integration. Furthermore, there are no formal methods for defining a GraphQL API based on an ontology. In this paper, we introduce a framework for using GraphQL in which a global domain ontology drives the generation of a GraphQL server that answers requests by querying heterogeneous data sources. The core of this framework contains an algorithm to generate a GraphQL schema based on an ontology and a generic GraphQL resolver function as a library based on semantic mappings. We implement a prototype of this framework. Furthermore, we provide a real case evaluation in the materials design domain and a synthetic evaluation based on a benchmark.

title: Position bias Weight Capsule Network for Aspect based Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Aspect based sentiment analysis aims to determine the sentiment polarity of differ ent aspects in a sentence. Although the existing models have achieved remarkable performance, they always ignore the semantic relationship between aspect terms and their context, resulting in the lack of position bias representations that could improve the performance of expressive and robust. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel model based on the position bias weight mechanism that would focus on the position of relational expression related. In particular, the position bias weight mechanism proposed is combined with the capsule network, in which the relative position infor mation between an aspect and its context is utilized to compute the position bias weights of context word, to reduce the importance of words far away from the as pect. Experimental results show that the proposed method can capture the position bias information to generate an enhanced representation thus to improve the perfor mance based on the MAMS and SemEval2014 benchmarks.

title: Impact of the Characteristics of Multi Source Entity Matching Tasks on the Performance of Active Learning Methods
abstract: Entity matching aims at identifying records in different data sources that describe the same real world entity and is thus the foundational technique for setting RDF links in the context of the Web of Data. By applying active learning methods for training entity matchers, it is possible to reduce the human labeling effort by selecting informative record pairs for labeling. Although active learning has been extensively researched for the two data source matching case, only recently it was applied for the task of matching records in multi source settings, such as the Web of Data. A multi source matching task has certain inherent characteristics which are different from the two source matching task and can be exploited by the active learning query strategy to further reduce the labeling effort. In this paper, we propose a set of profiling dimensions which capture these inherent characteristics of multi source matching tasks and study their impact on the performance of different active learning methods for training entity matchers. To enable our analysis, we develop ALMSERgen, a multi source matching task generator and curate a continuum of 252 matching tasks along the suggested profiling dimensions. We use the generated tasks to compare the performance of three query strategies: a committee based strategy, a graph based strategy, and a strategy that exploits grouping signals. Our results show that graph signals are relevant for multi source matching tasks involving a large amount of records describing the same real world entities with heterogeneous attribute values while using grouping signals is beneficial if there exists a small number of groups of matching tasks sharing the same underlying patterns.

title: Learning ontologies from text by clustering lexical substitutes derived from language models.
abstract: Many tools for knowledge management and the Semantic Web presuppose the existence of an arrangement of instances into classes, i.e. an ontology. Creating such an ontology, however, is a labor intensive task. In this paper, we present an unsupervised method to learn an ontology from text. We rely on pre trained language models to generate lexical substitutes of given entities and then use matrix factorization to induce new classes and their entities. Our method differs from previous approaches in that (1) it captures the polysemy of entities; (2) it produces interpretable labels of the induced classes; (3) it does not require any particular structure of the text; (4) no re training is required. We evaluate our method on German and English WikiNER corpora and demonstrate the improvements over state of the art approaches.

title: Optimal ABox Repair w.r.t. Static EL TBoxes: from Quantified ABoxes back to ABoxes
abstract: Errors in ontologies expressed in some Description Logic (DL) are often detected when a DL reasoner computes unwanted consequences. The question is then how to repair the ontology such that the unwanted consequences no longer follow, but as many of the other consequences as possible are preserved. The problem of computing such optimal repairs was addressed in recent work in the setting where the data (expressed by an ABox) may contain errors, but the schema (expressed by an EL TBox) is assumed to be correct. Actually, this work considers a generalization of ABoxes called quantified ABoxes (qABoxes) both as input for and as result of the repair process. The advantage of using qABoxes for repair is that more information can be retained, but the disadvantage is that standard DL systems do not accept qABoxes as input. This raises the question, investigated in the present paper, whether and how one can obtain optimal repairs if one restricts the output of the repair process to being ABoxes. In general, such optimal ABox repairs need not exist. Our main contribution is that we show how to decide the existence of optimal ABox repairs in exponential time, and how to compute all such repairs in case they exist.

title: Ensemble based Fact Classification with Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: Numerous prior works have shown how we can use Knowledge Graph embeddings for ranking unseen facts that are likely to be true. Much less attention has been given on how to use embeddings for fact classification, which is a related task where we do not rank facts but label them either as true or false. A direct conversion of the ranked lists of facts into true/fact labels tends to yield a low accuracy. This makes fact classification with embedding a non trivial problem. In this paper, we tackle this challenge with a new technique that exploits ensemble learning and weak supervision, following the principle that multiple weak classifiers can make a strong one. Our method is implemented in a new system called DuEL. DuEL post processes the ranked lists produced by the embedding models with multiple classifiers, which include supervised models like LSTMs, MLPs, and CNNs and unsupervised ones that consider subgraphs and reachability in the graph. The output of these classifiers is aggregated using a weakly supervised method that does not need ground truths, which would be expensive to obtain. Our experiments show that DuEL produces a more accurate classification than other existing methods, with improvements up to 72% in terms of F1 score. This suggests that weakly supervised ensemble learning is a promising technique to perform fact classification with embeddings.

title: Completing Scientific Facts in Knowledge Graphs of Research Concepts
abstract: In the last few years, we have witnessed the emergence of several knowledge graphs that explicitly describe research knowledge with the aim of enabling intelligent systems for supporting and accelerating the scientific process. These resources typically characterize a set of entities in this space (e.g., tasks, methods, evaluation techniques, proteins, chemicals), their relations, and the relevant actors (e.g., researchers, organizations) and documents (e.g., articles, books). However, they are usually very partial representations of the actual research knowledge and may miss several relevant facts. In this paper, we introduce CAFE++, a new link prediction approach for completing scientific statements in knowledge graphs. CAFE++ was evaluated against nine alternative approaches on six benchmarks, yielding excellent results. We applied CAFE++ to the Artificial Intelligence Knowledge Graph (AI KG), a large scale automatically generated open knowledge graph including 1.2M statements extracted from the 333K most cited articles in the field of Artificial Intelligence and generated a new version of this knowledge graph with 300K additional triples.

title: The Problem with XSD Binary Floating Point Datatypes in RDF
abstract: The XSD binary floating point datatypes are regularly used for precise numeric values in RDF. However, the use of these datatypes for knowledge representation can systematically impair the quality of data and, compared to the XSD decimal datatype, increases the probability of data processing producing false results. We argue why in most cases the XSD decimal datatype is better suited to represent numeric values in RDF. A survey of the actual usage of datatypes on the relevant subset of the September 2020 Web Data Commons dataset, containing 14 778 325 375 literals from real web data, substantiates the practical relevancy of the described problems: 29 %68 % of binary floating point values are distorted due to the datatype.

title: Slot Filling for Extracting Reskilling and Upskilling Options from the Web
abstract: Recent disturbances in the job market such as advances in science and technology, crisis and increased competition have triggered a surge in reskilling and upskilling programs. Information on suitable continuing education options is distributed across many sites, rendering the search, comparison and selection of useful programs a cumbersome task. This paper, therefore, introduces a knowledge extraction system that integrates reskilling and upskilling options relevant to the Swiss education market into a knowledge graph, which will serve as a single point of entry for the search and selection of suitable continuing education options. The system applies content extraction and content classification techniques to identify and label page segments containing information on continuing education programs in websites retrieved from 488 different education providers. Afterwards, entity recognition and entity linking techniques draw upon an existing job and skill ontology to identify relevant entities such as skills, occupations and topics in these page segments. Finally, slot filling integrates entities based on their context into the corresponding slots of the reskilling and upskilling knowledge graph. We also introduce a German gold standard comprising partitions of (i) 169 documents with 575 page segment annotations, and (ii) 75 documents with 3291 entity annotations and slots filling entries. The created dataset supports evaluating the performed content extraction, entity linking and slot filling tasks, paves the way for competitive evaluations, and provides initial performance metrics of the presented system.

title: Query Planning for a Free Market of Data
abstract: Trading data in a marketplace allows data to be reused and monetised. The existing marketplace designs use a query engine to collect data from compliant sellers to answer buyers queries. However, sellers may not trust the centralized marketplace, and not wish to share information with it. Also, because several marketplaces can exist, including individual sellers, buyers need a way to answer their queries across multiple marketplace endpoints. We envision a free market of data that enables multiple marketplaces and individual sellers with different content and prices. The current research on query engines has been focused on time efficiency and optimizing query time from open or free access sources. We propose a query engine in a free market scenario to purchase answers for queries from different, independent sellers with different pricing functions that reduces the cost to the buyer. We cast the price based query planning problem into a minimum spanning tree problem where the weight of an edge in a graph is the estimated costs of joining with a triple pattern in a query, and propose two greedy based algorithms, Gen Greedy and Sum Greedy. Through evaluation, our algorithms can reduce 80\% costs of query answers comparing to the state of the art study.

title: Multilingual Neural Machine Verbalization of Link Specifications for The explainable Integration of Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Linked knowledge graphs build the backbone of many data driven applications such as search engines, question answering and digital assistants. Declarative link discovery frameworks use complex link specifications to express the conditions under which a link between two resources can be deemed to exist. However, understanding such complex link specifications is a challenging task for non expert users of link discovery frameworks. In this paper, we address this challenge by introducing NMV LS, a multilingual neural machine verbalization approach for verbalizing complex link specifications into natural language. NMV LS used the results of rule based link specification verbalization to train encoder decoder neural models based on GRU, LSTM/BiLSTM, and transformer. The results of our evaluation on three English and German datasets suggest that our approach performs well for both languages. For instance, we achieved a BLEU score of 99.82, a METEOR score of 0.84, a ChrF++ score of 1, and TER of 0 using a 2 layers encoder decoder based on GRU.

title: In the Head of the Beholder: Comparing Different Proof Representations
abstract: Ontologies provide a strong logical underpinning for the Semantic Web, but their consequences can sometimes be surprising and then must be explained to users. A promising kind of explanations are derived from proofs generated during automated reasoning. We report about a series of studies with the purpose of finding out how to explain such formal logical proofs to humans. We compare different representations, such as tree vs. text based visualizations, but also vary other parameters such as length, interactivity, and the shape of axioms. We did not find evidence to support our main hypothesis that different user groups prefer different proof representations: there were no significant differences in the participants' performance and subjective comprehensibility ratings. On the other hand, when participants had to compare different proof representations, their subjective rankings showed some tendencies such as that most people prefer short tree shaped proofs. However, this did not seem to impact the user's understanding of the proofs as measured by an objective performance measure. We also report on the lessons learned while designing these studies.

title: Ontolex2SKOS: Automatically Generating Thesauri From Lexicons
abstract: Different types of knowledge organization systems (KOS) can be built using semantic web technologies, with different objectives and formality levels. In this paper, we focus on two of them, lexicons and thesauri, which can be specified using the Ontolex Lemon and the Simple Knowledge Organization System (SKOS) vocabularies. Because thesauri and lexicons have complementary applications, organizations may end up developing both for the same domain, which creates a maintenance issue for them, since manually keeping them consistent and synchronizing changes is laborious and error prone. As a solution, we propose the Ontolex2SKOS, a model driven transformation from Ontolex Lemon lexicons to SKOS thesauri that leverages the interface between the two vocabularies, while filling in eventual gaps in them. It allows organizations to have both KOS while building just one, the lexicon. We implemented Ontolex2SKOS in Java and tested it in a proof of concept with the Dutch national healthcare institute. We evaluated the transformation in terms of utility and correctness of its output.

title: Answering Count Queries with Explanatory Evidence
abstract: A challenging case in web search and question answering is count queries, such as number of songs by John Lennon. Prior methods merely answer these with a single, and sometimes puzzling number or return a ranked list of text snippets with different numbers. This paper proposes a methodology for answering count queries with inference, contextualization and explanatory evidence. Unlike previous systems, our method infers final answers from multiple observations, supports semantic qualifiers (e.g., songs written by Lennon for the Beatles), and provides evidence by enumerating representative instances. Experiments with a wide variety of queries show the benefits of our method. To promote further research on this underexplored topic, we release an annotated dataset of 5k queries with 175k relevant text spans.

title: Harmonizing the OQuaRE Quality Framework
abstract: Measuring ontology quality using metrics is far from a trivial task one has to pick the right metrics for the right task and then interpret these values in a meaningful way. Without help, these interpretations are often highly subjective, even for trained knowledge engineers. Quality frameworks can assist and objectify the evaluation. One of the more prominent frameworks in ontology evaluation is OQuaRE, which builds upon the SQuaRE standard for software evaluation. Not only provides it tangible metrics for assessing an ontology, but it also suggests an interpretation for these values in the form of a quality rating and links these metrics to a broader quality framework. However, during an implementation effort, the authors identified some drawbacks. In the last years, various metrics have been proposed that sometimes seem to conflict with each other or are inconclusive in their descriptions. The resources on the quality framework are distributed over web pages and papers. The following paper aims first to present the drawbacks the framework currently has. At the next step, we aim to resolve the current heterogeneities and collect the information of the various sources. We aim to provide a one stop information re source on OQuaRE to enable our further research and applications efforts.

title: An Unsupervised Approach for Question Answering Over Knowledge Graphs by Leveraging Pre trained Language Models
abstract: Most Knowledge Graph based Question Answering (KGQA) systems rely on training data to reach their optimal performance. However, acquiring training data for supervised systems is both time consuming and resource intensive. In this paper, we propose an unsupervised KGQA system leveraging pre trained language models. Entity and relation linking are essential components of any KGQA system. We employ several pre trained language models in the entity linking task to recognize the entities mentioned in the question and obtain the contextual representation for indexing. Furthermore, we leverage a pre trained language model previously trained for language inference to perform relation linking. Finally, we propose a novel algorithm for extracting the answer entities from a KG, where we construct a forest of interpretations and introduce tree walking and tree disambiguation techniques. Our algorithm uses the linked relation and predicts the tree branches that eventually lead to the potential answer entities. The proposed method achieves 4.5% and 7.1% gains in F1 score in entity linking tasks on LC QuAD 2.0 and LC QuAD 2.0 (KBpearl) datasets, respectively, and a 5.4% increase in the relation linking task on LC QuAD 2.0 (KBpearl). We demonstrate that our unsupervised KGQA approach outperforms other supervised state of the art methods on the WebQSP WD test set (1.4% increase in F1 score) without training on the target dataset.

title: Language Model Guided Knowledge Graph Embeddings
abstract: Knowledge graph embeddings (KGE) have become a popular approach for knowledge graph (KG) completion by predicting the plausibility of (potential) triples. Such models transform entities and relations into an embedding space in order to measure the likelihood of triples. However, knowledge graphs often include further textual complementary knowledge stored in literals, which is ignored by the KGE models. We bridge this gap by leveraging the capabilities of pre trained language models (PLMs) to include this textual knowledge in the learning process of KGEs. This is achieved by introducing a new loss function that guides KGE models in measuring the likelihood of triples by including PLM embeddings. Our experimental evaluation on various benchmarks confirms the advantage of using PLMs for boosting the accuracy of several KGE models across multiple standard benchmarks.

title: Knowledge Graph Representation of TV Tropes Ideas based on Conceptual Dependency Framework
abstract: Due to language use heterogeneity and variation, ideation research studying idea content generally focuses on the statistical relationships between se mantic fragments. However, assessment of an ideas value depends on qual itative factors such as the taxonomic or causal relations between ideas in its domain. We propose an alternative approach to studying idea content based on constructing a knowledge graph representation of ideas using Conceptu al Dependency (CD) Theory. CD Theory provides a framework to under stand language and break down text into meaningful conceptual units. We focus on studying trope ideas as a vehicle to understanding ideas in general using data from TVTropes.org. We designed and ran a custom concept ex tractor based on CD Theory and compared its effectiveness against a SpaCy implementation of ClauseIE as a baseline. We then devised an algorithm to grow more complex conceptualizations from these extracted atomic con ceptual units, thereby transforming them into triples for input into a graph database. Finally, we tested our knowledge graph representation of trope ideas and managed to retrieve taxonomic and causal information using que ries designed to exploit the knowledge graph representations semantic con tent. We also tested the capability of generating new ideas from the knowledge graph representation, resulting in the recommendation of seman tically similar yet unconnected trope ideas that could potentially be recom bined to inspire new ideas.

title: The Importance of Being Ordered: Entity Typing with RDF2vec Embedding Variants
abstract: The entity type information in Knowledge Graphs (KGs) such as DBpedia, Freebase, etc. is often incomplete due to automated generation. Entity Typing is the task of assigning or inferring the semantic type of an entity in a KG. This paper presents ENTIRE, a novel approach for Entity Typing with newly developed RDF2vec variants. RDF2vec first generates graph walks and then uses a language model to obtain embeddings for each node in the graph. We show that the walk generation strategy and the embedding model have a significant effect on the performance of the entity typing task. In multiple experiments on DBpedia we find that order aware RDF2vec embeddings achieve the best results.

title: s RDF2vec: Injecting Knowledge Graph Structure Into RDF2vec Entity Embeddings
abstract: RDF2vec is a representation learning method for creating embedding vectors for entities in a knowledge graph. It is built upon extracting sequences of random walks from a knowledge graph and running the word2vec embedding approach on those sequences. While the similarity metric in the RDF2vec space mixes entity relatedness and entity similarity, the two are not equally useful. Especially in many downstream modeling tasks, entity similarity is more important than entity relatedness. On the other hand, in downstream tasks where all entities are already similar or related, an embedding model which emphasizes the other aspect is better suited for fine grained distinctions. In this work, we introduce s RDF2vec, a variant of RDF2vec which incorporates knowledge graph structure in the RDF2vec embeddings and hence puts more emphasis on entity relatedness. Furthermore, we present methods of combining RDF2vec embedding vectors of different flavors. We show that those combinations often outperform "classic" RDF2vec embedding vectors, especially in tasks where the distinction of structurally dissimilar entities is useful.

title: KERMIT A Transformer Based Approach for Knowledge Graph Matching
abstract: One of the strongest signals for automated matching of knowledge graphs and ontologies are the textual descriptions of the concepts. The methods that are typically applied, such as character or token based comparisons, are relatively simple and do not capture the actual meaning of the texts. With the rise of transformer based language models, text comparison based on meaning (rather than lexical features) is available to researchers. However, comparing all textual descriptions of concepts in two knowledge graphs scales at least quadratically since concepts may have more than one textual description. A typical solution is to fall back on a blocking approach which sacrifices recall for runtime performance. In this paper, we present KERMIT, a matching system which uses sentence transformers (so called bi encoders) to select matching candidates. In a second step, we use fine tuned transformer cross encoders to select the best candidates. We evaluate our approach on multiple datasets and show it is feasible and produces competitive results.

title: DCWEB SOBA: Deep Contextual Word Embeddings Based Semi Automatic Ontology Building for Aspect Based Sentiment Classification
abstract: In this paper, we propose the use of deep contextualised word embeddings to semi automatically build a domain sentiment ontology. Compared to previous research, we use deep contextualised word embeddings to better cope with various meanings of words. A state of the art hybrid method is used for aspect based sentiment analysis, called HAABSA++, to evaluate our obtained ontology on the SemEval 2016 restaurant dataset. We achieve a prediction accuracy of 81.85% for the hybrid model with our ontology, which outperforms the hybrid model with other ontologies. Furthermore, we find that the ontology obtained from our proposed domain sentiment ontology builder, called DCWEB SOBA, on itself improves the accuracy for the conclusive cases from 83.04% to 84.52% compared to the ontology builder based on non contextual word embeddings, WEB SOBA.

title: Generating gradual self explanatory SHACL constraints from expert knowledge and probabilistic reasoning
abstract: The Shape Constraint Language (SHACL) has been defined by the W3C to answer the rising need of controlling and assessing the ever growing knowledge bases. However, these shapes can be complex and numerous to construct. In this paper, we propose a method to automatically generate SHACL constraints from a knowledge base and expert knowledge. We present a formalization of such knowledge allowing the learning of a causal probabilistic model, from which explaining rules are extracted and used to assess the quality of the knowledge base and detect odd values. We introduce two kinds of SHACL constraints: descriptive and reasoning, to permit a better assessment of the quality of both the current knowledge base and possible new data to be integrated.

title: Discovering Causal Rules in Knowledge Graphs using Graph Embeddings
abstract: Discovering causal relationships between different observations is the goal of many experiments in science. When observational data are available, the potential outcome framework is a well used framework for discovering such relationships. To study the effect of a treatment, similar individuals can be examined to estimate counterfactuals. In this paper, we adapted this framework to be used in Knowledge Graphs (KGs) to discover causal rules that express that differences in treatments lead to differences in a studied characteristic. However, quantifying the similarity between individuals represented in a knowledge graph is challenging, especially because their descriptions can be incomplete and erroneous. In this work, we developed a new matching method based on knowledge graph embeddings. We also developed a new algorithm that uses this new matching method to discover causal rules in KGs. Finally, the experiments that we conducted on a scientific knowledge graph, by involving a domain expert, showed that our approach is able to discover rules that explain much more differences in the studied characteristic, than existing state of the art approaches.

title: Session based Recommendation with Self Distillation Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Recommendation systems have become fundamental in e commerce scenarios, and session based recommendation plays an increasingly significant role in recommendation systems because of its flexibility and highly practical value. Although there have been some promising results in previous works, they are still insufficient to achieve superior recommendation performance due to the limited even noisy information involved in the next click in each session. To obtain more accurate predictive vectors without the misleading of potential noisy information, we propose Self Distillation Graph Neural Networks to make full use of the valuable information in a session, which is termed as SD GNN for brevity. Specifically, we employ the well evaluated and flexible deep ensemble in deep learning as the teacher model, which assembles multiple randomly initialized GNNs in a simple way. Furthermore, we leverage the soft target distribution produced by the teacher model to train each GNN in the ensemble to achieve self knowledge distillation. Our whole method is easily implementable and scalable due to the proposed Self Distillation technique. Extensive experiments on two benchmark datasets verify that the proposed method (SD GNN) significantly outperforms state of the art baselines and shows superior performance in the session based recommendation.

title: Using Artificial Intelligence for Prevention of Falls from Height
abstract: Safety is the most important aspect that a company should guarantee to its employees. To reduce the risk, it is necessary to analyze HIgh POtential (HIPO) hazards. In this study, we focus on Fall From Height (FFH) which is one of the main causes of worker fatalities. In order to improve the prevention plan, artificial intelligence (AI) can help to determine the causes and the safety actions from FFH historical data. This paper aims to : (i) develop and populate an ontology for FFH with the help of domain experts, and (ii) analyze and extract key information from a HIPO database through Natural Language Processing (NLP). Experimental results are conducted in order to evaluate the proposed approach.

title: Efficient Join Ordering for SPARQL Queries through Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Finding an efficient join ordering for SPARQL queries is fundamental to speed up queries execution. Recently, deep reinforcement learning (DRL) approaches paved a new way to find good join orderings for SQL queries. When sufficiently trained, the learned SQL optimizers can outperform traditional query optimizers. In this paper, we show that SQL deep reinforcement learning techniques are not suitable for SPARQL queries, mainly due to the complexity of SPARQL queries and the inaccuracy of cost models. We propose to refine SPARQL cost models with statistics collected during the partial execution of queries. By improving the accuracy of cost models, maximizing the reward of a query plan is now correlated with a better query execution time. In our experiments, the learned SPARQL optimizer divides the workload execution time by three compared to the state of the art Virtuoso optimizer.

title: MediCause: Causal Relation Modelling and Extraction from Medical Publications
abstract: Causal relations are one of the most important types of information that can be extracted from medical publications. As such, the automated extraction of such relations from medical text and the development of ontologies for representing this information are active fields of research. Due to the increased complexity of the causal relation extraction task and the lack of annotated data, recent research has focused on decomposing the causal relation extraction task into the sub tasks of causal sentence detection, entity recognition and relation extraction. This study addresses the entity recognition sub task, which remains largely unsolved because no complete ontological model and corresponding annotated dataset of causal sentences and their entities currently exist. Therefore, as part of this work, we propose MediCause, a simple ontological model of causal relations, and a novel dataset using it to annotate entities involved in the causal relations of 1,202 sentences from existing datasets. We then use the labeled dataset to train various BERT models that can recognize and label the entities in unseen texts, and we find that a BioBERT large model fine tuned with our dataset is the best model at this task (macro averaged F1 score of 0.844). We also use MediCause to annotate entities in causal sentences from unseen, recent publications, and have experts evaluate them.

title: R GCN: The R Could Stand for Random
abstract: The inception of R GCNs marked a milestone in the Semantic Web domain as it enabled researchers to train end to end machine learning models that operate on Knowledge Graphs (KGs). However, training these models does not scale well and quickly bumps into resource issues for real world KGs. In this paper, we propose a technique that constructs embeddings for node classification by randomly aggregating information from neigbors.
