This random message passing strategy allows for node representations of higher dimensions while taking into account information from larger neigborhoods. We empirically show that our Random Relational Graph Convolutional Network (RR GCN) method results in predictive performances that match and in some cases outperform those of fully trained R GCNs. The implications of these results are two fold: on the one hand, our technique can be used as a quick baseline for further research. On the other hand, it clearly indicates that more research into trained R GCNs is required to fully exploit all of the information present in a KG, such that they can significantly outperform R GCNs.

title: What Really Matters in a Table? Insights from a User Study
abstract: A better understanding of humans visual attention while reading some content can provide valuable insights for developing user centred computations models, e.g., personalised document summarisation. A considerable amount of data, presented in a tabular form, is used in daily activities and is available on the Web nowadays. Several approaches have proposed an automated table summarisation method to improve the users' experience and give them succinct summaries of the information stored in tables. However, there has been little attention to considering user behaviour in the design of automated table summarisation. In this paper, we present the findings of an empirical study, where we investigate, with the help of standard User Experience tools (eye tracking technology and surveys), how users approach the reading of a table. We especially focus on evaluating how the domain knowledge and interest of the users influence their comprehension, eventually identifying four possible user profiles and their different information needs. In order to show the impact of our findings on the selection of the information to keep in the summary, we present and release a tool that, in addition to supporting the development of similar experiments, allow to check the information presented in the summary in the form of RDF triples, by exploiting the semantic annotation of the table.

title: DualLoop: Efficient Ontology Matching with Short term and Long term Active Learners
abstract: High quality ontologies play an important role for data integration and knowledge based reasoning in various domains like eHealth and material science. Ontology matching is a crucial task to help domain experts in integrating domain specific ontologies. Existing learning based or heuristic based ontology matching approaches can help to identify matches, but their capability and efficiency is limited in finding further, more sophisticated matches. Human in the loop approaches such as active learning and interactive data programming can help, but they are not efficient to deal with the extreme class imbalance of ontology matching due to their limited bootstrapping and exploration capability. To overcome this problem, we propose a novel interactive machine learning approach, called DualLoop, to further improve the efficiency of engaging domain experts based on three key elements: 1) an adaptive blocking strategy based on change point detection to largely reduce potential match candidates without losing any true matches; 2) tunable labeling functions with automatically tuned parameters to control the exploration capability of a dynamic committee; 3) a new interactive learning framework with two collaborative and parallel learning loops to balance the needs of exploitation and exploration. The evaluation results based on three benchmark datasets show that DualLoop can help to discover true matches more efficiently than existing approaches, reducing the effort for finding the same number of matches by more than 50%.

title: Never Mind the Semantic Gap: Modular, Lazy and Safe Loading of RDF Data
abstract: Any attempt at a tight integration between semantic technologies and object oriented programming will invariably stumble over the gap between the two underlying object models. We illustrate how this semantic gap manifests from the point of view of data retrieval with SPARQL. We present a novel mechanism to load data from RDF knowledge graphs into object oriented languages that gives static guarantees about the data access and modularly integrates the mapping between the program and the RDF view with the class definition in the program. This allows us to preserve the separation of concerns between the class system of RDF (geared towards domain modeling and data), and that of the program (geared towards typing and code reuse). Loading of RDF can be performed lazily, when required by the program, based on query futures subqueries that are only evaluated if and when the data is accessed. The type safety is based on query containment. We formulate a Liskov principle for the mapping queries to characterize when they respect the subclass relation. Moreover, we provide tool support to detect when the user provided mapping would cause the loading mechanisms to result in data structures that manifest the semantic gap.

title: Improving Question Answering Quality Through Language Feature based SPARQL Query Candidate Validation
abstract: Question Answering (QA) systems are on the rise and on their way to becoming one of the standard user interfaces (UI). However, in conversational UIs, the information quantity needs to be kept low as users expect a limited number of precise answers (often it is 1) similar to human human communication. The acceptable number of answers in a result list is a key differentiator from search engines, where showing more answers (10 100) to the user is widely accepted. Hence, the quality of QA is crucial for the wide acceptance of such systems. The adaptation of natural language UIs for satisfying the information needs of humans requires high quality and not redundant answers. However, providing compact and correct answers to the users' questions is a challenging task. In this paper, we consider a certain class of QA systems that work over Knowledge Graphs (KGQA). We developed a system agnostic approach for optimizing the ranked lists of SPARQL query candidates produced by the KGQA system that are used to retrieve an answer to a given question. We call this a SPARQL query validation (QV) process. For the evaluation of our approach, we used two well known KGQA benchmarks. Our results show a significant improvement in the QA quality. As the approach is system agnostic, it can be applied to any KGQA system that produces query candidates.

title: Learning Concept Lengths Accelerates Concept Learning in ALC
abstract: Concept learning approaches based on refinement operators explore partially ordered solution spaces to compute concepts, which are used as binary classification models for individuals. However, the number of concepts explored by these approaches can easily grow to the millions for complex learning problems. This often leads to impractical runtimes. We propose to alleviate this problem by predicting the length of target concepts before the exploration of the solution space. By these means, we can prune the search space during concept learning. To achieve this goal, we compare four neural architectures and evaluate them on four benchmarks. Our evaluation results suggest that recurrent neural network architectures perform best at concept length prediction with a macro F measure ranging from 38% to 92%. We then extend the CELOE algorithm which learns ALC concepts with our concept length predictor. Our extension yields the algorithm CLIP. In our experiments, CLIP is at least 7.5 times faster than other state of the art concept learning algorithms for ALC including CELOE and achieves significant improvements in the F measure of the concepts learned on 3 out of 4 datasets. For reproducibility, we provide our implementation in the public GitHub repository at https://github.com/ConceptLengthLearner/LearnLengths

title: Dihedron Algebraic Embeddings for Spatio temporal Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Many knowledge graphs contain spatial and temporal information. Most knowledge graph embedding models are designed for triple based fact representation and often neglect the simultaneous consideration of the spatial and temporal dimensions. Encoding such higher dimensional knowledge necessitates the consideration of true algebraic and geometric aspects of the underlying models. Hypercomplex algebra provides the foundation of a well defined mathematical system among which the Dihedron algebra with its rich and relativistic framework is suitable to handle multidimensional knowledge. In this paper, we propose an embedding model that is facilitated by Dihedron algebra for learning high dimensional knowledge on spatial and temporal aspects. The evaluation results show that our model performs effectively and significantly better than other adapted models for the completion and link prediction with space and time information.

title: Incorporating KB Self Attention with Transformer model into Goal Oriented Dialogue Systems
abstract: End to end goal oriented systems face multiple challenges in incorporating knowledge bases to generate knowledge grounded responses, especially when the knowledge base is state full and changes from one dialogue to the other. The existing approaches depend on concatenating the knowledge to the input which leads to misrepresenting the KB entities and to introducing long range dependencies. In this paper, we explore the Transformer network models to benefit from their advantage in performing parallel computation to encode the dialogue. We also apply the multi head attention mechanism over the knowledge base to fully include the KB entities into the dialogue context. The model further incorporates an entity tracker which keeps track of all previous entities and then enforces the newly generated entities to be focused on relevant entities and the dialogue history. Experimenting on multiple public datasets, the empirical evidence proved that incorporating the proposed modules with the Transformer model can aid in enhancing the performance of goal oriented dialogue systems compared to the state of arts.

title: Enriching Wikidata with Linked Open Data
abstract: Large public knowledge graphs, like Wikidata, contain billions of statements about tens of millions of entities, thus inspiring various use cases to exploit such knowledge graphs. However, practice shows that much of the relevant information that fits users' needs is still missing in Wikidata. In this paper, we investigate the feasibility of enriching Wikidata with structured data sources from the linked open data (LOD) cloud. We propose a method that consists of several steps: gap detection, external graph selection, schema alignment, knowledge retrieval, and validation. We evaluate our method on enriching Wikidata with two LOD sources: DBpedia and Getty. Our experiments show that our LOD based method can enrich Wikidata with millions of new high quality statements in a short time. We analyze the nuances of our method across properties and user queries. We make our code and data available to facilitate future work: \url{https://anonymous.4open.science/r/hunger for knowledge 315D/}.

title: Entity Linking and Filling for Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs (KGQA) aims to compute answers for natural language questions over a knowledge graph. Recent KGQA approaches adopt a neural machine translation (NMT) approach, where the natural language question is translated into a structured query language. However, NMT suffers from the out of vocabulary problem, where terms in a question may not have been seen during training, impeding their translation. This issue is particularly problematic for the millions of entities that large knowledge graphs describe. We rather propose a KGQA approach that delegates the processing of entities to entity linking (EL) systems. NMT is then used to create a query template with placeholders that are filled by entities identified from the text in an EL phase. This approach gives rise to what we call the ``entity filling'' problem, where we must decide which placeholders to replace with which entities. To address this problem, we propose a solution based on sequence labelling and constraints. Experiments for QA with complex questions over Wikidata show that our approach outperforms pure NMT approaches: while the task remains challenging, errors relating to entities in the translated queries are greatly reduced.

title: Hierarchical Topic Modelling for Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Recent years have demonstrated the rise of knowledge graphs as a powerful medium for storing data, showing their utility in academia and industry alike. This in turn has motivated substantial effort into modeling knowledge graphs in ways that reveal latent structures contained within them. In this paper, we propose a non parametric hierarchical generative model for knowledge graphs that draws inspiration from probabilistic methods used in topic modelling. Our model discovers the latent probability distributions of a knowledge graph and organizes its elements in a tree of abstract topics. In doing so, it provides a hierarchical clustering of knowledge graph subjects as well as membership distributions of predicates and entities to topics. The main draw of such an approach is that it does not require any a priori assumptions about the structure of the tree other than its depth. In addition to presenting the generative model, we introduce an efficient Gibbs sampling scheme that leverages the Multinomial Dirichlet conjugacy to integrate out latent variables, making the posterior inference process adaptable to large datasets. We quantitatively evaluate our model on three common datasets and show that it is comparable to existing hierarchical clustering techniques. Furthermore, we present a qualitative assessment of the induced hierarchy and topics.

title: Document Structure aware Relational Graph Convolutional Networks for Ontology Population
abstract: Ontologies comprising of concepts, their attributes, and relationships, form the quintessential backbone of many knowledge based AI systems. These systems manifest in the form of question answering or data discovery in business analytics, master data management, and data fabric applications. While there have been efforts towards populating domain specific ontologies, we examine the role of document structure in learning ontological relationships between concepts in any document corpus. Inspired by ideas from hypernym discovery and information retrieval, our method performs about 15 points more accurate than a stand alone R GCN model for this task.

title: APPTeK: Agent Based Predicate Prediction in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
abstract: In knowledge graph reasoning, we observe a trend to analyze temporal data evolving over time. The additional temporal dimension is attached to facts in a knowledge base resulting in quadruples between entities such as (Nintendo, released, Super Mario, Sep 13 1985), where the predicate between two entities is de ned in a time interval or at a timestamp. Multi hop reasoning on inferred subgraphs connecting entities within a knowledge graph can be formulated as a reinforcement learning task where the agent sequentially performs inference upon the explored subgraph. The task in this work is to infer the predicate between a subject and an object entity, i.e., (subject, ?, object, time), being valid at a certain timestamp or time interval. Given query entities, our agent starts to gather temporal relevant information about the neighborhood of the subject and object, simultaneously. We refer to the encoding of information about the explored graph structures as ngerprints. Subsequently, we use the two ngerprints as input to a Q Network. Our agent decides sequentially which relation type needs to be explored next, expanding the local subgraphs of the query entities. The evaluation shows that the proposed method not only yields results being in line with stateof the art embedding algorithms for temporal Knowledge Graphs (tKG), but that we also gain information about the relevant structures between subjects and objects.

title: Novelty Detection in Community Question Answering Forums
abstract: Community Question Answering (CQA) forums are a popular place for open ended question answers and discussions by the public. Popular question answering sites has become a one stop solution for the diverse information seeking needs of the netizens. However, it is quite common that users sometimes ask the same question which may have been posted before and appropriately answered by the community members. It is not uncommon that users do not perform a proper search and pose the same question again. Community members start responding to that question, however, the answer may already have been proposed previously on a different thread. When two questions are getting at exactly the same problem, community members (moderators) in the forum often flag one as a duplicate of the other, to help route traffic to high quality \textit{novel} questions and the correct answers. However, they usually do this manually based on the novelty or redundancy of the question. Here, in this work we take up this problem to detect semantically equivalent \textit{non novel} questions automatically, flag those, and propose our approach to identify \textit{novel} questions from CQA forums. We make use of a deep Dynamic Memory Network (DMN) to assimilate information from multiple source questions to answer whether a new question is \textit{novel} or a \textit{semantically equivalent} question already exists. We introduce a new dataset for semantic level novelty detection on community question answering. Our proposed approach attains significant performance improvement over recent textual novelty detection methods.

title: Formally Grounded Evaluation Measures for Semantic Parsing based Knowledge Graph Question Answering
abstract: Knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) is important to make information accessible without formal query language expertise on the part of the users. The semantic parsing (SP) flavor of this task maps a natural language question to a formal query that is machine executable, such as SPARQL. The SP KGQA task is currently evaluated by adopting measures from other tasks, such as information retrieval and machine translation. However, this adoption typically occurs without fully considering the desired behavior of SP KGQA systems. To address this, we articulate task specific desiderata, then develop novel SP KGQA measures based on a probabilistic framework. We use the desiderata to formulate a set of axioms for SP KGQA measures and conduct an axiomatic analysis that reveals insufficiencies of established measures previously used to report SP KGQA performance. We also perform experimental evaluations, using synthetic and state of the art neural machine translation approaches. The results highlight the importance of grounded alternative SP KGQA measures.

title: Verbal Aggressions Detection in Mexican Tweets
abstract: Verbal aggressions are a struggle that a great number of social media users have to face daily. Some users take advantage of the anonymity that social media give them and offend a person, a group of people, or a concept. The majority of proposals which pretend to detect aggressive comments on social media handle it as a classification problem. Although there are a lot of techniques to face this problem in English, there are a lack of proposals in Spanish. In this work, we proposed to use several Spanish lexicons which have a collection of words that have been weighted according to different criteria like affective, dimensional, and emotional values. In addition to them, estructural values, word embeddings and one hot codification were taken into account. The combination of these features proved to be a novel proposal because competitive scores were obtained when this model was applied over a dataset which contains Mexican Spanish tweets that are labeled as aggressive and non aggressive.

title: Co Comment Network: A novel approach to construct social networks within Reddit
abstract: This work analyzes the online Reddit comment posts and proposes a novel approach to construct a social network automatically within Reddit that connects users of it. The investigation reveals that users tend to form links to others who have a mutual interest in interacting with some topics or posts. This mutual interest among users can make connections among them in the network. This study shows that Reddit contains a large, strongly connected core of high degree nodes, surrounded by many small clusters of low degree nodes which the authors define as the Co Comment network. One of the important research focuses is to examine whether the networks built from the Reddit comments show the desirable social network properties, e.g., power law distribution, small world effect, and clustering coefficient properties. Results obtained from the experiment confirm that the Co Comment network conforms to social network properties. The authors also discover communities within the Co Comment network and verify them to validate the constructed network.

title: Abjad Numerals Recognition in Medieval Arabic Mathematical Texts based on Bi directional LSTM CRF Model
abstract: Abjad numerals, also called hisab al jumal, is a numeral system based on the twenty eight letters of Arabic. In ancient Arabic mathematics, all problems and solutions sentences were completely expressed in natural language. There was no mathematical symbolism. This is the first algorithmic approach that explore the use of a Bi directional Long Short Term Memory (Bi LSTM) network with a conditional random field (CRF) layer to automatically analyze and recognize Abjad numerals in mathematical expression in medieval Arabic mathematical texts. Since that the numerological calculation of hisab al jumal contain no ambiguity, we also translate hisab al jumal terms detected in the previous step which written out in natural language to modern numeral system. Experimental results on the Hj Tagged Corpus demonstrate that the proposed methods is efficient in correctly classifying mathematical components (such as numerical constants, hisab al jumal numbers, mathematical operation..etc), where it achieves an F1 score of 98.1%.

title: Pedestrian safety analysis using Time Petri Nets and Non monotonic Logic: Theoretical Foundations
abstract: In this article we attempt to analyze the accident risk of crossing pedestrians. For this purpose, we develop a Petri nets model for the vehicle pedestrian infrastructure interaction. The proposed Petri nets model is then translated into non monotonic logic using a fragment of the normal theory of defaults logic theory. Thus, knowing if a state can be reached in the accessibility graph of the associated Petri net, will be expressed by a non monotonic proof process derived from defaults logic theory. The risk of pedestrian crossing behavior is modeled from some crossing scenario. The effects of spaces per ception and behaviors' temporality, on their risk of crossing were analyzed using Time Petri Nets. Thus, the Petri temporal model translation to defaults logic is given to allow the formal pedestrians' safety analysis.

title: A Reinforcement Learning based Stabilization Module for Airplane Flight with Q Learning
abstract: In recent years, there have been many advances in the field of reinforcement learning (RL). RL algorithms have achieved human master abilities in games such as go, chess, etc. The capabilities of RL algorithms have also now been tested in the automated transportation field for self driving cars. In this paper we apply reinforcement learning models to simulated airplane flight. In particular, we develop and test a reinforcement learning based methodology for airplane stabilization. In essence, through reward functions and Q learning based modeling, we analyze and evaluate how a simulated Cessna 172 can learn to stabilize itself while in flight. Our results show that, after training, the airplane learns to maintain a stable course and attitude. We perform the analysis on X plane 11 which is a realistic flight simulator. Results of the analysis are presented and discussed.

title: The importance of signal pre processing for machine learning: The influence of Data scaling on a driver identification classification problem
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) algorithms have overtaken the attention of the scientific community for their important capabilities and their over the top results. However, the excessive focus on hyperparameters and the models architectures made the pre processing step often neglected. In spite of its importance, it represented a weak point for most of the machine learning applications as well as a blind spot in many research studies. In this paper, we will demonstrate through a CAN Bus vehicle data based driver identification case study, the importance of testing the use of different methods of data scaling and normalization while demonstrating their role in improving the performance of several Machine Learning algorithms.

title: How knowledge driven class generalization affects classical machine learning algorithms for mono label supervised classification
abstract: Beyond class imbalance and the sample size per class, this research paper studies the effect of knowledge driven class generalization on the accuracy of classical machine learning algorithms for mono label classification. We apply our analysis on five classical machine learning models (Perception, Support Vectors, Random Forest, K nearest neighbors, and Decision Tree) to classify a set of animal image files generated from Wikimedia Commons, a large scale repository of free images. Thanks to our analysis, we found that the accuracy rates of mono label classification models, mainly Support Vectors and K nearest neighbors, are affected by class generalization. The increasing or decreasing behavior of accuracy rates is driven by the settings of the classification categories and the generalization. The analysis of class generalization should be useful to understand the limitations of classical machine learning algorithms and to fuel debates about the improvement of classical models and supervised classification evaluation methods within the framework of Explainable Artificial Intelligence.

title: Learning Activity Matters When Gamifying It
abstract: Motivational affordances used in gamification can enhance the motivation of a learner by increasing the perceived value of the activity. However, such an effect is dependent upon the level of pre existing motivation towards the learning activity and on the persons view of these affordances as interesting or valuable. Therefore, it is necessary to create methods that can make the decisions for gamifying learning more systematic. In this context, this paper is examining the suitability of the Expectancy Value Cost Scale as an instrument for estimating the potential motivational value towards a learning activity, which can make the targeted effects of its gamification more predictable.

title: Automatic Searching of Deep Neural Networks for Medical Imaging Diagnostic
abstract: Medical imaging diagnosis is the most assisted method to help physicians diagnose patient diseases using different imaging test modalities. But Imbalanced data is one of the biggest challenges in the field of medical imaging. To advance this field, this work proposes a framework that can be used to find the optimal DNN architectures for a database with the challenge of imbalanced datasets. In our paper, we present an open source framework for automatic deep neural network search for medical imaging diagnosis.

title: Optimization of Electronically Scanned Conformal Conical Antenna Array Synthesis Using Artificial Neural Network Algorithm
abstract: Studying of mechanically steerable antennas has been considered the subject of feature research. To decrease the cost of the mechanical system and to enhance the steering potentials of the radar applications, we suggest renewing any mechanical antenna components with an electronically controlled 3D or Conformal Conical Antennas arrays. 3D antenna arrays can be readily fabricated with existing manufacturing technologies and offer considerable interests in terms of the 3 D steerable radiation beam, size, directivity, HPBW, and SLL reduction. In this paper, we have elaborated the neural networks method based beamforming that will be employed to the array pattern synthesis for three dimensional (3D) Conformal Conical Antenna arrays. This procedure authorizes to model and to optimize the antenna arrays system, by acting on various parameters of the array and taking into account planned general criteria. The goal is then to develop a feedforward neural network with supervised learning that approximates the following array patterns function. It explains how to introduce the basic principles of artificial neural network (ANN), some fundamental networks are examined in detail for their ability to solve simple pattern synthesis problem in conical antenna arrays. This fact increases the complexity of the problem under consideration and fitting the neural network models, such as training function, architecture, and parameter that would improve and result in more accuracy about input output relations. Then, the used neural technique showed its effectiveness in improving performance using the identified conformal conical isotropic antenna arrays

title: Improved chemical reaction optimization for distributed flexible job shop problem with transportation times
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a variant of the Distributed Flexible Job shop Scheduling Problem in which they introduced the transportation time as an additional constraint. The Distributed Flexible Job shop Scheduling Problem with transportation times (DFJSPT), that we study in this work, consists on each operation can be executed on one of the available machines and this in a set of geographically distributed factories. Each factory has a set of machines on which a set of jobs must be executed and the transport of jobs between machines is made by one or several transport robots. The DFJSPT combine three NP Hard problems: The problem of assigning jobs to machines, the distribution problem of jobs to factories and the robot routing problem. In this paper, we study the DFJSPT with a single robot in each factory and we propose an improved chemical reaction optimization metaheuristic to solve it in order to minimize the makespan. We tested our approach on two different categories of instances that we designed on purpose, the first category is composed of instances of flexible job shop scheduling problem with transportation times to which we have integrated the constraints of jobs distribution between factories, the second category is composed of instances of distributed and flexible job shop scheduling problem to which we have integrated the constraints of Transportation times.

title: what can do a deep learning based approach on sentiment analysis?
abstract: In recent years, online video content has gained a lot of popularity and exponential growth. Thus, understanding the Quality of Experience (QoE) perceived by end users of video streaming services is crucial for both network operators and service providers. However, it is not trivial to ensure an adequate QoE because QoE is multidisciplinary. Thus, user experience is affected by various influencing factors (e.g., context factors, human factors, and system factors), and it is still challenging to identify the QoE key influencing factors. To address these challenges, we focused on improving the performance of QoE estimation models by exploiting valuable human and context information (users comments provide important information). In this paper, we employ the Long Short Term Memory algorithm to process users comments and classify them into a negative and positive comments. Specific features from the application level, user level, and context level are fed into the convolutional neural network and artificial neural network for further processing to estimate QoE. The proposed approach is evaluated with standard evaluation metrics, such as accuracy and loss.

title: An Exact Algorithm for A Multi Period Inventory Routing Problem with Lateral Transshipment
abstract: In a supply chain, inventory is the main source of costs for a company. The idea of reducing logistics costs is therefore to control inventory costs, which are essentially the inventory holding cost and the transportation cost. One of the most used models to solve these two problems jointly is the Inventory Routing Problem (IRP), which will be the subject of this study. This paper deals with the case of a deterministic demand from a set of customers to a single supplier with a single vehicle that will be used to replenish them for a single product type over a finite planning horizon. Our paper will first analyse the impact of increasing supplier lead times on network costs. Then, we will study the effects of using the lateral transshipment (LT) technique on the overall network cost. In this paper, we developed a mathematical model and solved it by an exact method. The obtained results will show that LT is an effective tool capable of improving the total network cost and balancing the customers' inventory level.

title: Traffic Sign Recognition approach based on Haar Cascade and Deep learning
abstract: Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) systems can instantly assists drivers directly or through Automated Driving Systems (ADS) to improve the driving process and to avoid road accidents, which are incremental and dangerous for human life. In order to develop a TSR system, various methods can be used, first, based on detecting and extracting the candidate regions of the road sign and then classify them according to their predefined classes. The challenge of TSR system is to recognize road signs with the highest possible accuracy and the shortest processing time. In this paper, we first study different Traffic Sign Detection and Traffic Sign Classification methods aiming to choose the best ones in terms of accuracy. Then, we propose a new real time approach, based on Haar like Cascade technique for the detection step and on a deep learning model (which we called DeepSL) for the classification step. In order to validate the efficiency of our pipeline, we choose speed limit road signs images from the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark (GTSRB) dataset to achieve real tests. Obtained results show a good acceptable accuracy rate (95%) after two training time for the recognition of speed limit road signs.

title: A comparative study on the importance of each face part in facial gender recognition via convolutional neural networks
abstract: Nowadays, gender recognition systems are very important in several fields such as security, human machine interaction, surveillance and targeted advertising. However, many factors, such as makeup and disguise, can affect recognition and extend the processing time. Our research revolves around this issue. This is a comparative experimental study of the significance of each part of the face (eyes, mouth, nose) in the gender facial recognition via convolutional neural networks (CNN). As a first step our goal is to find the most crucial part of the face in order to determine the most important part in the gender recognition. The used method was tested on the UTKFace dataset and the preliminary results confirm that the eyes contain the most discriminating information regarding gender identification. We achieve a classification accuracy of 92% for eyes, 91% for mouth and 89% for nose. Then we propose a second study on the degree of importance of the eyes for both genders by training the system using only eyes. We achieve a classification accuracy of 99% for eyes of men and 99% for eyes of women.

title: The impact of Weather and Panel characteristics Features on Photo voltaic Power Forecasting
abstract: Solar energy intermittency is causing an enormous problem in smart grid management, the energy needed is not always meet due to the unequal dispatchability during the day. So, accurate solar energy forecasting becomes a necessity to satisfy the demand. During this work, Artificial Neural Network (ANN) was deployed within brute force search algorithm to pick the category (categories) of features that fit the model accurately using data generated from photo voltaic (PV) plants installed in Eugene, Oregon within weather data of the same location. Several combinations were tested and evaluated using two error measures to conclude that plane of array irradiance and predetermined panel characteristics are the most effective features to attain good accuracy.

title: Agent Architecture for Pedestrian's Crowd in Public Places: Combination of Individual and Cooperative Reasoning
abstract: A major problem in a crowd evacuation is rescuing frightened and trapped people. This paper presents a decision making process based on a combination of individual and social cooperative reasoning to evacuate people during a crowd evacuation. Specifically, we propose to evacuate crowds by modeling the social cooperative behaviors of multi agent systems. In this context, cooperative reasoning contributes to the collaboration between agents to find missing data in a multi variable environment. Cooperative reasoning allows agents to exchange information and reach an agreement in order to exit quickly and safely. Experimental results showed that cooperative reasoning combined with individual reasoning has a great impact on final decision and can lead to a successful evacuation with a percentage of 90.

title: Supervised learning approach for section title detection in PDF scientific articles
abstract: The majority of scientific articles is available in Portable Document Format (PDF). Although PDF format has the advantage of preserving layout across platforms it does not maintain the original metadata structure, making it difficult further text processing. Despite different layouts, depending on the applied template, articles have a hierarchical structure and are divided into sections, which represent topics of specific subjects, such as methodology and results. Hence, section segmentation serves as an important step for a contextualized text processing of scientific articles. Therefore, this work applies binary classification, a supervised learning task, for section title detection in PDF scientific articles. To train the classifiers, a large dataset (more than 5 millions samples from 7,302 articles) was created through an automated feature extraction approach, comprised by 17 features, where 4 were introduced in this work. Training and testing were made for ten different classifiers for which the best F1 score reached 0.94. Finally, we evaluated our results against CERMINE, an open source system that extracts metadata from scientific articles, having an absolute improvement in section detection of 0.19 in F1 score.

title: Frame Semantics for Social NLP in Italian: Analyzing Responsibility Framing in Femicide News Reports
abstract: We propose using a FrameNet based approach for analyzing how socially relevant events are framed in media discourses. Taking femicides as an example, we per form a preliminary investigation on a large dataset of news reports and event data covering recent femicides in Italy. First, we revisit the EVALITA 2011 shared task on Italian frame labeling, and test a recent multilingual frame semantic parser against this benchmark. Then, we experiment with specializing this model for Italian and perform a human evaluation to test our models real world applicability. We show how FrameNet based analyses can help to identify linguistic constructions that background the agentivity and responsibility of femicide perpetrators in Italian news.

title: WikiCSSH: Extracting and Evaluating Computer Science Subject Headings from Wikipedia
abstract: Hierarchical domain specic classication schemas (or subject heading vocabularies) are often used to identify, classify, and disambiguate concepts that occur in scholarly articles. In this work, we develop, apply, and evaluate a human in the loop work ow that first extracts an initial category tree from crowd sourced Wikipedia data, and then combines community detection, machine learning, and hand crafted heuristics or rules to prune the initial tree. This work resulted in WikiCSSH; a large scale, hierarchically organized vocabulary for the domain of computer science (CS). Our evaluation suggests that WikiCSSH outperforms alternative CS vocabularies in terms of vocabulary size as well as the performance of lexicon based key phrase extraction from scholarly data. WikiCSSH can further distinguish between coarse grained versus fine grained CS concepts. The outlined work ow can serve as a template for building hierarchically organized subject heading vocabularies for other domains that are covered in Wikipedia.

title: Can we assess research using open scientific knowledge graphs? A case study within the Italian National Scientific Qualification
abstract: The need for open scientific knowledge graphs is ever increasing. While there are large repositories of open access articles and free publication indexes, there are still few free knowledge graphs exposing citation networks, and often their coverage is partial. Consequently, most evaluation processes based on citation counts rely on commercial citation databases. Things are changing thanks to the Initiative for Open Citations (I4OC, https://i4oc.org) and the Initiative for Open Abstracts (I4OA, https://i4oa.org), whose goal is to campaign for scholarly publishers to open the reference lists and the other metadata of their articles. This paper investigates the growth of the open bibliographic metadata and open citations in two scientific knowledge graphs, OpenCitations COCI and Crossref, with an experiment on the Italian National Scientific Qualification (NSQ), the National process for University Professor qualification which uses data from commercial indexes. We simulated the procedure by only using such open data and explored similarities and differences with the official results. The outcomes of the experiment show that the amount of open bibliographic metadata and open citation data currently available in the two scientific knowledge graphs adopted is not yet enough for obtaining results similar to those provided using commercial databases.

title: Towards Neural Schema Alignment for OpenStreetMap and Knowledge Graphs
abstract: OpenStreetMap (OSM) is one of the richest openly available sources of volunteered geographic information. Although OSM includes various geographical entities, their descriptions are highly heterogeneous, incomplete, and do not follow any well defined ontology. Knowledge graphs can potentially provide valuable semantic information to enrich OSM entities. However, interlinking OSM entities with knowledge graphs is inherently difficult due to the large, heterogeneous, ambiguous and flat OSM schema and the annotation sparsity. This paper tackles the alignment of OSM tags with the corresponding knowledge graph classes holistically by jointly considering the schema and instance layers. We propose a novel neural architecture that capitalizes upon a shared latent space for tag to class alignment created using linked entities in OSM and knowledge graphs. Our experiments performed to align OSM datasets for several countries with two of the most prominent openly available knowledge graphs, namely, Wikidata and DBpedia, demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms the state of the art schema alignment baselines by up to 53 percentage points in terms of F1 score. The resulting alignment facilitates new semantic annotations for over 10 million OSM entities worldwide, which is more than a 400\% increase compared to the existing semantic annotations in OSM.

title: Reasoning Subevent Relation over Heterogeneous Event Graph
abstract: Subevent relation identification (SRI) is a challenging natural language processing task of great value for knowledge acquisition and reasoning. Given an event pair, previous work mainly defines SRI as a classification task and usually rely on hand crafted features extracted from a limited context. However, there are lots of evidence information in external knowledge bases which are not well explored by prior work but helpful for this task. To fill this gap, we propose to reason the subevent relation based on plentiful evidence information in addition to limited context features. Specifically, we notice that evidence information together with the input event pair can be organized into a heterogeneous event graph, which comprises various types of event relations. To facilitate this, we present a heterogeneous graph attention model with mix hop reasoning mechanism to reason subevent relation over heterogeneous event graph. In particular, our model allows nodes to capture more extensive and intact event knowledge by mixing feature representations of neighbors at multiple distances to aggregate information from diverse types of neighbors. Moreover, to explicitly model the hierarchical relations between event pairs and to improve the model consistency, we devise a novel hierarchy loss function for the proposed model. Our model is evaluated on two annotated datasets with subevent hierarchies: SeRI and HiEve. Experimental results show that our approach can outperform state of the art baseline methods. Further evaluation suggests that reasoning paths in the heterogeneous graph can regard as a reasonable explanation for the prediction result.

title: Out of Vocabulary Knowledge Graph Embeddings for Web Person Name Disambiguation
abstract: Web Person Name Disambiguation (WPND) is to group web pages according the individuals they refer to. It is particularly useful in Information Retrieval (IR) and Natural Language Processing (NLP). Most state of the art systems use the Vector Space Model and clustering methods. However, these systems do not perform well in text information extraction and cross text association. In this paper, we explore the use of Knowledge Graph Embeddings (KGEs) with out of vocabulary (OOV) triples to solve the problem of WPND. We propose a novel KGE model named TransOOV, which projects KGE in the word vector space and represents the uncertainty of OOV entities and relations by multidimensional Gaussian distribution. It fully utilizes and structurally understands semantic information. The main idea is to combine defined triples provided by external Knowledge Graphs (KGs) with OOV triples extracted from unstructured text for TransOOV training. Then, we define the similarity calculation and clustering methods. We validate our model with the state of the art systems on WePS datasets. The results show that our model is superior to the baselines. In addition, compared with other KGE models, TransOOV solves the problem of embedding OOV triples into KGs, and achieves the best results on WPND, OOV link prediction and triple classification.

title: LOD connected offensive language ontology and tag set enrichment
abstract: Introduction The main focus of the paper is the definitional revision and enrichment of offensive language typology making reference to publicly available offensive language datasets. We review more than 60 existing corpora and compare tagging schemas applied there while making an attempt to explain semantic differences between particular concepts of the category OFFENSIVE in English. As a result, we propose a finite set of classes that cover all aspects of offensive language representation along with linguistically sound explanations. We propose a core ontology which represents the encoding of the defined offensive language schema and justify those using Sketch Engine tools and non contextual word embeddings i.e., Word2Vec, Glove. The ontology will enable further comparable research and effective use of already annotated corpora. It will also be applied in building an enriched tag set to be trained and used on new data. Related work We make a detailed review of the existing offensive (also called abusive, toxic, etc.) language tag set systems, exemplify their classes and provide representations in our current ontology with examples of encoding of instances in the proposed schema. To the best of our knowledge, there is no prior work that would systematically review possible aspects of offensive language and propose a consistent schema. Therefore, we constrain it and define the semantics of the concepts used in our ontology model, finding support and justification in the linguistic data and their computational representation. Most of the currently available datasets as they are used at present seem to have been created rather ad hoc as a part of computational linguistic evaluations that ignore linguistic explanations. A survey of computational models in detecting offensive language is presented basing on the HatEval Task 5 of Semeval 2019 (more precisely on multilingual detection of hate speech against immigrants and women in twitter; Basile et al., 2019) and on the OffensEval Tasks of SemEval 2019 and SemEval 2020 (Zampieri et al., 2019a, and 2019b). Reference is made in the paper to automatic identification systems of offensive language using feature based linear classifiers (Waseem and Hovy, 2016; Ribeiro et al., 2018), neural network architectures (Kshirsagar et al., 2018; Mishra et al., 2018; Mitrovic et al., 2019), and fine tuned pre trained language models, such as BERT and RoBERTa, among others (Liu et al., 2019; Swamy et al., 2019). At the same time, the priority of the systems based on pre trained language models has been recognized to currently outperform other proposed models (Caselli et. al, 2020). Attempts at using LOD for modelling and detection of offensive language have also been consulted. Basis of the ontology The ontology of offensive language we propose in this research was originally inspired by the three level hierarchy of offensive language put forward by Zampieri et al. (2019a, 2019b). Contrary to Zampieri et al. (2019a, 2019b), however, in our research, offensive language is further refined and divided into two basic levels of analysis (Level I and II), and four sublevels (A, B, C, D) within Level I. Level I distinguishes lexical items that are offensive from those that are not (Level A: offensive vs. non offensive). Secondly (Level B: targeted vs. non targeted), the question whether the selected items are targeted at some addressee should be answered. If there is no identifiable addressee then the use of offensive language is an example of self expression, which has an exclamatory function, e.g., the use of swear words to express anger, frustration, pain etc (abusive swearing in Andersson and Trudgill 2007: 197). Targeted offensive items are further divided into either implicit or explicit cases of offensive language (Level C: implicit vs. explicit language). While implicitness may be encoded by, for example, sarcasm and irony, whereby offence is veiled, explicitness entails more straightforward forms of verbal attack. Classes of explicit targeted categories of offence are further subcategorized into types characterized by varying kinds of internal or external targets as well as partly distinct characterization of the lexicon. Some of the identified classes overlap between social media i.e., online space use and outside world (offline) linguistic and behavioural content, such as e.g., cyber bullying, which will be discussed as a particularly pertinent type of offence in our ontology. To provide justification for the proposed classification and the definitional constraints of the (sub) categorical class labels we use the corpus management platform Sketch Engine (SK) and generally pre trained word embeddings (Word2Vec, Glove) for both qualitative and quantitative analysis of the proposed category concepts. Using word embeddings will enable access to all word forms in the neighbouring contexts of selected terms, yielding data comparable to the collocation ranges of Sketch Engine, and it will also enable distance calculations between words/word groups. Additional insight to the present study concerning both the ontology structure and offensive language distances as presented in the data is gained through a detailed comparison between Sketch Engine results and relevant word embeddings calculations. Conclusions Details of the proposed annotation methodology and the ontology schema with its application are exemplified in the paper. The proposed work will be further investigated for contextual embeddings within the existing annotated datasets. The methodology for mapping from existing corpora to a unified ontology as presented in this paper will be provided. References Andersson, L. G., Trudgill, P. 2007. Swearing. In: L. Monaghan, J. title: Measures of sentiments with giants components in social networks
abstract: We propose a framework to analyse large streams of tweets and detect offensive messages which have a High Impact. We use the Word2Vec vectors v0s of small dimension associated to words, to first sample the tweets and then associate a measure to decide if they are offensive.

title: Extending and Using a Sentiment Lexicon for Latin in a Linked Data Framework
abstract: In this paper we present the methodology followed to extend a Latin sentiment lexicon (called LatinAffectus), the process of inclusion of the lexicon in a knowledge base of interoperable linguistic resources for Latin and one use case performed on the treebank of Dante Alighieri's Latin works annotated following the Universal Dependencies guidelines. In addition, we report on our first attempt at linking the polarity scores of SentiWordNet 3.0 to a manually revised version of Latin WordNet.

title: Emotion analysis of user reactions to online news
abstract: Social media allow for observing different aspects of human behavior, in particular those that can be evaluated from explicit user expressions. Based on a dataset of posts with user opinions collected from social media, this paper shows an insight into how the readers of different news portals react to online content. The theoretical model and corresponding hypotheses address the dynamic nature of how social media content impacts on user participation. The findings show the influence of social media content on emotional user engagement, thus provide a more comprehensive understanding of emotional aspect of online user behavior.

title: Prospectus Embeddings & Sentiment Analysis for IPO Pricing & Withdrawal
abstract: A firms Initial Public Offering (IPO) is its first entrance into the publicly traded stock market; while the number of IPOs has been very low for the last two decades, 2020 experienced 480 IPOs and 2021 has experienced 420 at the time of writing for a total of 900, which is 63 more than the preceding four years combined. Pricing this offering has historically been very difficult and average returns on the first day of trading have historically been very high, often larger than the markets annual return. This phenomenon, also known as underpricing, has attracted great attention from practitioners and academics alike. In conjunction with underpricing, IPO withdrawal is the phenomenon in which companies who file to go public, ultimately rescind the application before the offering. Most companies report poor market conditions to be the primary reason for withdrawing, but current financial theories posit that firm incentives, such as perceived firm sentiment, are of meaningful significance. This research proposes to utilize advancements in machine learning (ML) and natural language processing (NLP) to evaluate existing theories concerning firm sentiment on first day trading performance and the probability of withdrawal, which has thus far not been explored empirically. The results suggest that firms attempting to go public experience a lowered probability of withdrawal with the increased presence of positive, litigious, and uncertain language in their initial prospectus, while the increased presence of strong modular language leads to an increased probability of withdrawal. The results also suggest that frequent or large adjustments in the strong modular language of subsequent filings leads to smaller first day returns.

title: Multilingual Knowledge Systems as Linguistic Linked Open Data for European Language Grid
abstract: In the world depending on knowledge sharing, data driven businesses and research communities are concerned with creating, sharing, and using language resources in accordance with Linked Data principles. We present Coreon Multilingual Knowledge System as a Linguistic Linked Open Data resource (LLOD) for discovery, access, retrieval, and reusability of terminologies and other interoperability assets. Coreon enriches language data with structure and expands the resulting knowledge graphs with multilingual terminology, using European Language Grid (ELG) as a platform for making the published resources discoverable and retrievable via the SPARQL interface. A Multilingual Knowledge System is an important Semantic Interoperability Asset: a semantic graph based knowledge repository that enables information exchange among acting systems, ensuring that the precise meaning of the exchanged information is understood and preserved among all parties, in any language. Robust, coherent, and multilingual information standards are needed to enable information exchange among European public organizations, similar to standards that have been fostering technical interoperability for decades. ELG is a shared platform for the European LT landscape that tackles the fragmentation of the LT market space, bridging together datasets, applications, and other LT services that can benefit European society, industry, and politics. ELG launched an initiative which encourages the use of automated, easy to integrate mechanisms that allow such cross platform exchange of services, models, datasets, and metadata records, providing structured and semantically aligned information about the contents of the respective platforms. Instead of using the proprietary API, Coreon integration into other systems is now tool independent and is able to rely on well pronounced standards of the LLOD and the Sematic Web communities. W3C SPARQL is the established query syntax for the Semantic Web; while existing SPARQL tools enable users to query knowledge graphs, they are rarely used for termbases and other terminology resources that represent core sources of data for translation and localization. Seeing this as a lost opportunity for the reach of terminology resources, we implemented a solution for Coreon MKS, making termbases discoverable and accessible for systems powered by the best Semantic Web and LLOD practices. To achieve this goal, data owners needed to investigate, select, and deploy an alternative technology like an RDF triple store for their terminology tool, often developing and/or setting up a tedious data mirroring process. We also demonstrate a way to overcome the limits of RDF/knowledge graph editors, which tend to be good at relation modeling but have weaknesses when it comes to capturing of linguistic information. We analyzed and implemented data mirroring process from Coreon data model to an RDF graph, establishing the RDF vocabulary for classes, relations, additional term descriptive information, and administrative meta data, binding these elements into RDF triples that feature atomic, isolated nature. With the vocabulary ready, Coreons export engine was equipped with the RDF publication mechanism, including RDF export in all relevant syntax flavours (Turtle, N3, JSON LD, etc.). Coreon cloud service was also supplied with a real time accessible SPARQL endpoint via Apache Jena Fuseki: running as a secondary index in parallel to the repositorys data store, it catches any changes made by data maintainers, updating the state of the repositories in real time. The outcome of this project is many fold: besides making the SPARQL endpoint available to Coreon users, it is a productized piece of software that provides multilingual TBX like terminology resources in the RDF data model and the Semantic Web context. Beyond establishing structural interoperability, the implemented interface acts as a bridge between the MKS and other Semantic Web systems, enabling querying of elaborated multilingual terminologies stored in knowledge graphs. In a longer perspective, MKS as a LLOD resource provides relevant input for standardization bodies and interoperability communities. It acts as a blueprint for similar integration activities and can be viewed as a starting point for an international standard: we share our experience with ISO / TC37 SC3 working groups as a draft for a technical recommendation on how to represent TBX as RDF. Once deployed on the ELG platform in summer 2021, Coreon SPARQL interface will enable the Semantic Web community to query rich multilingual data with a familiar, industry standard syntax, promoting data accessibility and contributing to the development of multilingualism within the Semantic Web. The completed project is a pilot service contribution of the funding winning proposal to the ELG Open Call \#1.

title: Extending General Sentiment Lexicon to Specific Domains in (Semi )Automatic Manner
abstract: This paper describes an approach for the construction of a sentiment analysis system that uses both automatic and manual processes. The system includes a domain specific sentiment lexicon, modifier patterns and rules that are used to derive their sentiment values. The lexicon that includes single words (unigrams) is obtained in an automatic manner from the distribution of ratings for all words in the labelled training data. The sentiment values of phrases is derived from a list of modifier patterns, built/developed manually. These include a modifier and a focal element. The modifiers can be of different types, depending on whether the operation is intensification, downtoning or reversal. This approach was applied to texts on economics and finance in European Portuguese. In our view, this line of work deserves more attention in the community, as the system has not only reasonable performance, but also can provide understandable explanations to the user.

title: Automatic Generation of Domain Specific Sentiment Lexicon
abstract: Sentiment analysis (SA) has attracted a lot of attention both as a research topic and area for applications (Bing, 2012). Many approaches exist and can be divided into two basic groups. The first one includes machine learning (ML) approaches, which construct a model on the basis of examples of texts annotated with a sentiment value. The ML and recen tly deep learning based approaches produce a good predictive accuracy for sentiment analysis task but lack explainability on how and why such predictive performance is achieved (Clos et al., 2017). The second group involves a usage of a lexicon that includes a list of sentiment bearing words or expressions. Our work falls into this group, although certain ML methods (hybrid approach) play an important role in the process of evaluating our lexicons. The advantage of the lexicon based approaches is that the predictions of sentiment values (or class in case of classification) can be justified in terms of the number of sentiments bearing words, and thus fall into the category of explainable AI. However, many previous studies create general sentiment lexicons manually by extracting only adjectives from a text and assign a semantic orientation to the corresponding words. This makes the lexicon generation process laborious and time consuming. Also, the application of sentiment analysis is rapidly increasing to different domains, it is impractical to create a sentiment lexicon manually for every domain. Almatarneh et al., (2017) developed a method for automatically constructing sentiment lexicons using only two part of speech categories: adjectives and adverbs. The work of V.S. Subrahmanian et al. (2008) shows that the combination of adjective, verb and adverb increases the performance of the sentiment analysis task. Our work aims to develop a domain agnostic approach that automatically generates domain specific sentiment lexicon from any text associated with ratings (e.g., IMDB review). In addition, the approach creates sentiment lexicons from different combination of part of speech as shown in Table 1. The average accuracy results (MAE) among the different setting show that the combination of Adjective, Adverb and Verb has both higher performance in terms of mean absolute error (MAE), equal to 1.27, and a smaller number of lexicon entries. In the full paper, we will provide more details, including how we deal with less frequent words, which should obviously not appear in the lexicon, how the predictions are rescaled to minimize the error and provide a detailed report of the results. We have compared our approach with the automatic approach by Almatarneh et al., (2017), and ours has shown improved performance.

title: Aspect based sentiment analysis of conference review forms with LD enabled review criteria
abstract: Conference (or journal) review forms represent a particular kind of sentiment bearing documents, which has been to date left largely unexplored. Leveraging on the recent tendency towards open reviewing, as well as through collaboration with conference PC members and chairs, we obtained a multipart review corpus including a subset or a whole of anonymized conference reviews from four conferences. Furthermore, by a thorough manual analysis of the review forms and guidelines of eleven conferences (all from the semantic technology field, such as ISWC, ESWC, EKAW, K CAP, SEMANTiCS, etc.), we identified a set of generic review criteria (or, metrics), which we used as aspects in aspect based sentiment analysis of the review form texts. As a side activity, we also designed a provisional RDF ontology containing review related concepts such as ReviewMetrics, ReviewForm and ReviewFormField,and expressed the proposed set of aspects in RDF as instances of ReviewMetrics. The review form fields of a specific conference can be mapped on the generic aspects through a web application. A sentiment lexicon was then created specifically for the domain of conference paper reviews. A dictionary based sentiment lexicon analysis method was implemented and applied to a set of reviews from three different conferences. The first step of the lexicon construction method was the manual definition of a two level taxonomy, where the 1st level were the review criteria names and the 2nd level were 2 7 other terms: either synonyms of the review criteria or other obvious terms judged highly probable to appear in the respective portion of the review. In the second phase, noun phrases observed as frequently appearing in the given portions of the review, as well as frequent adjectives (as another typical sentiment ingredient), were automatically collected. 57 new terms were added to the lexicon in the second phase (a few other were removed via manual validation of the taxonomy). The results were then evaluated by comparing the numerical scores estimated by the algorithm with the numerical scores from the reviews. The outcome was then explored further by inspecting the accuracy of criterion identification and sentiment analysis on a sentence level. The precision of criterion identification was evaluated at 57.38% and the recall at 53.44%. As such, the error rate is quite high, however even the annotators had a substantial level of disagreement, initially diverging in their criterion labeling in over a third of the comments. This suggests that reconstructing the intended meaning of the review comments is a particularly difficult task even for human annotators. As regards the sentiment polarity, it was correct in over 75% of cases. This is an improvement on the result of a similar sentiment analysis carried out in a comparable study with focus on peer reviews of scientific publications, by Bucur et al. (from K CAP19). Their analysis algorithm only managed to reach an accuracy level of about 73% even though the sentiment analysis was not aspect based, which presumably made determining the sentiment easier. In particular, we observed that the polarity for a particular aspect expressed in a sentence may differ from the overall polarity of that sentence, provided the sentence covers multiple aspects of the review. Our algorithm is capable of being substantially improved when given the availability of a significantly larger dataset. This could help put together both a better aspect expression dictionary and a vast sentiment lexicon, the creation of which would heavily rely on the frequency of terms across reviews. Additionally, should a larger dataset be available, it would be possible to perform a more detailed exploration of the specifics of the language used in similar data, creating a more complex algorithm using the discovered knowledge. Another possible way to improve the results would be to put together specialized rules for the different criteria. For example, as comments about the presentation criterion often lead to false positives matches on other criteria, it would be possible to create a rule where criteria expression found in a sentence where there is also a match on presentation would be discarded. While there is already a two fold relationship between linked data and the presented research (the aspects are modeled via an RDF ontology and data, and the experiments were carried out on data from semantic technology conferences), the exploitation of linguistic LOD has not yet been tried. A very preliminary review of available LLOD resources indicates that those addressing sentiment analysis are often biased toward emotion analysis. The lexica developed in the project could possibly give rise to a complementary resource, which would rather target the sentiment (or, assessment polarity) expressed in a relatively emotion free and more rigorous language, as typically used in scientific reviews.

title: Sentiment Analysis of Hausa Tweets using English Translated Benchmark Sentiment Lexicon
abstract: Background: Sentiment Analysis (SA) is the identification and collection of peoples opinions conveyed in a text. SA is currently one of the most researched areas in Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Artificial Intelligence (AI). This is due to the continued need to identify and understand peoples opinions. The social media and the advancements in web technologies, beginning with the development of web 2.0 brought about research in SA. Early studies in SA are generally focused on basic classification of documents into positive, negative or neutral sentiments [1]. However, in later studies, more refined SA approaches were proposed focusing on the sentiment of individual aspects in the texts and the strength of the sentiments [2]. In recent studies, several applications of sentiment analysis have been explored. Notably, political prediction [3], disaster management [4], tourism [5], and healthcare management [6]. Purpose: Despite the numerous benefits of the SA, there are insufficient methods and very few studies on SA in many low resources languages. Most of the existing studies are on high resources languages, predominantly the English language. Hausa language is one of the most widely spoken languages in Africa. It has over 150 million speakers and is predominantly used in Northern Nigeria, Niger Republic, Chad, and many other West African countries. Yet, no available resources for sentiment analysis in Hausa language. Wan [7] proposed cross lingual sentiment analysis (CLSA) for low resource language. However, the success of the approach rely on an intermediary machine translation system between the two languages. In a similar study, Saif M. Mohammad et al. [8] have shown that Arabic sentiment analysis using automatically translated English sentiment lexicons produces good accuracy. Sentiment lexicon is one of the most important resources for sentiment analysis. It is a dictionary of sentiment bearing words together with their sentiment values. The lexicon can be used to classify texts into positive, negative, or neutral sentiments based on the sentiment words the text contains. This method of sentiment analysis is called the lexicon based sentiment analysis. Another method of sentiment analysis is the machine learning based SA where popular machine learning algorithms are trained to classify the text. Our work focused on lexicon based sentiment analysis using English translated sentiment lexicons. To this effect, we automatically translate sentiment lexicon from three widely use English sentiment lexicon. We also develop the first manually annotated sentiment corpus for Hausa language from social media

title: Authorship Identification using Morphological Global vectors with stacked Bi directional LSTM
abstract: Authority Recognition is a technique cast off only to stratify unauthorized papers recognizing and processing feature vectors of the critic. In the contemporary, the real world applications for authorship identification have intense magnification in domains like surveillance, culprit, civil cybersecurity. The subsist models be stow better precision by using the n gram method for assembling features. We come about with a proposal that cornerstone pre dominantly on vocabulary and morphological word analysis. We drafted specific tokens to every input article. Using Global Vectors, we strapped each word to its relevance index and brought out an embedding layer. Using SpatialDropout1D, we reduced a certain percentage of each word vectors proportions in the training sample. We permit those features to Stacked Bi directional LSTM. Our Proposed model outperformed effectively on both train and test data of C50. We have attained 64% accuracy invalidation, which is much better than any other existing approaches.

title: Predicting Paper Acceptance via Interpretable Decision Sets
abstract: Measuring the quality of research work is an essential component of the scientific process. With the ever growing rates of articles being submitted to top tier conferences, and the potential consistency and bias issues in the peer review process identified by scientific community, it is thus of great necessary and challenge to automatically evaluate submissions. Existing works mainly focus on exploring relevant factors and applying machine learning models to simply be accurate at predicting the acceptance of a given academic paper, while ignoring the interpretability power which is required by a wide range of applications. In this paper, we propose a framework to construct decision sets that consist of unordered if then rules for predicting paper acceptance. We formalize decision set learning problem via a joint objective function that simultaneously optimize accuracy and interpretability of the rules, rather than organizing them in a hierarchy. We evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed framework by applying it on a public scientific peer reviews dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the learned interpretable decision sets by our framework performs on par with state of the art classification algorithms which optimize exclusively for predictive accuracy and much more interpretable than rule based methods.

title: Unlocking the potential of Natural Language Processing (NLP) in Health care
abstract: During the COVID 19 pandemic, Natural Language Processing(NLP) plays a strategic role in disease detection, intensive care,drug discovery and controlling the mushrooming of infections.. It energizes chat programs to assist in the reduction of outbreaks during the initial stages of coronavirus infection. NLP technologies have reached new heightsin terms of utility, and are at the heart of the success of a multilingual conversation system, Chatbots, and Deep learning language models. It supports a total of 13 languages around the world. NLP powered AI such as Health map and Copweb platforms track patient requests and perform incident detections. This chapter looks at the role of NLP and its technologies, challenges, and future possibilities using AI and machine learning for crisis mitigation and easier EHRs in the health care industry.

title: Supporting digital healthcare services using NLP
abstract: Public computerized programs exist to help human health services, for example, those of the National Health Mission of India based on center frameworks of patient and supplier vaults, clinical and analytic imaging frameworks, clinical reports and inoculations. This chapter shall describe the digital healthcare services in the context of NLP and discuss a case study on NLP in digital healthcare.

title: Clinical Text Mining of research papers using low cost resources
abstract: Mining huge volumes of data with low cost NLP resources is a challenge. But recent advancements in NLP have made it possible to do this. The trick lies in using a strategy to mine huge volumes of data with low cost and limited resources. When the world is fighting with COVID 19, there is a flux of information coming through research papers. And for a front line medical worker, it is not possible to go through all the papers and find the right response. For instance, a medical worker may need guidance on ways to scale up Non pharmaceutical interventions in a more coordinated way (e.g., establish funding, infrastructure, and authorities to support real time, authoritative (qualified participants) collaboration with all states to gain consensus on consistent guidance. For a low cost scenario, a suggested way is to follow a step wise approach is presented to mine clinical data. Here, only a subset of a document is scanned to determine whether this is likely to provide intended information.

title: Healthcare NLP infrastructure for the Greek language
abstract: Although English is by far the richest language in terms of resources and tools for Natural Language processing (NLP) in the domain of biomedicine and healthcare, this is not the case for the less widely used languages such as Greek. The aim of this chapter is to present a structured description of an NLP infrastructure for the Greek language, developed initially for the processing of general language, and extended later on to incorporate biomedical texts as well. The infrastructure comprises: (a) components developed de novo to meet the needs of the domain specific requirements, such as a biomedical corpus, a generic and application independent medical ontology, and a multi word term extraction mechanism, (b) general language processing tools that were enhanced for the processing of the corpus, such as tokenization and sentence splitting tools, and a lexicon based morphosyntactic tagger. Future developments should focus on the fine tuning of the components concerning term extraction and semantic annotation, and the enrichment of the language resources with additional bilingual information (i.e., Greek English). Improvement of the above will enable interoperability among the Greek NLP infrastructure and other bi/multilingual tools in the field of biomedicine.

title: Low Cost Topic Model Generation for NLP Applications
