abstract: Nowadays, there is high availability of digital Clinical data. In this scenario, there is a need to analyze this data efficiently which can be useful for medical practitioners and fraternity. If the data can be correlated to clinical dictionary (ontology), that could be a good assistance to medical fraternity. Especially the area of triaging, if a system can suggest areas to investigate, this could be highly beneficial. Low cost NLP techniques can be utilized in this scenario.

title: Clinical NLP for Drug Safety
abstract: {Dr. Yashodhara V. Haribhakta, Bhasha Khose} College of Engineering Pune. Drug safety plays a critical role in Healthcare and Drug Development Lifecycle. Most countries follow the common practice of managing the Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) database for drug monitoring. Countries coordinates with the international Drug Monitoring system maintained by the World Health Organization (WHO). WHO has the Collaborating Center for International Drug Monitoring, Uppsala Monitoring Center (UMC), in Sweden, with over 3 million reports of suspected ADRs. Drug safety and the ecosystem around the Drug development life cycle are greatly emphasized in situations like the one world is going through currently COVID 19. WHO dashboard says "Globally, 9 October 2020, there have been 36,361,054 confirmed cases of COVID 19, including 1,056,186 deaths, reported to WHO." "More than 100 Covid 19 vaccine candidates are under development, with a number of these in the human trial phase", as per WHO. Due to the enormous impact and continuously evolving consequences of Covid 19 on humanity, vaccine development is getting pushed through the development lifecycle. The rise in the fatality rate of COVID 19 and the early results from the human trial phase asks for strict monitoring and tracking of these vaccines. AstraZeneca's recent announcement, a vaccine jointly developed by AstraZeneca and the University of Oxford, is put on hold after one UK participant in a Phase 3 trial developed a severe and unexplained illness. Patients increasingly use social media platforms to discuss & enquire about their medical conditions. These communications can be leveraged to generate insights that can improve drug safety. Patients are comfortable and prefer sharing in their native language. Clinical entity resolution and key attribute extraction from the native language text depends on the availability of standards like UMLS, MedDRA in the native language, or on the accurate machine translation of the native text in a rich language like English. Example of Marathi (Indian language) text: Mala Malmalat hota ani mag khup dok dukhyala lagla. English Translation: "First I was feeling nauseated and then had a severe headache". Bing Translator: "I had a property and had a lot of dock injury". Google Translate: "I got sick and I was very sad". None of the Bing translator or Google translator could detect the stated medical conditions in the raw text. This chapter will discuss challenges and possible approaches to extract ADR and insights from native social media text to improve drug safety.

title: Short Text Topic Modeling with Gibbs Sampling DirichletMultinomial Mixture: Sketching a solution for clustering Spanish medical appointments admission records
abstract: Topic modelling (TM) is a machine learning method used to discover latent semantic structures (i.e. topics) in text corpora, where each one is defined as a probability distribution over word occurrences (Albalawi et al., 2020). Thus, TM does not need a priori knowledge of the topics present in a collection since these are inferred from word occurrence patterns. The most studied and frequently used TM algorithm is latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) (Mazarura & de Waal, 2016). Despite LDAs results and popularity, it has been observed that its performance significantly diminished when applied to short texts (i.e. texts comprising 100 words or less), given the difficulty such texts present for extracting meaningful word co occurrence patterns (Yin & Wang, 2014). Given this challenge, short text topic modelling (STTM) has emerged as a distinct line of research aiming to develop new methods to tackle the issue of scarcity for word pattern extraction (Yang et al., 2019).Within this line of research, Dirichlet multinomial mixture (DMM) based algorithms have shown to perform better in STTM tasks over English texts from social media, particularly in their implementation with Gibbs Sampling (GS DMM) (Agarwal et al., 2020; Qiang et al., 2020). This project, exploratory in nature, aims to implement GS DMM for STTM over a corpus of short text in Spanish corresponding to admission records for medical appointments in the San Juan de Dios de Curico Hospital, a Public Hospital in the Maule region, Chile. Currently, a significant percentage of this hospital medical appointments admission records correspond to a few words with no associated categories, which hinders the facilitys management of these data and impairs its capability for localized data driven decision making. Using standard natural language processing tasks (normalization, tokenization, stopwords removal) and topic modelling over unannotated records, we aim to sketch a solution that could ease this facilitys use of clinical text data, thus impacting in its decision making capabilities and, by extension, in patients experience. Our project will be structured as follows: in section 1 we will establish a theoretical background for natural language processing and short text topic modelling; in section 2 we will present our methodology and explore the peculiarities of our working corpus; section 3 will focus on the projects results, contrasting the resulting topic coherence of GS DMM with that of LDA for the working corpus as well as a control biomedical corpus. Finally, in section 4, we will discuss limitations and future work.

title: Development of a Machine Translation system for promoting the use of a low resource language in the clinical domain: the case of Basque
abstract: In multilingual environments where there is a strong language spoken by a majority and a low resource language spoken by a minority, Machine Translation (MT) can be useful for allowing clinical practitioners to write their reports in the minority language, which then can be automatically translated into the majority language. Current state of the art approaches for MT require large quantities of parallel sentences of the desired languages and the specific domain, so MT systems developed for translating clinical text from/into a low resource language will usually need to go through a domain adaptation process. When there are enough in domain resources for the target language, back translation is commonly used for domain adaptation. In our case, since we have access to many Electronic Health Records (EHR) in Spanish, we make use of this and similar techniques that leverage monolingual data for translating clinical text from Basque into Spanish. Moreover, one of the main characteristics of clinical domain text is its rich terminology, which is not always available for any given language, so before developing a MT system for the clinical domain, it is beneficial to make a special effort to translate the clinical terminology into the low resource language. If the final objective is to implement a system that can be useful for clinical practitioners, it is important to work with them for defining the terminology and any other aspect that can affect the final performance of the systems. Needless to say, given the special relevance of the content to be translated, users of the MT systems should be aware of possible errors made; and whenever it is possible, a human translator should review the generated translations to guarantee their accuracy. In this Chapter we describe the approach we have followed to develop a MT system for translating clinical text from Basque into Spanish. In the first Section we introduce Basque language and give some details about the sociolinguistic situation in the Basque Country. In the second Section we present Itzulbide, the project carried out together with the Basque public health service for compiling clinical domain corpora to be used for developing a MT tool for the healthcare domain. In the third Section we overview the diverse corpora we have used in our systems, and specify how the training and evaluation are performed. The fourth Section discusses the results obtained in the defined settings. Finally, the fifth Section presents some conclusions and points to possible future directions.

title: Formalizing the Recognition of Medical Domain Multiword Units
abstract: The papers deals with the recognition of multiword units (MWU) in texts from medical domain written in Croatian language. We focus on the automatic recognition of complex MWU using low resource settings. These units are complex in terms that they consist of two or more noun or prepositional phrases. Recognized MWU are manually checked, marked as medical terms and stored in a lexicon in order to enhance the clinical text mining, analytics and machine translation at later stages of the project. The building of the medical lexicon is an ongoing project [1,2], divided into several phases. In previous steps of this project we collected the Croatian medical corpus, which contains pharmaceutical instructions for medicaments and which is made publicly available through the Sketch Engine interface. Further, the corpus was analyzed and medical terms consisting of single nouns were annotated. In the subsequent phase we dealt with terms consisting of nouns and one or more adjectives serving as attributes. We were able to annotate domain specific attributes by using the already marked nouns from the previous step. We also recognized NPs which belong to the medical domain both due to the meaning of an adjective (e.g. bubrezna funkcija kidney function) and/or of a noun (e.g. akutna bol acute pain). Whereas in such cases where the meaning of nouns is not specific for the medical domain, due to specific semantics of adjectives, the whole MWU is marked and stored as a medical term (e.g. vodene kozice chickenpox). In this work we expand our focus to MWU such as simptomatsko (ADJ) lijecenje (NOUN nominative) bolesnika (NOUN genitive) symptomatic treatment of patients; biljni (ADJ), sirup (NOUN nominative) protiv (PREP) kaslja (NOUN genitive) herbal antiasthmatic syrup, as well as more complex ones like kontinuirano pracenje omjera koristi i rizika lijeka continuous evaluation of the risk benefit balance of the medicinal product. For the recognition of extended MWU we are developing a set of syntactic graphs in the form of finite state grammars that are used on the syntax level of the analysis. The grammars are designed in the platform NooJ (used for various other NLP tasks) with the preliminary aim of automatic building of the lexicon of medical terms from a medical domain corpus. Such a digital lexicon will be valuable for further processing of medical texts and various NLP tasks in this domain. References: 1. K. Kocijan, S. Kurolt, L. Mijic: Building Croatian Medical Dictionary from Medical Corpus. In: Rasprave: Casopis Instituta za hrvatski jezik I jezikoslovlje 46/2 (2020). 2. K. Kocijan, K. Sojat, S. Kurolg: Multiword Expressions in the Medical Domain: Who Carries the Domain Specific Meaning, In: Formalizing Natural Languages with NooJ 2020 and Its Natural Language Processing Applications, Springer 2021 (in print).

title: Domain Adaptation in Clinical Natural Language Processing (Clinical NLP)
abstract: Natural language processing has an impact on living and society. Machine Translation, Language learning, and Sentiment analysis are some core NLP applications. Clinical NLP is another challenging application. This chapter revolves around domain adaptation that will work on publicly available data to create a solution for limited health care research problems. Domain adaptation is the task of adapting models across domains. There is an inherent shift or drift in the data distribution of the source and target domains that requires tweaks to transfer the learning. This article discusses possible solutions that prove that domain adaptation is necessary to solve healthcare challenges under low resource settings. Further, we analyzed challenges faced by health care NLP and the limitations of various state of the art approaches used by NLP in healthcare. The article covers many downstream NLP tasks such as Machine Translation and Summarization that help bridge the communication gap between health care people and their patients. Finally, It concludes with the immediate solutions to domain adaptation challenges by the number of experiments and analysis.

title: Towards Medical Text Translation for Endangered Languages: The case of Canadas Indigenous Languages
abstract: Machine Translation (MT) has proven to be a useful tool to assist human translators in the case of rich resource Languages. However, for low resource languages and domains, there is still a long path to meet up with our expectations, especially in sensitive domains such as the medical. Our research deals with the possibility of achieving fully automatic machine translation of high quality in making medical information understandable to both physicians and patients, face to the fact that most medical records and instructions, such as the COVID 19 ones, are written in English and human translators are not often available for users. The recent outbreak of COVID 19 revealed a critical emergency in improving data collection for First Nations, Inuit and Metis communities in Canada as well as in preserving elders of Indigenous communities, as they are most at risk of becoming very ill if they contract COVID 19. It has reported a need for medical translation to cure life threatening diseases. The fast and inexpensive way this can be done is through MT system. However, MT was not able to provide high quality translations in the medical domain due to the low resource scenarios for most of Canadas indigenous languages. In this research, we examine the case of Canadas indigenous languages through experiments on the medical text translation for low resource languages with an emphasize on COVID 19 pandemic. The objective of this research is to ensure that authentic medical sensitive information and instructions reaches the common people in their own languages, primarily those in marginalized indigenous communities, whos native languages are most of the time endangered or with limited linguistic resources. This will help these communities and their governments to take appropriate measures to fight the pandemic without being disturbed by fake news and infodemic arising from the COVID 19 crisis. Our first step towards a multilingual Neural Machine Translation (NMT) framework that will involve several endangered Indigenous languages of Canada, is essential, as the only parallel corpus freely available for research is the Nunavut English Hansard corpus (Joanis et al., 2020). We focus on (1) the preprocessing phase to build (2) NLP applications for Indigenous languages, such as Named Entities Recognition (NER) and a Neural Machine Translation (NMT). Inspired by the work of Farley (2012), on the creation of the first Inuktitut morphological analyzer based on grammar rules, we built a deep learning based word segmentation for the Inuit languages family (Le and Sadat, 2020). This method of combining the strengths of both linguistics based and neural models can be achieved by exploring ways of exploiting the explicit and implicit knowledge into NMT. We incorporate this preprocessing for the source within our first Inuktitut English NMT. Our results, in the context of low resource Inuktitut English, show that our approach leads to significant improvements compared to the state of the art. So far, we intend to apply our approach to more Indigenous languages, especially to the Inuit family and other endangered languages such as Inuinnaqtun. Thanks to the collaboration of Indigenous communities, we can collect reliable data from the native speakers to improve the performance of NLP applications and conduct suitable evaluations, that could increase the medical translation quality in the Healthcare domain.

title: Empowering Korean Speakers with Distributional Semantics Techniques to Identify Misinformation about COVID 19
abstract: In comparison to the 1.5 billion English speakers, there are only 75 million speakers of the Korean language, and as such, it would be classified as a low resource language. Irrespective of the smaller number of speakers, Koreans are equally as concerned about misinformation. Interestingly, a quick google query of Korean+misinformation yields an overabundance of relevant content. Modern day natural language processing techniques for evaluating misinformation are increasingly prevalent and continuously advancing. There are dozens of available datasets and formal academic efforts. According to googletrends, the interest in misinformation has tripled in the last year and is continuing to increase. Unfortunately, the artificial intelligence software and models that are available for low resource languages, face challenges because the lack of available labeled data to train upon. We are encouraged, as our research shows that the lack of labeled content is not fatal flaw. Natural language processing approaches based on statistics, like Latent Dirichlet allocation or latent semantic indexing, show promise. These techniques and their models, while designed and implemented on high resource languages, such as English, can be generalized and applied to other alphabetic languages. The approaches can be designed on one language and applied to another, based on a foundation that is mathematical instead of lexical. We propose a chapter that lays out the problem faced by Korean speakers in automating the identification of misinformation, while providing an elegant solution: 1. Introduction definitions for misinformation vs. disinformation vs. propaganda 2. Koreans concern with misinformation on COVID 19 (NY TIMES, Korea Herald, Guardian) *this is not to say that misinformation projects themselves are devoid of bias 3. Misinformation identification in the medical domain. Use of statistical approaches for identification of misinformation. We will leverage this powerful source (40 languages) > https://www.poynter.org/ifcn covid 19 misinformation/ 4. Evidence that statistical models can be generalized to low resource languages 5. Case study and results of LDA/LSA for identification of misinformation

title: (Co BOT) Psychiatric COVID 19 ChatBOT for Indian Languages
abstract: Abstract: The Indian Psychiatry Society estimates that the number of mentally ill people in India has risen by 20 % during this pandemic period. Lots of people seeking mental support end up depressed and many are still suffering. To provide an AI support, we are proposing a Multilingual ChatBot enabling to addresses this issue with the help of an interact interface to the end user by psychological behavior pattern analysis. The proposed Co BOT has well designed architecture along with a structured knowledge engine which supports to provide a language independent interface with extendible scope to add further languages. The design consists of three components with well balancing of cohesion and coupling. These components are an NLP Engine, a Knowledge engine and an interactive interface enriched by a virtual avatar. It would be supported by a structured resource repository of COVID 19 related information by means of medical knowledge and conversation dialogue as well. For language engines, a Sequence to Sequence Transformer model acts as our primary conversational model. This model forms the core of the NLP Engine design and processes user requests and responds accordingly. A sentiment analysis model operates in the background. This model detects negative or depressive elements in the users dialogs after conversation. Based on the accuracy of prediction, the patient would be recommended for the PHQ 9 depression test to detect the degree of depression of a person to classify the users depression intensity into one of five categories, from Mild Depression to Severe Depression. The second module of our system calculates the probability of a user contracting COVID 19 using parameters including age, gender and symptoms like fever and fatigue. The information is obtained from the user in the form of a questionnaire, and thus calculates the probability as mentioned earlier. Based on the probability calculated from system, it warns the user about having / not having contracted COVID 19 and advises accordingly. The next module of our system is an interactive interface with a virtual AVATAR in a rich environment supported by Virtual Reality technologies with voice and language support. Tentative Content: Literature survey will be presented in Section 2 for the architecture, algorithms of sentiment analysis and chatbot system. Referring to the architecture, Section 3 will explain our three main modules with their inter relations. In Section 4, each individual module will be discussed in detail. Section 5 will talk about the results and evaluation. Section 6 will conclude the paper with a discussion on the future scope.

title: Employing Computational Linguistics to Improve Patient Provider Secure Email exchange: The ECLIPPSE Study
abstract: Electronic patient portals (web based platforms providing patients immediate access to their health records) are a popular channel and increasingly available for patients and providers communication using secure messaging (SM). These exchanges offer an unprecedented possibility of employing computational linguistics to estimate patients health literacy (HL) as well as providers language complexity. This chapter describes the NLM funded ECLIPPSE project and discusses various approaches employed to develop the HL and language complexity measures, the results to date. ECLIPPSE represents an interdisciplinary effort that brought together primary care clinicians with computational linguistics, computers, communication and health services scientists, to harness online SMs exchanged between the patients and the providers to 1) create an automated and valid patient Literacy Profile (LP) that characterizes a patients HL, 2) develop an automated and valid physicians Complexity Profile (CP) to determine their SMs linguistic complexity, 3) assess whether physicians tailor their SM responses to accommodate limited HL patients communication needs, and 4) design a CP based automated aid that provides clinicians with real time feedback to curtail their SMs complexity. Herein, the progress related to Aims 1 and 2 is reported. During the course of LP and CP development, several natural language processing (NLP) tools measuring different language aspects were used and various challenges encountered. To enable successful implementation, solutions were devised for challenges related to data mining, analyses related to NLP and machine learning (ML) and interdisciplinary collaboration. Ultimately, patients self reported HL, physician linguistic complexity and patients HL rated by experts scores were used to train and evaluate ML classification models for building the patients LP and physicians CP. Ability to rapidly assess patients HL at scale could improve clinical care and population health among diverse populations, and determining whether physicians CP can be modified to mitigate the untoward effects of limited patient HL is of interest to healthcare delivery systems focused on promoting health equity. This research can reduce HL related disparities in healthcare by supporting the health systems and healthcare organizations in becoming health literate.

title: HealFavor: Machine Translation Enabled Healthcare Chat Based Application
abstract: Personalized user service has recently flourished, given the technological advancement in computing. One such personalized user application is a chatbot. This application is inherently designed to personalize user based system interaction. It allows the user to interact with the system as he would interact with a real life person, and hence its design must accommodate real time feedback to deliver precise decisions. The decisions taken by the system become more and more important with the sensitivity of the domain area of the application. Since a user is more likely to diverge if the language of interaction with the chatbot is foreign to him. We facilitate user based interaction in a local language that the user is comfortable with it. The system will specifically target the low resource language of the north eastern region of India. These languages would include the Assamese. The Assamese language belongs to the Indian state of Assam. It is a widely used language in the entire north eastern region of India. The system will be provided with the expert domain information in the field of healthcare to deliver large scale prediction and prognosis of commonly occurring diseases as well as initial advice to other contagious diseases, thereby helping in containing the further spread. The major benefit of such a system is its scalability to remote and underprivileged sections of society. In this chapter, the authors have discussed various relevant systems, as well as developed a healthcare chat dataset for the underlying deep learning based chatbot application.

title: A clinical practice by machine translation on low resource languages
abstract: In this book chapter introduces the clinical practice by machine translation, especially for low resource languages.

title: OdiCoviCorp: A labelled dataset for title generation of COVID 19 related topics in Odia language
abstract: Automatic title generation and recognition are considered a difficult activity in the area of natural language processing. In the case of multilingual situations, especially for low resource, morphologically complex languages, the availability of title data sets is uncommon and difficult to create. Most of the social computational analysis, based on the challenges encountered by developing nations, focuses on online content written in a world language like English, often lacking a significant portion of the lexicon written in a loosely resourced and commonly dominant first language of the region concerned. These omissions are popular and easy due to the sheer mismatch between the linguistic capitals provided in a world language and its low resource equivalent. In this work, we concentrate on one of the low resource languages, Odia, also written as Oriya. The goal of this study is to create an Odia title dataset (OdiCoviCorp) for the review of health care information gathered from different online sources, including social media, news articles, blogs, and transcripts reporting on COVID 19 (Novel Corona Virus epidemic 19) in particular. The work results in the development of a corpus of more than 50,000 titles from numerous electronic media websites, social media articles, blogs, and transcripts. The data set will be a new benchmark data set in the Odia language. We have used unsupervised pre trained models like Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA) and Bi directional encoder representation from transform (BERT) to train the data and the developed model had been used to test unknown input data in Odia language related to COVID 19. We are offering this new benchmark dataset for a follow up analysis to the researcher group to build different applications on top of it to discuss various facets of disinformation handling, anxiety identification, etc. linked to pandemics in low resource languages such as Odia.

title: Understanding factors causing stress and anxiety in a low resource language using speech summarization
abstract: There is an urgent need of mental health awareness in developing countries like India, where there is a severe lack of knowledge and literacy pertaining to this subject. This requires better understanding of the causes and factors behind such disorders, and the communication of such knowledge among the general population. This communication is a challenge because in a nation of diverse culture, there are many languages which have very low resources. This paper aims to detect stress and anxiety, and its associated causes by using an extractive speech summarization method, based in Assamese language. This paper proposes a novel sentence ranking technique where the linguistic characteristics combined with prosodic features of spoken sentences are incorporated in the ranking of the candidate sentence. The presence of linguistic and acoustic features in the sentence, which indicates stress and anxiety, will increase the relevance of that candidate sentence and be included in the resulting summary. A convolutional neural network is used to extract the prosodic features like pitch, intensity, and fundamental frequency, which are the most common biomarkers of stress and anxiety in an audio signal. The linguistic characteristics of stress and anxiety in Assamese are trained using a neural network architecture. The summary would then be able to highlight the most common causes of such mental disorder, which would lead to further awareness and diagnosis.

title: Specialized neural machine translation for health information in under resourced languages in Africa : the case of somali
abstract: During the covid 19 pandemic, awareness and access to health information have become the best vectors to stem the spread of this pandemic. The scarce linguistic resources of under resourced African languages prevent Africans from accessing health information in their mother tongues, whether in private clinics, hospitals or public media. The aim of this work is to ensure that authentic medical information related to COVID 19 reaches Somalis in their own language, primarily those in village or rural communities with limited language resources, so that they can take appropriate action. to fight the pandemic while avoiding falling into the infodemic, very present in Africa during this COVID 19 crisis. In this chapter, we will talk about our methodology for building a parallel medical corpus to assess the quality of two neuronal MT system specialized in the medical field of English Somali and French Somali language pairs. These two neural machine translation(NMT) systems built will be used to allow the development of multilingual applications in the field of health for speakers of the Somali language living in East Africa (Somalia, Ethiopia, Djibouti and Kenya). This chapter is organized as follows. After the introduction , the section 2 describes the related works in this field , our methodology used to build dataset for this task was described in section 3. Then section 4 describes the details of our experiment and results . Finally section 5 concludes and gives some perspectives. Introduction Related Works Dataset Development Experiment and Results Conclusion References

title: Natural language processing for mental disorders: an overview.
abstract: In recent years, there has been a surge in interest in using natural language processing (NLP) applications for clinical psychology and psychiatry. Despite the increased societal, economic, and academic interest, there has been no systematic critical analysis of the recent progress in NLP applications for mental disorders, or of the resources available for training and evaluating such systems. This chapter addresses this gap through two main contributions. First, it provides an overview of the NLP literature related to mental disorders, with a focus on autism, dyslexia, schizophrenia, depression and mental health in general. We discuss the strengths and shortcomings of current methodologies, specifically focusing on the challenges in obtaining large volumes of high quality domain specific data both for English and for lower resource languages. We also provide a list of datasets publicly available for researchers who would like to develop NLP methods for specific mental disorders, categorized according to relevant criteria such as data source, language, annotation, and size. Our second contribution is a discussion on how to support the application of these methods to various languages and social contexts. This includes recommendations on conducting robust and ethical experiments from a machine learning perspective, and a discussion on how techniques such as cross lingual transfer learning could be applied within this area.

title: Language and Domain Independent Approach to Automatic Detection of COVID 19 Fake News
abstract: The COVID 19 pandemic, a global phenomenon, has caused the spread of deceptive information on social media. This means that people can commit bad practices, such as the use of incorrect medications or prevention methods. Proposed methods for detecting fake news have assumed that all content in a document is deceptive; however, those texts can include truthful claims. This study shows that the key ideas are more likely to transmit deceptive claims by including a summarization process, which removes secondary ideas from documents, before its classification as truthful or deceptive. The classification results on datasets in Arabic and English languages show an F measure over 92%. Chapter outline Section 1. Introduction; Section 2. Related work; 3. The proposed approach for the detection of COVID 19 fake news; Section 4. Experimental results; Section 5. Conclusion.

title: Analyzing the role of emotions in Spanish tweets posted during the COVID 19 pandemic
abstract: During the course of 2020, COVID 19 was the main topic of discussion around the world. Social media serves as a platform for people for expressing themselves and also for sharing information about this topic. The users perception of such a situation was changing throughout the time. In this work, we analyzed the role of different emotions ranging from broader categories to finer grained emotions. Besides, we also analyze a set of psycholinguistics aspects. Such information can be useful for developing tools that could have several applications as sentiment analysis, emotion detection, and human need detection, which are important parts in the human affective states. In the development of this work we can identify 5 important stages: data collection, preprocessing, storage, analysis, and visualization. Each of these stages plays an important role and is described in detail. The purpose is to have a tool that allows to carry out the analysis of the information effectively. The proposed methodology is useful both for tweets downloaded directly, with some hashtags or following up on a conversation thread, as well as for the use of a corpus of tweets that you want to analyze or even carry out a comparison between these two scenarios. The obtained results serve to validate the potential of exploiting such knowledge for analyzing users emotions towards this complex and challenging topic.

title: A REVIEW OF THE NATURAL LANGUAGES PROCESSING METHODS AND RESOURCES OF DIFFERENT LANGUAGES TO IDENTIFY CONFUSABLE DRUG NAMES
abstract: A medication error is a risk for the patient safety causing at least one dead per day and harming approximately 1.3 million people a year in the United States. According to the World Health Organization, the estimated annual cost of medication errors is around at US$ 42 billion. The pharmacovigilance agencies of each country have reported that errors in the medication administration process are very frequent with different types of harm to the patient. One of the most common medication errors is the orthographic and phonetic confusion of the drugs names. This problem has been mainly addressed by government agency investigations for three decades where lists of confusing drug pairs have been compiled periodically with the aim of avoiding the registration of new potentially confusing drug names or modifying the presentation of previously registered confusing drug names, and alert healthcare professionals. The research reviews that have been carried out are particularly focused on the problem of managing the drug administration process in the case of the United States. However, the reviews do not delve into natural language processing methods with a focus on languages and cases from different countries such as Australia, Germany, Canada, Brazil, Spain, Ireland, and Mexico. This chapter deals with a broad review of what are the research needs in this area, similarity resources, methods and measures that has been developed and published by different countries in the last three decades for the problem of confusion of drug names. In particular, 26 proposed measures of orthographic and phonetic similarity are described, the evaluation methodologies used, the individual and combined baseline measures, the assembly approaches between the different authors, the databases used of pairs of confusing names from different countries, the adaptation of the agreement methods with the needs and requirements of the regulatory organizations of the aforementioned countries.

title: Feature Analysis and Classification of Impaired Language Caused by Brain Injury
abstract: Language impairment occurs from different illnesses, having a variety of causes. In this work, we focus on the analysis of impaired language caused by a traumatic brain injury (TBI) which can vary from aphasia, apraxia, dysarthria, or other sort of alterations. Modifications that cannot be explained with the characteristics, or at least part of them, describing, for instance, aphasic language cases from other causes. Furthermore, we concentrate on the post traumatic recovery period which has been barely studied. This can be considered a low resource language given the scarcity of data and the complication to generate synthetic data. The interest of researching modifications in impaired language has maintained and keeps growing, following a diversity of approaches. Particularly, the period corresponding to the post traumatic recovery stage in atypical language caused by a traumatic brain injury has been scarcely explored. The samples of our study were extracted from information collected as part of a long term research called Communication recovery after TBI. For the current analysis, the different phases of recovery (after three, six, nine, and twelve and twenty four months) were considered. The findings reported specify the steps followed during the inspection of lexical and syntactic feature sets with the objective of not only determine which contribute most to describe TBI affected language singularities, but also to analyse which of them are sensitive enough to capture changes throughout the different stages of recovery. For this purpose, we employ language technologies, statistical analysis, and machine learning. Starting with an initial full feature set, after conducting an analytical process, we attained selected sets with fewer attributes, employing varied classification algorithms (Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Bayes Net), and reaching comparable efficacy measures to those obtained from the complete feature sets taken as baseline. Moreover, the reduced feature sets allow to identify key attributes to detect the language impairment evolution.

title: REDUCING THE RISK OF LOOK ALIKE AND SOUND ALIKE DRUG NAMES IN PORTUGUESE
abstract: There are hundreds of drug names that are used in a pharmacotherapy treatment that goes through different communication means and circumstances that increase the risk of confusion when they are prescribed, written, advertised, listened to, searched, and administered; because the drug names look and sound very similar. Look Alike and Sound Alike (LASA) drug names have caused cost and damage health. For this problem, several countries have implemented programs in the last years to compile pairs of confusing drug names that have been related to medication errors. The LASA pairs are published to help healthcare professionals to avoid the error. In the United States of America, the Food and Drug Administration agency has been implemented computational linguist resources to deal with the identification of orthographic and phonetic confusion in English drug names. These methods are used to reject new drug name proposals or to implement alerts in prescription systems when it can occur potentially confusing between two drug names. However, countries with different spoken language like Brazil also have reported a list with the common Portuguese LASA drug names, but there is no evidence if the previously proposed methods for the drug names in English are useful for the list in Portuguese or whether it is required to adjust and update them for the Portuguese language. The aim of this chapter is to improve the identification of LASA drug names in Portuguese. First, we update the state of the art by evaluating all the individual similarity measures proposed previously and, then, all the models that combine these measures with the list in Portuguese. Second, we updated the models with new individual measures and then adjusted them with the list in Portuguese to improve the identification. Afterward, 25 individual similarity measures and 8 models to identify confused drug names in Portuguese are assessed to show the baselines for this task and the best improved method.

title: LiSSS: a new multi annotated multi emotional corpus of Literary Spanish Sentences
abstract: In this work we present LiSSS, a new multi annotated and multi emotional corpus of Literary Spanish Sentences. We consider that this corpus may be strongly useful in the area of Computational Creativity (CC) to evaluate emotions classifier algorithms. A large number of literary sentences were manually classified by 12 annotators in five emotions: Love, Fear, Happiness, Anger and Sadness/Pain. Some classical classifiers were tested on this corpus. LiSSS corpus is available to the community as a linguistic free resource.

title: An algorithm to detect changes in writing styles of political journalists after major political changes.
abstract: Writers tend to follow a certain style that can be detected, or at least sketched, by an appropriate algorithm. Journalists in newspapers, being also writers, have their own style. Style tends to be stable once writers reach maturity, however, it may be influenced and subjected to changes due to internal or external circumstances. Here, we apply a bag of words approach to explore the style of several columnists working in Mexican newspapers. Also, we track their style along time with the aim of investigating if changes in style and in external circumstances, in particular political ones, appear at the same time. This provided us with an environment to detect variations in stylomics, which is as close as we can get to an experiment. In particular, we compiled hundreds of writings by various columnists, from before and after the 2018 Mexican presidential elections. We build different supervised and not supervised learning algorithms to study the documents, such as random forest, principal component analysis, and k means. Likewise, we implemented different validation procedures. As a result, we detected that the style in several journalists suffered tangible changes at specific times, some of which may be related to the 2018 Mexican presidential elections.

title: Recognition of named entities in the Russian subcorpus Google Books Ngram
abstract: This paper describes how to build a recognizer to identify named entities that oc cur in the Google Books Ngram corpus. In the previous studies, the text was usually input to the recognizer to solve the task of named entities recognition. In this paper, the decision is made based on the analysis of the word co occurrence statistics. The recognizer is a neural network. A vector of frequencies of bigrams or syntactic bigrams including the studied word is fed at the input. The task is to recognize named entities denoted by one word. However, the proposed method can be further applied to recognize two or multi word named entities. The recog nition error probability obtained on the test sample of 10 thousand words, which are free from homonymy, was 2.71% (F1 score is 0.963). Solving the problem of word classification in Google Books Ngram will allow one to create large dic tionaries of named entities that will improve recognition quality of named entities in texts by existing algorithms.

title: Cognitive representation of words in a corpus of short text messages
abstract: The problem of meaning is of the upmost importance in Artificial Intelligence. In the field of Natural Language Processing, modeling human language semantic properties is one of the most challenging problems, as it resorts to technically sophisticated implementations of methods and processes, including the development of cognitively plausible computational models of how language processing and learning might occur in humans. Over the last decade, research on this matter has been directed towards embedded representations popularly known as word embeddings, whose computation is carried out using various algorithms based on artificial neural networks. In this paper we propose a cognitive based scoring system for words in a corpus of short texts written by patients suffering of depression via a smartphone application. This scoring pretends to account for the emotional weight carried by each word. The score of each word depends on its cognitive content and semantic similarity with a predefined list of positive and negative words. The cognitive content of a word is estimated as the contribution that it makes towards the tag of each message where it appears; these tags are given by the patient writing the text message. We hypothesize that this scoring system might have predictive potential for suicide prevention.

title: A dialogue design methodology for virtual assistants
abstract: The use of virtual assistants is getting bigger every day. Advances in areas such as speech recognition and natural language processing have allowed the development of highly advanced frameworks for the construction of virtual assistants. However, moving from an example of dialogue to a virtual assistant that obeys that dialogue is a task that is regularly done in an artisanal way, which makes it difficult to define an industrial process for the development of assistants. In this work we propose a formal methodology, based on finite automata, for the design of dialogue systems, once the design is done, its capture in a framework such as Dialogflow is immediate and makes it possible to formalize a software development process.

title: Inteligencia Artificial en la Prueba de Software: una Revision Sistematica de la Literatura
abstract: Este estudio presenta el metodo y el resultado de una revision sistema tica de la literatura para identificar las tecnicas de Inteligencia Artificial (IA) usa das en la prueba de software (PS). Cincuenta y un estudios fueron seleccionados y analizados para encontrar las tecnicas que han sido utilizadas para asistir acti vidades de PS e identificar nichos de oportunidad para investigaciones futuras. En estos estudios 18 actividades de la PS fueron abordados con 20 tecnicas de IA. Como resultado se obtuvo que las tecnicas de IA mas utilizadas en la PS son la Inteligencia de Enjambre, los Algoritmos Geneticos y las Redes Neuronales Artificiales. Por otro lado, las actividades de PS mas abordadas con IA fueron la generacion de casos o datos de prueba y localizacion de fallas. Por ultimo, los resultados muestran que la colaboracion de estas dos disciplinas ha ido en au mento, lo que confirma que la relacion de estas dos areas es activa y prometedora.

title: Mining hidden topics from newspaper quotations: The COVID 19 pandemic
abstract: In this paper, we extract quotations from Al Jazeeras news articles containing keywords related to the COVID 19 pandemic. We apply Latent Dirichlet allocation (LDA), coherence measures, and clustering algorithms to explore latent topics from the dataset of about 3400 quotations to see how coronavirus impacts human beings. The result is promising, covering some of the top issues that our world has been facing against the COVID 19 pandemic.

title: Deteccion del Alcance de las Negaciones en Espanol Usando Conditional Random Fields
abstract: Detectar automaticamente el alcance de las negaciones en los textos es un tema de mucha importancia para varias tareas del procesa miento de lenguaje natural como el analisis de sentimientos, la recupera cion de informacion y la extraccion de informacion. El presente trabajo propone un enfoque h brido basado en el modelo Conditional Random Fields con caracater sticas sintacticas y el uso de reglas del mismo tipo para resolver el problema del alcance de las negaciones en un corpus de rese nas de pel culas, libros y productos escritas en espa nol. El sistema propuesto alcanza 0,77 en la medida Macro F1 para esta tarea, superan do a un fuerte baseline que obtuvo 0,73.

title: Necessary Building Blocks for Conversational Emotion Understanding with Deep Learning
abstract: Deep learning based methods have gotten great traction lately across various artificial intelligence (AI) fields, including natural language processing (NLP). This popularity has primarily been driven by the stupendous availability of data, often conversational, over the internet. Naturally, the conversations among the users specifically, customer base lend companies various arsenals to make many critical business deci sions, such as marketing, risk management, resource allocation, etc. Un derstanding the emotions of the participants, therefore, has paramount importance in these decision. Thus, in this paper, we point out various crucial concepts and components in the field of emotion recognition in conversations from the perspective of deep learning.

title: Impacto del uso de word embeddings preentrenados en arquitecturas transformer para tareas de traduccion tutomatica en lenguas romances
abstract: Los sistemas actuales de traduccion autmatica basados en la arquitectura transformer han logrado un nivel de exactitud no visto anteriormente por otros paradigmas, sin embargo al ser una arquitectura basada en redes neuronales profundas, la importancia de algunos de sus componentes sigue siendo desconocida. El siguiente trabajo realiza una evaluacion del impacto del uso de word embeddings en traduccion automatica usando una aqruitectura transfor mer y evaluando para el par de lenguas espa nol portugu es 3 tipos de word embeddings, generados aleatoriamente, Muse y fast text

title: Prediccion de viralidad en Twitter utilizando PLN y aprendizaje automatico
abstract: De individuos a instituciones y desde chismes hasta causas sociales, todos quieren ser escuchados. Un mensaje en las redes sociales es un mensaje para el mundo o, al menos, para un grupo. Para que el mensaje se propague, tener una audiencia es una necesidad imprescindible. Twitter es uno de los espacios de discusion de mas rapido movimiento (una cantidad increible de noticias y mensajes politicos pasan cada segundo) y se ha convertido en una fuerza increible para la propagacion de informacion. Los medios tradicionales estan perdiendo terreno ante estos entornos mas agiles y colaborativos. Para mantenerse competitivos, los medios tradicionales tienen que publicar noticias en la plataforma y hacerlo de tal manera que sean influyentes. Proponemos un metodo para predecir si un tuit es influyente a priori. Con este fin, usamos exclusivamente el texto del tuit; luego lo clasificamos como influyente o no influyente mediante aprendizaje automatico, entrenado en un corpus de 6 000 tuits etiquetados automaticamente segun su influencia. Nuestro metodo alcanza un F1 de 78 %; entrena y clasifica en 1,36 segundos. Esta precision y velocidad hacen posible entrenar el algoritmo en tiempo real con muy pocos tuits. Por lo tanto, las aplicaciones industriales son inmediatas.

title: RoBERTa wordwise sentiment multi label classification
abstract: Transformer based models are flagships in improvements in the field of natural language understanding for today. In this article, we research words extraction problem: retrieving words from given sentence that highly influence on text sentiment or define it. Over last decade, the amount of social network users has been growing. As a result, a lot of companies around the globe are facing the issue of understanding senti ment part of given texts. For example, it is quiet important for tracking persons mood or dissatisfaction of product automatically. Rise of deep pre trained models solutions made possible large amount of texts to be analyzed, providing extremely valuable feedback. We apply the transfer learning techniques as well as selected the appropriate error function for our sparse data problem with RoBERTa model as token encoder. As a resulting metric, we have obtained Jaccard Index 0.715. Fitted model not only demonstrates good performance on tokens extraction task, but can also give an insights on reasons sentiment classification models choice.

title: Leveraging Negation Features at Word and Document Level for Polarity Detection in Spanish Sentiment Analysis
abstract: The Sentiment Analysis task is a spotlight in the NLP com munity. Some of the most important questions are about what features to consider when modeling the phenomenon, and despite the big progress, this question is not fully answered. This paper focuses on the influence of negation for polarity detection in Spanish sentiment analysis. We ex tracted negation features from SFU ReviewSP NEG corpus, a dataset annotated with negation structures, and throughout extensive exper iments, we illustrated how the usage of negation features benefit the models performance. Moreover, our implementation is a simple exten sion of the bag of words baseline which also outperforms state of the art results in SFU ReviewSP NEG corpus.

title: Sentiment Analysis in Texts on Economic Domain
abstract: Deriving intelligence from text is very important as it can provide valuable information about events. In this work, a study investigation was carried out using n grams to classify sentiments with different methods of machine learning. We used this approach, which combines existing techniques with the problem of predicting sentence labels to understand the advantages and problems confronted with using n grams in text analysis techniques. Our study aims to fill the gap by evaluating the output of n grams on different texts with the comparison of nine sentiment analysis techniques and found more insights. The evaluation involves assessing the precision, recall, f1 score and accuracy of the function output of several machine learning algorithms using unigram, bigram and trigram features. The method is tested using Amazon, IMDB, Reuters, and Yelp economic review datasets and our comprehensive experiment shows the effectiveness of n grams in the performance of different sentiment analysis methods.

title: Analisis e implicaciones de la deteccion del humor en textos
abstract: El presente trabajo tiene como objetivo analizar el fenomeno de la deteccion de humor en textos y aquellas implicaciones que conlleva, como puede ser el preparar los datos para tener un analisis correcto del set tomado, asi mismo algunas metodologias actuales, todo esto tomando como base una seleccion de trabajos del periodo 2018 2019 los cuales hablan de la deteccion de humor, creacion de datasets y talleres de deteccion de humor. Los trabajos fueron seleccionados dado el interes y los resultados que obtuvieron los autores, ya que entre ellos hay algunos con un enfoque mas vanguardista. Como resultado, se obtuvo un analisis de los trabajos elegidos. Se puede observar que los metodos para detectar diferentes tipos de humor, aun teniendo la misma tarea por resolver, pueden ser variados y arrojar resultados competitivos uno frente a otros.

title: PROTOTIPO DE SISTEMA PARA LA CLASIFICACION DE RESENAS DE PELICULAS
abstract: Clasificar es una tarea que consiste en ordenar informacion de una manera correcta, si no se tienen los conocimientos necesarios sera dificil, por ejemplo, a una persona comun si se le dan unos libros de filosofia los clasificaria a su propio entendimiento, lo cual seria muy diferente si fuera una persona docta en el tema, pero aun teniendo los conocimientos, si la cantidad de documentos, libros o textos es grande, una persona no lo podria hacer por si misma, aun con la ayuda de un grupo de expertos esta tarea sigue siendo larga y fatigante llegando a consumir dias, meses, incluso anos. En este sentido muchas empresas que ofrecen servicios a traves de la web como Netflix, Uber, Amazon, etc. tienen la problematica de manejar comentarios en sus productos o servicios, los cuales, al carecer de una clasificacion adecuada, no son tomados en cuenta, ademas teniendo miles de comentarios por producto hacen que la tarea de revisar los comentarios sea abrumadora. Debido a que estas empresas dependen de la satisfaccion del usuario respecto a sus servicios o productos, se ven en la necesidad de revisar los comentarios para tener una retroalimentacion, teniendo una mejora continua, por lo que se ven obligados a tener un metodo para poder clasificarlos eficientemente.

title: Analisis de sentimientos en redes sociales basado en aspectos: un caso de estudio
abstract: El analisis de sentimientos, o tambien conocido como mineria de opiniones, es un proceso que utiliza tecnicas del procesamiento del lenguaje natural con el objetivo del estudio computacional de las opiniones y valoraciones hacia los productos, servicios, eventos, temas o individuos. Existen tres niveles diferentes de analisis de sentimientos: basado en documentos, basado en oraciones y basado en aspectos. En este articulo, presentamos nuestro enfoque de analisis de sentimientos basado en aspectos sobre resenas u opiniones que existen en las redes sociales.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Detect Suicide From Social Media
abstract: In the modern world, people share their mental health con ditions and depressive thoughts on social media. Such mental depression leads to certain dangerous acts i.e., suicides. Consequently, suicide rates are increasing day by day that makes it an important problem to deal with. Therefore, it has become a trend in research studies to find out such people with suicidal ideation so that early detection may prevent suicide attempts. Certain models of deep learning can detect such individuals to investigate and detect early suicidal thoughts. The current study retrospectively analysed 50 cases of various celebrities who committed suicides. The sizeable dataset containing long term tweets from 2013 to 2019 has been taken from their twitter accounts that helped in investigat ing their mental conditions before committing suicide. Also, 50 common figures were taken for comparison. For the purpose of investigating this problem, deep learning models are utilized in this research study namely Bi LSTM, LSTM, and 1D CNN. We achieve highest accuracy of 84% using Random Forest.

title: Mapping Pre trained Extractive Question Answering on TweetQA Social Media Tweets
abstract: The paper attempts to answer the problem of social media question answering through an extractive approach. The task of question answering involves taking a context and question to retrieve an answer from the context. Our approach uses models fine tuned on SQuAD which is used for extractive question answering to achieve human accuracy in social media TweetQA setting. Our experiments on multiple trans former models indicate the importance of understanding pre processing in the social media question answering and elucidates that extractive question answering settings can achieve near to human evaluation results on ROUGE, METEOR, and BLUE metrics.

title: Graph based and multimodal summarization techniques: a survey
abstract: The rapid growth of data in recent years from the internet and a variety of sources indicates a necessity of summarization of the data for collecting the main theme of the sources. The large volume of data usually contains lots of invaluable and redundant information. In a certain newspaper article, data contains not only text, rather, it is a summation of image, audio, and also videos. A multimodal summarization needs from that perspective. In this paper, we described all recent trends for the summarization of the multimodal data, and a graph based approach summarization to identify the most salient sentences from the document.

title: Multi label Emotion Classification using Content Based Features in Twitter
abstract: Multi label Emotion Classification is a supervised classification problem that aims to classify multiple emotion labels from a given text. Recently, Multi label Emotion Classification has appealed to the research community due to possible applications in E learning, marketing, education, and health care, etc. We applied content based methods (words and character n grams) on Twitter Tweets to show how our purposed content based method can be used for the development and evaluation of the Multi label Emotion Classification task. The results achieved after our extensive experimentation demonstrate that content based word unigram surpassed other content based features (Multi label Accuracy = 0.452, MicroF1 = 0.573, MacroF1 = 0.559, Exact Match = 0.141, Hamming Loss = 0.179).

title: Generalidades para Funciones de Correlacion entre Distribuciones de Probabilidad
abstract: The paper introduces similarity and dissimilarity based correlation functions between probability distributions. The similarity and distance measures that are used compare two probability distributions or tuples of real numbers.

title: Understanding of COVID 19 pandemic and the role of Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The emerging issue of COVID 19, which is caused by the coronavirus SARS CoV 2 is a significant problematic issue. This disease has impacted worldwide and covered the globe in its threat. Scientists and physicians have been investigating pathophysiological aspects of this pandemic to understand the virus structure for the treatment development. In this minireview, we briefly discuss the characteristics of SARS CoV 2, its origin, diagnosis, and treatment. This study will provide an understanding of the role of artificial intelligence in this emerging COVID 19 pandemic along with the impact in our society, economy, health, and industrial level.

title: Clasificacion de Mensajes de Twitter Bot Humano
abstract: La identificacion de bots ha tomado relevancia dentro de las redes sociales debido a su capacidad de influenciar la opinion de los usuarios en temas pol ticos, de consumo e ideologicos. Es por esto que la investigacion relacionada a la identificacion de bots ha crecido en los utimos a nos. Diversos modelos se han propuesto para la identificacion de bots, pero este es un tema que aun no ha sido resuelto. En este art culo se propone un modelo que, mediante el uso de un preprocesamiento espec fico y una red neuronal de cuatro capas, mejora la precision de la clasificacion bot humano de mensajes de Twitter, alcanzando una preci sion de 0.9462, la cual representa un avance con respecto a lo presentado en el estado del arte con el mismo corpus.

title: Deteccion de noticias falsas en sitios web y redes sociales: Una investigacion del Estado del Arte
abstract: La divulgacion de noticias falsas en redes sociales ha provocado grandes impactos en la sociedad durante los ultimos anos, por lo que es importante evitar su propagacion. En la actualidad, existen diferentes formas de atacar este problema, las cuales parten por la deteccion de estas noticias e incluso perfilar a los usuarios que tienden a divulgar este tipo de noticias, ya sea de forma intencional o no. El presente articulo discute las caracteristicas que posee una noticia para ser catalogada como falsa, algunas propuestas de solucion en el estado del arte, para finalmente concluir sobre los resultados obtenidos y sugerir posible trabajo a futuro en el area. Todo esto con un enfoque en las red sociales y sitios de internet dedicados a la divulgacion de noticias.

title: Effect of Smart Feature Embeddings on SemEval 2018 Multi label Emotion Classification Task in Spanish
abstract: The detection and classification of emotions is a very popular and useful task in the field of Natural Language Processing. Emotions in written text provide us with information related to the mental state of the user during an experience. This information can be mined to gain useful insights which have a wide array of applications ranging from marketing, product reviews, feedback mining and more. Being a task with such wide ranging applications, efficient algorithms must be in place for the successful detection and classification. However, there is a limit to the proficiency of machine learning models as they are based on statistical models and the outcome largely depends on the input feature set. In this paper we analyse the effect of stylistic features and smart feature embeddings on the performance of multi label emotion classifiers on the Spanish data set. We observe that smart feature embeddings gain a performance increase of at least 2 4% over standard cleaning and feature extraction procedures.

title: Uso de n gramas sintacticos en la atribucion de traductor
abstract: La atribucion de traductor es la tarea de atribuir un texto traducido a su traductor. La tarea es similar a la mas conocida tarea de atribucion de autor a en procesamiento de lenguaje natural, pero a diferencia de esta tarea, la atribuci on de traductor puede ser mas dif cil ya que el tema esta determinado ya por el autor del texto original, lo que restringe el vocabulario a usar por el traductor. En este trabajo se presentan los resultados de representar los textos usando n gramas sintacticos para hacer la clasificacion de textos a su traductor usando algoritmos de aprendizaje autom atico.

title: Deteccion de ciberataques en mensajes de Redes Sociales
abstract: En este trabajo presentamos una revision de algunas de las investigaciones dirigidas a el analisis de la informacion generada en las diversas redes sociales, y que tienen como objetivo el detectar aquellos eventos o actos que reflejen comportamientos y/o actividades de riesgo que amenacen la seguridad del ciberespacio. Dichas investigaciones han tomado un enfoque de analisis similar a los realizados en otras areas; por ejemplo la aceptacion de algun nuevo producto en el mercado, eventos pol ticos, de salud, econ omicos, entre otros. Pero con la diferencia que los siguientes trabajos estan orientados hacia eventos de ciberseguridad como es la deteccion de diferentes tipos de ciberataques, predicci on de los eventos relacionados a la ejecucion de un ciberataque, incluso las posibilidades de usar una falla en software para poder ejecutar un ataque tomando ventaja de la misma, entre otras amenazas.

title: Analysis of news influence on financial coefficients on insurance data
abstract: In nowadays world there are plenty of open sourced news media origins that cover various closed field domains. News articles are being generated in huge amounts, influencing society and creating their own informational space. In this paper, we are going to explore latent dependencies be tween relative financial coefficients of real world companies and specific news space, which is presented by topics. We found patterns in open in formational space, that have significant statistical relationship with com panys coefficients. We have created a framework to face this task, which includes searching the most influential topics for given rated coefficient among other companies by implementing LDA techniques as well as Logis tic Regression and Markov Chains approaches. With this framework, we have obtained a predictive model, that determines whether the coefficient will rise in rating or lose its value to other companies. As a quality mea surements, we used the Leave One Out Time Dependent Cross Validation approach with an f1 score for fitting Markov Chains and statistical depen dency tests for additional analysis.

title: Generacion de un corpus en espanol con expresiones agresivas
abstract: El bullying es un concepto que se refiere al acoso fisico, verbal o psicologico entre una o mas personas hacia un individuo o un grupo de individuos. Este tipo de agresion evoluciono al mismo paso que los avances tecnologicos y es conocido como cyberbullying. Ahora los agresores hacen uso de las redes sociales para continuar con tales ataques hacia sus victimas. Por otra parte, las redes sociales no cuentan con filtros efectivos que sean capaces de identificar este tipo de conductas entre sus usuarios y ello complica la deteccion a tiempo y las consecuencias psicologicas que sufren las victimas. Se busca crear un corpus en espanol que contenga las expresiones mas utilizadas entre un grupo especifico de personas para identificar la violencia en los mensajes publicados en Twitter.

title: A Statistical Prediction of COVID 19 Behavior in Mexico
abstract: This research uses a new method to predict the COVID 19 pandemic peak and end in Mexico. The advantage of this model over the other statistical models is that it is less sensitive to the sudden changes in the behavior of the pandemic because this model uses the data of the countries in which the pandemic is in its advanced stages. In this method, the data of daily infected cases in Italy and Spain is normalized with the data of Mexico. The new data gives us an estimate about the future of Mexico since we fit the characteristics of the data of Mexico to the data of Italy and Spain and generate a new data for Mexico that has the patterns that Italy and Spain have followed.

title: Resolucion de anafora directa basada en conocimiento para pronombres definitivos
abstract: El fenomeno de anafora es utilizado frecuentemente en la mayor a de los idiomas debido a que permite economizar palabras, per mitiendo realizar omision de antecedentes previamente mencionados en una oracion y sustituirlos con referentes, esta investigaci on se enfoca en la resolucion de la relacion anaforica presente en los pronombres definitivos especialmente con aquellos que no presentan restricciones lingu sticas de genero y cantidad. Actualmente la tendencia inclina a la mayor a de los enfoques a abordar los problemas de procesamiento natural utilizando WordEmbedding por los resultados obtenidos, debido a esto ha perdido popularidad en la utilizacion de enfoques basados en conocimiento, por lo que en esta in vestigacion se mostraran resultados de diversos experimentos utilizando este enfoque mostrando que se pueden obtener resultados representativos ante estos nuevos enfoques. Se proponen diferentes m etodos para encontrar los antecedentes correc tos en una oracion que presenta relacion anaforica utilizando funciones para extraer las similitudes l exicas basadas en WordNet, calculando las distancias que existen entre cada candidato y el contexto presente en la oracion utilizando la medida de similitud de coseno, a nadiendo peso a los candidatos que presenten una frecuencia mayor en las colocaciones con los verbos presentes en la oracion .

title: A Comparative Study on the Effectiveness of Naive Bayes Classifiers in Spam Filtering
abstract: Naive Bayes algorithms are among the very effective machine learning methods being used in the area of spam filtering. However, there are different kinds of Naive Bayes classifiers based on their training and classification algorithms and their attitude toward the data distribution. In this research, conducting a comparative study on the effectiveness of multinomial, Bernoulli, and Gaussian Naive Bayes classifiers in filtering spam emails, we show that each of these three classifiers can be effective for a specific task in spam filtering; however, multinomial and Bernoulli Naive Bayes algorithms are more suitable for this task.

title: Tecnicas de procesamiento de lenguaje natural para el analisis de malware
abstract: Nowadays almost all the people have at least one mobile de vice, Google Inc. created Android operating system in 2008 that would become in the most operating system used in the mobile devices around the world, however as it covers over 80% of the mobile device in the world it becomes as well in a target for attackers, the risk in the applica tions that all of us install in our devices might have malware (malicious software), analyze all applications stored into application store before to make them available to the people this a hard task. There are several works that have been dealing with a malicious application to analyze them, applying techniques such as Natural Language Processing (NLP), in this paper is presented those work that applied NLP, analyzing those works the techniques used, results and future work.

title: Revision de metodos estadisticos para la busqueda de colocaciones en textos
abstract: En el area de procesamiento de lenguaje natural, una de las tareas a resolver es la busqueda y descubrimiento de colocaciones dentro de un texto. Por un lado, hasta hoy en dia es complicado definir el concepto de colocacion de forma intuitiva es una expresion que se compone de dos o mas palabras considerada como una forma de decir cosas. En este articulo de revision expondremos los principales metodos pertenecientes a la literatura de PLN estadistico los cuales sirven como linea base para comparar el desempeno de nuevas propuestas producidas en la actualidad.

title: Deteccion de humor en tweets en espanol utilizando clasificadores de scikit learn
abstract: Identificar el humor es una tarea compleja, ya que existen distintos factores que nos provocan la risa. Esto que complica la tarea de caracterizar el humor de forma que una computadora pueda entender que es lo que nos parece comico. En este trabajo se presenta una comparacion entre distintos clasificadores disponibles en scikit learn con el proposito de identificar si un tweet es humoristico o no.

title: Un algoritmo randomizado de busqueda basado en evaluacion de reglas para generacion automatica de musica
abstract: En el presente trabajo se describe un algoritmo randomizado capaz de generar piezas musicales polifonicas. El algoritmo realiza una toma de decisiones aleatoria sobre un subconjunto de acordes candidatos previamente reducido en base a una funcion de evaluacion creada a partir de reglas de composicion musical. La funcionalidad del algoritmo se prueba mediante la generacion de piezas a cuatro voces de estilo SATB.

title: COVID 19 on the Time, Mexico and the World
abstract: This paper describes a brief analysis on the COVID 19 over the time Globally and specifically centered in Mexico. In this work, we created a website and using Google Data Studio for analytical dashboards we track the daily data of the pandemic which is collected and represented graphically, for all data collecting we developed various scripts mainly based on bash scripting and python which extract data from specific web sites and once we have the initial inputs we start transforming the data making aggregations, correlations and mappings giving the facility of using that transformed data for future works. We also use an specific model for studying the dynamics of the epidemic and this is presented to analyze the rates, model is discussed and it is shown how it can be used to track impactful decisions to reduce the positive cases identified. The data has been collected and treated for study from different sources [1][2][3][4]. Additionally, all the results and final data after treatment, we are publishing it on a daily basis in the following sites. [5][6][7][8].

title: Lemmatization of Russian Language by Tree Regression Models
abstract: In this article, we consider the problem of supervised morphologi cal analysis using an approach that differs from industry spread analogs. The article describes a new method of lemmatization based on the algorithms of machine learning, in particular, on the algorithms of regression analysis, trained on the open grammatical dictionary of Russian language. Comparison of obtained results was performed with existing alternative applica tions that are used nowadays for addressing lemmatization problems in NLP problems for Russian language.

title: Automatic Story Generation: State of the Art and Recent Trends
abstract: Throughout history, human beings have used tales as a way of communicating ideas and transmitting knowledge. One of the great advances in this area was obtained thanks to writing, a fact that substantially facilitated the transmission of these stories. Being such an ancient activity in human history, it is not surprising that it has been the object of study of artificial intelligence, from a very early time in the development of the latter, leading, among other things, to the emergence of the automatic generation of stories. The automatic generation of stories has been a challenge that has been sought to be solved using different approaches. This review brings together some of these guidelines for carrying out this endeavour.

title: An algorithm for extracting terminology from wiki resources in the tasks of extending the ontological knowledge base
abstract: This article describes the proposed model of the domain ontology core domain using the products of the FSPC Mars as an example. The article presents an algo rithm for automatically extending the core of the OWL ontology using the seman tic analysis of the enterprises internal wiki resources. The software was devel oped to create an organizations semantic network based on the ontology core to evaluate the effectiveness of the developed model and algorithm. An extended on tology is created automatically based on user parameters. The accuracy of the generated semantic network was 70%. A feature of the proposed algorithm is the solution of the problem of terms ambiguity. This problem was solved by compar ing the context sets of terms of homonyms wiki pages.

title: Data driven and Psycholinguistics motivated approaches to Hate Speech Detection
abstract: Computational models of hate speech detection and related tasks (e.g., detecting misogyny, racism, xenophobia, homophobia etc.) have emerged as major Natural Language Processing (NLP) research topics in recent years. In the present work, we investigate a range of alternative implementations of three of these tasks namely, hate speech, aggressive behaviour and target group recognition by presenting a number of experiments involving different learning methods, including regularised logistic regression, convolutional neural networks (CNN) and deep bidirectional transformers (BERT), and using word embeddings, word n grams, character n grams and psycholinguistics motivated (LIWC) features alike. Results suggest that a purely data driven BERT model, and to some extent also a hybrid psycholinguisticly informed CNN model, generally outperform the alternatives under consideration for all tasks in both English and Spanish languages.

title: Task of Question Classification of Cooking related Question Answering System
abstract: Question Answering is a very common filed of Natural Language Processing where the most current research work is going on Question Classification module of a Question Answering System plays a very important role in determining the expectations of the user.
